title: Evaluating a large language model-powered system for semi-structured interview in health research.
abstract: Objectives: Conducting qualitative health research with marginalized populations presents persistent challenges related to trust, disclosure, and resource constraints. Traditional in-person interviews can be costly and difficult to scale, while participants may hesitate to share sensitive experiences openly. This study assessed the feasibility and acceptability of a large language model (LLM)-powered conversational interview system as an alternative to semi-structured qualitative interviews with marginalized populations in a community-engaged health research context. Materials and Methods: We developed a web-based, LLM-powered interview system informed by a community-based participatory research framework. The system was tested with 28 caregivers of children with asthma living in subsidized housing. Postinterview evaluation sessions and researcher observation notes were analyzed to assess the system's feasibility and acceptability and identify usability, accessibility, technical, and implementation considerations. Results: Participants reported that the system was easy to use and appreciated its empathetic and nonjudgmental tone. They also rated the system positively for clarity, comfort, and accessibility, indicating that conversational artificial intelligence (AI) systems can be adapted to support qualitative data collection in underserved communities. The Effect of Profit Character on Company Market Value in Communication Services Sector Companies Listed on The Indonesia Stock Exchange In The 2016-2025 Period
abstract: This study aims to analyze the influence of earnings characteristics, Cash Flow from Operations (CFO), and Net Income (NI) on the market value of companies in the Communication Services sector listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX) from 2016 to 2025.Design/Methodology/Approach – Focusing on companies in the Communication Services sector listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange between 2016 and 2025, this study employs a quantitative approach with a causal research design. A total of 174 observations were obtained using a purposive sampling method based on predefined criteria. Data were analyzed using multiple linear regression. In the research model, earnings characteristics are represented by two dummy variables, with the conditions (CFO < NI) and (Total Accruals [TA] < NI) serving as the reference categories.Findings – The results demonstrate that, on an individual basis, only Cash Flow from Operations (CFO) has a positive and significant impact on a company's market value. Conversely, earnings characteristics—represented by dummy variables D1 and D2—as well as Net Income (NI), do not show a significant influence. However, when tested collectively, all independent variables in the model exert a significant influence on the company's market value. title: Is ESG Performance Priced in the Chinese A-Share Market
abstract: This paper examines whether ESG performance is priced in China's A-share market using a comprehensive framework by changing ESG measure, empirical approach, and pricing horizon. Unadjusted raw ESG scores do not have predictive power, as the gross return of the unadjusted long/short portfolio is insignificant and negative. When the ESG score is controlled for industry and size effect, the composite portfolio obtains a positive and significant annual return of 2.89% with a FF5+UMD alpha of 3.12% (t=4.02). The predictive power of ESG score comes from governance (G) dimension (alpha=2.60%, t=3.57) while environmental and social dimension are insignificant. The Fama-MacBeth regression analysis shows that each year 1 standard deviation increase in ESG leads to a 0.76 percentage point higher return next year (p=0.0093), while next-month return is positive but insignificant. Event study around the 2024 April announcement of the guidelines for the compulsory sustainability information disclosure exhibits an asymmetric response among big firms, which is indicative of relative revaluation. These findings are robust even if the Wind ESG rating is substituted by Sino-Securities ESG rating.

title: Multistakeholder market orientation: an integrated framework for nonprofit services
abstract: Purpose This study aims to reconceptualize market orientation (MO) as multistakeholder market orientation (MSMO) to better reflect the complex stakeholder environment of nonprofit services (NPS). It examines how MSMO influences NPS performance through innovation, the role of brand orientation (BO) and the effects of transformational leadership and stakeholder engagement. Design/methodology/approach A mixed-methods approach was used in the Indonesian museum sector. Qualitative interviews informed the development of the conceptual framework, while survey data were used to test the relationships among MSMO, BO, innovation, performance, transformational leadership and stakeholder engagement. Findings The results indicate that MSMO positively affects NPS performance through innovation. BO complements MSMO by strengthening internal identity coherence and mission alignment, thereby enhancing innovation and sustainable NPS performance outcomes. Transformational leadership and stakeholder engagement amplify the effects of MSMO and BO on innovation and NPS performance. Practical implications NPS managers can enhance performance by leveraging stakeholder intelligence in decision-making and innovation, aligning multistakeholder responsiveness with a coherent brand identity and using transformational leadership and stakeholder engagement to translate insights into sustainable outcomes. title: The Influence of Earnings Characteristics, Operating Cash Flows, and Net Income on the Market Value of Banking Firms on the Indonesia Stock Exchange
abstract: This study aims to analyze the influence of earnings characteristics, net income, and operating cash flow on the market value of banking companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange during the 2016–2025 period. Earnings characteristics are proxied through a classification based on the relationship between operating cash flow, net income, and total accruals, while market value is measured using the year-end stock closing price. The research sample consists of 39 banking companies, yielding 390 firm-year observations. Secondary data were obtained from annual reports, financial statements, and stock price data. The analysis was conducted using multiple linear regression with a pooled ordinary least squares (OLS) approach. The results indicate that the regression model is simultaneously significant (F = 19.606; p < 0.001), with an Adjusted R² of 0.161. Individually, the dummy variables for the first and second categories of earnings characteristics have a significant negative effect on market value compared to the reference category. Net income has a significant positive effect, whereas operating cash flow has a significant negative effect. The Kolmogorov–Smirnov test indicates that the residuals are normally distributed, while the Glejser test suggests the presence of heteroskedasticity. Consequently, the OLS coefficients in this study should be interpreted with caution; furth…

title: Serum, dried blood spot and urine steroid profiles in trained females: impact of oral contraception and consequences for the athlete biological passport
abstract: Introduction The objective of this study was to explore in young female athletes, with normal menstrual cycle (NMC) or using combined oral contraceptives (COC) (low ethinylestradiol/levonorgestrel), the impact of the hormonal status on the serum, dried blood spot (DBS) and urine steroid profiles of the Athlete Biological Passport (ABP) simultaneously. Method We therefore examined in 15 COC female athletes during active hormone intake and washout phase compared to 20 NMC female athletes in early follicular, end follicular and mid-luteal phases, 6 urinary steroidal markers and their relative ratios, i.e., testosterone (T), epitestosterone (E), androsterone (A), etiocholanolone (Etio), 5 α -androstane-3 α ,17 β -diol (5 α Adiol), 5 β -androstane-3 α ,17 β -diol (5 β -ADiol), T/E, A/T, A/Etio, 5 α Adiol/5 β Adiol and 5 α Adiol/E, while testosterone, androstenedione (A4) and T/A4 ratios were determined both in serum and DBS. Results While NMC phases only impacted few parameters, COC intake induced significant changes in urine steroid profile with significant decrease in E coupled to higher T/E and 5 α Adiol/E ratio. COC also modified blood ABP steroid profiles, as its administration influenced, irrespective of the inactive/active phase, not only A4 levels but also T/A4 ratio in both serum and DBS. title: Does ESG Add Incremental Information to Multi-Factor Portfolios in China's A-Share Market? Evidence from CSI 300 Constituents
abstract: In recent years, more and more investors around the world have started to think about environmental, social, and governance (ESG) issues when they invest, not just financial numbers. However, it is still not fully clear whether ESG adds real, extra information to a systematic, rule-based (quantitative) investment strategy, beyond what common risk factors already explain. This paper studies whether ESG shows incremental explanatory power in a quantitative stock portfolio, using stocks from the CSI 300 Index in China and ESG ratings from Huazheng ESG, one of the most widely used domestic ESG rating providers. Based on the Fama-French five-factor model plus a momentum factor, this study sorts stocks into an ESG long-short portfolio and uses a time-series regression to test whether this portfolio still earns a return that the other six factors cannot explain. This study expects the ESG portfolio to show a small but positive extra return (alpha) after controlling for size, value, profitability, investment, and momentum, though this result may partly overlap with these existing factors rather than being fully separate from them. The findings will help clarify how much new information ESG really adds to a standard quantitative portfolio in China's A-share market.

title: Beyond guesswork: how market knowledge and social influences impact investment decisions in Brazil
abstract: Purpose This study aims to investigate how market knowledge and social influences are associated with investment decisions in Brazil. It examines the relationship between investment participation and two cognitive enablers – self-declared market knowledge and education – as well as three information channels: professional guidance, autonomous search and informal sources. Investment decisions are differentiated according to the complexity of financial products, classified as low, medium or high. Design/methodology/approach Annual data from the Brazilian Association of Financial and Capital Market Entities (ANBIMA)/Datafolha “X-ray of the Brazilian Investor” survey (2018–2023) are analyzed, comprising 26,428 individuals aged 16 and over across all Brazilian regions. Financial products are classified into low-, medium- and high-complexity categories. Separate binary logistic regression models are estimated for each category because respondents may hold investments across multiple complexity levels and the proportional odds assumption of ordinal logistic regression is violated. The models assess associations between investment decisions, market knowledge, education and information sources, controlling for demographic, socioeconomic, regional, temporal and pandemic-related factors. title: The regulating role of governance framework on the association between external financing and accounting manipulation: evidence from an emerging market
abstract: Purpose The study aims to investigate the moderating role of corporate governance mechanisms on the relationship between corporate external financing and accounting manipulation in an emerging market. Design/methodology/approach The study uses data extracted from the annual reports of 118 publicly traded companies spanning 13 categories of non-financial companies in Bangladesh from 2011 to 2024. The data were analyzed and hypotheses tested using multivariate linear regression with the ordinary least squares method. Corporate governance index (CGI) was used to examine the moderating effect of governance mechanisms on the association between external financing and earnings management. Findings Empirical evidence shows that firms relying more on external debt financing are more likely to practice earnings management. However, equity financing exhibits a statistically significant inverse relationship with earnings management. Corporate governance mechanisms significantly negatively impact earnings management as well as significantly moderate the association between external financing and accounting manipulation. Practical implications Policymakers can use the findings of this study to formulate the decision for external financing. Investor can choose companies that give priority to equity financing. title: Quality behind the label: fatty acid label accuracy, oxidative status and vitamin E composition of omega-3 food supplements on the Slovenian market
abstract: Introduction Omega-3 food supplements are widely used to increase the intake of long-chain n-3 polyunsaturated fatty acids, particularly EPA (C20:5n-3) and DHA (C22:6n-3). However, their quality may vary in terms of fatty acid content, label accuracy, antioxidant composition and oxidative status. Methods This study evaluated 26 commercially available omega-3 food supplements from the Slovenian market. Fatty acid composition was determined by gas chromatography and compared with the declared label values, while oxidative status was assessed using peroxide value (PV), p-anisidine value (p-AV), Totox and malondialdehyde (MDA) levels. Vitamin E compounds were determined by HPLC. Results Substantial variability was observed among products. Only 44% showed close agreement with the declared EPA + DHA content, while close agreement for the individual EPA and DHA contents was observed in 39.1% of comparable products. PV ranged from 1.3 to 26.2 meq O 2 /kg oil, with 26.9% of samples below 5 meq O 2 /kg oil and 80.8% below 10 meq O 2 /kg oil. In contrast, p-AV values were generally low; among the 21 applicable non-krill products with valid p-AV results, 20 (95.2%) had values at or below 20. Totox values ranged from 13.3 to 72.8, with 11 of 21 applicable non-krill products (52.4%) having values at or below 26. MDA concentrations ranged from 0 to 22.6 nmol/g oil. title: Market Microstructure and Ownership Structure as Determinants of Stock Returns: Evidence from Indonesian Listed Companies
abstract: Background: Limited evidence jointly examines trading activity, scripless shares, detailed ownership categories, and free float as correlates of stock returns in Indonesia. The MSCI ban on February 2026 on any index adjustments related to Indonesian securities, which was partly due to the low transparency regarding free float and ownership structure, prompted the study. Objective: This study examines these relationships among Indonesia Stock Exchange-listed firms during 2021–2025. Methods: Balanced panel data cover 624 firms and 3,120 firm-year observations obtained from KSEI, IDX, Bank Indonesia, and the World Bank. Fixed-effects regression was selected using Chow and Hausman tests and estimated in Stata 17 with Driscoll–Kraay standard errors. Results: At the 5% significance level, corporate and individual ownership are positively associated with stock returns, whereas insurance and pension fund ownership are negatively associated. Trading volume activity, scripless shares, free float, and the remaining ownership categories are not statistically significant. Market capitalization is positively associated with returns, interest rates are negatively associated, and GDP growth is not statistically significant. The reported adjusted R² is 0.249. Conclusion: The findings highlight heterogeneous ownership associations within a unified market microstructure framework. They inform inv…

title: Unregistered landlords in an emerging housing market: measuring rental supply through a national tax-enforcement campaign in Türkiye
abstract: Purpose Housing market analysis counts dwellings, prices and tenure, but not the suppliers of rental housing. This paper aims to measure a national landlord population, its registration compliance and its geography. Design/methodology/approach Türkiye’s 2024–2026 rental-income enforcement campaign, which combined data-matching, mass warnings, 425,000 inspections, tenant counter-declaration and compulsory bank transfer of rent, is treated as an interrupted administrative measurement process. A registration model (registered taxpayers equal compliance multiplied by true landlords) is applied to monthly counts for 81 provinces (December 2022–December 2025), with census tenure benchmarks, event studies with formal pre-trend tests and a placebo registry. Findings The registry grew by 0.8% in the pre-campaign year and by 41.5% (+940,549) over two campaign years. At least 0.7–0.9 million previously unregistered rental-income taxpayers were revealed. Pre-campaign compliance is estimated at 40–68%, implying 3.3–4.6 million landlords against 2.27 million registered taxpayers. The registration response was largest where tenant households per registered taxpayer were highest (2.2 in Istanbul and 30.5 in Mus), including within regions. Research limitations/implications Estimates are bounds rather than point estimates; registration does not imply truthful declaration; and the campaign was st…

title: Consumer Preferences for Ice Cream Candy in a University Market: A Usage–Attitude–Image Analysis of Product Design and Value
abstract: Backgrounds: A familiar frozen snack can be made more distinctive through coating, texture, and presentation, but its value also depends on affordability and convenient access. Objectives: This study applied Usage–Attitude–Image (UAI) to identify product preferences, consumption settings, desired image, and price–value expectations for an Ice Cream Candy concept among consumers in Iligan City. Methodology: A descriptive consumer survey gathered 300 usable responses, including a separate three-layer choice module reported for 281 respondents. Frequencies, percentages, item means, and descriptive content categories informed an integrated market profile. Findings: The sample was 90.00% students, and 74.33% reported monthly allowance/income below ₱5,000. Afternoon consumption (60.00%) and fixed-booth preference (76.67%) were prominent; lack of availability was the leading barrier (49.67%). Chocolate base flavor (70.33%), dark-chocolate coating (55.33%), crunchy texture (58.00%), and popsicle format (48.67%) led key selections. Clean, mess-free eating had the highest image-item mean (M=4.21). The largest willingness-to-pay group selected ₱20–₱30 (39.67%). title: A Study of L'Oréal's Product Marketing Strategies in the Context of Livestream E-Commerce —A Case Study of the Chinese Market
abstract: Livestream e-commerce has become a major sales channel in China, converting real-time content engagement into immediate purchases. Existing research mainly takes a consumer psychology perspective and pays little attention to how multinational brands design their marketing mix within livestreaming, leaving theoretical, empirical, and contextual gaps. This study examines L'Oréal, China's largest beauty group, to understand how it enhances perceived product value, balances promotional pricing with a premium brand image, builds an omnichannel platform system, and converts engagement into sales. Using a single-case study design, it draws on consumer purchase behaviour theory and the 4Ps marketing mix framework to analyse a corpus of company disclosures, trade press reports, regulatory documents, and academic literature published between 2021 and 2026. The data are examined using directed content analysis. The findings show that livestreaming compresses trust-building mechanisms (perceived value, perceived risk, and situational triggers such as scarcity and social proof) into a single real-time, multiplatform event across product, price, place, and promotion. Four structural problems arise from the tension between brand control and platform decentralisation: pricing governance, KOL dependency, data fragmentation, and tightening regulation. Artificial Intelligence in Financial Market Microstructure: Implications for Liquidity, Price Discovery, and Systemic Risk
abstract: Market microstructure research is about the understanding of how trading rules, information asymmetries and the behaviour of the participants affect asset prices and market quality. The future of financial markets around the world is being transformed by artificial intelligence (AI). AI has reshaped market execution, transforming the dynamics of liquidity, price discovery, and market-making, from high-frequency trading (HFT) to deep learning and large language models (LLMs). This paper takes a holistic approach to synthesizing the role of AI in the markets, leveraging 15 fundamental papers and studies on classical market microstructure, algorithmic execution, deep learning order book forecasting, and decentralized finance (DeFi) game theory. This research considers AI as a new General-Purpose Technology (GPT) that augments the classical continuous auction models. This study then examines the empirical impact of algorithmic and HFT on price spreads and market liquidity. The paper then explores deep learning models and LLMs for forecasting order books and the sentiment analysis of unstructured data. Lastly, it examines the systemic risks associated with algorithmic authority and rational opacity and suggests future regulatory and economic modelling.

title: Hybrid Value Creation in Public Corporations: A Resource Orchestration Perspective on Balancing Public Service Obligations and Market Competitiveness
abstract: This study addresses the growing challenge faced by public corporations in balancing public service obligations with market competitiveness in increasingly dynamic and uncertain environments. In many emerging economies, public corporations such as local government-owned firms operate under hybrid institutional logics that demand both social value creation and financial performance. However, prior studies have largely examined these dimensions separately, leaving a critical knowledge gap regarding how organizations strategically integrate dual mandates through internal capabilities. Here, we show how resource orchestration provides a strategic mechanism to align, bundle, and leverage organizational resources to achieve hybrid value creation. Using empirical evidence from a public enterprise, this study reveals that effective orchestration enhances governance quality, operational efficiency, and adaptive capacity despite constraints such as bureaucratic rigidity, political intervention, and limited digital maturity. The findings demonstrate that organizations capable of dynamically reconfiguring resources are better positioned to reconcile competing objectives and sustain long-term competitiveness. The implications highlight the need for strengthening managerial capabilities, advancing digital transformation, and fostering governance reforms to support hybrid value creation in Pu…

title: Main practices, drivers and barriers of sustainable fashion entrepreneurship in an emerging market
abstract: Purpose This study examines the sustainable practices, drivers and barriers of sustainable fashion entrepreneurs in an emerging Latin American market. Design/methodology/approach This qualitative multiple-case study examines 24 small fashion brands in Chile through semi-structured interviews, triangulated with follow-up discussions and over 150 customer reviews. Data were analysed using inductive coding guided by the triple bottom line framework. NVivo 14 supported coding, while within- and cross-case comparisons identified sustainability practices, drivers and barriers. Findings Key practices include using environmentally responsible materials, reducing waste, ensuring fair wages, supporting local production and selecting sustainable suppliers. Key drivers include social and environmental values, commitment to reducing ecological impact, promotion of fair labour conditions, growing consumer awareness and opportunities for differentiation. Barriers include high production costs, limited consumer understanding of sustainable fashion and cultural stigma surrounding second-hand and repurposed materials. Research limitations/implications The study focuses on small fashion entrepreneurs in a single emerging market, limiting generalisability. Nevertheless, methodological rigour strengthens the credibility of the findings and provides a basis for future research on sustainable entrepr…

Consider the multi-field coupling influence mechanism of different spot sizes in the laser cladding process of Fe31 under the effect of light powder
abstract: Abstract To address the unclear mechanisms regarding how different spatial energy distributions of laser spots affect powder-laser interaction and multi-physical field responses in the melt pool during off-axis powder feeding laser cladding on curved substrates, this study conducted a comparative investigation on powder transport and cladding processes under rectangular and circular laser spot conditions. Continuous-discrete phase and thermo-fluid-stress multi-field coupled numerical model was established for laser cladding of Fe31 powder with off-axis powder feeding on a Q235 curved substrate. The model employs a 1200 W laser power, a scanning speed of 6 mm s −1 , and a powder feed rate of 10 g min −1 . Considering the particle size distribution and the temperature-dependent thermal properties of the material, it conducts a comparative analysis of the transient evolution of powder temperature, concentration, flow velocity, as well as the temperature field, flow field, and stress field in the melt pool under both rectangular and circular beam spot conditions. The results show that, under the same total laser power, the rectangular light spot has a wider and more uniform energy distribution area, reducing the concentration of local heat input. When the laser irradiation lasts for 2 s, the maximum flow velocity of the rectangular light spot increases by approximately 21.1%; the m…

title: Do Fund Flows Respond to Past Market Returns
abstract: This paper investigates whether the return on the China Securities Index (CSI) stock market index in the preceding quarter affects the flows into Chinese equity and mixed funds. This section describes the data and empirical procedure used to answer the question raised above. The sample includes 52,380 fund-quarter observations from 2,619 funds retrieved from Wind from the beginning of 2020 through the end of 2024. The pooled ordinary least squares regressions regress Flow on the proportional quarterly change in fund shares with both conventional and quarter-clustered standard errors calculated separately for each of the two groups of funds. The estimates indicate that the coefficients are positive yet statistically insignificant for the full sample and mixed funds regardless of error clustering, whereas the positive coefficient is significant for equity funds based on conventional standard errors and becomes insignificant otherwise. A close scrutiny of the results suggests a low R² value in all equations, implying that most variations in Flow remain unexplored.

title: Multi-Source Data Fusion Based Market Demand Forecasting and Intelligent Business Decision Optimization
abstract: New retail demand is determined by unpredictable sales dynamics, inventory level, promotion actions, weather conditions, and time factors, whereas stockouts may lead to demand underestimation due to distorted sales and negative replenishment decision-making. In order to solve the issue, a multi-source forecasting and business decision system has been designed with the help of FreshRetailNet-50K. First, stockout-affected demand was restored, followed by encoding and dynamic fusion of historical demand, inventory, promotion, weather, calendar, and product data via gated attention network to obtain seven days point and quantile forecasting. After that, forecasting was integrated in the rolling replenishment strategy with regard to ordering, holding, spoilage, stockout, capacity, shelf-life, and lead-time costs. According to experimental results, the proposed multi-source model yielded an MAE score of 6.84, an RMSE score of 10.27, and WAPE value of 29.36% along with the cost index reduction of the replenishment strategy from 424 to 326. The stockout ratio was lowered to 5.8%, spoilage ratio – to 3.7%, inventory turnover became equal to 8.6, and demand fulfillment to 94.2%. Consequently, one may state that incorporation of heterogeneous market data into probabilistic forecasting may lead to better demand estimation and operational efficiency. Thus, the system offers practical ground…

title: Young consumers’ behavioral intentions toward farm-to-table restaurants in a Muslim-majority market: motivations, emotions and well-being perceptions
abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine how the theory of consumption values (TCV), consumption motivations and emotions influence young consumers’ well-being perceptions, which subsequently shape brand love, brand respect and behavioral intentions toward halal farm-to-table (FTT) restaurants. It also compared same-ethnic and cross-ethnic Generation Z consumers to examine whether cultural background moderates the proposed relationships within this restaurant context. Design/methodology/approach This study used a quantitative research design by collecting data from 420 Generation Z consumers who had recently dined at halal FTT restaurants serving ethnic cuisine. Data were collected through on-site surveys at selected restaurant locations to ensure that respondents had a direct and recent dining experience for the study’s context. The data were subsequently analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling. Findings Economic value, consumption motivations and emotions were found to significantly enhance young consumers’ well-being perceptions, which in turn positively influenced brand love and brand respect. Importantly, well-being perception significantly influenced behavioral intentions indirectly through both brand love and brand respect, highlighting these brand-related mechanisms as important pathways linking well-being perceptions to behavioral intentions toward …

Digital Divide, Public Service Digitalization, and Community Participation in Rural Tourism Governance
abstract: This study examines the relationship between public service digitalization, the digital divide, and community participation in rural tourism governance in Selasari Village, Indonesia, part of the National Tourism Strategic Area (KSPN). Although digital public services are expected to strengthen participatory governance, limited research has explored how digital inequality shapes participation in rural tourism contexts. This study addresses that gap by integrating digital governance, digital divide, and communitybased tourism perspectives. The research employed a mixed-methods sequential explanatory design. Quantitative data were collected through a survey of 100 residents and analyzed using descriptive statistics and Pearson correlation analysis. Qualitative data were obtained through interviews, field observations, and document analysis. The findings show that public service digitalization, internet access, and digital literacy are positively associated with community participation. However, participation through digital platforms remains limited due to unequal infrastructure, low procedural digital literacy, and the administrative orientation of digital services. Most digital platforms primarily support administrative efficiency rather than collaborative governance. The study concludes that digitalization alone does not automatically create inclusive participation. Participat…

title: Uncovering the Drivers of Innovation Performance in Public Service Organizations: A Smart PLS-based Study
abstract: This study examines what drives innovation performance in Indonesian public service organizations by focusing on information and communication technology (ICT), leadership style, and human resource capacity. Using a quantitative explanatory design, survey data were collected from 92 employees of licensing service agencies (DPMPTSP) in three regions and analyzed with partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) in SmartPLS 4.0. The model explains a substantial share of the variance in innovation performance (R-squared of 0.79). ICT has no statistically significant effect, which indicates that the availability of technological infrastructure does not automatically produce innovation. Leadership style and human resource capacity both have positive and significant effects, however, human resource capacity is the strongest determinant. These results challenge technology-centered approaches to public sector innovation and highlight the role of human and organizational capabilities. Drawing on evidence from a decentralized governance setting, the study offers an integrated, human-centered explanation of innovation performance in developing-country public service organizations. These findings can help policymakers balance investment in technology with leadership development and workforce capacity.

title: Beyond service delivery: Maintaining a human-centred academic support model
abstract: Universities are redesigning academic support services to improve scale and responsiveness, with an ongoing challenge of maintaining meaningful human connection. This concise paper reports a case study of Academic Assist, a centralised teaching support service introduced after a long-standing hybrid support model. The study examines how course convenors experience Academic Assist, what factors shape engagement, and how responsive support influences teaching confidence and capability. Data are drawn from an anonymous survey of academic staff who served as course convenors in 2025, including both users and non-users of the service. Analysis combines descriptive statistics with thematic analysis of open-text responses. Findings are organised around three dimensions: connection, capability, and accessibility. The paper argues that academic support should be understood not only as a service function but also as a relational educational practice. It concludes by identifying design principles for centralised academic support services that remain relational, visible, trusted and capability-building during organisational change.

Developing Students’ Leadership and Entrepreneurial Mindsets through Soft Skills Training at SMAN 10 Pandeglang: A Community Service Report
abstract: Secondary school is an important period for developing the interpersonal and entrepreneurial capabilities that support students’ transition to further education, work, and community life. On 22 October 2026, Universitas Pamulang PSDKU Serang conducted a community-service activity at SMAN 10 Pandeglang focused on leadership, teamwork, entrepreneurial thinking, communication, and confidence. A total of 200 students participated. The activity used interactive explanations, case discussions, group discussion, educational games, reflection, and question-and-answer sessions. This article presents a descriptive account based on the activity materials, event photographs, information from the organizing team, and contemporaneous media coverage. The percentage improvement in students’ leadership, teamwork, communication, and entrepreneurial competencies, as well as the number and quality of student group outputs and entrepreneurial ideas, require further evaluation. The article therefore reports the implementation and learning focus without claiming numerical competency gains.

ServiceGameX: a method for designing service gamified experiences
abstract: Purpose The integration of service design (SD) and gamification is essential to ensure that game elements introduced throughout the customer journey are coherent and mutually reinforcing, rather than implemented in isolation. To address this gap, this study aims to propose ServiceGameX, a method that integrates SD and gamification perspectives. The method supports the intentional design of gamified service experiences, particularly in contexts where customer engagement and motivation are critical. Design/methodology/approach Using a Design Science Research (DSR) methodology, the ServiceGameX method addresses a class of design problems related to the integration of gamification principles into complex service journeys, which require orchestrating multiple stakeholders through a structured SD process. Findings ServiceGameX is organized into four stages: service exploration, service visualization, gamification ideation and idea evaluation and prototyping. It combines SD and gamification principles and tools and was applied in the design of an educational library service, illustrating its feasibility in a real-world service context. Originality/value This study contributes to gamification and SD research by developing a design-oriented method that integrates principles from both fields. The method provides structured guidance for designing gamified service experiences across entire…

title: Field monitoring study of reaction walls and pedestals during construction and service phases
abstract: This study presents a full-scale field monitoring investigation of a prestressed reaction wall and pedestal system throughout both construction and service phases using an integrated network of vibrating-wire and fiber-optic strain sensors. The monitoring program captures the evolution of concrete microstrain and reinforcement stress under hydration, prestressing, and quasi-static service loading conditions. During construction, tendon tensioning induced a redistribution of internal strain and stress, with the maximum concrete compressive strain increasing from −168.37 με before tensioning to −290.90 με after tensioning, accompanied by an increase in reinforcement compressive stress. During subsequent quasi-static loading, the maximum concrete compressive strain reached −321.36 με, corresponding to approximately 54% of the design strain limit, while the maximum reinforcement stress remained below 25% of the design strength. All monitoring locations remained under compression throughout the monitored stages, indicating stable overall mechanical behavior of the prestressed system. Comparative evaluation of the sensing methods indicates that fiber-optic sensors are effective in capturing localized strain anomalies associated with cracking, whereas vibrating-wire sensors provide stable measurements for long-term response tracking. The findings provide full-scale experimental eviden…

title: From anxiety to agency: pre-service localized digital literacy and digital teaching anxiety among rural novice Chinese language teachers
abstract: This mixed-methods study examines the manifestations, antecedents, and pre-service cultivation pathways of digital teaching anxiety among rural novice Chinese language teachers in China. Drawing on three datasets from Guangdong Province—a rural teacher digital teaching survey ( N = 333), a novice language teacher anxiety questionnaire ( N = 1,248), and a pre-service teacher internship survey ( N = 277)—the study reveals a “volcano-type” anxiety structure: low baseline levels punctuated by high-stakes situational eruptions. Public demonstrations, leadership observations, and multimedia malfunctions constitute the three primary triggers, suggesting that digital teaching anxiety is often entangled with broader evaluation anxiety in high-stakes digitized environments. The “adaptive mismatch” between standardized digital resources and rural students' local learning contexts is associated with anxiety, with the teaching internship identified as a critical threshold phase. Building on these findings, the study proposes “localized digital literacy” (LDL)—teachers' capacity to select, adapt, and create digital resources responsive to rural students' cultural backgrounds and learning needs—and outlines its integration into pre-service teacher education. The findings contribute to teacher digital anxiety research by shifting analytical focus from individual psychological traits to structu…

title: Policing the 100 most harmful suspects of violence against women and girls in London: an impact evaluation of the metropolitan police service V100 program
abstract: Abstract Objectives Estimate the effect of the Metropolitan Police Service’s V100 program, which tasks the 100 highest-harm suspects of violence against women and girls (VAWG) in London each month for special investigation, on subsequent offending harm. Methods A fuzzy regression discontinuity design exploiting the rank-101 eligibility cutoff on the Cambridge Crime Harm Index (CCHI), estimated with local polynomials and quarterly controls, using 25,535 offenders ranked across eight quarters (June 2023–March 2025) and followed for three to six months. Results Tasked offenders averaged 213 fewer total CCHI points and 201 fewer violence-only CCHI points, equivalent to − 54% and − 53% relative reductions, or a total of 56,658 fewer total CCHI points (equivalent to 155 person-years in prison). Total CCHI points at six months fell by − 50%; the violence-only six-month estimate (− 44%) was imprecise. Statistical power exceeded 0.95 for the main estimates. Conclusions Concentrating police attention on the highest-harm VAWG suspects substantially reduced victim-reported offending harm as measured by sentencing guidelines. Limitations include imperfect compliance with tasking and short follow-up periods. Subgroup analyses and standardized tasking protocols merit future research.

title: ASN Digital Competence: Achieving Public Service Transparency in Bogor Regency
abstract: Public service digitalization has become a national strategic agenda under the 2020– 2025 Bureaucratic Reform Grand Design and the 2025–2029 National Medium-Term Development Plan (RPJMN). However, its implementation continues to face various challenges, as reflected in Indonesia’s ranking in the 2024 E-Government Development Index (EGDI). This condition indicates a gap between digitalization policies and the digital readiness of the civil service workforce. One example is Bogor Regency, which has a large population and diverse geographical characteristics, requiring public services that are transparent, accessible, and equitable. At the same time, studies examining the digital competence of Civil Servants (ASN) in supporting public service transparency at the local government level remain limited. Therefore, this study aims to analyze the digital competence of ASN in supporting public service transparency in Bogor Regency and to formulate strategies for its improvement. This study employed a mixed-methods approach using in-depth interviews, observations, and questionnaires administered to ASN involved in delivering public services in Bogor Regency. The findings indicate that the digital competence of ASN and the level of public service transparency in Bogor Regency are generally in the good category. Nevertheless, further improvements are needed in the areas of innovation, digi…

title: Building sustainable Community Health Worker (CHW) programs: barriers & facilitators to implementation in HIV service organizations in Memphis, Tennessee and St. Louis, Missouri, USA
PRE-SERVICE PRIMARY SCHOOL TEACHERS’ PERCEPTION OF LEARNING ENGLISH FOR FUTURE TEACHING
abstract: This study investigated pre-service primary school teachers’ perceptions of learning English for future teaching using an explanatory sequential mixed-methods design. Participants were 49 Primary School Teacher Education (PGMI) students at an Indonesian Islamic university. Quantitative data were collected through a 30-item questionnaire covering six dimensions: perceived importance, learning motivation, teaching readiness, self-confidence, perceived difficulty, and professional value, and analysed using descriptive statistics and Cronbach’s alpha. Eight purposively selected participants joined semi-structured interviews to explain the quantitative patterns. Overall perception was positive (M = 3.20 on a four-point scale). Professional value received the highest mean (M = 3.36), followed by perceived importance, learning motivation, and teaching readiness (M = 3.29–3.35), while self-confidence (M = 2.95) and perceived difficulty (M = 2.93) were lower. Interviews showed participants valued English for anticipated teaching responsibilities, access to educational resources, and professional development. However, grammar and vocabulary difficulties, limited practice, restricted time, fear of making mistakes, and previous learning experiences constrained their confidence. The findings reveal a notable gap between the perceived professional value of English and confidence in using it.…

title: RNA Interference Mediated Regulation of Tumor Cell Apoptosis
abstract: Evasion of apoptosis is an important mechanism to resistance to anticancer therapy. This review summarizes the principles of RNA interference, tool selection, representative experimental evidence, and current progress of regulating tumor cell apoptosis. Studies have shown that silencing BCL2 can increase tumor cell apoptosis in breast cancer xenografts and enhance the anti-tumor effect of chemotherapy. Tumor cell dependence on MCL1 is influenced by compensatory activity from other anti-apoptotic proteins. The CREB3L2 and ATF5 pathways can maintain glioma cell survival through MCL1. BIRC5 silencing mainly led to impaired colony formation and abnormal mitosis, suggesting that the anti-tumor effect cannot be attributed solely to apoptosis. RNA interference identifies survival dependencies and targets for combination therapy, but its application remains limited by off-target effects, insufficient silencing, and delivery challenges. Validation using clustered regularly interspaced short palindromic repeats (CRISPR), together with studies in multiple models, is necessary to advance its therapeutic application. In particular, independent perturbations and rescue experiments can help establish whether observed phenotypes result from suppression of the intended target. Differences among tumor models also indicate that target expression alone does not establish functional dependence. Fur…

title: Physics-interpretable topological machine learning identifies domain-wall contributors to high-frequency loss in a nanocrystalline soft magnet
abstract: Abstract High-frequency core loss constrains efficiency and power density, yet loss models do not identify which parts of an evolving domain-wall network carry the dominant reversal resistance. We present a physics-interpretable topological machine-learning workflow combining micromagnetic simulations, persistent homology, principal component analysis and inverse mapping for an idealized nanocrystalline soft-magnet model driven at nominal frequencies of 100 kHz–10 MHz using α = 1.0 and frequency-specific integration. Because reversal here is dominated by domain-wall motion, we treat the shape and energy of the wall network, captured by persistent homology, as the governing factor of loss. The first coordinate tracks magnetization, whereas the second captures frequency-associated domain subdivision and correlates with the exchange contribution to domain-wall energy. Their feature-space gradient reveals a reversal barrier near coercivity that increases with frequency. Inverse mapping localizes the largest contributions to propagating reversed-domain tips and selected fine wall segments rather than uniformly across the wall network. Consistent structure–energy–mechanism relationships connect the representation to magnetic physics. Within this protocol, reversal resistance is associated not simply with wall amount, but with a spatially selective subset of high-energy wall configura…

title: The Boundaries of the Public Policy Exception: The Abuse of Article V(2)(b) of the New York Convention and Its Regulation
abstract: The public policy exception under Article V(2)(b) of the New York Convention was meant to be the "last safeguard" in the international commercial arbitration system for protecting the fundamental legal principles and moral baseline of the place of enforcement, yet in practice it has gradually been alienated into a tool frequently invoked by courts of various countries to evade international arbitration obligations and block the enforcement of foreign awards. The abuse of the public policy exception manifests in two typical forms: substantive expansion and procedural abuse, with its root causes lying in the ambiguity of the concept itself and the external intervention of sovereign will. In response, regulation should proceed from two aspects: formulating interpretation guidelines for public policy and establishing a three-tier filtering mechanism, so as to seek a dynamic balance between maintaining the finality of arbitration and respecting sovereign will.

Short-video shopping as maladaptive emotion regulation: a three-wave longitudinal study of compulsive buying and psychological distress among university students
abstract: Background Short-video platforms increasingly integrate entertainment, personalized promotion, live-stream selling, and frictionless payment. This convergence raises concern that emotionally driven shopping may develop into compulsive buying and contribute to psychological distress. Methods A three-wave longitudinal study was conducted among 1,000 Chinese university students. Valid follow-up data were obtained from 903 participants at four weeks and 828 at eight weeks. A longitudinal conditional-process model tested whether T1 short-video shopping engagement predicted T3 psychological distress through T2 compulsive buying and whether T1 emotion-regulation shopping motive moderated the first-stage pathway. A random-intercept cross-lagged panel model provided complementary within-person evidence. Results Greater T1 engagement predicted higher T2 compulsive buying (B = 0.931, β = 0.156, p< 0.001), and this association strengthened as emotion-regulation shopping motive increased (B interaction = 0.637, β = 0.105, p< 0.001). T2 compulsive buying subsequently predicted greater T3 psychological distress (B = 0.167, β = 0.151, p< 0.001). The indirect effect was supported at the mean motive level (effect = 0.156, 95% CI 0.071–0.256) and was stronger at +1 SD (effect = 0.262, 95% CI 0.126–0.417). The index of moderated mediation was 0.106 (95% CI 0.044–0.184), whereas the direct…

title: Temporal regulation of the heat-responsive retrotransposon ONSEN by HSFA2 during prolonged heat stress and recovery in Arabidopsis
abstract: Transposable elements respond rapidly to environmental cues, but how their activity is maintained during prolonged stress and recovery remains poorly understood. The Arabidopsis thaliana Ty1/copia retrotransposon ONSEN is strongly induced by heat through host heat shock transcription factors. Here, we examined the role of HEAT SHOCK FACTOR A2 (HSFA2) in ONSEN regulation during prolonged heat stress (37 °C for up to 48 h) and subsequent recovery. RT-qPCR analysis of a subset of ONSEN copies ( ONSEN1 , ONSEN5 , ONSEN6 , and ONSEN7 ) revealed transcript accumulation in both wild-type and hsfa2 plants during heat treatment, but the temporal patterns differed between genotypes. Although HSFA2 transcript levels declined after an early peak, HSFA2 protein remained detectable throughout the 48-h treatment, and ChIP-seq showed persistent association of HSFA2 with ONSEN chromatin. After heat removal, ONSEN transcripts declined with different dynamics in wild-type and hsfa2 , particularly following 48 h of heat stress. Actinomycin D reduced ONSEN transcript levels during recovery in wild-type plants but had no significant effect in hsfa2 , supporting continued transcription as a contributor to ONSEN RNA levels after heat removal. Together, these results indicate that HSFA2 contributes to the temporal regulation of the measured ONSEN transcript population during prolonged heat stress and e…

title: Editorial: ncRNAs regulation of immune cells and their role in cancer therapies: challenges and implications
Digital leisure, exercise frequency, and reported study planning and monitoring in PISA 2025
abstract: Background Digital-leisure duration can encompass different patterns of use and daily organization. We examined whether its association with reported study planning and monitoring differed across groups defined by exercise frequency before and after school. Methods We analyzed cross-sectional Programme for International Student Assessment (PISA) 2025 data from 506,993 students in 80 education systems. Exercise, digital leisure, and study practices were self-reported. The high-frequency exercise group reported at least three days in each school-day period; the low-frequency group reported zero or one day in each. Weighted nine-group models adjusted for socioeconomic status and the public-use gender category. Fay replicate weights estimated uncertainty for equal-system mean contrasts. Results High versus low digital leisure was associated with lower GOALSET in the low-frequency group (−0.124 index units, 95% confidence interval [CI] − 0.145 to −0.104) and a smaller difference in the high-frequency group (−0.052, −0.070 to −0.034). The additive interaction was 0.072 (0.045 to 0.099), ranging from 0.035 to 0.119 under alternative thresholds. Under stricter cutoffs, the digital-leisure contrast in the high-frequency group had a confidence interval spanning zero. Exercise-group contrasts were positive at both leisure levels. In 75 systems, the paired GOALSET-minus-perseverance intera…

title: Artificial Intelligence Feedback Based Investigation of Emotional Regulation Effects in Music Learning
abstract: With increasing use of artificial intelligence for performance evaluation in music education, repeated mistakes may cause frustration, anxiety, and even withdrawal from practice due to lack of proper feedback mechanisms addressing such problems. This study developed a multimodal feedback system based on MIDI performance, facial expression coefficients, and interaction logs where an attention-based BiLSTM predicted valence, arousal, and need for high regulation and then used contextual Thompson sampling to select affect-adaptive feedback. In the pilot study, the dataset consisted of 1,080 practice segments from 45 novice piano players, and the six-week experiment included 90 subjects allocated into affect-adaptive, fixed technical, and metric-only feedback conditions. The full multimodal model obtained the following scores: Macro-F1 = 0.873, AUC = 0.936, ECE = 0.029, and MEEL = 46.7 ms. At posttest, note accuracy for the adaptive condition amounted to 93.1%, while in two other conditions, it amounted to 89.4% and 87.5%. Also, restart latency for the adaptive condition reduced to 7.3 seconds. Moreover, multilevel mediation analysis revealed a significant indirect effect through emotional recovery, β = 0.16, 95% CI [0.07, 0.27]. This research shows that integrating affect recognition with feedback selection is a promising direction for improving computational responsiveness and em…

title: Tryptophan metabolism in maternal–fetal health: nutritional regulation and clinical implications
abstract: Purpose of review Pregnancy represents a critical window during which maternal metabolism, placental function, and fetal growth are tightly coordinated. This review summarizes recent advances in tryptophan metabolism across the maternal–placental–fetal axis, with particular emphasis on gestational regulation, placental metabolism, fetal exposure to tryptophan-derived metabolites, and implications for early neurodevelopment. Recent findings Tryptophan metabolism extends beyond serotonin synthesis, with the kynurenine pathway and its bioactive metabolites emerging as key regulators of immune tolerance and signaling. The placenta functions as an active metabolic interface, controlling fetal exposure to tryptophan-derived compounds. In parallel, the maternal gut microbiota modulates systemic tryptophan availability and produces indole metabolites that may affect placental physiology and developmental pathways. These data support an integrated network linking nutritional states, microbial metabolism, and fetal development. Summary Tryptophan metabolism is increasingly recognized as a central component of gestational metabolic programming rather than a single nutrient-dependent pathway. Interactions among maternal diet, immune and endocrine status, placental transport and metabolism, and microbiota may provide opportunities for biomarker discovery and targeted nutritional or microbio…

title: Comparison of artifact elimination strategies during postprocessing for the numerical assessment of localized low frequency magnetic field exposure of the hand
abstract: Abstract Numerical computations of induced electric field strength E i inside the human body are prone to so-called ‘staircasing errors’, i.e. physically incorrect local enhancements of the computed E i at the edges of the cubical cells. Similar artifacts can occur due to imperfections in the anatomical body models used. In order to eliminate such numerical artifacts, International Commission on Non-Ionizing Radiation Protection suggested in their 2010 guidelines to use the 99th percentile of the distribution of the 2 × 2 × 2 mm 3 averaged induced electric field strength E i, avg for comparison with the basic restrictions instead of the maximum computed E i, avg value. However, this suggestion was based on very early computational studies using anatomical body models with relatively low spatial resolution. Moreover, a 99th percentile-based assessment of E i, avg appears generally questionable in case of highly localized exposure scenarios, where large fractions of the body remain almost unexposed, and therefore true local hot spots of E i, avg that should be considered may be excluded from the analysis, simply because the exposed tissue fraction is less than 1% of the total body volume. Although this problem has been repeatedly pointed out by several research groups in the past, the 99th percentile-based assessment unfortunately spread out as a ‘general rule’ into some guidelin…

title: Student-centered learning, nutritional behaviors, and self-regulation: psychological and health-related associations with performance readiness among higher education music students
abstract: Higher education music students experience substantial cognitive, emotional, and physical demands that require effective self-regulation, healthy lifestyle behaviors, and adequate preparation for sustained musical performance. Although educational experiences, nutritional behaviors, and psychological factors have been individually associated with student wellbeing, their interrelationships with performance readiness remain insufficiently understood. This study examined the associations among student-centered learning environments, self-regulation capacity, health-related behaviors, nutritional practices, subjective vitality, recovery capacity, and performance readiness among higher education music students. A cross-sectional questionnaire survey was conducted among 468 undergraduate and postgraduate music students, and structural equation modeling was employed to evaluate the hypothesized associations among the study constructs. Student-centered learning environments were positively associated with self-regulation capacity ( β = 0.45, p < 0.001), which was positively associated with health-related behaviors ( β = 0.52, p < 0.001). Health-related behaviors were associated with nutritional practices ( β = 0.55, p < 0.001) and recovery capacity ( β = 0.48, p < 0.001). Nutritional practices were positively associated with subjective vitality ( β = 0.39, p < 0.001), w…

title: Editorial: The function and regulation of T cell subsets in inflammatory disease
Peripheral Neural Regulation of Antitumor Immunity: Pro-tumor and Anti-tumor Mechanisms Across Nerve Subtypes and Cancer Types
abstract: With the research on the interaction between nerves and tumor cells, immune responses, etc. in the tumor microenvironment (TME), the three major neural substars (sympathetic nerve, parasympathetic nerve and sensory nerve) have all been confirmed to have both tumor-promoting and tumor-suppressing effects. The specific effects depend on the type of neurotransmitter, receptor subtype, target immune cell population and tumor background. Critically, tumors are not passive recipients of neural input: they actively remodel local innervation by secreting neurotrophic factors, thereby shaping the receptor landscape of the neural signals they subsequently receive. This article integrates the research on eight types of cancer, consolidates the findings into two major modules: tumor-promoting and tumor-suppressing neural mechanisms.

title: Understanding Football Attendance and Willingness to Pay in China: Evidence from Consumer Preferences and Ticketing Demand
abstract: This study examines the determinants of match attendance intentions and willingness to pay (WTP) in China's professional football market, with particular attention to consumer engagement, match characteristics, income differences, and matchday experiences. Using survey data collected through the Wenjuanxing platform, the study analyzes responses from 216 participants. Spearman correlation analysis, Welch's t-tests, analysis of variance (ANOVA), logistic regression, and ordinary least squares (OLS) regression are employed to investigate consumer preferences and heterogeneity in ticket demand. The findings indicate that football interest, previous attendance experience, and emotional attachment to clubs are positively associated with future ticket purchase intentions. In terms of payment willingness, income and baseline ticket valuation are positively associated with WTP for regular tickets, derby premiums, and value-added matchday packages. Match attractiveness also influences attendance decisions, whereas preferences for online or television viewing are negatively associated with stadium attendance intentions. These findings highlight the importance of consumer segmentation, differentiated ticket pricing, fan engagement, and improved matchday experiences.

Scoping review of digital pathology for neoadjuvant rectal cancer response
abstract: Aim: Neoadjuvant therapy for locally advanced rectal cancer (LARC) yields variable patient responses. Artificial intelligence (AI) and digital pathology offer a novel approach to preoperatively predict treatment outcomes using histomorphological features, potentially guiding organ-preserving strategies. This scoping review maps the current literature on AI-driven neoadjuvant response prediction in LARC to evaluate algorithmic performance and identify methodological gaps. Methods: Following Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for scoping reviews (PRISMA-ScR) guidelines, a structured search of PubMed, Embase, and the Cochrane Library was conducted for studies published within the last 10 years. Studies applying AI algorithms to pretreatment whole-slide images (WSIs) to predict neoadjuvant response in LARC were included. Results: Eleven publications were included. Ten studies used retrospective cohorts only, whereas one study also included a prospective validation cohort of 100 patients. Algorithmic frameworks predominantly featured classical machine learning, using software extraction of predefined features, and deep learning for autonomous pixel analysis. Across heterogeneous endpoints and cohorts, standalone classical machine-learning models reported external validation area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.81…

title: Clinicopathological Characteristics and Therapeutic Response to Concurrent Chemoradiotherapy in Stage IIB–IVA Cervical Cancer
abstract: Objectives: This study aimed to describe the response to concurrent chemoradiotherapy in stage IIB–IVA cervical cancer and its association with histopathological subtype, age, stage, and tumor size.Methods: This retrospective analytical cross-sectional study reviewed the records of 109 women who completed external beam radiotherapy, intracavitary brachytherapy, and weekly cisplatin at Al Ihsan Regional General Hospital, West Java, from 2022 to 2024. Response was assessed approximately three months after treatment using the Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors version 1.1. Histopathological subtype was analyzed using the Fisher–Freeman–Halton exact test, whereas age, stage, and tumor size were analyzed using Spearman rank correlation.Results: Complete response occurred in 77.1% of women, partial response in 18.3%, stable disease in 3.7%, and progressive disease in 0.9%. Complete response rates were 77.3% in squamous cell carcinoma (80.7% of women), 82.4% in adenocarcinoma, and 50.0% in adenosquamous carcinoma (4 women). Complete response rates were 84.6% in stage IIB and 73.8% in stage IIIB; these two stages together comprised 95.4% of women. No variable was significantly associated with response (all p > 0.05).Conclusion: Most women achieved a complete response after concurrent chemoradiotherapy. Response was not significantly associated with histopathological subtype, …

title: Optimization of Sensor Response Time in Microfluidics-Based Biosensors with Balanced Analyte Transport
abstract: Abstract The combined effect of geometric obstruction and auxiliary inlet on sensor response time for a microfluidics-integrated biosensor has been numerically investigated in this study. The flow behavior and mass transfer of an analyte have been modeled using incompressible Navier–Stokes equations coupled with convection–diffusion and Langmuir adsorption kinetics equations for comparable time scales of diffusion and surface reaction. Introduction of a block increases the analyte velocity near the sensor surface with subsequent reduction in diffusion boundary layer thickness, thereby ameliorating the sensor response time. Insertion of an auxiliary inlet diminishes the sensor response time to a greater extent by confining a thin layer of analyte above the sensor surface. A systematic parametric study is conducted to evaluate the blended effects of block height, block position, block width, auxiliary inlet position, and auxiliary inlet velocity on sensor performance. Taguchi-based optimization techniques employing an L27 orthogonal array alongside signal-to-noise ratio analysis and analysis of variance have been utilized for identification of optimal parameter combinations. The results indicate that the auxiliary inlet velocity is the most influential parameter with a contribution of 65.8% toward the decrement in sensor response time. The findings demonstrate that the combinatio…

Translating patient-derived xenograft tumor growth inhibition data to clinical dose–response prediction for antibody-drug conjugates: a QSP modeling approach
abstract: Introduction Antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs) represent a transformative oncology modality, yet existing model-informed drug development (MIDD) methods have not yet demonstrated satisfactory predictive performance for clinical efficacy. Methods Here we develop a model-based framework that integrated patient-derived xenograft (PDX) data with quantitative systems pharmacology (QSP) modeling and virtual patient population simulations to predict clinical patient response in terms of objective response rates (ORR). The QSP model mechanistically incorporated compartmental ADC metabolism and pharmacokinetic distribution, receptor-mediated ADC tumor cell disposition, payload bystander effect and tumor killing. Data of two HER2-ADCs, trastuzumab deruxtecan (T-DXd) and trastuzumab emtansine (T-DM1) were used as case demonstrations. Results The QSP model framework was successfully parameterized to capture tumor growth inhibition dynamics across 16 different HER2-expressing PDX models, and by formulating model-based virtual patients, it is shown that simulation-predicted clinical ORR for T-DXd can match with the ranges observed across actual T-DXd trials. Simulated dose–ORR relationship identified a dosage of about 5-6 mg/kg Q3W for T-DXd as the optimal clinical dose, beyond which further dose escalation yields diminishing returns, and the clinical utility and generalizability of this frame…

title: Defining a therapeutic immunological window for cannabidiol: an exposure-response framework for assessing immunomodulation and immunotoxicity
abstract: Cannabidiol (CBD) has been studied in neurological, inflammatory, and immune-mediated disorders. However, its immunological safety cannot be determined solely by anti-inflammatory properties or the absence of overt cytotoxicity. This conceptual analysis introduces an unvalidated therapeutic immunological window (TIW) to evaluate the relationship between CBD exposure, disease-relevant immune regulation, immunometabolism, and potential immunotoxicity. Targeted PubMed/MEDLINE searches from January 2016 to July 2026 were supplemented with reference-list screening and foundational studies. Evidence was prioritized for translational relevance, emphasizing prospective human trials and primary human immune-cell models that reported CBD formulation, exposure conditions, functional outcomes, and metabolic or clinical safety measures. Current evidence demonstrates substantial heterogeneity across immune-cell lineages, biological models, CBD formulations, and exposure durations. For instance, a short-term study in healthy participants showed selective changes in activation-induced lymphocyte responses, such as reduced T-cell and B-cell proliferation, mixed cytokine alterations, and an increased proportion of effector-memory T cells. However, these studies did not evaluate whether protective immune function was preserved. Additional experimental studies identified potentially regulatory eff…

title: A Laboratory on the Road: Europe’s Regulatory Response to the Opacity of Autonomous Vehicles
abstract: Established frameworks for vehicle regulation are not equipped to certify autonomous driving systems, given that their behaviour in real-world conditions cannot be fully inspected or verified in lab situations. This article examines how European regulators have responded to this challenge in Regulation 2022/1426, the first type approval framework for automated driving systems in Europe. The article extends Burrell’s three forms of algorithmic opacity to also capture the opacity of behaviours emerging from interactions in open, physical environments and uses this to analyse how the regulation responds to each form of opacity and how it distributes responsibilities between vehicle manufacturers, regulators and the public. The analysis identifies three regulatory transformations: operational design domains limit the scope of autonomous driving; scenario-based testing evaluates overall system behaviour rather than the mechanisms of specific components; and a shift towards on-road testing and after-market surveillance dissolves the boundary between testing and deployment. The result is a real-world experiment in which the public have been enrolled as subjects of a continuously extended laboratory. The article concludes that the current regulatory framework never resolves the uncertainties and risks within the type approval process, and instead opts for a continuous modulation of bot…

Practice in modeling holiday effect on retail demand forecasting: a systematic review
abstract: Purpose The purpose of this study is to systematically review and synthesize the academic literature on modeling holiday effects in retail demand forecasting. This paper aims to clarify how holidays are incorporated into forecasting models, identify key methodological trade-offs and evaluate the strengths and limitations of commonly used approaches. By consolidating evidence across retail, operations and related demand-forecasting domains, this review seeks to provide both researchers and practitioners with a structured understanding of how holiday-induced demand distortions can be modeled effectively. Design/methodology/approach This study conducts a structured literature review of peer-reviewed research on holiday effect modeling in retail and related demand-forecasting contexts. The reviewed studies are categorized according to their modeling strategies, including unified holiday indicators, holiday-specific variables, interaction terms, temporal decay structures, historical uplift features and two-stage modeling frameworks. The review emphasizes methodological design choices, data requirements and estimation challenges, with particular attention to issues arising from sparse holiday observations and demand heterogeneity. Findings This review finds that simple holiday indicators are widely used but often fail to capture heterogeneity across holidays, products and time. More …

title: Phonon-Modulated Momentum-Space Geodesic Response Probed by Second-Harmonic Sidebands
abstract: Abstract The quantum metric of Bloch states endows electron dynamics with a Riemannian geometric structure. However, probing its dynamical signatures is severely hindered by the entanglement with ubiquitous band dispersion and topological responses. In this work, we propose a dynamical approach to isolate the momentum-space gravitational analog by investigating the interplay between strong-field driven electrons and coherent optical phonons. We reveal that phonon-induced lattice displacements introduce a time-dependent perturbation to the quantum metric, generating geometric distortions analogous to gravitational waves, which manifest as sidebands of the harmonic spectrum and are quantitatively analyzed at the second-harmonic (SHG) order. Within this model, symmetry analysis and the phase and frequency dependence of the sidebands help distinguish the geodesic contribution from the Drude background. Together with its stronger enhancement as the gap decreases, these features suggest an optical approach to probing the momentum-space gravitational analog within the range of validity of the model.

title: Flexible Adaptive Cyber Risk Management: A Predictive Analytics Model for Adaptive Governance in U.S. Healthcare
abstract: Abstract This research proposes the Generative AI-enhanced Flexible Adaptive Cyber Risk Management (FACRM) framework to address critical cybersecurity challenges in the U.S. healthcare sector. By integrating SAP-LAP theory with predictive analytics and GenAI interpretation, our study develops a dynamic model that balances technical controls (SAP) with organizational adaptation (LAP) through a time-weighted risk assessment formula. The research employs a multi-method approach, utilizing real-world data from HHS breach records and network intrusion datasets and operationalizing theoretical constructs into measurable indicators. Our findings reveal a SAP/LAP ratio of 1.254, indicating that healthcare organizations place a stronger emphasis on technical controls over long-term adaptation, resulting in an integrated risk score of 0.299. The framework demonstrates practical utility through GenAI-generated governance recommendations and cross-regulatory compliance mapping, showing 72.3% HIPAA alignment and effective adaptation to international standards. This study contributes to flexible management theory by quantifying SAP-LAP constructs in cybersecurity, advances methodology through GenAI-enhanced interpretive ranking, and provides healthcare leaders with an evidence-based model for adaptive governance in an evolving threat landscape.
venue: Global Journal of Flexible Systems Management

title: The Accuracy of Linear Models in Stock Price Volatility Prediction: An Investigation and Comparison with Artificial Intelligence Approaches
abstract: Stock volatility forecasting is always crucial for investors and stock owners to make financial decisions, portfolio allocation, and risk management. Even though there are a lot of popular volatility forecasting models existing in the stock market, it is hard to know which one was the best depending on different situations in the market. And so, this review examines the accuracy of linear models in forecasting stock price volatility, and evaluates the performance of these models compared with relatively complicated nonlinear and artificial-intelligence-based approaches. The review analyzes previous studies on major volatility forecasting models, including ARCH, GARCH, ARIMA, and HAR-RV. It compares findings from traditional linear models with more recent research on nonlinear models, machine learning, and artificial intelligence. In addition, the review also considers how forecasting performance changes across different markets, forecasting horizons, and market conditions. The reviewed evidence showed that linear models remain competitive because they are interpretable, computationally efficient, and effective when capturing persistent volatility patterns. Recent studies indicate that machine-learning models do not consistently outperform linear models in every situation, although AI approaches may provide advantages when financial relationships are more complex or when additio…

title: Digital twin capabilities as a dynamic mediating mechanism between supply chain digital transformation and logistics performance in seaport operations
abstract: Purpose This study aims to investigate the persistent translational gap between digital transformation (DT) investments and perceived logistics performance (PLP) in seaports. It seeks to explain how DT generates tangible improvements by theorizing and empirically validating the mediating role of digital twin (DTw) capabilities as a key intermediary dynamic mechanism. Design/methodology/approach Grounded in the Dynamic Capabilities View (DCV) and Resource-Based View, the study proposes an integrated mediation model. The model posits that while DT provides foundational resources, DTw capabilities (real-time synchronization, simulation, predictive analytics and integration) are the higher-order capabilities enabling value capture. The hypotheses were tested using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) on survey data collected from 236 professionals at Jeddah Islamic Port, Saudi Arabia. Findings The results indicate a significant positive direct association between DT and PLP. However, a substantial portion of the association is indirect, operating through DTw capabilities. The mediation analysis identifies DTw as a significant intermediary mechanism, accounting for approximately 62% of the total association between DT and PLP within a complementary partial mediation framework. Originality/value To the best of the authors' knowledge, this study provides the fi…
