title: Serious games for disaster resilience: an interpretative synthesis of reported participant perceptions
abstract: Purpose This study aims to synthesize reported participant perceptions of serious games used in humanitarian logistics and disaster-management contexts, focusing on experiential, ethical and cognitive dimensions of learning. Design/methodology/approach An interpretive qualitative synthesis examined 57 empirically distinguishable applications from 46 eligible articles within an initial 59-article corpus (2014–2024). Inductive content analysis and reflexive thematic analysis were combined with a source-level audit and operational codebook. Findings Five analytical axes emerged: engagement, empathy and social responsibility (29.8%); collaboration and inter-institutional coordination (26.3%); preventive learning and preparedness (26.3%); situational learning and decision-making (14.0%) and innovation, research and science-policy integration (3.5%). Positive affective-interpretive orientations were most frequent (54.4%). These patterns describe reported participant evidence, not causal training effects. Research limitations/implications The study relies on secondary qualitative evidence reported in prior publications. This creates a second-order interpretive layer and entails potential publication and reporting bias, incomplete source reporting and limited visibility regarding sustained competencies, behavior change, long-term dissemination, routine use or organizational adoption of…

title: Renewable investment dynamics, green innovation markets, and transformation of the national carbon profiles in China
Green Bonds and Financing Costs: A Case Study of CATL
abstract: There is broad agreement in the literature that if a company's Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) performance is better, the cost of its debt financing will be lower. Because Contemporary Amperex Technology Limited (CATL) is the world's leading power battery enterprise, its green bond issuance has been highly active, and its relevant information is publicly and freely available, this company was selected as the case to compare the coupon rates of green bonds and conventional bonds. It was found that the average rate of CATL's 2026 green bonds is 1.56%, clearly below the 3.655% average for conventional bonds issued between 2019 and 2020. The mean spread is about 210 basis points. This substantial difference suggests that green bonds may indeed enjoy a pricing advantage over conventional bonds. The conclusion is that green bonds can generate substantial interest savings. Firms should value ESG disclosure, and regulators should support small and medium-sized enterprises in improving ESG capabilities and regulate green bonds to prevent greenwashing.

title: Promotion-rule Complexity and Checkout Abandonment in E-commerce Sales Events: The Mediating Role of Consumer Confusion
abstract: With the rise of big e-commerce sales events, multiple layers of promotions exist, such as platform coupons, store coupons, stacking, membership discounts and category discounts, which make the checkout process more complex. Promotional mechanisms can help to make the product more attractive, but can also diminish price transparency and add to cognitive load. This research examines the relationship between promotion-rule complexity and consumer checkout abandonment tendency and the role of consumer confusion in this relationship. A mixed-method approach was adopted to analyze a publicly available dataset of 12,330 online shopping sessions, and a survey based on a set of scenarios with 218 valid responses. The findings show that the complexity of the promotion rule has a significant effect on consumer confusion, which consequently results in a higher checkout abandonment tendency. Promotion-rule complexity is positively related to checkout abandonment through consumer confusion. The results contribute to the promotion literature by focusing on the last mile of the promotion process and have implications for e-commerce platforms that aim to minimise the friction involved in decisions by creating simpler rules and more transparent pricing.

title: Manufacturing 4.0 adoption and productivity performance in developing economies: a resource-based view from Colombia's North Coast
abstract: Purpose This study examines the strategic value of Manufacturing 4.0 technologies, namely robotics, additive manufacturing and the Internet of Things (IoT), in developing economies, where empirical evidence remains limited. Focusing on Colombia's North Coast, it assesses how firms deploy these technologies to improve supply chain and organizational performance under structural constraints such as limited infrastructure, skill shortages and financial restrictions. Design/methodology/approach Data were collected from 125 supply chain managers in manufacturing firms through a structured online survey. Structural equation modeling (SEM) was employed to analyze the relationships between technological adoption, supply chain practices and organizational outcomes. Findings Robotics and additive manufacturing significantly enhance supply chain efficiency and, in turn, organizational performance. IoT shows no significant effect on supply chain efficiency, reflecting integration challenges and infrastructural limitations. The value of Manufacturing 4.0 technologies is therefore context-dependent, shaped by local capability and resource conditions. Research limitations/implications The study is limited to one region of Colombia and relies on managerial perceptions. Future research should include longitudinal, multi-regional and multi-informant designs to validate and extend findings. Pract…

title: Empowerment, delegation and vision awareness: motivational pathways to workplace creativity
abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine how employee empowerment and task delegation influence workplace creativity through harmonious and obsessive work passion, and whether organizational vision awareness (OVA) strengthens these motivational pathways in a public sector context. Design/methodology/approach Survey data were collected from 533 employees across two Namibian public sector ministries using stratified random sampling. Employee self-reports were matched with supervisor ratings of incremental and radical creativity to reduce common method bias. Structural equation modeling tested indirect and conditional relationships among empowerment, delegation, work passion and creativity. Findings Empowerment and task delegation are indirectly related to creativity through distinct forms of work passion. Harmonious passion predicts both incremental and radical creativity, whereas obsessive passion is primarily linked to incremental creativity. OVA strengthens selected motivational pathways, showing that shared vision enhances the effectiveness of leadership practices in fostering creativity. Originality/value This study demonstrates that empowerment and delegation operate through differentiated passion-based mechanisms rather than uniform effects. By distinguishing between incremental and radical creativity, it clarifies how motivational processes translate managerial practices into d…

title: Emerging threat of Liriomyza spp. (Agromyzidae, Diptera) in horticultural crops: Species distribution, habitat shift and its semiochemical-based management strategies
abstract: The genus Liriomyza (Diptera: Agromyzidae) has recently gained a reputation as a highly invasive and damaging leafminers group causing heavy economic damage in horticultural crops globally. The rising pest status of Liriomyza species is linked to climate change, protected cultivation, agricultural intensification, globalisation and movement of infested planting material, resulting in rapid geographic spread and host range expansion. The overreliance on broad-spectrum insecticides has led to insecticide resistance, pest resurgence, imbalance of predator-prey population dynamics and environmental pollution, thus making eco-friendly control approaches imperative. Among such approaches, kairomone and herbivore-induced plant volatiles (HIPVs) based strategies appear as very promising tools for species-specific monitoring and pest management. The current review provides an overview of the recent research on Liriomyza species diversity, invasion history, biology, adaptations to new environments, as well as morphological and molecular taxonomy. It also gives insight into ecological factors influencing habitat shift and host interactions, including host recognition, response of plants to herbivory, hormonal modulation and volatiles-based communication. Finally, recent achievements in semiochemical-based management, involving host plant volatiles, kairomones, synomones and HIPVs along wi…

title: The Bandwagon Effect and Cognitive Biases in Internet-Famous Restaurant Choice: A Mechanism of Distorted Consumer Decision-Making
abstract: The selection of dining venues increasingly relies on user-generated content (UGC) on local-life platforms. The check-in practice of internet-famous restaurants is not just a dining-related behavior anymore, but rather a dual behavior including experiential consumption and online identity performance. This paper examines how the bandwagon effect, compounded by three cognitive biases, shapes restaurant choice, drawing on publicly observable UGC from Xiaohongshu and Dianping. Unlike the previous studies, which mainly repeat the conclusion of conformity effect, the current paper makes a clear difference between the informational bandwagon, which is derived from genuine consumer experience, and the commercial bandwagon created by marketing activities. In addition, it reveals how representativeness bias, confirmation bias, and availability bias successively exert their effects at each stage of the entire consumer decision process: information exposure, preference formation, pre-consumption expectation formation, and post-purchase feedback. However, it generates systematic mistakes in decision-making as well. Commercial bandwagon signals and the cognitive biases they exploit distort dining choices, inflate expectations, and misallocate capital. The paper proposes a three-party remedy: consumer psychological literacy, platform governance reform, and a merchant reorientation toward cor…

title: A Two-Stage SARIMA–GARCH Approach to Forecasting Global Monthly Carbon Dioxide Emissions: Trend, Seasonality, and Mitigation Implications
abstract: Accurate near-term projections of carbon dioxide (CO₂) emissions help governments gauge progress toward the Paris temperature goals and time demand-side mitigation. Most forecasts rely on annual figures, overlook the pronounced within-year movement of emissions and their reaction to sudden shocks, and rarely model the resulting volatility. Using the IEA–EDGAR v8.0 global monthly fossil CO₂ inventory (156 observations, January 2010–December 2022), this study builds a two-stage model: a seasonal autoregressive integrated moving-average (SARIMA) mean equation selected by an exhaustive search, followed by a GARCH(1,1) variance equation when an ARCH-LM test detects heteroskedasticity. STL decomposition shows a mild upward trend with a strong annual cycle—the seasonal component accounts for 73.9% of short-term fluctuation, with December–January peaks and August–September troughs. The selected mean model is SARIMA(1,0,0)(1,1,1)12 with drift (Ljung–Box p = 0.96), and the GARCH(1,1) removes the remaining ARCH effect (p = 0.27). With MAPE of 1.01% in sample and 2.55% in a held-out 2022 test set and Theil's U of 0.76, it projects 38.86 Gt in 2023 and 39.00 Gt in 2024, a rise of only 0.38% consistent with the Global Carbon Budget's near-plateau. A plateau is far from the rapid, sustained cuts needed for 1.5 °C, so the paper closes with season- and sector-targeted mitigation measures.

title: Research on the Impact of Digital Finance Usage Depth on SME Financing Efficiency and Corporate Performance
abstract: Small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) often struggle to obtain external funding. Digital finance has been proposed as one remedy. This paper asks whether the intensity with which such services are used translates into better access to finance, and what that implies for short-run accounting performance. The evidence comes from Chinese A-share firms on the SME Board and ChiNext, observed annually from 2011 to 2023, and is analyzed with a two-way fixed-effects specification. Three results stand out. First, an additional unit of usage depth accompanies a 0.0690-unit gain in financing efficiency, an estimate significant at the 5% level. Lagging the regressor by one year, or substituting the aggregate Digital Financial Inclusion Index, leaves both sign and significance intact. Second, financing efficiency and short-run return on assets move in opposite directions. The estimated coefficient is -0.1147, significant at the 1% level. One explanation is the interval between spending on research and development (R&D), capacity, and digitalization and the arrival of the associated payoffs. Third, the association is not uniform across firm sizes: it is stronger in the small-firm subsample (0.0118, significant at the 10% level) than among large firms (0.0026), yet the size interaction term is not significant. This paper treats financing efficiency as an outcome rather than a channel. Doin…

title: Construction and Quality Management of Prefabricated Elevated Highway Projects: A Case Study of the Elevated Section of Chongqing Expressway in Qingdao
abstract: The prefabricated construction of urban expressway viaducts can reduce on-site wet operation and traffic occupation time, but component prefabrication, transportation, hoisting, and joint construction restrict each other, and the progress and quality are closely related. Taking the viaduct project of Chongqing Expressway in Qingdao as an example, this paper analyzes the collaborative control methods from the aspects of component supply and demand coordination, digital scheduling, night lifting, prefabrication quality, and joint construction. The research shows that the project relies on the smart beam yard and BIM+GIS platform, through the production, inspection, transportation, and erection status with the unique code of components, and forms a dynamic closed loop through "status acquisition - deviation identification - plan rearrangement - resource adjustment - result feedback"; Adjust the production scheduling and transportation batch of the Beam Yard according to the on-site erection rhythm, and take the quality acceptance as the precondition for entering the next process, which can reduce downtime and invalid stockpiling. During night construction, the risk of low illumination and fatigue operation is reduced through measurement review, mutual inspection by two persons, post rotation, and monitoring. The case shows that efficient construction needs to integrate the constru…

title: The Digital Infrastructure Construction and Regional Income Gap
abstract: As the material carrier of the growth of the digital economy, how digital infrastructure development affects regional income gap has become a frontier topic in the cross field of development economics and regional economics. Digital infrastructure was only a kind of communication network at the earliest, and now it has developed into a new infrastructure system with 5G, Gigabit optical network, computing power network, data infrastructure with so on. Digital infrastructure has expanded information availability, reduced transaction costs, promoted industrial upgrading, and improved public services. Yet it can also create a digital divide arising from differences in regional construction capabilities, digital skills, and industrial agglomeration. In recent years, as the advancement of China's Broadband China and other strategies, the research scale has further sunk from the transnational and provincial levels to the prefecture and city level, and the marginal effect, spatial spillover and digital transmission infrastructure have become new research hotspots. The association of digital infrastructure and regional income inequality may vary in developmental stages. Only when network coverage can be transformed into application ability, employment opportunities and industrial undertaking ability, will it have the effect of inclusive growth.

title: Supplier Concentration and the Cost of Debt Financing: Evidence from Midea Group and Gree Electric Appliances
abstract: This research employs the balanced panel data of Midea Group and Gree Electric Appliances, which are two major listed companies in the Chinese white goods industry, for the period of 2018-2024. The sample consists of 14 observations and tests the hypothesis that supplier concentration influences the cost of debt capital and whether there exists an influence-moderating effect from gross margin. Ordinary least squares regression analysis with heteroskedasticity-robust standard errors demonstrates that there exists a positive and significant relationship between supplier concentration and the cost of debt. There is no statistical significance between the relation of supplier concentration and the gross margin, and the relationship observed between the two firms is inconsistent with the mechanism underlying this hypothesis, hence Hypothesis two does not hold. The sample size is too small for the results to be generalized, and it would be best to consider this study as exploratory in nature with a comparison of two well-matched firms; the most important contribution of this paper is the data set collected on an individual firm level relating to the underexplored link between supply-chain concentration and financing cost of debt in China.

title: Cross-Screen Emergence in Game IP Transmedia Expansion: A Case Study of Blizzard Entertainment
abstract: To maintain audience engagement between individual releases, game firms are rapidly expanding their Intellectual Property (IP) across many media. Drawing on Blizzard Entertainment as a case study, the paper explores that process from the analytical standpoint of Cross-Screen Emergence. It draws on published literature and secondary case materials on novels, comics, animation, films, esports, merchandising, and offline events. The investigation indicates four interrelated mechanisms: core-setting anchoring, layered narrative release, community migration, and screen-external value extension. Their capacity to contribute to cumulative value is hampered by loss of agency in linear adaptations, fragmented release dates, unequal deployment of resources across the IP portfolio, and diluted creative control in external licensing. The governance strategies concerned are: transforming the emotional experience of a choice into a linear narrative; synchronizing the story and release schedules; allocating resources according to the IP life cycle and media function; and separating protected core settings from flexible forms of expression. The case indicates that the cross-media value rests on what each extension adds to the audience's understanding and continuous engagement. The resulting structure connects narrative creation with production and commercial coordination. The postulated correl…

title: Application of Intelligent Agents in Anti-money Laundering Transaction Detection
abstract: Anti-money laundering (AML) transaction detection faced scarce labels, extreme class imbalance, relational dependencies, and future-information leakage. This study developed a validation-gated ensemble detection framework combining temporally constrained transaction features, historical account statistics, explicit transaction-network motifs, and seven heterogeneous XGBoost experts. A large language model (LLM) proposed candidate rules from aggregated validation evidence, which a programmatic rule-validation agent assessed through threshold fitting and out-of-time validation. A validation-gated router integrated expert predictions and validated rule signals. On the temporal test set of the synthetic HI-Small dataset, the framework achieved PR-AUC, F1, and recall of 0.5965, 0.5532, and 0.4299, respectively. These values exceeded those of the evaluated XGBoost and GIN-family baselines; the explicit-motif XGBoost baseline achieved a PR-AUC of 0.4788. Stage-wise analysis attributed most gains to explicit transaction-network motifs and validation-weighted expert voting. The router provided only a small improvement, and the rule branch did not improve PR-AUC. Under this experimental setting, the findings supported using the LLM for candidate-rule generation and auxiliary analysis, but did not establish it as the source of the overall performance gain.

title: Field necropsy findings in removed sows from a spanish breeding system: primary causes of removal and concomitant lesions
abstract: Abstract Background This study investigated the probable causes of removal over a one-year period in a Spanish breeding herd, as well as the frequency and patterns of concomitant macroscopic findings. Sow mortality and involuntary removal remain major welfare and economic concerns in modern pig production, with rising rates reported internationally. Field necropsy, although not a substitute for complementary laboratory diagnostics, is a practical tool to establish the probable cause of removal. However, causes of removal are typically reported and interpreted individually, with limited attention to whether concomitant findings relate to the primary problem or to a sow’s ultimate failure to recover. Results Field necropsies were performed on 319 removed sows in a production system of approximately 10 000 sows in south-eastern Spain, November 2024-August 2025, of which 178 (55.8%) were euthanized and 141 (44.2%) died spontaneously. Locomotor disorders were the leading cause (86/319, 27.0%), followed by visceral torsion (46, 14.4%), prolapse (46, 14.4%; uterine, rectal, or bladder), and undetermined causes (40, 12.5%). A concomitant macroscopic finding, distinct from the stated primary cause, was recorded in 236/319 sows (74.0%), and two or more concomitant findings co-occurred in 116/319 (36.4%). The most frequent concomitant findings were macroscopic bladder lesions (68/319, 21.…

title: Markedly reduced skeletal muscle oxidative capacity with elevated circulating GDF-15 in children with cerebral palsy
abstract: Abstract Background Cerebral palsy (CP) is associated with progressive skeletal muscle weakness and reduced physical capacity, yet the contribution of mitochondrial dysfunction to these impairments remains incompletely understood. Methods We therefore evaluated skeletal muscle mitochondrial health in children with CP and typically developing (TD) children (12.9±3.4years) using a comprehensive approach integrating high-resolution respirometry, targeted protein analyses, circulating biomarkers, and plasma proteomics. Thirty-six skeletal muscle biopsies from 22 children with CP, and 15 muscle biopsies from TD children were collected during planned orthopedic surgery. Results Skeletal muscle from children with CP exhibited markedly reduced oxidative capacity (−50% in CP vs TD, p <0.001), accompanied by broad reductions in mitochondrial and substrate transport proteins suggesting reduced mitochondrial content. Despite the absence of local or systemic inflammation, circulating growth differentiation factor-15 (GDF-15), a biomarker of mitochondrial distress, was elevated in children with CP (337±53 vs 626±547pg·ml −1 for TD vs CP, p <0.05) and was highest among those with more severe motor impairments. Conclusion These findings demonstrate that previously reported reductions in skeletal muscle mitochondrial protein content in CP translate into profound impairments in mitochondrial fun…

The Effects of Strategic Agility, Technology Absorptive Capacity, and Digital Governance on Strategic Renewal Capability in Digital-Based MSMEs in Indonesia
abstract: This research aims to examine the effect of Strategic Agility, Technology Absorptive Capacity, and Digital Governance on the Strategic Renewal Capability of digital-based Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) in Indonesia. This research uses a quantitative approach with survey methods, to the owners and managers of MSMEs that use digital technology in their business operation. The respondents were selected by purposive sampling and had to be actively employing digital technology, to have decision-making power and to have been managing their firms for at least one year. The data collection will be carried out through an online questionnaire distributed via Google Forms with a five-point Likert scale and data analysis will be done using multiple linear regression. The results of the proposed study model show that Strategic Agility, Technology Absorptive Capacity, Digital Governance and Strategic Renewal Capability are positively related. The study has practical implications and suggests that MSMEs need to build strategic sensitivity, resource fluidity, technological learning, digital strategic alignment, and data governance to underpin strategic reorientation, business model renewal, strategic resource reconfiguration, innovation-driven renewal and organizational transformation capability. Strengthening of these three characteristics is expected to contribute to the improv…

title: What factors influence the enhancement of network dynamic collaboration capacity in medical surge response: a composite NCA–QCA analysis
abstract: Purpose Enhanced network dynamic collaboration capacity is crucial for effective emergency response and diagnosis in public health crises. This study aimed to analyze the configurational framework of such capacity in medical surge response and to propose effective pathways for enhancement. Design/methodology/approach Data were collected via online questionnaire from 68 healthcare personnel in China with experience in medical surge response. Fuzzy-set Qualitative Comparative Analysis (fsQCA) and necessary condition analysis (NCA) were employed to explore the causal mechanism underlying high-level network dynamic collaboration capacity in medical surge response. Key factors examined included the completeness of information technology (IT) infrastructure, information sharing and communication mechanism, flexibility in medical resource allocation, dynamic sensing capability, interdepartmental coordination efficiency, collaboration closeness among medical institutions. Findings No single factor was found to be a necessary condition for achieving high-level network dynamic collaboration capacity in medical surge response. However, seven configurations were identified as sufficient conditions to enhance capacities: Core Element Integration Type, Key Process Optimization Type, Technological Support and Collaboration Type, Flexible Resource Allocation Type, Information Sharing Centric T…

title: ESG implementation and disclosure as a governance mechanism
abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine how environmental, social and governance (ESG) implementation is constructed and governed within Brazilian credit cooperatives, with particular emphasis on disclosure as a governance mechanism. Design/methodology/approach Adopting a qualitative multiple case study design, the research draws on 19 in-depth interviews with senior managers across five credit cooperatives. Data were analysed using an inductive coding approach, allowing analytical categories to emerge from the empirical material while being informed by the literature on ESG, disclosure and corporate governance. Findings ESG implementation unfolds as a process shaped by regulatory pressures, cooperative principles and organisational capabilities. Disclosure emerges not merely as a reporting output, but as a recursive governance mechanism that connects strategic planning, accountability, performance monitoring and stakeholder engagement. Originality/value The study develops an empirically grounded analytical framework that explains how disclosure-oriented governance practices contribute to the formalisation and stabilisation of ESG initiatives in cooperative financial institutions. By focusing on an underexplored organisational form and an emerging economy context, the article contributes to the disclosure and governance literature. It offers practical insights for managers and regul…

title: Interaction of NADPH oxidase, PARP and mitochondrial dysfunction in the mechanism of pathology of endometriosis and adenomyosis
abstract: Abstract Background Endometriosis is an implantation and growth of endometrial-like tissue (glands and stroma) outside the uterine cavity, while adenomyosis is a growth the tissue in the myometrium. This pathology affects every tenth women in the world, but the treatment is not effective due to unclear initial mechanisms of this disease. Methods Using primary cells from patients with endometriosis and adenomyosis we studied the role of mitochondrial energy metabolism and redox balance in the cellular mechanism of pathology. Results We have found that cells with endometriosis or adenomyosis induced reactive oxygen species (ROS) overproduction from NADPH oxidase that trigger lipid peroxidation and decreased the level of glutathione. Patients’ cells were characterized by abnormal mitochondrial membrane potential and redox index due to the lack of mitochondrial NADH. Mitochondrial dysfunction led to increased rate of ROS production in this organelle. Inhibitors of NADPH oxidase or PARP restored mitochondrial NADH level and mitochondrial membrane potential suggesting that production of ROS in NADPH oxidase activates PARP that sequestering NADH in mitochondria and leads to mitochondrial dysfunction. Importantly, patients’ cells with recurrence of pathology exhibit the same pathology despite the intensive hormone treatment. Conclusions Thus, activation of NADPH oxidase trigger overact…

title: Influence and mechanism of pre-wetted coal gangue lightweight aggregate on the performance and microstructure of ultra-high-performance concrete
abstract: To simultaneously tackle the pronounced autogenous shrinkage and high early-age cracking susceptibility of ultra-high-performance concrete (UHPC), pre-wetted high-strength coal gangue lightweight aggregate (CLWA) was used as an internal curing agent, completely replacing quartz sand to fabricate reduced-density UHPC. The results indicate that incorporating CLWA not only maintained adequate workability but also reduced the density of the UHPC by 15.4% to 2250 kg/m3, while achieving a 28-day compressive strength of 117 MPa. More importantly, the use of CLWA resulted in remarkable internal curing efficiency, reducing the 60-day autogenous shrinkage by 51.5% and the chloride migration coefficient by 60%. Furthermore, no detectable carbonation depth was observed after 56 days of exposure. Microscopic analysis further indicated that the slow water-release characteristics of CLWA promoted sustained hydration and were associated with a more favourable composite pore-size distribution (with the combined fraction of pores below 50 nm reaching 38.0%) and a denser, locally stronger aggregate–paste interfacial region, collectively underpinning the improved macro-performance of UHPC. A multi-scale relationship between the water-storage/release characteristics of CLWA, pore and interfacial transition zone evolution, and the resulting shrinkage and durability performance of UHPC was establishe…

title: Research Progress on the Coupling Mechanism of Climate Change Mitigation and Carbon Footprint
abstract: The trend of global warming continues to intensify, and carbon emissions generated by human activities keep rising, which has become a key contradiction hindering the sustainable development of ecosystems. Carbon footprint can quantitatively describe the carbon emission intensity of human production and living activities and the resulting environmental pressure. This indicator has a two-way interactive and mutually restrictive coupling feedback relationship with climate change mitigation. Cumulative emissions measured by carbon footprint serve as an important driver of rising temperatures and frequent extreme climate events. In turn, various ecological risks derived from climate change constrain carbon emission behaviours of industrial sectors and push all sectors to carry out low-carbon transformation, forming a dynamically operating coupling system. This paper sorts out existing theoretical achievements concerning carbon footprint accounting systems and climate change mitigation. It analyses the internal logic of interactions between carbon footprint and climate change from four coupling dimensions: driving force, process, response and regulation. It summarises the objective rules of coordinated evolution between carbon footprint and climate responses at regional, industrial and product scales. It also identifies feasible coupling regulation paths including low-carbon emissio…

title: An "ON'', Switch Mechanism Modulating Expression of IL-l8 and Osr2 to Enhance the Effcacy of CAR-T Therapy in Pancreatic Ductal Adenocarcinoma
abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) remains difficult to treat, and its fibrotic, immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment are major obstacles to chimeric antigen receptor (CAR)-T cell therapy due to the T cell exhaustion and reduction in T cell activation. This proposal asks whether inducible interleukin-18 (IL-18) and biomechanical checkpoint Osr2 knockdown can improve the efficacy of mesothelin-targeted CAR-T cells in PDAC. The proposed CAR-T cell combined split CAR as a "ON" switch which can be integrated by lenalidomide, and inserted with inducible IL-18 cassette and Osr2 shRNA cassette. The drug-dependent CAR provides a method to control the T cell expression which can help reduce the toxicity. Furthermore, IL-18 is intended to support immune activation, while Osr2 shRNA is aimed to knockdown Osr2, in turn, reduce the exhaustion of CAR-T cells associated with the tumor environment. We proposed experiments in different treatments of CAR-T cells including combining a CAR-T cell control group without any modification, CAR-T cell with both modifications, CAR-T cell with only single modification lacking either cassettes, a T-cell group, a mesothelin-negative group, and a vehicle group. By comparing the tumor burden, survival, CAR-T infiltration, exhaustion markers, and toxicity, the results will prove whether "ON" switched CAR-T cells with inducible IL-18 and Osr2 shRNA ca…

title: Financial Incentive Mechanism for High-Carbon Industry Transformation: A Case Study of Shandong Weiqiao Transition-Linked Loan
abstract: Low-carbon upgrading of existing high-carbon industries faces serious and complex financial adaptation challenges. Traditional green finance is difficult to adapt to the gradual transition needs of high-carbon industries, and linking transition finance with sustainable development loans has become an important solution for real-world industrial development. This article takes the 200-million-yuan aluminum industry transition-linked loan in Shandong Weiqiao as the research object. It uses single case study method and mechanism analysis method to explore the practical logic of its incentive mechanism in the green transition of the aluminum industry. Research has found that through a complete mechanism design of standard definition, performance-linked pricing, and third-party verification, transition-linked loans effectively realize the economic value transition of enterprise emission reduction behavior. At the same time, through multi-party coordination to prevent "green washing", "false transition" and other risks. This study can provide practical reference for the innovation and large-scale implementation of financial instruments for the transition of high-carbon industries.
venue: Advances in Economics, Management and Political Sciences

title: A Guide-Pulley-Free Staggered Cable-Driven Reduction Mechanism for an Elbow Exoskeleton
abstract: This paper presents a guide-pulley-free, staggered cable-driven reduction mechanism for an elbow exoskeleton and other limited-rotation assistive devices. The design uses a motor, a small helical-groove shaft, one continuous cable, and a single integrated sector-shaped output part. The cable wraps around the small shaft about six times, and its two ends travel directly to two height-offset arc grooves on the sector part, so that the two cable segments cross when viewed from above without touching. No guide pulley, tensioning pulley, slider, or spring appears anywhere in the cable path. The small shaft has an effective diameter of 18 mm and the sector output part an effective diameter of 210 mm, giving a theoretical reduction ratio of about 11.67:1. Cable tension is set by wrapping and clamping each cable end onto a screw fixed on the sector part, eliminating any separate tensioning component. The small shaft is printed in carbon-fibre-reinforced PLA and the remaining structure in PLA by additive manufacturing. A working prototype has been built and tested for basic function, verifying bidirectional motor rotation, a 160-degree output range, and stable cable tension during motion; output torque, efficiency, weight, noise, and fatigue life remain to be measured.

title: Autophagy-Lysosome Dysfunction in Cancer: Molecular Mechanism and Therapeutic Prospects
abstract: The autophagy-lysosomal pathway constitutes a fundamental intracellular degradation system that recycles cellular components and eliminates damaged organelles through both non-selective and selective mechanisms. Selective autophagy is mediated by specific receptors that target substrates for degradation, including mitochondria (mitophagy), the endoplasmic reticulum (ER-phagy), lipid droplets (lipophagy), and intracellular pathogens (xenophagy), collectively forming a network that maintains cellular homeostasis. In tumors, autophagy-lysosomal dysfunction plays a dual role: on the one hand, it suppresses malignant transformation during early tumorigenesis by maintaining genomic stability and limiting oxidative stress; on the other hand, it drives the progression of established tumors by enhancing metabolic adaptation, promoting therapeutic resistance and facilitating immune evasion. This functional shift is driven by metabolic reprogramming within the tumor microenvironment, ferroptosis inhibition, inflammasome activation and spatiotemporal heterogeneity. Recent therapeutic strategies have evolved from broad-spectrum inhibitors toward precision interventions, including nanodrug delivery systems, patient stratification guided by single-cell and spatial multi-omics and targeted protein degradation. Technologies such as proteolysis-targeting chimeras and lysosome-targeting chimeras …

title: Study on the Coupling Mechanism of Organic Matter Degradation and Microplastic Capture by Algal-Bacterial Symbiosis in Low-Concentration Organic Wastewater Systems
abstract: Algal-bacterial symbiosis (ABS), as an emerging wastewater biological treatment technology, shows unique advantages in the treatment of low-concentration organic wastewater. At the same time, the aggravation of microplastic pollution in water bodies has put forward new challenges to traditional treatment processes. Studies in recent years have shown that algal-bacterial symbiosis can not only efficiently degrade the organic matter in low-concentration organic wastewater, but also has the potential to capture and transform microplastics, and there may be a deep coupling mechanism between the two. This paper systematically reviews the mechanism of algal-bacterial symbiosis degrading organic matter in low-concentration organic wastewater, the main pathways of capturing microplastics, and the coupling relationship and interaction mechanism between the two, and elucidates the bidirectional coupling pathway of "organic matter degradation-microplastic removal" at three levels: organic matter metabolism drive, microplastic stress feedback, and quorum sensing molecule regulation. On this basis, the influence of microplastics on the performance of the algal-bacterial symbiosis system and the key influencing factors are analyzed, in order to provide a reference for the theoretical improvement and application promotion of algal-bacterial symbiosis technology in the treatment of compound po…

title: Protecting mental well-being against perceived work stress: the mitigating mechanism of CSR-oriented HRM via job social support
abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine how corporate social responsibility-oriented human resource management (CSR-oriented HRM) relates to employees’ mental well-being, drawing on conservation of resources (COR) theory. It considers job social support (JSS) and perceived work stress (PWS) as mediating mechanisms. Design/methodology/approach A quantitative, two-wave survey yielded 869 matched responses from employees in foreign direct investment (FDI) enterprises in Southeast Vietnam. Structural equation modelling and bootstrapping were used to test the proposed relationships. Findings CSR-oriented HRM was associated with greater JSS and lower PWS. Greater JSS was also associated with lower stress, which in turn was linked to better mental well-being. The mediation results showed that CSR-oriented HRM was indirectly associated with lower stress through JSS and with better mental well-being through lower stress. JSS and PWS also formed a significant serial pathway linking CSR-oriented HRM with mental well-being. Originality/value The study clarifies the resource pathway connecting responsible HR practices with employee mental well-being in Vietnamese FDI enterprises. By distinguishing workplace support from stress appraisal, the serial model explains how an interpersonal resource may connect HR practices with psychological functioning. The findings support COR-based reasoning, while…

title: Air cavities as the primary drag-reduction mechanism in a superhydrophobic sphere
abstract: Abstract Precise control over air cavity generation in liquids is critical in numerous underwater marine systems, where cavity formation can largely reduce fluid resistance and minimize energy consumption. However, how the instability of the three-phase contact line at the microscopic scale induces the formation of macroscopic air cavities and thereby achieves drag reduction has not yet been fully elucidated. In this study, superhydrophobic (SHB) spheres with contact angles as high as 152° were fabricated using a spray-coating method. The liquid film evolution, flow field structure, pressure distribution, and hydrodynamic characteristics during the vertical immersion of spheres were systematically investigated through a combination of experiments and numerical simulations. The findings indicate that surface wettability is the key factor determining air cavity formation. The results show that the hydrophilic sphere did not generate an air cavity under identical immersion conditions, whereas the SHB sphere formed a stable encapsulated air cavity. The underlying mechanism is that, owing to the low adhesion characteristic of the superhydrophobic surface, the adverse pressure gradient induces separation of the liquid film, which triggers pinning of the contact line near the equator of the sphere, prevents the liquid film from closing toward the poles, and thereby promotes air cavity…

title: Time Pressure and Impulse Buying: The Mechanism of Limited-Time E-Commerce Promotions in Shaping Consumer Decision-Making
abstract: Time-limited offers are ubiquitous in online retail, and it is important to understand how they operate and the risks they pose. Drawing on behavioural economics and cognitive psychology, this study uses Tmall's Double-11, Pinduoduo's "flash sales" and Amazon Prime Day as examples, and argues that multi-modal interface signals, such as the countdown clock, real-time inventory, and transaction volume displayed, can narrow the window of consumer deliberation and encourage more impulsive purchases. Although such designs may improve conversion performance, they also create structural vulnerabilities, such as manufactured scarcity in the interface, consumer cognitive overload and irrational herd behaviour resulting in over-buying. When misused, the application of these interfaces can be a form of psychological coercion. To mitigate these risks, the paper suggests three solutions: adding standardised interface rules with independent third-party audits to remove false urgency; enhancing the chances of cooling off and reducing information overload on the pages; and reducing social-proof cues and including rational-consumption reminders to prevent unnecessary spending. The research is both theoretically and practically relevant in terms of balancing commercial efficiency with consumer protection, and it probably has long-term consequences in terms of the sustainability of the e-commerce…
venue: Advances in Economics, Management and Political Sciences

title: The Impact of Medium-Capacity Differences Between Long and Short Dramas on the Presentation of Homologous Scripts: A Case Study of the IP How Dare You!?
abstract: Short dramas, as a recognized new medium, are characterized by "short," which is also their marked difference from long dramas. This paper takes "medium difference" as the entry point and starts from "short", using the long-drama and short-drama adaptations of the IP How Dare You! ? as the research objects to compare the differences between the two. The study finds that the series narration is fast because of short and broken because of short, characters are cut and merged because of short, character relations are made explicit, and plots are simplified and displaced because of short. And the "short" of short dramas strengthens the "pleasure" of watching.

title: Financial constraints and ESG investment: a dual-track mechanism analysis
abstract: Purpose The relationship between financial constraints and environmental, social and governance (ESG) investment yields paradoxical findings, with some studies reporting negative effects and others positive. The authors argue that part of this inconsistency reflects measurement choice. Binary and continuous transformations of financial constraints emphasize different sources of variation that correspond to signaling predictions and resource-crowding-out predictions. This study aims to develop a dual-measurement framework to distinguish these empirical patterns without treating the two measures as conclusively independent mechanisms. Design/methodology/approach Using 3,172 firm-year observations from Chinese A-share listed companies (2019–2022), the authors employ a dual-measurement strategy, using binary constraint classification (financial constraints (FC)_High) to represent a firm’s relative constraint position within each year and a continuous standardized size-age (SA) index (SA_std) to represent within-firm changes in constraint severity. Firm life cycle follows Dickinson (2011). China’s 2021 ESG disclosure policy provides the setting for an exploratory difference-in-differences (DID) analysis of differential responses to a common policy change. Findings Constrained firms exhibit higher ESG scores on the relative-position (FC_High) dimension, with the clearest signaling-co…

title: A human-centred framework for AI integration in the curriculum
abstract: This paper reports ongoing work at La Trobe University to cultivate a shared understanding of effective artificial intelligence (AI) integration through the design of a human-centred framework for embedding AI literacies into teaching and learning. In response to conceptual ambiguity of AI curriculum integration, the Online Education Design team developed an operational definition positioning AI as infrastructure for active learning and the educator as the central decision-maker in the learning design process. This definition was translated into the AI-Informed Learning Design Framework, a four-step process, in which educators define the learning goal, select an AI pedagogical role, apply an AI Assessment Scale boundary check, then design learning activities that develop disciplinary knowledge and AI literacy. Supported by a four-level scaffolding model governing students' growing independence in AI use, the framework was piloted through two rounds, using a design-based research methodology. Feedback from Round one highlighted opportunities to refine the framework whilst also emphasising broader sector-wide tensions surrounding AI integration, including educators’ reluctance to use AI and concerns about the framing of some AI roles in teaching and learning. Early findings from the second round suggest improved educator engagement and a stronger understanding of the framework.

title: TEA-XFEL: trustworthy and energy-aware explainable federated edge learning for secure heterogeneous healthcare intelligence
abstract: Introduction Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Internet of Medical Things (IoMT)-enabled Healthcare systems have significantly improved intelligent clinical decision-making through distributed data analytics. However, conventional centralized learning approaches remain vulnerable to patient privacy leakage, excessive communication overhead, limited transparency, adversarial attacks, and inefficient resource utilization in edge-based Healthcare environments. Although Federated Learning (FL) provides a decentralized paradigm for privacy-preserving collaborative learning, existing Healthcare FL frameworks frequently rely on static privacy configurations and provide limited integration of trust management, explainability, and resource-aware client participation. Methods This study proposes a secure and scalable Trustworthy and Energy-Aware Explainable Federated Edge Learning (TEA-XFEL) framework for distributed Healthcare intelligence across heterogeneous data modalities. The framework integrates (i) adaptive differential privacy budgeting, (ii) blockchain-enabled reputation-aware secure aggregation, (iii) energy-aware client selection, (iv) Explainable Federated Learning (XFL), and (v) lightweight knowledge-distillation-based edge inference. The framework is evaluated independently using the MIMIC-III Electronic Health Records dataset for in-hospital mortality prediction and the NI…

title: Editorial: Enhancing data collection and integration to reduce health harms and inequalities linked to violence
Synergistic Suppression Effect of Composite Suppressants on Hydrogen Explosion Characteristics
abstract: Abstract This study employs a 20 L spherical explosion apparatus and the CHEMKIN software to explore the suppression effect of CO2/CF3I on H2 explosion characteristics. The results show that using the CO2/CF3I, the Sn and (dP/dt)max gradually decrease as the proportion of CF3I increases. When the total volume fraction is small, CF3I shows a dual effect of explosion promotion and inhibition. As the total volume fraction increases, the explosion-promoting effect of CF3I weakens. When the total volume fraction reaches 20% and the proportion of CF3I reaches 20%, H2–air mixtures with φ ranging from 0.6 to 1.8 fail to explode. Meanwhile, the synergistic factor of the CO2/CF3I composite suppressant is less than 1. CO2 inhibits hydrogen combustion through inert dilution and radical scavenging while keeping core elementary reactions unchanged. CF3I realizes chemical suppression by radical cycling and multi-step oxidative decomposition of fluorinated groups. Their synergistic effect restrains hydrogen explosions effectively.

title: Towards a process framework for Virtual Reality integration in higher education: An educator-centred synthesis
abstract: Virtual Reality (VR) continues to be promoted as a transformative technology for experiential, human-centred learning, yet its integration into mainstream education remains limited and unevenly understood. Prior work on VR in education has tended to examine isolated instances of adoption such as a single deployment, a single set of barriers, or a single evaluation of learning outcomes, without articulating what VR integration means as a sustained, practice-oriented process for the educators who plan and sustain it. Drawing on three connected studies from a broader research project, i.e. a systematic literature review, educator VR exposure sessions and planning interviews, and in-the-wild classroom implementation and reflections, this paper synthesises findings across the whole research programme to propose and articulate a three-phase process framework for VR integration: (a) VR Awareness and Exposure, (b) VR Integration Planning and (c) VR Implementation, Practice and Reflection. Rather than a linear adoption pathway, the framework is shown to operate cyclically, with implementation experience continuously reshaping planning and awareness, and presents a working definition of pedagogically supportive VR integration. The cross-cutting synthesis presented in this paper is a conceptual and practical resource for educators, learning designers and researchers.

title: Electronically active Sn nanosheets enable Sn-to-Pt interfacial charge redistribution for acidic and alkaline hydrogen evolution
abstract: Regulating Pt-support electronic coupling is crucial for improving the activity, durability, and Pt utilization of hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) electrocatalysts. However, the weak electronic interaction between Pt nanoparticles and conventional carbon supports in commercial platinum-on-carbon (Pt/C) limits further performance enhancement. Herein, we report a two-dimensional Sn nanosheet-supported Pt nanoparticle catalyst (Pt/Sn NSs) constructed by liquid-phase exfoliation and atomic layer deposition. Structural and surface chemical analyses reveal pronounced interfacial electronic coupling between Pt nanoparticles and the Sn-based support. Combined with density functional theory calculations, the results demonstrate Sn-to-Pt interfacial charge redistribution and enhanced Pt stabilization on Sn nanosheets. Benefiting from this strengthened Pt-support electronic interaction, Pt/Sn NSs exhibit superior HER performance compared to commercial Pt/C in both acidic and alkaline media, requiring only 28 mV in 0.5 M H2SO4 and 37 mV in 1.0 M KOH to reach 10 mA cm-2, with Tafel slopes of 13.5 and 35.7 mV dec-1, respectively. The calculations further show support-induced modulation of the Pt electronic structure, a more nearly thermoneutral H* adsorption state, and more favorable reaction thermodynamics for the key HER steps. This work demonstrates that electronically interactive Sn na…

title: Mapping satellite NO2 hotspot typology: India’s shifting pollution burden from Delhi–NCR to eastern energy–industrial corridors
Rapid FE-informed surrogate benchmarking for peak-temperature sequence prediction in Ti-6Al-4V laser-directed energy deposition
abstract: Purpose This study aims to benchmark next-state reconstruction of one FE-generated scalar peak-temperature sequence for Ti-6Al-4V laser-directed energy deposition (L-DED) as a methodological study, not a deployment-ready process model. Design/methodology/approach A conduction-dominated 10-layer wall was simulated in ANSYS Workbench Mechanical APDL 2025 R1 with temperature-dependent properties, layer activation, a Goldak-type source and convective-radiative losses. The 823-state sequence compared LSTM, XGBoost and DNN using a common target, 20-state context, chronological split, training-only scaling, scoring convention and CPU timing; model-specific inputs are documented. Findings Across the 803-state prediction region, XGBoost achieved RMSE = 12.36 K and MAE = 7.80 K; in the 165-state late validation interval, these rose to 24.58 K and 21.14 K. Cycle- and phase-resolved diagnostics localized the strongest degradation to late-build and rapid heating/near-peak states. XGBoost gave the best accuracy-cost compromise for this data set. Research limitations/implications The high accuracy is strictly an intra-case interpolation result for one FE-generated sequence, not evidence of cross-condition generalization or experimental fidelity. Latent heat and thermo-fluid melt-pool flow are excluded. Practical implications The present model supports only FE-sequence reconstruction and offli…

title: Understanding the Effect of Feedstock Pretreatment on Asphaltene-Derived Carbon Fiber Performance
abstract: Abstract Pretreatment is widely reported to improve asphaltene-derived carbon fiber performance, yet its intrinsic effect remains difficult to isolate because prior studies often vary melt-spinning conditions, fiber diameter, and thermal history simultaneously. Here, this ambiguity is resolved through a viscosity-matched melt-spinning protocol in which five asphaltene precursor variants are processed at identical melt viscosities (40–50 Pa·s), producing carbon fibers with statistically indistinguishable diameters of ∼14 μm. Rheometry, TGA-FTIR gas evolution analysis, NMR, FTIR, and GPC show that pretreatment results in measurable changes in precursor composition and molecular characteristics, with particularly pronounced effects on melt rheology and processability. At matched diameters, pretreatment increases average tensile strength from 534 MPa in untreated feedstock to 718 MPa, while Weibull analysis confirms corresponding changes in characteristic strength and tensile failure variability. The 380N pretreatment also enables stable spinning of finer carbon fibers (7.5 μm), yielding an average tensile strength of 1050 MPa, associated with the combined effects of precursor modification and finer fiber production. CHN analysis, XRD, Raman spectroscopy, and SEM-EDS reveal that substantial heteroatom content and structural disorder persist after carbonization, with no decisive pre…

title: Environmental taxation policy, a tool to achieve the dual objectives of energy transition and sustainable environmental development
Longitudinal integration and dynamic knowledge coexistence in medical education: a comparative conceptual framework
abstract: Background Curricular fragmentation remains a challenge in medical education, particularly in the articulation of biomedical sciences, clinical learning and transversal competencies. Objective To critically examine selected Latin American medical curricula and propose a longitudinal conceptual framework for knowledge integration and clinical reasoning. Methods A conceptual analysis was informed by a structured documentary comparison of six purposively selected medical programmes in Peru, Mexico and Ecuador. Curricular plans and graduate profiles were examined using predefined analytical dimensions and qualitative interpretative comparison. Results The selected programmes illustrated the coexistence of disciplinary foundations and different forms of basic–clinical articulation, clinical exposure and transversal curricular components. These documentary observations informed the proposed framework but do not establish national patterns or educational effectiveness. Conclusion The proposed framework conceptualises curricular integration as the longitudinal coexistence and reorganisation of disciplinary, interdisciplinary and multidisciplinary knowledge, with clinical reasoning as its central articulating axis. Its implementation and educational impact require empirical evaluation.

title: What AI can and cannot do: A cognitive-depth framework for differentiated AI integration in higher education
abstract: Higher education has responded to generative AI largely by regulating it by task, specifying where the technology may or may not be used in each assessment. This paper argues that task-based regulation uses the wrong unit of analysis. A single task typically spans several types of cognitive work, and a tool that can be welcomed for one type may quietly displace another. This conceptual paper proposes a four-level framework of cognitive engagement, adapted from classical Chinese expressions about knowing and articulated in contemporary cognitive terms: broad knowledge acquisition, analogical transfer, contextual inference, and original creation. The levels are ordered along a single axis, from cognitive work that is codifiable and reducible to rules and patterns, to work that is situated and dependent on human judgement. This axis maps closely onto the boundary of what generative AI can and cannot do: capability is near-complete at the codifiable end and degrades sharply as work becomes situated. The framework thus functions as a diagnostic lens for design, allowing educators to assign AI a role matched to the cognitive work a task is meant to develop. Two illustrative cases show the framework guiding differentiated, defensible decisions about AI integration within a single assessment.

title: Context-Aware AI-Based PPE Compliance and Occupational Risk Assessment in Construction Environments Using Lightweight YOLO Models
abstract: Automated personal protective equipment (PPE) monitoring in construction environments requires not only accurate object detection but also contextual interpretation of workplace safety. This study proposes a context-aware framework integrating lightweight YOLO detectors, worker–PPE association, workplace-context validation, worker–equipment proximity analysis, and interpretable heuristic risk assessment. A publicly available Construction Site Safety dataset comprising 2,801 images was used, including 2,605 training, 114 validation, and 82 independent test images. YOLOv8n and YOLO11n were trained under identical conditions for 100 epochs using 640 × 640-pixel inputs. On the independent test set containing 760 annotated instances, YOLOv8n achieved a precision of 0.848, recall of 0.682, mAP@0.50 of 0.743, and mAP@0.50:0.95 of 0.455, outperforming YOLO11n in recall and both mAP metrics. Consequently, YOLOv8n was selected for contextual risk assessment. Of 155 detected persons, 126 were retained as context-applicable workers, while 29 were excluded due to insufficient workplace-context evidence. Worker-specific analysis identified 101 helmet-positive, 5 helmet-violation, 59 safety-vest-positive, and 48 safety-vest-violation cases. The heuristic risk assessment classified applicable workers as SAFE (57; 45.2%), MODERATE (52; 41.3%), HIGH (9; 7.1%), or CRITICAL (8; 6.3%). The findings…

title: Educator-centred VR integration
abstract: Despite Virtual Reality’s (VR) promising potential to support experiential, perspective-taking and human-centred learning, a key gap in the literature is the lack of practice-oriented accounts of VR integration by tertiary educators (Khukalenko et al., 2022; Mikropoulos & Natsis, 2011) in authentic classroom settings (Jin et al., 2022). This poster presents a three-phase VR Integration Process Framework (Sembey et al., in press), developed inductively from three studies conducted across a PhD project. This framework reframes VR integration as a staged, cyclical and educator-centred process rather than a one-off technology adoption event. The framework comprises three interconnected phases: (a) VR Awareness and Exposure examines how educators make sense of VR’s potential for teaching and learning. A systematic literature review revealed that current research emphasises technological effectiveness and student outcomes over educator perspectives (Sembey et al., 2024). First-hand VR exposure sessions with 15 educators surfaced emotional engagement, empathy, immersion, and health and accessibility concerns as the lenses through which educators made sense of VR’s pedagogical potential (Sembey et al., 2026a). (b) VR Integration Planning captures how educators translate awareness into practical classroom decisions. Interviews with the same educator cohort identified 21 practical consid…

title: Enzyme blend supplementation in reduced-energy diets supports feed efficiency, nutrient digestibility, and intestinal morphology in weaned piglets under tropical conditions
Navigating the new frontier: Early insights into student perspectives on Generative AI integration in Bhutanese higher education
abstract: Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) is increasingly influencing teaching and learning practices across higher education institutions worldwide. While universities in developed countries have begun exploring the pedagogical potential of GenAI tools such as ChatGPT, there remains limited evidence regarding their adoption within developing-country contexts. This paper examines students’ perspectives on the integration of GenAI in teaching and learning at the Royal University of Bhutan (RUB). Using a quantitative survey design, the study examined students’ awareness, patterns of use, perceived opportunities, challenges, and ethical concerns associated with GenAI. The paper provides the rationale for the study, outlines the research design, and discusses preliminary insights into students’ perspectives from the online survey conducted. The findings indicate widespread use and generally positive perception of GenAI for supporting learning, alongside concerns about the reliability of AI-generated informations, academic integrity, and responsible use. The study contributes contextually relevant evidence to inform policy development, professional learning initiatives, and responsible AI governance within Bhutanese higher education.

title: X-Ray to Mid-infrared Spectral Energy Distributions: A Catalog of X-Ray-selected Active Galactic Nuclei in the XMM-COSMOS Survey
abstract: Abstract We present a component-resolved analysis of the IR–X-ray connection in a sample of 104 spectroscopically confirmed Type 1 active galactic nuclei (AGNs). By combining XMM-Newton, Swift/UVOT, and new high-angular-resolution JWST/NIRCam imaging for a subset of the sources, we constructed detailed spectral energy distributions (SEDs) in which the IR emission was explicitly decomposed into accretion-disk, torus, and polar-dust components. This approach enables us to isolate the intrinsic AGN IR luminosities with minimal host-galaxy contamination, providing a clean assessment of the physical relationship between the accretion flow, circumnuclear dust, and the X-ray corona. By incorporating JWST/NIRCam observations into our SED decomposition, we significantly reduce host-galaxy contamination and isolate the nuclear infrared emission with greater fidelity, particularly at near-infrared (NIR) wavelengths. This improvement is most apparent at 1 μ m, where sources with JWST coverage exhibit a markedly steeper relation between ν L ν (2 keV) and the NIR luminosity than those without JWST data. This behavior is naturally explained by starlight dilution, whereby host-galaxy emission dominates lower-resolution measurements.

title: Research on Energy-Efficient Adaptive Processing Control Method for Industrial Robots Driven by Multi-Source Perception in Complex Working Conditions Toward Green Manufacturing
abstract: This paper provides an energy-efficient adaptive processing control algorithm design for robotic systems functioning in intricate grinding conditions. The testing system includes the following elements: ABB IRB 2600 industrial robot, ATI Mini45 six-axis force sensor, Basler acA1920-40gm industrial camera, Yokogawa WT310 power meter, and National Instruments USB-6363 data acquisition unit. Multiple signals – force, vision, electrical, and robotic movement – are acquired simultaneously in equal intervals of time. The robot performs 180-second grinding operations of 36 stainless steel test specimens possessing smooth, bent, and rough surfaces. Filtering is performed for the force and power signals (with frequency of 10 Hz) while images are processed with rate of 20 Hz. Logs of robotic movement are aligned by means of 0.1 seconds. Adaptive adjustment of feed rate, reference contact force, and rotation speed of the tool is implemented by using MATLAB/Simulink and RobotStudio tools. The adaptive algorithm results in reducing energy consumption by 13.8%, on average, compared to the case of constant control parameters (standard deviation of 2.6%, -13.8 ± 2.6%) while peak power decreases by 118.4 W (standard deviation of 24.7 W, -118.4 ± 24.7 W).

title: Letter to the Editor Integration and Implementation of Psychological Aid for Caregivers of Cancer Patients
abstract: This letter highlights the significance of providing evidence based, culturally appropriate mental health care to cancer care givers, moving farther than assessment and identification of psychological problems simply.

title: Negotiating identity and relationality: An AI-enhanced polylogue on human-centred learning design practices
abstract: This poster presents a developing AI-enhanced polylogue methodology and conceptual framing to understand how third-space professionals in higher education are negotiating their shifting roles and identities while designing human-centred learning and assessment. Recent technological disruptions (e.g., widespread proliferation, advancement and use of generative AI, focus on cybersecurity, adoption of data-enabled technologies and ecosystems) have intensified tensions around higher education assessment structures and practices, exposing the limitations of isolated, task-based evaluation of student learning (Boud et al., 2020; Corbin et al., 2025). In response to the challenges posed to learning and assessment in the contemporary higher education landscape, emerging scholarship has foregrounded relationality and human connection alongside a shift to more program-wide approaches to assessment and assurance of learning (Lodge et al., 2023; Nicola-Richmond et al., 2025). This has highlighted questions about how educators can sustain meaningful relationships with each other and with students amidst these disruptions (Maldon et al., 2025). In this work-in-progress project, we focus on these relational questions and explore how technological disruptions are reshaping the roles and identities of educators, specifically curriculum designers working in third-space roles at the boundary of a…

title: Inside the black box of scenario design: Tracing the cooperative creation of video-based classroom scenarios
abstract: Simulation scenarios that bridge theory and practice are not designed in isolation; they require collaboration between practitioners from distinct professional worlds. Yet, the process of bringing diverse expertise together into a coherent representation of practice remains largely invisible in the literature. This paper presents a case narrative of a one-year cooperative design process for creating video-based classroom scenarios for simulated work practice in primary teacher education. Using the conceptual lens of boundary objects, we trace the transformative journey of the scenario script as it travelled across the professional worlds of academia, school, media production, and theatre, culminating in three interactive scenarios of challenging classroom situations. Our case demonstrates how following the script as a boundary object can reveal the messy and creative process of meaningful scenario design, and how iterative boundary crossings are mediated through the interplay between evolving artefacts and people capable of working across professional worlds. As such, our case provides insight into the black box that is scenario design, with implications for collaborative and cooperative educational design in broader contexts.

title: Enabling human-centred learning design through trust-based third-space partnerships
abstract: As higher education responds to learner diversity and digital transformation, human-centred learning design is increasingly important for inclusive, engaging and meaningful learning experiences. This paper shifts attention to the relationships and leadership practices that enable such design. It argues that human-centred learning design rarely results from individual educators working alone. Rather, it emerges through partnerships among academics, academic leaders and third-space professionals working across organisational, disciplinary and professional boundaries. Drawing on third-space theory and distributed leadership, this paper examines how trust, respect and collaboration enable inclusive educational innovation. A practice-based vignette spanning RMIT University’s School of Science and the STEM College Learning Design and Development team illustrates this argument, showing how established cross-boundary relationships were extended through school-wide professional learning and ongoing curriculum redesign across disciplinary areas. The paper positions trust-based third-space partnerships as an enabler of human-centred learning design and argues that distributed leadership, supported by relational conditions, can build institutional capacity for inclusive educational innovation.

title: Compassionate AI by design: Reconnecting students with learning through course-tailored AI
abstract: Generative artificial intelligence is becoming part of students’ everyday study practices, yet institutional debate still tends to position it as either an efficiency tool or an academic-integrity threat. This binary framing obscures a more educationally useful question: can AI be designed to help students engage meaningfully with difficult concepts while helping educators see where understanding breaks down? This project evaluates a course-tailored AI learning assistant embedded in a large undergraduate course at an Australian public university. The tool was bounded to authoritative course materials and instructor-provided resources. Students could ask questions, receive course-grounded answers and explanations, and clarify or organise their understanding without having assessed tasks completed for them. Informed by self-determination theory and cognitive load theory, the design sought to support competence and autonomy, reduce unnecessary cognitive burden, and provide low-stakes help at the moment of uncertainty (Ryan & Deci, 2000; Sweller, 1988). Students were randomly assigned either access to the tool or standard course resources. Evaluation drew on complementary sources of evidence gathered across the teaching period, combining students’ own accounts of their experience with routinely captured indicators of engagement and achievement. The evidence points in a consistent d…

title: Audio-Based Gamified UI/UX Design for Blind Players
abstract: Electronic games still rely heavily on visual interfaces, and information about game status, actions, and rewards is commonly conveyed through buttons, icons, colors, text, and animations, which creates accessibility barriers for blind and low-vision (BLV) players. Although feasible approaches such as audio cues, spatial audio, voice feedback, and haptic assistance already exist, related practices are often implemented separately and lack a systematic framework for integrated accessible game UI/UX design. This paper examines how audio-based gamified UI/UX design can support accessible, easy-to-operate, and immersive gaming experiences for BLV players. Combining literature review and case analysis, the paper analyzes accessible games, audio interaction, existing difficulties in game UI/UX, and psychological factors such as flow, motivation, and immersion. The study identifies key obstacles created by visual-by-default interfaces and reviews existing auditory and tactile approaches and provides suggestions for audio-based game UI/UX design, including information, interaction, positioning, motivation, and flow. The analysis suggests that audio-led and multimodal design can improve accessibility and support richer interaction but cannot fully eliminate limitations related to information bandwidth, cognitive load, individual differences, and hardware requirements. The paper conclude…

title: Designing together: Using a boundary object to support collaborative unit design conversations
abstract: Designing learning experiences in higher education requires the negotiation of multiple priorities; aligning learning outcomes, teaching activities, assessment design, student workload, academic integrity, accreditation requirements, and implementation feasibility (Bearman et al., 2016). Yet, these considerations are often distributed across documents, systems, and stakeholders, making it difficult to develop a shared understanding of a unit as an integrated learning experience (Bearman et al., 2016). Visual learning design representations can make pedagogical decisions explicit and support communication and reflection between academics and designers (Agostinho, 2011; Conole et al., 2013) This Pecha Kucha explores the use of a visual consultation board using Miro at The University of Western Australia. The approach originated during the collaborative redesign of a unit, where two Learning and Assessment Designers and a Unit Coordinator mapped the assessment sequence as part of the student learning journey. The board connected the cadence of learning activities and assessments, feedback opportunities, student and staff workload, and relationships between tasks into a shared visual structure. Iterative conversations around the board informed changes to unit design. Reflection on this case study and feedback from the Unit Coordinator informed further refinement and adaptations of …

title: Forecasting Home Values in Los Angeles: Research Design and Empirical Results
abstract: This study examines how forecast accuracy varies across horizons for 85 Los Angeles County cities, the county, and California. The data are monthly Zillow Home Value Index values from January 2000 through August 2026. Holt's linear trend, damped exponential smoothing (ETS), autoregressive integrated moving average (ARIMA), and an equally weighted ARIMA and ETS combination are compared with naïve and drift benchmarks. Specifications are selected using data through 2016. Expanding window forecasts are evaluated one, three, six, and twelve months ahead over a 2017–2019 preliminary evaluation and a test period from January 2020 through August 2026. Errors are measured in dollars within locations and by mean absolute scaled error (MASE) across cities. At one month, ARIMA reduces MAE relative to drift by a median of 71.1% across cities. Its advantage declines as the horizon increases. At twelve months, drift has the lowest median error across cities, and ARIMA's MAE is a median of 9.8% higher. Drift also leads in every price and volatility tercile at this horizon, but rankings vary across subperiods. Residual correlation and convergence failures limit claims about ARIMA's fit. Accuracy estimates are retrospective because the data come from a single revised vintage. Naïve and drift benchmarks should remain part of model comparisons at every horizon.
venue: Advances in Economics, Management and Political Sciences

title: Engagement by design: Character.AI and the decision to unplug its teenage users
abstract: Research methodology The case has been developed entirely from publicly available secondary sources: federal court records in Garcia v. Character Technologies, Inc. (the complaint and the published May 21, 2025 order, 785F. Supp. 3d 1157), written Senate testimony, Federal Trade Commission (FTC) and Texas Attorney General releases, the enacted text of California S.B. 243, company press releases and blog posts and reporting by established news organizations. Each material fact was corroborated against at least one primary document or two independent news sources, following established practice for secondary source case development (Leenders et al., 2001).
