No primary data were collected, and no ethics board approval was required. Case overview/synopsis In October 2025, Character Technologies, Inc. (Character.AI) faced converging legal, regulatory and societal pressure over its AI companion chatbot platform. A wrongful death lawsuit arising from the 2024 suicide of a 14-year-old user, an FTC inquiry, state investigations and new federal legislation restricting minors’ access to AI companions reached newly appointed chief executive officer Karandeep Anand within five months of his taking office. Character.AI had built its growth on open-ended, emotionally immersive conversation, and a May 2025 federal court ruling allowing the wrongful death claims to proceed treated that design, r…

title: Bandedge-State-Limited Single-Photon Emission from Volumetric Quantum Design of 2D Colloidal Quantum Wells
abstract: Abstract Present-day solution-processable single-photon sources are dominated by three-dimensionally confined colloidal quantum emitters, yet their particle-to-particle variation in single-exciton properties limits reproducibility and scalability. Here, to avoid such heterogeneity, we demonstrate reliable room-temperature single-photon emission from atomically flat two-dimensional (2D) colloidal quantum wells (CQWs) with inherently uniform one-dimensional quantum confinement, despite their long-standing limitations of efficient multiexciton emission and pronounced exciton-surface susceptibility. We resolve these challenges through volumetric quantum design (VQD) of CQWs, yielding a highly localized, single bandedge state. This design laterally confines the bandedge excitonic domain within the exciton coherent area and vertically decouples it from surface states via a thick, strain-relieved quantum-barrier shell that preserves strong confinement, overcoming the daunting thickness-confinement trade-off in 2D CQWs. Statistical single-particle spectroscopy reveals that VQD-CQWs deliver near-blinking-free (on-time: >99.5%) and fluence-insensitive antibunching (g(2)(0): ∼0.041), protected by a bandedge-state-filling bottleneck, together with linear polarization of up to 73% under cavity-free conditions, originating from synergistic transition-dipole and electric-field anisotropies…
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Which design features of a digital simulation predict sustainability competency gains? Evidence from a large first-year business cohort
abstract: Digital simulations offer experiential learning environments where students make consequential decisions under constraints. Yet little empirical evidence identifies which specific design features of these environments drive learning outcomes. This study examines a hotel carbon reduction simulation embedded in a first-year management unit (n=1,079 students, 190 teams) and investigates which of ten simulation design features predict gains in sustainability competencies. Students completed pre- and post-simulation surveys measuring 25 competency items aligned to an eight-domain sustainability competency framework (n=212 matched pairs), alongside a ten-item simulation evaluation scale (alpha=0.92). All self-reported 25 competency items improved significantly (composite d=0.62, p<.001). Regression analysis revealed that active learning engagement (beta=6.13, p<.001) was the strongest predictor of competency gains, followed by feedback quality and realistic scenarios. Full-cohort performance data showed 97.4% of teams maintained profitability while reducing emissions, with 45.8% clustering in a 'productive struggle zone' just below the target. These findings suggest that simulation designers should prioritise active engagement mechanisms and timely feedback over surface-level realism. Implications for the design of technology-enhanced experiential learning environments are discussed.

title: Centring relationships when using technology in human-centred learning design
abstract: In this symposium, we present a series of case studies examining how digital innovations can support human-centred learning design by strengthening relationships and enrich learning experiences in higher education. From virtual environments to collaborative learning spaces, podcasts, and AI innovations, we argue that technology is a tool to enable meaningful interactions and relationships. Our studies illustrate how human-centred digital environments can address persistent challenges of disengagement and isolation in online and blended learning.

title: Influence of Shear-Wall Configuration on Ground-Floor Column Design and Material Quantities in a 12-Storey Reinforced Concrete Building
abstract: Shear walls can be utilized to enhance the lateral strength of tall buildings; however, their arrangement can also have an effect on gravity load demands on the ground floor columns. This study sought to conduct an analysis to compare column demands and material quantities for four different types of shear wall arrangements in a 12-story reinforced concrete structure in Cambodia with four configurations of shear walls: without additional walls (M1), core walls (M2), perimeter walls (M3), and combined walls (M4). The three-dimensional linear elastic models were analyzed in Autodesk Robot Structural Analysis Professional 2021 using the factored gravity load combination of 1.2DL + 1.6LL. Four important cases of ground-floor columns (GFC13 in M1, M2, and M3, and GFC23 in M3) were then evaluated for slenderness, moment magnification, P-M interaction, and shear using ACI 318-08 guidelines. Compared to the reference model, the combined walls model decreased the column concrete volume from 50.63 m³ to 40.36 m³ (20.3%) and column steel reinforcement from 10.75 t to 9.65 t (10.2%). But such reductions cannot be made solely based on axial capacity since both reduced 300 x 300 mm column GFC23 in M3 fails the P-M check (Mc/ϕMn ≈ 2.1) and GFC13 in M3 has a very small amount of moment capacity (≈ 0.96), while other reduced columns have not been tested for that. For practicing engineers, walls…
venue: Scientific Journal of Engineering, and Technology

title: The World Café as a method to foster science-society exchange, collaboration and public engagement design
abstract: Public engagement (PE) is increasingly recognised as a pathway for generating societal impact, yet researchers' capacity to design and implement PE remains limited, with scarce opportunities to engage societal actors during early-stage PE project development. This workshop report examines the World Café (WC) as a structured method for science-society exchange and participatory PE design, drawing on its application within the IETI Hub for Research Impact, a six-month PE capacity-building programme developed as part of the IETI project (Impact-oriented Public Engagement) at the Museum für Naturkunde Berlin. The WC brought together five researchers and research-related professionals developing PE projects within the IETI Hub and twenty-two societal actors from diverse backgrounds, for small-group discussions on the projects' development. This was evaluated through registration data, feedback questionnaires, semi-structured interviews and project documentation. Findings indicated the WC's effectiveness in integrating societal perspectives into early-stage PE design while fostering reciprocal learning. Hub participants reported gaining perspectives that challenged disciplinary assumptions and shaped design decisions, sharpening project focus and yielding conceptual and methodological ideas to improve PE accessibility, engagement and impact. Project documentation corroborated these f…

title: From anthropomorphic design cues to dual trust: adoption intention toward autonomous delivery robots in Hanoi, Vietnam
abstract: Purpose Autonomous delivery robots (ADRs) perform a functional logistics task, yet scenario-based evaluations may depend substantially on whether the robot appears readable and approachable. This study examines how perceived anthropomorphic design cues relate to ADR adoption intention in Hanoi through interaction fluency, instrumental value, social trust and competence trust. Design/methodology/approach A standardised scenario-based online survey of 410 respondents in Hanoi, Vietnam, was analysed using covariance-based structural equation modelling in AMOS. The original structure and an exploratory extension linking instrumental value to social trust were compared. Latent-model bootstrap contrasts assessed specific and aggregate indirect associations. Findings Perceived anthropomorphic cues are positively associated with adoption intention and interaction fluency. Instrumental value is positively associated with both trust dimensions, whereas the direct interaction fluency–social trust association is unsupported. The aggregate indirect association through social trust exceeds that through competence trust in the bootstrap comparison. Limited measurement fit and construct overlap qualify these findings. Originality/value Using the stimulus-organism-response framework, the study integrates signaling, Technology Acceptance Model (TAM)-derived appraisal and multidimensional human-r…
venue: Asia Pacific Journal of Marketing and Logistics

title: Impact of altitude and EGR on the combustion, performance and emission characteristics of a hydrogen-blended Wankel rotary engine
abstract: Purpose This study aims to investigate the effectiveness and operational limits of exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) on a hydrogen-blended Wankel rotary engine (HWRE) operating under elevated altitude conditions, with the goal of clarifying the combined impacts of intake dilution and reduced ambient pressure on combustion, performance and emissions. Design/methodology/approach Three-dimensional computational fluid dynamics simulations were conducted on an HWRE model with a fixed 10% hydrogen mass fraction. The performance of the engine was evaluated at sea level and 15,000 ft altitude. EGR was modeled by introducing CO2 and H2O into the intake charge, with in-cylinder EGR rates varying from 0% (baseline) to 15% in 5% increments. Findings High-altitude operation suppresses the heat release rate and thermal efficiency due to lower ambient pressure and reduced oxygen availability. Incorporating EGR intensifies these charge-dilution effects, leading to altitude-dependent power losses. Applying 15% EGR reduces indicated power by ∼20% at sea level and ∼24% at 15,000 ft compared with that indicated under baseline conditions. However, NOx emissions drop sharply by approximately 84% at sea level and 87% at high altitude. Originality/value This work reveals the tradeoff between NOx mitigation and performance penalty when applying EGR to hydrogen-enriched Wankel engines operating at high al…
venue: International Journal of Numerical Methods for Heat & Fluid Flow

title: Liquid-Phase Deep Carbon Elongation from C1 to Crystalline Graphite
abstract: Abstract Wet-chemical synthesis of well extended sp2-carbon from simple carbon feedstocks under mild solution-phase conditions remains a longstanding challenge due to the stringent requirements of reversible C–C coupling and error-correcting aromatization. Here, we show that a Lewis-acid-assisted triflic acid medium, TfOH/Hg(OTf)2, promotes the direct conversion of chloromethane solvents into condensed hydrocarbon products and even into crystalline graphitic flakes in a one-pot solution synthesis. GC–MS, time-resolved MALDI-TOF mass spectrometry, nuclear magnetic resonance, and Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy experiments reveal the spontaneous establishment of a dynamic hydrocarbon pool. Within this pool, short-chain hydrocarbon intermediates from early C–C coupling were observed and evolved into highly branched alkanes and polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) ensembles prior to the precipitation of crystalline graphitic solids. Raman, transmission electron microscopy, and angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy measurements confirm the graphitic crystallinity and linear Dirac band dispersion of the isolated flakes. This work demonstrates that the dual-acid system can drive continuous carbon–carbon coupling and consecutive C(sp3)-C(sp2) hybridization transitions, overcoming kinetic barriers that conventionally require pyrolytic temperatures.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Molecular Engineering of Customizable Resin-Derived Hard Carbon Framework for Efficient Sodium Storage
abstract: Abstract Owing to their high carbon yield and molecular controllability, resins have emerged as promising precursors for hard carbon (HC) anodes in sodium-ion batteries (SIBs). However, achieving synergistic optimization of carbon microcrystals and sub-nanopores during resin pyrolysis to enhance sodium storage capacity remains a significant challenge. Herein, a spatial-chemistry-directed crosslinking (SCDC) strategy, based on the Mannich reaction of selected target molecules (TMs) within a resin network, is proposed. Owing to the steric hindrance of gem-dimethyl groups and the carboxyl-group-mediated interactions, the formation of nanoscale closed pores was facilitated while the continuity of sp2-hybridized carbon microcrystals was ensured and a large interlayer spacing was maintained. Through this approach, an HC architecture with elongated pseudo-graphitic domains and abundant closed pores is constructed in a synergistic manner, affording excellent electronic and ionic transport kinetics. The engineered HC exhibits an enhanced reversible capacity of 427.5 mAh g–1 and an outstanding initial coulombic efficiency (ICE) of 90.18%, along with a high reversible initial capacity of 346.7 mAh g–1 at 2 A g–1 and a capacity retention of up to 85.3% after 500 cycles. This study provides new insights into the microstructural design for high-capacity, high-rate sodium storage.

title: Trading time, not authority: A partnership facilitator model for sustainable student–staff partnerships
abstract: Effective student–staff partnerships rely on a reciprocal relationship that is built on trust, shared understanding, and meaningful dialogue (Cook-Sather, 2013; Thomas & Sorbara, 2023). However, implementing student–staff partnerships often places significant additional demands on academics, who must balance these partnership activities alongside their teaching and administrative responsibilities. One solution to this problem is the introduction of a partnership facilitator to lead the student–staff partnership. However, the facilitator does not simply take on the tasks traditionally undertaken by the course authority. Rather, they strengthen the partnership by redistributing responsibilities so that course authorities can dedicate their limited time to educational decision-making while retaining overall responsibility. In this study, the partnership facilitator (casual academic or professional staff) worked with student partners throughout a teaching term to facilitate dialogue, synthesise feedback, and support academics in implementing timely, student-information improvements. This exchange was mediated through regular reporting and meaningful actions taken by the course authority, acknowledging student input and empowering the partnership to deliver co-designed solutions where needed. Through post-partnership surveys, this study explored two key questions: (1) Does the prese…

title: CBAM's Impact on Thai Exporters' Low-Carbon Strategy: The Moderating Role of Green Transformational Leadership
abstract: The European Union Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM) introduces new compliance requirements for exporters in carbon-intensive sectors, including firms in emerging economies. This study examines the association between CBAM regulatory pressure (CRP) and low-carbon strategy (LCS) adoption among Thai listed exporting firms and tests whether green transformational leadership (GTL) moderates that association. The study uses a quantitative, cross-sectional documentary design. The auditable profile archive contained 100 numbered records; removal of five duplicate/replacement entries produced a final analytical sample of 95 unique firms. CRP, GTL, and LCS are arithmetic means of documentary items scored on a 1–5 scale. Models control for Firm Size, Export Intensity, and eight sector dummies, with Steel & Metals as the reference category. CRP was positively associated with LCS in Model 2 (standardized 𝛽 = .872, t = 13.31, p < .001; ΔR² = .421). In Model 4, GTL had a positive main effect (𝛽 = .766, p < .001), whereas the CRP × GTL interaction was not statistically significant (𝛽 = −.034, t = −0.82, p = .415; ΔR² < .001). Conditional CRP effects were positive at low, mean and high GTL, and the Johnson–Neyman transition points lay outside the observed GTL range. H1 was supported and H2 was not supported. The findings indicate that CBAM regulatory pressure and GTL are both positivel…

title: Green innovation and corporate carbon intensity: firm-level evidence from China
abstract: Introduction Green innovation can support corporate decarbonization, but its relationship with firms’ carbon performance requires empirical examination. This study investigates the relationship between green innovation and carbon intensity among Chinese A-share listed companies using data from the China Stock Market and Accounting Research (CSMAR) database for 2010–2023. Methods We estimate models with firm and year fixed effects and employ lagged explanatory variables, instrumental variable estimation, and two-step system Generalized Method of Moments (GMM) to address potential endogeneity and dynamic persistence. Results The results reveal a negative and statistically significant association between green innovation and carbon intensity. In the fully controlled baseline specification, a 10% increase in green patent applications is associated with approximately a 0.1% decrease in carbon intensity. The negative relationship persists across the additional estimation approaches and remains robust to alternative patent transformations, carbon-intensity reporting precision, financial-ratio winsorization, and various sample observations. Subsample analyses demonstrate large heterogeneity in this relationship. Discussion These findings provide firm-level evidence linking green inventive activity to lower emissions per unit of revenue and identify the corporate settings in which this …

title: Editorial of Special Column on Carbon Dot-based Functional Materials
Does Financial Access Enable Carbon Monitoring? Evidence from Small and Medium-Sized Enterprises in Developing Asia and the Pacific
abstract: Carbon monitoring is often the first step toward managing and reducing emissions. Financial constraints can limit small and medium-sized enterprises from investing in environmental management activities, particularly in developing economies. Using World Bank Enterprise Survey data covering 20,089 small and medium-sized enterprises across 24 developing economies in Asia and the Pacific between 2022 and 2026, this study examines whether access to finance influences firms’ adoption of carbon dioxide emissions monitoring. Survey-weighted logit models are employed to account for the stratified sampling design, and the results are robust to probit and linear probability specifications. The findings suggest that general access to finance is not consistently associated with carbon dioxide emissions monitoring. However, the source of finance matters. Lending from state-owned banks is associated with an increased likelihood of emissions monitoring among small firms, whereas financing from private banks shows no significant effect. Reliance on informal financing is associated with a lower likelihood of monitoring.

title: Carbon trading and corporate climate risk absorption measured from disclosure in China
abstract: Carbon markets are primarily designed to reduce greenhouse-gas emissions, yet their relationship with corporate physical climate-risk signals remains insufficiently understood. This study examines whether exposure to China’s regional carbon markets is associated with corporate climate-risk absorption capacity (CRA). CRA is constructed as the sign-reversed standardized log-transformed intensity of physical climate-risk language in corporate annual reports. Using panel data for Chinese listed firms and a difference-in-differences design based on the staggered launch of regional carbon markets, we find that carbon-market exposure is associated with a higher CRA measure. Transition-risk containment provides evidence consistent with a potential mechanism, whereas improvements in green transformation capacity do not form a significant transmission channel. Information transparency strengthens the relationship between carbon-market exposure and CRA. Subgroup estimates are positive in both managerial-green-cognition groups and more pronounced among state-owned enterprises. Overall, the findings extend carbon-market evaluation beyond conventional mitigation outcomes and provide empirical evidence for the further conceptual development of a corporate climate-resilience footprint (CRF).

title: Global overview on vehicular emission control: current strategies, effectiveness, challenges, and future research priorities
Land-use intensification alters soil carbon-nitrogen balance, with associated restructuring of microbial communities and nitrogen-cycling potential
abstract: Whether and how land use change regulates soil microbial communities by shifting soil carbon-nitrogen (C–N) balance remains unclear, even though C–N balance is known to govern microbial community structure and function. Here, we examined four land use types—natural land use (wasteland and shrubland) and agricultural land use (tobacco–maize rotation and continuous tobacco cropping)—and compared bacterial and fungal communities between natural and agricultural systems, with particular attention to rotation vs. continuous cropping. Relative to natural land use, agricultural land use was associated with higher soil nitrogen availability and microbial biomass but a lower microbial biomass C/N ratio. Compared with rotation, continuous cropping significantly reduced soil organic matter by 29.3% and total nitrogen by 16.5%, lowered the soil C/N ratio by 15.3%, and decreased hot-water extractable organic carbon and light-fraction organic matter by 21.4% and 30.6%, respectively. Microbial biomass carbon and nitrogen, by contrast, were significantly higher under continuous cropping, and the microbial biomass C/N ratio fell by 52.4%, accompanied by a 57.6% increase in nitrate nitrogen. Microbial diversity tended to rise from natural to agricultural land use, whereas within agricultural systems continuous cropping was associated with declining trends in bacterial and fungal diversity and wi…

title: Coupled carbon-nitrogen dynamics and soil stabilization under perennial alley cover cropping in raspberry planting
abstract: Agriculture faces the dual challenge of sustaining productivity and mitigating climate change through soil organic carbon (SOC) sequestration. The current management practice in perennial raspberry production in the Fraser Valley, British Columbia, Canada, pre-disposes the soil to continual degradation via incessant tillage of the alleys with no C input. Therefore, a regenerative approach is critical for restoring SOC and structural stability. The objective of this study was to determine how specific cover crops and selected mixtures influence the reorganization of soil organic matter fractions and the distribution of C and nitrogen (N) across water-stable aggregates and Silt+Clay size fraction after eight years of production. Five cover crop treatments including Red Clover (RCl, Trifolium pratense ), Ryegrass (RG, Lolium multiflorum ), RCl+RG mixture, Mustard+RCl+RG (Mustard, Mu, Brassica juncea ) mixture, and Radish+RCl+RG (Radish, Ra, Raphanus sativus ) mixture were compared with a tilled Control treatment. Results showed that alley cover cropping significantly improved soil structural stability by increasing the macroaggregates (2000-250 µm) from 24.67% in the tilled Control to 38.61% under RG monoculture and RCl+RG mixture. Conversely, mesoaggregates (250-53 µm) decreased from 51.72% in the tilled Control to 41.56% under RCl+RG, but the effect was not significant. The mean…

title: Experimental investigation on emission optimization of a diesel engine fueled with used temple oil methyl ester at different injection pressures
abstract: Abstract Biodiesel recognized as a renewable energy source, is increasingly considered a viable alternative to diesel in internal combustion engines. Given the cultural and religious significance of Used Temple Oil (UTO) in India, there is a growing interest in utilizing UTO as a feedstock for biodiesel production. This study aims to investigate the effect of injection pressure on the emission characteristics of a diesel engine fueled with biodiesel derived from Used Temple Oil (UTO), while also evaluating key parameters to determine the lower emissions. The biodiesel was produced through a transesterification process, and its fuel properties were assessed according to ASTM standards. Emission and performance tests were conducted on a 4-stroke, direct-injection diesel engine at injection pressures of 180, 200, and 220 bar, under various load conditions. The results revealed that CO and HC emissions were significantly reduced with the B20 biodiesel blend, especially at 200 bar injection pressure, with model R 2 values of 97.95% and 95.96%, respectively. However, NO x emissions and smoke opacity were slightly higher compared to diesel, with NO x having an R 2 value of 99.81%, indicating a strong dependence on engine load. Smoke opacity exhibited a similar trend, with a model R 2 of 97.85%. These findings highlight the critical role of injection pressure and engine load in control…

title: An adaptive spatio-temporal framework for carbon-aware and privacy-preserving DNN partitioning
abstract: Introduction Choosing where to split a deep neural network (DNN) between device and cloud requires balancing latency, carbon emissions, privacy and device thermal state, which existing partitioning methods rarely address jointly. Methods We propose GreenSplit, an adaptive spatio-temporal framework that selects the split layer and cloud region by minimising a normalised four-term cost under a hard privacy exclusion zone, with an Adaptive Weight Controller (AWC), current and forecast carbon intensity, Laplace noise on transmitted activations, a thermal-battery model, and a dynamic voltage and frequency scaling (DVFS) safeguard. We evaluated it in simulation on MobileNetV2 across three cloud regions (200 sustained-load trials), extended the decision model to ResNet-50, ViT-Base and the CLIP ViT-B/32 image encoder, and tested the noise mechanism on a pretrained ImageNet MobileNetV2 with 1,000 real images. Results Under our assumed energy constants, offloading a lightweight CNN is carbon-costly (5.8–6.7 × on-device carbon), so the framework keeps MobileNetV2 local; it then behaves as local execution with DVFS, emitting 66.0% of the carbon of unmanaged local execution with no privacy-zone violations (4% for baselines without the zone). Its 32.5% throttle rate at nominal thermal parameters is not robust (0–100% over plausible parameters), although DVFS lowers throttling in every draw.…

title: Half-metallic ferromagnetism and multifunctional properties of cubic perovskite nitrides HfTaN3, SrMoN3, and YWN3: a first-principles study with spin–orbit coupling
Artificial Intelligence-Augmented Analysis of Automobile Tire Wear Based on Advanced Friction-Deformation Coupling Theories under Real-World Dynamic Driving Conditions
Education, public expenditure and carbon emission in Ghana: the moderating role of the Kyoto Protocol
abstract: Purpose Education and government expenditure are increasingly recognized as key variables for climate policy. However, their effectiveness in African contexts as shaped by the Kyoto Protocol remains limited. This study addresses this gap by examining the moderating role of the Kyoto Protocol on government expenditure impacts on carbon emissions in Ghana. Design/methodology/approach Employing the Stochastic Impacts by Regression on Population, Affluence and Technology framework, we analyse 32 years of time-series data (1990–2022) using fully modified ordinary least squares (FMOLS) and autoregressive distributed lag (ARDL) cointegration techniques. Findings From the FMOLS results, a 1% increase in education and government expenditure significantly reduces carbon emissions in Ghana by 0.0007% and 0.68%, respectively. The study further shows that the Kyoto Protocol negatively moderates the effect of government expenditure on carbon emissions. Other results show that industrialization, mineral rent and urbanization significantly and positively impact carbon emissions in Ghana. Practical implications The study recommends that Ghana should expand renewable energy education in primary curricula. This will minimize the benefit of renewable energy consumption knowledge deficit. Moreover, the government should increase green infrastructure expenditure to leverage Kyoto-driven efficiencies…

title: Spatial effects and mechanisms of the digital economy’s impact on agricultural carbon emissions
abstract: To explore the spatial effects and mechanisms of the digital economy in promoting low-carbon agricultural transformation, this paper measures digital economy development and agricultural carbon emissions based on panel data for 31 provinces in China from 2011 to 2023, and analyzes their spatial distribution characteristics. Spatial Durbin and mediating models are employed to investigate the effects and mechanisms of the digital economy on agricultural carbon emissions. The results show that both the digital economy and agricultural carbon emissions present a “high-high and low-low” spatial agglomeration pattern, and agricultural carbon emissions have a significant positive spatial spillover effect. The digital economy significantly reduces agricultural carbon emissions in local and neighboring provinces, with obvious regional heterogeneity. In major grain-producing areas, the digital economy only inhibits local agricultural carbon emissions. In non-major grain-producing areas, the digital economy has a weaker effect on local emissions but can reduce carbon emissions in adjacent areas through cross-regional technology diffusion. From 2011 to 2018, agricultural carbon emissions exhibit a spatial clustering pattern, while the digital economy significantly reduces emissions in both the local and neighboring provinces. By contrast, in 2019–2023, agricultural carbon emissions shift t…

title: Revisiting Stock Price Bubbles: Behavioral Evidence from Pop Mart
abstract: This paper examines whether strong fundamental growth can coexist with speculative stock-price dynamics, using Pop Mart as a case study. With data from December 2020 to June 2026, I apply the supremum augmented Dickey–Fuller (SADF), generalized SADF (GSADF), and log-periodic power law singularity (LPPLS) methods and examine trading activity, public attention, and reactions to corporate announcements. GSADF identifies an explosive regime from October 2024 to October 2025, while rolling LPPLS indicators provide complementary evidence of nonlinear acceleration during the expansion. Bubble weeks exhibit higher returns, trading volume, and Google search attention. Lagged attention remains positively associated with bubble status across alternative specifications and measures. Event studies show positive abnormal returns around the 2024 interim results but negative reactions to the 2025 profit alert and 2026 annual-results announcement. These findings are consistent with fundamental improvement and speculative amplification occurring together, although they do not establish causal effects or directly measure mispricing.
venue: Advances in Economics, Management and Political Sciences

title: Forecasting the Monthly-Average U.S. Treasury 10Y–2Y Term Spread: A VARX Model with Macroeconomic Controls
abstract: This paper aims to figure out whether the monthly-average 10-year minus 2-year U.S. Treasury term spread can be forecast by its yield-curve and extra macroeconomic information. The research uses monthly data from January 1990 to July 2026 and sets 53 recursive origins during this period. Then the spread is forecast one and three months ahead against a driftless random walk, comparing a second-order vector autoregressive (VAR(2)) model in first differences with a second-order vector autoregressive model with exogenous variables (VARX(2)) that adds inflation, the policy rate, the Chicago Board Options Exchange Volatility Index (VIX) and the economic policy uncertainty (EPU) index. VAR reduces root mean squared error (RMSE) by 7.76% at one month and 3.96% at three months, and the one-month gain survives Holm adjustment (p = 0.0136); the VARX-versus-VAR increment is insignificant at both horizons, so the macroeconomic contribution is weak and not robust. Ex-post groupings concentrate the gains where the spread actually narrowed, which describe forecast-error heterogeneity only. Conditional on other yield lags and the macro controls, lagged 2-year changes carry no robust incremental linear information. The results are pseudo-out-of-sample because the data used are revised.
venue: Advances in Economics, Management and Political Sciences

title: Forecasting the Cybersecurity Vulnerabilities of Agentic AI Systems toward 2030: A Framework for Autonomous AI Security
abstract: Aims: Agentic artificial intelligence (AI) systems plan, call tools, hold credentials, and act with little human supervision, yet their security is still assessed mostly after incidents occur. This study forecasts vulnerability disclosures in a selected set of open-source agentic AI components to 2030 and proposes a security framework that responds to those forecasts. Methodology: Four public datasets were assembled: (i) 943 unique, dated vulnerability disclosures (April 2023 to October 2026) in 87 open-source agentic components from PyPI and npm, enriched with CVE records, CVSS vectors, and CISA SSVC decisions; (ii) the CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalogue; (iii) a census of 30,054 Model Context Protocol (MCP) and agent projects on PyPI; and (iv) MITRE ATLAS. Six forecasting models were backtested from four origins, and the identifiable models were combined in a quantile-averaged ensemble. Results: Annual disclosures rose from 19 in 2023 to 164 in 2025 and reached 705 by mid-October 2026, with an April 2026 changepoint that lifted the monthly mean from 8.9 to 94.5. Agent platforms contributed 54% of disclosures, and access-control flaws overtook code injection as the largest weakness family. Nine agentic platform flaws entered KEV in 2026, with a median interval of 30 days between publication and listing; because KEV listing follows confirmed exploitation, this…
venue: Journal of Engineering Research and Reports

title: Formation of green purchase behavior among Indonesian Generation Z consumers: extending norm activation theory with green price sensitivity
abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine why environmental awareness among Indonesian Generation Z consumers does not consistently translate into green purchase behavior (GPB) by testing the roles of awareness of consequences (AC), ascription of responsibility (AR), personal norms (PN) and green price sensitivity (GPS) within norm activation theory (NAT). Design/methodology/approach Survey data from 342 Indonesian Generation Z consumers were analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling to test direct, mediating and moderated mediation effects. Findings PN significantly predicted GPB, whereas AC had no significant direct effect but showed a significant indirect effect through PN, indicating indirect-only mediation; AR had both significant direct and indirect effects through PN, indicating partial mediation; and GPS did not significantly moderate either indirect relationship. Practical implications Social marketing interventions should move beyond awareness raising by linking environmental consequences to consumers’ personal responsibility and strengthening PN. Interventions should also support accessible, affordable and credible green choices. Social implications Sustainable consumption initiatives should help young consumers recognize their role as marketplace actors and translate environmental concern into PN that guide everyday purchasing decisions. Simulation-based comparison of unsupervised anomaly detection and conventional multi-rules for clinical biochemistry quality control
abstract: Background Internal quality control is commonly carried out using rule-based systems such as Westgard multirules and the exponentially weighted moving average. However, these methods may be slow to detect gradual drift and imprecision changes in current analyzers. Unsupervised anomaly detection algorithms, trained on in-control quality control data, provide an additional data-driven approach that does not require patient data. Methods We generate synthetic IQC data with four faults: a +2 SD step shift, a linear trend to +2 SD, an abrupt doubling of the SD, and intermittent ±4 SD outliers (3% of post-onset runs) on a standardized z-scale, including 54,000 QC-level series (12 analyte labels × 3 QC levels × 5 scenarios × 300 replications). We used Holm-corrected paired tests and bootstrap confidence intervals to summarise delay per replication (median across 12 analytes); outlier delay was calculated from the first injected outlier, and delay in fault-free streams served as the no-fault reference. A severity sweep changed the fault’s trajectory and size. Results Step shifts had median delays of 0.0–2.0 runs, while sudden imprecision increases had median delays of 0.5–3.5 runs, with CUSUM being the slowest. Delays from the initial injected outlier were 1.0 for EWMA, 12.5 for CUSUM, and 0.0 runs for Westgard, Isolation Forest, and One-Class SVM. The median delays for the trend were …

title: Corporate sustainable development practices and stock price synchronicity
abstract: Purpose Under China's shift toward sustainable corporate development, this study examines how corporate sustainability affects stock price synchronicity via informed trading, internal governance and external monitoring. Design/methodology/approach Using data on China's A-share listed firms from 2012 to 2023 and the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (UN SDG) ratings to measure corporate sustainability, we design empirical strategy that can identify the linkages between corporate sustainable development practices and stock price synchronicity. Findings The results show that sustainability enhances corporate reputation, eases financing constraints and improves informed trading, thereby reducing stock price synchronicity. Further analysis reveals that the inhibitory effect of sustainability on synchronicity is more pronounced for firms subject to strict environmental regulation, located in northwestern China, or classified as state-owned enterprises. Originality/value These findings advance the understanding of synchronicity mechanisms, suggest avenues for capital market stabilization and deepen insights into the economic consequences of corporate sustainability.

title: Temporally partitioned wind power forecasting with validation-calibrated residual diagnostics for PHM-oriented interpretation
abstract: Introduction Accurate wind-power forecasting is critical for the reliable integration of renewable energy into power grids, but reproducible evaluation requires explicit temporal partitioning and clearly defined feature-availability assumptions. This study presents a temporally partitioned, forecasting-first workflow utilizing the DaKS/Kassel synthetic wind-power dataset. Methods The canonical tabular benchmark establishes a target-time-aligned baseline by combining DaKS day-ahead numerical weather prediction covariates with recent observed-power history constructed relative to target valid time. Preprocessing parameters are fitted on the training partition, model and warning-threshold selection use validation data, and the test partition is reserved for final evaluation. For comparison, controlled subset experiments on four parks evaluated several advanced neural and sequential architectures, including a multilayer perceptron (MLP), a gated recurrent unit (GRU), a long short-term memory (LSTM) network, a temporal convolutional network (TCN), and PatchTST-Lite (Patch Time Series Transformer). Furthermore, we developed a validation-calibrated residual diagnostic layer that analyzes prediction errors across spatial, temporal, and operating-regime dimensions. Results Within the canonical comparable full-dataset benchmark, XGBoost achieved the lowest test mean absolute error (MAE) …

title: Analysis of the Current Development Status, Causes, Dilemmas, and Governance Paths of Price Wars in the New Energy Vehicle Industry
abstract: China's new energy vehicle (NEV) industry, after rapid expansion, is confronted with the predicament of growing output alongside squeezed profits. Its industrial profit margin dropped to 4.1% in 2025, a ten-year low, while vehicle manufacturing margins shrank to 1.5% in H1 2026. Price cuts launched by leading enterprises set off a chain reaction, trapping the sector in a prisoner's dilemma. This paper reviews NEV price competition and identifies its regional, continuous, transmissive and multi-dimensional evolutionary features. Drawing on the prisoner's dilemma game model and the "policy-technology-market" triple lock-in mechanism, it argues that the price war arises from firm gaming and institutional lock-in rather than supply-demand imbalance. A three-stage governance framework is put forward: short-term market regulation, medium-term unlocking of development paths, and long-term shift toward value-based competition. The study concludes that the industry can escape the price competition trap only by replacing price competition with value competition, supported by technological innovation, institutional improvement and global layout.

title: Spatial variation in housing affordability and policy price-ceiling alignment across Malaysian districts
abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine spatial variation in housing affordability across selected Malaysian housing markets and considers how residential prices align with local household purchasing capacity and a common policy reference price. It explores the implications of geographical differences for place-sensitive affordable housing assessment. Design/methodology/approach A quantitative, cross-sectional analysis uses a compiled secondary data set covering 48 selected districts and composite housing markets in 2025. Income-based affordable-price benchmarks, price-to-income ratios and monetary affordability gaps are calculated from reported residential median prices and household incomes. Descriptive comparisons examine differences between and within states, alongside dwelling-type prices, transaction activity, housing supply and a uniform RM300,000 reference threshold. Findings All selected markets are classified as seriously or severely unaffordable under the adopted price-to-income framework, although the intensity of pressure varies geographically. Lower nominal housing prices do not necessarily indicate greater affordability where corresponding household incomes are modest. Dwelling composition and composite-market boundaries also affect the interpretation of regional comparisons. Markets with prices below the common reference threshold can remain unaffordable relative to …

title: Maslahah-Based Food Price Stabilization Governance in Tanjung Jabung Barat
abstract: Background/ Introduction: Food price stabilization requires reliable monitoring and institutional responses that protect basic needs while maintaining market fairness. Research Objectives: This study examines food price developments, monitoring and response mechanisms, and their alignment with maslahah in Tanjung Jabung Barat Regency. Methodology: A qualitative, document-based case study examined 2025 price records for 18 commodities across 13 subdistricts, food reserve reports, field observations, and confirmatory interviews with one agency officer and one assistance recipient. Thematic analysis was supported by descriptive price statistics and cross-checking across sources. Results: Monitoring involved weekly surveys, monthly reporting, and additional surveys before major religious holidays. Chili exhibited the greatest price variation, while several commodities showed limited variation despite prices above relevant benchmarks. Reporting delays and supply constraints were documented. Rice reserves exceeded the reported target, and recorded distributions addressed disaster-related needs. However, the connection between price monitoring and intervention decisions was insufficiently documented in the materials examined. title: Do auditors price goodwill impairments? The role of audit committee accounting expertise
abstract: Purpose This study examines the association between goodwill impairments, under International Accounting Standard (IAS) 36, and audit fees in the French setting and tests whether audit committee accounting expertise moderates this relationship. Design/methodology/approach Based on a sample of 1,926 firm-year observations from 214 French publicly listed firms over the period 2011–2019, this study estimates panel regressions with firm and year fixed effects and panel-corrected standard errors, complemented by several robustness analyses. Findings The results show that goodwill impairments are positively associated with audit fees and that this association is stronger when impairment losses are larger. The interaction with the binary measure of audit committee accounting expertise is negative and marginally significant, while the continuous measure of expertise provides stronger evidence of a weaker audit fee premium. Research limitations/implications This study relies on archival data and cannot directly observe the coordination process between joint auditors; the coordination-based interpretation of the observed fee premium therefore remains indirect. Future research using more granular audit process data could provide stronger evidence on how joint auditors coordinate the assessment of highly judgmental accounting estimates such as goodwill impairment. title: The Impact of New Media Investor Sentiment on the Price Fluctuations of Domestic Stocks
abstract: With the deep integration of new media into the capital market, stock forums and financial forums have become important channels for individual investors to obtain information and exchange views. The impact of new media investor sentiment on stock price fluctuations has also become an important research topic in behavioral finance. Retail investors hold a significant proportion in the A-share market, making individual investors easily influenced by public sentiment. Abnormal stock price fluctuations induced by public sentiment pose a real challenge to market stability. This paper systematically reviews existing research, defines the core concepts of new media investor sentiment, investor emotions, and individual stock price fluctuations, and, based on theories of bounded rationality, herding effect, and noise trading, summarizes the transmission mechanism of "information diffusion — emotional mediation — feedback amplification." According to the research results in the existing literature, it can be seen that new media sentiment is significantly positively correlated with short-term stock price fluctuations, with its impact being timely, asymmetric, and showing significant differences across different industries and enterprises with varying levels of attention. This paper constructs a complete analytical framework, which can provide a theoretical reference for subsequent academ…

title: A Koopman-PINN Framework for Epidemic Models: Parameter Inference and Forecasting
abstract: We propose a Koopman-enhanced physics-informed neural network (K-PINN) framework for parameter inference and forecasting in nonlinear epidemic models. This method combines Koopman operator theory and physics-informed learning. It maps epidemic states into a latent observable space where the dynamics evolve approximately linearly while satisfying the governing epidemic equations through automatic differentiation. This integration improves interpretability, parameter identifiability, and long-term predictive stability. We apply the proposed framework to a normalized SEIRSD epidemic model and evaluate it using synthetic monkeypox (Mpox) data and real-world datasets from Germany, Morocco, and Sweden for the SARS-CoV-2 virus. Synthetic trajectories are generated using a structure-preserving, nonstandard finite difference scheme to ensure reliable training data. Numerical results demonstrate that K-PINN achieves more accurate parameter estimation, trajectory reconstruction, and long-term forecasting than classical PINNs and Koopman-EDMD approaches. These results suggest that K-PINN is an effective machine learning framework for epidemic modeling that can be extended to more complex systems.

title: Exploring the structural drivers of gold price dynamics: an expert-based interpretive analysis
abstract: Purpose This study aims to explore the structural drivers of gold price dynamics by uncovering the hierarchical and causal relationships among economic, geopolitical and market-related factors. Moving beyond correlation-based evidence, the study seeks to develop an interpretive understanding of how these drivers interact and propagate within the financial system. Design/methodology/approach The study adopts an expert-based interpretive research design. Key factors influencing gold prices are identified through an extensive review of prior literature and validated by domain experts. A total interpretive structural modeling framework is used to establish hierarchical relationships among the factors, while DEMATEL is used to assess causal influence and interdependence. The integrated approach enables the development of a structural and causal representation of gold price dynamics. Findings The results reveal a multi-level causal structure in which geopolitical risk, energy market shocks and macroeconomic uncertainty emerge as fundamental driving forces. These root drivers transmit their influence through intermediate financial and behavioral mechanisms, ultimately shaping gold price movements. The analysis highlights the systemic role of gold as a risk-sensitive asset responding to complex interactions rather than isolated determinants. Originality/value This study contributes to …

title: Consumer decision in online processed-food purchase: income, price, and digital quality perception
abstract: Purpose This study analyzes the association of consumer income with online processed-food demand through digital quality perception and perceived price on digital food platforms in Makassar, Indonesia. Design/methodology/approach This study uses a cross-sectional online survey of 162 female household food decision-makers. Data were analyzed using covariance-based structural equation modeling in International Business Machines Statistical Package for the Social Sciences Analysis of Moment Structures, with bias-corrected bootstrapping used to assess the indirect association. Findings Consumer income was positively associated with perceived price, but not with digital quality perception or online processed-food demand. Digital quality perception was positively associated with perceived price and online processed-food demand, whereas perceived price was not directly associated with demand. The indirect association was positive but not statistically significant. The model explained 56% of the variance in online processed-food demand. Research limitations/implications The single-city purposive sample and cross-sectional design limit causal interpretation and statistical generalizability. Future studies should use longitudinal, multisource, or platform-based transaction data. Social implications Reliable digital product information can support informed consumer choice and strengthen t…

title: A semi-discrete calibration-prediction framework for deposition uniformity in magnetron sputtering under complex magnetic fields
abstract: Abstract Uniform film thickness is an important requirement in magnetron sputtering, while achieving the desired deposition uniformity in practice often requires repeated adjustment of magnet positions followed by experimental deposition tests. To reduce such trial-and-error iterations, a semi-discrete calibration-prediction framework is developed to predict film-thickness distributions for different magnetic-field configurations. The horizontal magnetic flux density on the target is used to represent the spatial variation of the effective sputtering source, while sputtered-atom transport is described by an experimentally calibrated Gaussian deposition kernel. A key feature of the framework is that the calibration experiment does not require optimized deposition uniformity: a single deposition experiment under a convenient, non-optimized magnetic-field configuration can be used to determine the effective spreading parameter σ , after which alternative magnet configurations can be evaluated computationally before further experiments are performed. The framework is validated using Al magnetron sputtering experiments at 8 kW and 0.7 Pa under four magnetic-field configurations. The predicted thickness distributions agree well with the measurements, with a maximum relative error of 1.79% and MAPE values remaining below 1%. The proposed approach provides a rapid engineering tool for …

Reorder Prediction and Advertising Strategy Design for Retail Media Network Product Ranking
abstract: Reorder prediction has been widely studied as a classification problem in e-commerce, but little research has explored how to use the predicted reorder probabilities for downstream product ranking. Extend reordering prediction to Retail Media Network (RMN) advertising in this paper and consider sponsored products as competitors to organic recommendations for display slots. A LightGBM model trained on user-level, product-level, and user-product interaction features achieved a mean AUC of 0.6771 in five-fold cross-validation and 0.6968 on a held-out test set, and consistently outperformed logistic regression. Personalised Top-10 recommendation lists were generated for the organic baseline. A simulated RMN environment compared the four advertising strategies in terms of product selection, bid generation, and advertisement quantity. Each strategy was evaluated according to the quality of recommendations (Precision@10, Recall@10, NDCG@10) and advertising results (exposure rate, average ad rank, simulated revenue). As a result, the strategy that preserved the recommendation quality better (NDCG@10 = 0.8904) had a lower revenue (109.19), whereas the revenue-maximising strategy (542.40) resulted in more disruption (NDCG@10 = 0.7108). It was not due to the selection of products or the quantity of advertisements; random bidding unexpectedly had a lower average ad rank (2.9956) than conve…

Donor endothelial grading and specular images did not measurably improve graft-failure prediction over a clinical reference in the Cornea Preservation Time Study
abstract: Background Eye banks accept or discard donor corneas on endothelial criteria. Whether they predict postoperative outcomes beyond the clinical record and an independent cell density has not been tested with incremental-value statistics. Methods We analyzed 931 eyes with 69 all-cause graft failures from the public release of the Cornea Preservation Time Study, screened at eye-bank endothelial cell density (ECD) ≥ 2,300 cells/mm 2 . Five arms were compared on identical folds. The first was the eleven ordinal grades eye bank technicians record; the release carries no coefficient of variation or hexagonality. The other four were frozen representations of the donor image, three pretrained outside the modality, one in-domain. Each was appended to a clinical reference of covariates, ECD, diagnosis and site. The criterion was a 95% cluster-bootstrap interval on the paired difference in concordance excluding zero. Results The clinical reference reached C = 0.686. The grading did not measurably improve discrimination in any of six strata, with intervals about half the width of the learned arms’, and no representation improved on the reference. At 69 events only increments above a hazard ratio of roughly 2.7 per standard deviation could be excluded; smaller effects are unresolved. For six-month ECD on 770 eyes, the grading was worse than the reference (Δ R 2 −0.008, −0.012 to −0.004), thre…

title: Beyond counting clicks: Using the Resource Diversity Index (RDI) to improve early academic risk prediction in Virtual Learning Environments
abstract: Student attrition remains a persistent challenge in higher education, with institutions reporting substantial dropout rates and many at-risk students failing to receive timely intervention. Existing learning analytics models predominantly rely on click frequency and interaction volume where models count interactions but do not adequately interpret the quality, timing, and diversity of engagement. This paper uses the Resource Diversity Index (RDI), a novel behavioural engagement feature that measures how broadly students distribute their interactions across different Virtual Learning Environment (VLE) activity types. Using the Open University Learning Analytics Dataset (OULAD), which contains records for 32,593 students across 22 courses, RDI was evaluated alongside Engagement, Regularity, and Anti-Procrastination features within an Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) classification framework using stratified five-fold cross-validation. Preliminary results show that adding RDI improved Accuracy from 0.8303 to 0.8357, AUC-ROC from 0.9014 to 0.9068, and F1-score from 0.7852 to 0.7918. These pilot findings indicate that the click-distribution diversity captured by RDI provides meaningful predictive information beyond interaction volume alone and offers a promising direction for more interpretable and proactive academic risk prediction.

Early prediction of clinically important progression in children with traumatic intracranial hemorrhage treated at a high-altitude tertiary hospital: a single-center retrospective study
abstract: Background Early identification of clinically important progression in children with traumatic intracranial hemorrhage (tICH) remains challenging, particularly in high-altitude settings. This study aimed to develop and internally validate a prediction model integrating clinical, radiological, oxygenation, and coagulation indicators. Methods This single-center retrospective cohort study included 584 children with CT-confirmed tICH admitted between January 2016 and December 2025. The primary outcome was clinically important in-hospital progression, comprising radiological progression, neurosurgical intervention, TBI-related neurological deterioration, or TBI-related death. Predictors were selected using 10-fold cross-validated LASSO regression. Model performance was evaluated using discrimination, calibration, Brier scores, and decision curve analysis, with internal validation using 1,000 bootstrap resamples. Additional analyses assessed performance across age and GCS severity groups and compared the model with the Rotterdam CT score. Results Clinically important progression occurred in 78 patients (13.4%). The final model included seven predictors: GCS ≤8, seizures or recurrent vomiting, mixed hemorrhagic lesions, maximum hematoma thickness, SpO 2 < 90%, PLT <150 × 10 9 /L, and INR >1.2. The apparent AUC was 0.845 (95% CI 0.792–0.898), with an optimism-corrected AUC of …

title: Association rule mining identifies baseline clinical patterns associated with pulmonary infection in adults with acute leukemia: development and temporal validation of rule-derived prediction models
abstract: Objective To identify clinically interpretable baseline patterns associated with pulmonary infection in adults with acute leukemia using association rule mining and compare the predictive performance of rule-derived and conventional logistic regression models. Methods This retrospective cohort study included 1, 243 hospitalization episodes from 969 adults with acute leukemia. Episodes were chronologically divided into a development cohort (n=994) and a temporal validation cohort (n=249). Baseline demographic characteristics, treatment-related information, and laboratory measurements available within 24 h after admission were analyzed. Missing data were handled using multiple imputation within the development cohort. Association rule mining was conducted using the Apriori algorithm, and stable non-redundant rules were converted into binary indicators to develop a rule-derived logistic regression model. Its performance was compared with a conventional multivariable logistic regression model. Results Incident pulmonary infection occurred after admission in 620/994 (62.4%) episodes in the development cohort and 163/249 (65.5%) episodes in the temporal validation cohort. Five stable non-redundant association rules were identified, primarily involving induction chemotherapy, leukocytosis, neutropenia, thrombocytopenia, and elevated PCT. The strongest association was observed for indu…

title: Artificial Intelligence-Driven Prediction and Prevention of Phrenic Nerve Injury During Cardiac Surgery
abstract: Phrenic nerve injury (PNI) is an under-recognized complication of cardiac surgery associated with diaphragmatic dysfunction (DD), prolonged ventilation, and postoperative pulmonary morbidity. This narrative review examines contemporary evidence on PNI, focusing on intraoperative risk factors, diagnostic strategies, and emerging applications of artificial intelligence (AI). Thermal injury, mechanical traction, and anatomical proximity during internal mammary artery harvesting are important contributing mechanisms. AI may integrate real-time intraoperative variables, including temperature exposure, retraction duration, and ventilatory parameters, to identify patients at increased risk. We introduce the concept of a “pre-injury window,” during which escalating risk may be detected before irreversible nerve damage occurs. AI could facilitate earlier risk prediction and preventive intervention, although prospective clinical validation is required.

title: A hybrid machine learning framework for accurate petrophysical prediction: application to formation resistivity in the Nubian reservoir
abstract: Utilizing Machine Learning (ML) approaches to predict petrophysical parameters is becoming increasingly common due to their effectiveness in identifying non-linear relationships. Formation resistivity (RT) is a crucial petrophysical parameter that significantly impacts geophysical and geological applications; however, although ML algorithms have shown effectiveness in forecasting RT, several limitations have been identified in numerous investigations, particularly in handling the complex relationships within heterogeneous reservoirs. This study proposes two innovative hybrid ML frameworks for RT prediction using data from the Nubian reservoir in Libya. The primary hybrid model (ELM-RBF) integrates an Extreme Learning Machine (ELM) with a Radial Basis Function (RBF) network, while the secondary hybrid model (MLP-GPR) amalgamates a Multi-layer Perceptron (MLP) with a Gaussian Process Regressor (GPR). All algorithms are meticulously optimized via Grid Search Optimization (GSO). The models were evaluated against the corresponding standalone models. Prior to model development, a comprehensive data preprocessing workflow was implemented, incorporating a novel denoising process to enhance data quality. The proposed hybrid models have superior predictive accuracy and consistency compared to the Standalone models. Improved generalization performance and reduced overfitting were confirme…

title: A case of prurigo nodularis associated with giardiasis
abstract: Abstract Prurigo is a chronic, relapsing, polyetiological condition belonging to the group of neurodermatoses. It is clinically characterized by the appearance of hemispherical papular and nodular lesions, accompanied by intense itching. The term "neurodermatoses" encompasses a group of disorders in which neurogenic factors play a significant role in their development or transition to a chronic state; however, the etiology and pathogenesis of many of these conditions remain insufficiently understood. In adults, prurigo occurs twice as frequently in women—particularly those of middle or advanced age—as it does in men. In the Russian Federation, there is no official statistical tracking of patients with prurigo. Objective. To evaluate the efficacy of treatment for prurigo nodularis in the context of giardiasis, based on patient examination findings. Methods. The analysis was based on patient examination data, including a dermatological assessment, laboratory testing (clinical and biochemical blood analysis), and additional diagnostic procedures (enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay [ELISA] for the detection of Giardia antigens in stool samples). Results and Discussion. A 70-year-old female patient (Patient A) sought medical attention from dermatologists and oncologists at various medical centers, presenting with severe itching and skin eruptions. She received diagnoses of "L08.9 Pap…

title: « Se suffire ? Soi-même ? » Traverser la communauté dans Peer Gynt et Niels Lyhne
abstract: Peer Gynt (1867) by Henrik Ibsen and Niels Lyhne (1880) by Jens Peter Jacobsen, both major Scandinavian works from the second half of the 19th century, develop an extensive reflection on the construction and preservation of the individual. The two eponymous heroes cross several communities, either by choice or by the inability to fully integrate any of them. Through two different genres, and according to their own literary resources, Ibsen and Jacobsen address the same existential question from a confrontation with the collective: under what conditions can one be oneself? Weighing out the community social model and the subjectivist tendency inherited from romanticism, those two works present failed initiations, constantly repeated, which become the very content of the hero’s identity. The two paths, however, differ in terms of the trust placed in the individual and outline two models of humanist individualism.

title: The Role of Quantitative CT Enterography Parameters in Selecting a Treatment Strategy for Crohn's Disease
abstract: Abstract Relevance. In Crohn's disease (CD), choosing between conservative therapy, resection with primary intestinal anastomosis, and intestinal stoma formation requires an objective assessment of the extent and severity of the disease. CT enterography (CTE) enables the acquisition of reproducible quantitative parameters that are potentially useful for treatment planning. The aim of the study was to evaluate the prognostic significance of quantitative and semi-quantitative CT enterography (CTE) parameters for selecting treatment strategy, predicting the type of surgical outcome, and anticipating perioperative parameters in patients with Crohn's disease (CD). Materials and methods. A retrospective analysis of CTE scans and medical records was conducted for 103 patients (aged 18–76 years) with confirmed CD. The following parameters were assessed: extent of the lesion, bowel wall thickness, number of enlarged mesenteric lymph nodes (LNs), mean size of the three largest LNs, increase in LN density following intravenous contrast administration, and the CTE index. Anamnestic data and perioperative indicators were obtained from medical records covering the hospitalization period. Patients were divided into a conservative therapy group (Group I, n = 40) and a surgical treatment group (Group II, n = 63); the latter was further subdivided into patients undergoing primary intestinal anas…

title: Towards Energy-Efficient Non-thermal Plasma Chemistry: Lessons from CO 2 Splitting and Ammonia Synthesis
abstract: Non-thermal plasma (NTP) offers a promising route for electrifying chemical processes by enabling the activation of stable molecules under relatively mild conditions. However, evaluating the plasma process only by conversion or product yield may mask the substantial energy losses associated with power supply, electron excitation, molecular activation, and gas heating. This review examines energy efficiency in NTP-assisted CO 2 splitting and ammonia synthesis as two representative model systems to investigate the energy efficiency in NTP-assisted chemical conversion. For CO 2 splitting, different plasma discharges are compared in terms of CO 2 conversion, specific energy input and energy efficiency. For ammonia synthesis, the effects of discharge mode, reactor configuration, catalyst properties and suppression of NH 3 decomposition on energy yield are evaluated. Across both systems, higher conversion or product yield does not necessarily correspond to more efficient energy utilisation. Instead, the energy performance is dominated by the coupling between electrical energy deposition, molecular activation, plasma-surface interaction, and inhibition of non-productive pathways such as gas heating, recombination, and product decomposition. This comparison further highlights the need for consistent system boundaries and energy-accounting protocols, particularly when distinguishing pla…

title: Survival Strategies of Unicellular Microorganisms: Substance Acquisition and Energy Metabolism
abstract: Unicellular microorganisms are widespread in almost all natural ecosystems and face environmental stresses. Analyzing their adaptation process has a significant influence on microbial ecology. These microorganisms deeply affect chemical recycling in the global ecosystem. This research analyzes the survival strategies of three types of unicellular microorganisms: autotrophs, heterotrophs, mixotrophs, and explains the different metabolic ways under long‑term lack of resources. Result shows that microorganisms use structural and physiological rebuilding to survive in resource-limited conditions, but long-term resource consumption may limit their recovery. Autotrophic microorganisms fix inorganic carbon to make organic compounds, and this process may consume a lot of energy. Mixotrophic organisms combine these two metabolisms, but this may bring an extra energy burden. The research suggests that no strategy has absolute advantages, and all these adaptations may bring metabolic costs. This conclusion can explain how microorganisms in natural environments adapt to fluctuations in nutrient conditions.

Dew-point tracking with multi-objective FOPID control for energy-efficient peltier-based condensation
abstract: Abstract This paper presents an experimental case study of thermoelectric (Peltier) cooling in which the control reference is the dew point, computed in real time from ambient temperature and relative humidity, and the controller is a finite-memory discrete fractional-order PID (FOPID) tuned by multi-objective optimization. The FOPID parameters were selected from an NSGA-II Pareto front that trades off tracking error, electrical energy and control-signal variation. The resulting controller (OPT-FOPID) was compared on the same embedded platform with a PID and with a FOPID tuned by particle swarm optimization (PSO-FOPID), in five 300 s repetitions per controller, run in randomized order with a single firmware and calibration. The three controllers reached the dew point in 6–7 s and held it with an error dispersion of 0.03–0.04 $$^\circ $$ C; no statistically significant difference was detected among them in tracking error, settling time or energy per degree of cooling demand. The OPT-FOPID reduced the total variation of the PWM signal by 35–38% with respect to both baselines ( $$p<0.001$$ ), while the differences in peak electrical power were small (5–12%). In simulation, a multi-objective PID tuned with the same procedure reached a comparable trade-off, so the smoother actuation is attributed to the multi-objective tuning rather than to the fractional orders. title: Digital Literacy as a Factor in the Readiness of the Healthcare System of the Republic of Sakha (Yakutia) for Digital Transformation: Results of an Empirical Study
abstract: Abstract Relevance. Digital transformation reflects global trends in the healthcare sector of the Russian Federation across all levels of management. Objective. To assess the level of digital literacy among healthcare professionals in the Republic of Sakha (Yakutia) using the Russian version of the eHEALS questionnaire as an indicator of the regional healthcare system's workforce readiness for digital transformation. Materials and Methods. A cross-sectional medico-sociological study. Following a two-stage data cleaning process (starting with 2,538 responses), the analytical sample comprised 1,997 healthcare professionals from state medical organizations in the Republic of Sakha (Yakutia). Digital literacy was assessed using the 8-item eHEALS questionnaire (Russian adaptation); internal consistency was evaluated using Cronbach’s alpha coefficient. The primary measure of central tendency was the median (Me [Q1; Q3]), with the mean and standard deviation (M ± SD) provided for reference. Proportions were calculated with 95% confidence intervals (CI) using the Wilson method. Differences between groups (physicians vs. feldshers) were assessed using the Mann-Whitney test. Calculations were performed using the RStudio statistical computing environment. Results. title: Towards realizable free material optimization via energy bound hierarchy
abstract: We study free orthotropic material optimization for two-dimensional plane-stress compliance minimization with two well-ordered isotropic phases. To connect free material optimization and composite realizability, we construct a hierarchy of admissible sets using zeroth-order, Voigt, and Hashin–Shtrikman energy bounds. The zeroth-order and Voigt models are convex, with admissible sets that coincide at global volume-budget endpoints and satisfy strict inclusion at intermediate volume budgets. The Voigt model reduces to isotropic variable-thickness-sheet optimization, while the single-loadcase continuum zeroth-order problem admits an orthotropic optimum. The classical Hashin–Shtrikman bounds yield a tighter admissible set that is nonconvex jointly in the elasticity tensor and volume fraction and whose convex hull equals the Voigt set. We derive reduced formulations by explicitly characterizing the minimum volume fraction compatible with these bounds. For orthotropic tensors, this volume-fraction estimator reduces to a one-dimensional search over the strain trace. In the single-loadcase continuum setting, the Hashin–Shtrikman-constrained optimal value equals that of the classical Allaire–Kohn relaxation, attained by a homogenized design with sequential-laminate effective tensors. For multiple loadcases, the bounds remain necessary but are generally insufficient for realizability. Nu…

title: Local Protocol for the Diagnosis and Treatment of Secondary Immunodeficiencies in Children: Experience of the Clinic of the Research Institute of Maternal and Child Health (Khabarovsk)
abstract: Abstract Introduction. The article addresses the issue of diagnosing and treating secondary immunodeficiencies (SID) in children in the absence of approved clinical guidelines and/or standards for the diagnosis and treatment of this condition. Objective. To analyze and summarize current expert opinions on the management of children with secondary immunodeficiency and to present the findings as a local protocol for the medical institution. Materials and Methods. An analysis of 187 literature sources was conducted, focusing on the applicability of the results to Russian clinical practice, based on the equivalence of terminology and accepted disease assessment criteria. Results. A local protocol for the diagnosis and treatment of secondary immunodeficiencies in children was developed, piloted, and approved for the clinic of the Research Institute of Maternal and Child Health (RI MCH). Conclusion. The said local protocol was approved on November 25, 2025, by the Academic Council of the Khabarovsk Branch of the FESC PPR – RI MCH. It has currently been implemented into the institution's clinical practice. Its efficacy is being evaluated as part of ongoing research, the results of which will be presented later.

title: Habitat use characteristics of the Grey Partridge (Perdix perdix) in an agricultural landscape with energy cover crops for biogas production
Solvation-driven charge redistribution in high-voltage polyether electrolytes
abstract: Polyether electrolytes (PPEs) are promising for high-voltage lithium-metal batteries (LMBs) because of their good electrode wettability, continuous Li<sup>+</sup> transport pathways, and favorable compatibility with lithium metal. However, their application above 4.3 V is limited by electron-rich ether oxygen (EO) sites, oxidation-prone terminal groups, and unfavorable Li<sup>+</sup>-EO coordination. Increasing evidence indicates that high-voltage instability cannot be attributed solely to terminal-group oxidation, but is closely related to the coupling between Li<sup>+</sup> solvation and the local electronic structure of EO. In this review, we introduce solvation-driven charge redistribution as a unifying framework for understanding and designing high-voltage PPEs. We discuss how regulation of Li<sup>+</sup>-EO-anion coordination can redistribute or homogenize electron density around EO sites, reduce excessive Li<sup>+</sup>-polyether interactions, lower the oxidative activity of the polyether backbone, and simultaneously influence Li<sup>+</sup> transport and interphase chemistry. Recent molecular strategies, including solvation-regulating cross-linkers, weakly solvating cyclic-ether monomers, electron-withdrawing functional units, and optimization of the Li<sup>+</sup>/EO coordination environment, are systematically analyzed within this framework. Particular attention is gi…
