Advances and Prospects of Key Technologies for Dedicated Transmissions in New Energy Vehicles
abstract: Dedicated transmissions affect the efficiency, performance, durability, and noise, vibration and harshness (NVH) of new energy vehicles (NEVs). Previous reviews have examined battery-electric transmissions, hybrid architectures, control, and components separately. This systematic review connects these areas through an architecture–technology framework, comparing single-speed and two-speed battery electric vehicle transmissions with P2, power-split, and two-speed multi-mode hybrids. It covers five domains: thermal management, shift control, efficiency-oriented design, lightweight and NVH-aware optimization, and electromechanical integration. Evidence is assessed by study type and validation level. Additional ratios and modes can improve operating-point flexibility but add mechanical losses, shift events, calibration demands, and durability constraints. High-speed, integrated layouts can improve packaging and power density but increase thermal, lubrication, structural, and serviceability interactions. These trade-offs require system-level assessment. Rather than ranking architectures, the review identifies the conditions behind reported benefits and trade-offs that lack sufficient validation. Future priorities include common vehicle-level benchmarks, transparent system boundaries, and multi-domain experimental validation.

title: Uncovering the anatomical features of pneumatophores in the roots of date palm (Phoenix dactylifera)
abstract: Date palm (Phoenix dactylifera) is a keystone desert crop and thrives under extreme aridity by evolving an extensive and complex root system. In addition to deep soil-penetrating roots, it produces non-gravitropic growing pneumatophores. However, organisation of the tissues in the root meristem structure of these specialised roots is poorly characterised. Here, we show that date palm forms at least two morphologically distinct classes of pneumatophores. Both types possess an organised root meristem with a defined stem cell niche marked by the PLETHORA-like gene expression BABYBOOM (PdBBM), indicating conservation of core meristem regulatory modules. We found that the pneumatophores retain lateral root cap and columella identity as evidenced by PdSMB expression. Despite retaining key features of root meristem organisation, pneumatophores exhibit altered gravity-sensing properties, characterised by apolar, or absent, statolith accumulation, providing a potential explanation for their non-gravitropic growth. Our results establish pneumatophores as specialised root organs with distinct morphology, yet retaining a conserved meristem organisation and tissue anatomy. This developmental specialisation provides insight into how root architecture can be remodelled to support adaptation to the extreme and heterogeneous environments of desert ecosystems.

title: Multi-environment evaluation of rust and Septoria disease resistance, lodging, plant height, and grain yield in Ethiopian durum wheat (Triticum turgidum subsp. durum​​) germplasm in northeastern Ethiopia
Immersive simulation-based learning with virtual prototypes: advancing student engagement and educational quality in engineering
abstract: Purpose Immersive learning environments have been widely recognized for their potential to support student engagement in engineering education; however, their adoption is often constrained by high costs and limited accessibility. This study aims to examine the use of low-cost virtual prototypes as an alternative to high-cost immersive learning technologies in higher engineering education, with particular emphasis on accessibility and sustainability. Design/methodology/approach A one-group quasi-experimental pretest–posttest design was implemented with a sample of 92 undergraduate engineering students in a Latin American university context. Student engagement was assessed using a validated multidimensional instrument based on the Burch Engagement Survey for students framework, capturing physical, emotional and cognitive dimensions. Given the presence of both matched and unmatched observations, engagement differences were analyzed at the dimension level using statistical methods appropriate for partially overlapping samples, with effect sizes and confidence intervals reported to support interpretation. Findings The results showed pre–post increases in physical engagement and, to a lesser extent, emotional engagement after the intervention. In contrast, no statistically significant changes were found in synchronous or asynchronous cognitive engagement. These results suggest that v…

title: Law as a Game: Shaping Human Behavior in Virtual Worlds Through Gamified Regulatory Logic
abstract: This article introduces gamified regulation as a legitimate mode of governance for immersive virtual reality (VR) worlds commonly described as the Metaverse. It begins with the observation that such environments are ontologically distinct and architected, enabling forms of regulation that are not merely imposed externally but embedded within the conditions of participation themselves. Building on this premise and drawing on examples from online games and existing virtual platforms, the article explores how game and related design mechanisms, such as reputation systems, play-based sanctions, participatory adjudication, AI-assisted enforcement, and blockchain-based rule execution, can be leveraged to shape behavior and (self-)sustain normative order from within the virtual environment. Rather than offering a fixed framework or prescriptive model, the analysis develops a conceptual lens for understanding and critically assessing these regulatory possibilities. While gamified regulation promises more proactive and experientially coherent governance that resonates with the game-like nature of the Metaverse, it also raises significant ethical, legal, and social concerns, including risks of trivializing harm, surveillance, vigilantism, algorithmic bias, social stratification, and the normalization of behavior-based control. The article therefore positions gamified regulation as a conc…

title: CAUGHT BETWEEN POWER AND ORDER: LIVED EXPERIENCES OF LAW ENFORCEMENT OFFICERS UNDER POLITICAL INFLUENCE DURING ELECTORAL ACTIVITIES IN CENTRAL LUZON
abstract: This study explored the lived experiences of law enforcement officers operating under political influence during electoral activities in Central Luzon. Specifically, it examined the nature and forms of political influence encountered by law enforcement officers, the effects of political pressure and accountability mechanisms on their professional and personal lives, the challenges and ethical dilemmas they experienced, and the coping strategies they employed to maintain professionalism, accountability, and political neutrality during election periods. The study employed a qualitative research design using a descriptive phenomenological approach. Data were collected through in-depth interviews with selected Philippine National Police (PNP) officers who had direct experience in election-related operations within Central Luzon. The interview transcripts were analyzed using thematic analysis to identify essential themes that described the participants’ lived experiences. The findings revealed that political influence was commonly manifested through indirect political pressure, personal relationships with political actors, intervention in police operations, and expectations associated with electoral activities. Based on the findings, the study developed the Police Neutrality and Accountability Enhancement Program (PNAEP) as an intervention designed to strengthen ethical decision-mak…

title: Climate Change, Environmental Stress and Medicinal Plant Quality: Implications for Phytochemical Composition, Therapeutic Consistency and Conservation
abstract: Background: Climate change and associated environmental stresses are increasingly affecting the growth, distribution and phytochemical composition of medicinal plants. These changes may influence the quality, safety and therapeutic consistency of herbal medicines while posing additional challenges to the conservation and sustainable utilisation of medicinal plant resources. Aims: Climate change is altering the growing conditions of medicinal plants and, with them, the phytochemical profiles on which herbal medicines depend. This review synthesises how climate-related abiotic stresses affect secondary metabolites, the mechanisms involved, and the consequences for therapeutic consistency, safety and conservation. Methodology: A structured narrative review was conducted in accordance with the transparency principles of PRISMA 2020; Scopus, ScienceDirect, PubMed, Web of Science, and Google Scholar were searched for English-language, peer-reviewed studies published between January 2000 and October 2026 concerning medicinal plant phytochemistry, bioactivity, quality, conservation and environmental stress. Results: Elevated CO₂, warming, drought, salinity and UV-B reprogram the biosynthesis of alkaloids, phenolics, flavonoids, terpenoids and glycosides through ROS, phytohormone, transcription-factor and epigenetic networks. Depending on the species, organ, developmental stage, and lev…

title: Cloning and expression pattern analysis of salt exclusion gene FeSOS1 from common buckwheat
CRISPR/Cas-Mediated Genome Editing: Advancing Plant Disease Resistance through Promoter Precision
abstract: Infections with pathogens directly slow down the growth of crop biomass and the overall yield. Linkage drag is an issue for traditional breeding methods, while transgenic approaches raise biosafety problems because they use DNA from other organisms. The CRISPR/Cas system provides a more precise method for engineering by facilitating the specific modification of endogenous cis-regulatory regions. This review focuses on precise editing methods that are focused on promoter regions. In real experiments, changing coding sequences (CDS) directly can mess up the important jobs that proteins do in the body. On the other hand, fine-tuning promoter sequences can help the immune system and plant growth at the same time. They usually call this the growth-defense trade-off. We initially examined the principal enzymatic mechanisms involved in Cas9-mediated non-homologous end joining (NHEJ), Base Editors (BEs), and Prime Editors (PEs). After that, split the main goals that the labs are looking at into three groups. The investigation encompasses NLR receptor proteins, hormone-signaling hubs such as SlJAZ2, and susceptibility (S) genes that viruses exploit, including the SWEET family. We look at the different effects of breaking effector-binding elements (EBEs) or transcriptional repressor motifs by using phenotypic data from rice, tomato, and cassava mutants. The phenotypic results show that t…

Distributed fiber optic temperature sensing-based thermal monitoring system for power transformer applications
abstract: Purpose To address the limitation that existing digital twin models for power transformers lack real-time data and cannot reflect actual thermal conditions, this study aims to propose a thermal digital twin system using distributed optical fiber temperature measurement, enabling accurate condition monitoring and fault prediction. Design/methodology/approach The approach integrates gray wolf optimization with chaotic opposite-based learning and support vector regression for temperature correction. Multi-scale thermal features and temporal dependencies are extracted via an iterated dilated convolutional neural network, bidirectional long short-term memory networks and sparrow search algorithm, all validated against measured data. Findings The algorithm shows strong agreement with measurements (correlation 0.9413, root mean square error 0.23°C). Fault prediction accuracy reaches 98.72% (area under the curve 0.966). Warning lead times are 35.26 min (light load) and 25.81 min (heavy load), with handling success rates of 99.24% and 97.87%, respectively, outperforming comparative systems. Originality/value This work uniquely combines distributed optical fiber sensing with hybrid optimization-learning algorithms to construct a real-time thermal digital twin. It delivers robust adaptability under varying loads and provides a practical framework for intelligent transformer operation and …

title: Integrating virtual reality and 3D models in orthodontic education: Investigating student engagement with digital diagnostic workflows
abstract: The shift from physical plaster models to digital three-dimensional (3D) representations marks a significant change in orthodontic pedagogy, yet tertiary dental curricula have been slower to adopt digital workflows than clinical practice itself. This paper reports the conceptual framing, literature context, intervention design and methodology of a study investigating final-year Doctor of Dental Surgery (DDS) students’ engagement with virtual reality (VR) haptic interfaces and 3D orthodontic models when identifying malocclusions, specifically overjet (OJ) and the Index of Orthodontic Treatment Need (IOTN). A cohort of 43 students took part in a VR-enhanced seminar combining haptic simulation with 3D digital models, building on diagnostic concepts introduced earlier in the program. The study asks how students approach clinical measurement and diagnostic reasoning within an immersive digital environment, and how they envisage translating VR/3D outputs into the laboratory and clinical communication workflows still required of them. A mixed-methods design combines open-ended qualitative survey responses, analysed thematically, with quantitative Likert-scale ratings of task difficulty and teaching satisfaction. The intervention and methodology presented here situate VR-haptic simulation within the broader move toward “digital-native” clinical training that addresses the cost and scal…

Nano-Fe3O4 alleviates cadmium toxicity in Atractylodes lancea: a comparative study with ZnO and TiO2 nanoparticles and multi-omics insights
abstract: Abstract Background Soil cadmium (Cd) contamination severely threatens the growth and quality of medicinal crops, while nano-fertilizers show promise in mitigating heavy metal stress. This study aimed to compare the alleviative effects of different nanomaterials on Cd toxicity in Atractylodes lancea and to further elucidate the underlying mechanisms of the most effective nanomaterial. Results two-year-old A. lancea seedlings were exposed to 50 mg L − 1 Cd and foliar sprayed with 100 mg L − 1 Fe 3 O 4 nanoparticles (FeNPs_Cd), ZnO nanoparticles (ZnNPs_Cd), or TiO 2 nanoparticles (TiNPs_Cd) in the controlled-environment hydroponic experiments. Cd stress significantly inhibited the growth of A. lancea , reduced net photosynthetic rate and chlorophyll content, disrupted chloroplast structure, and induced oxidative damage. Notably, the three nanomaterials alleviated Cd toxicity to varying degrees, and FeNPs_Cd group showed the greatest effects by significantly increasing biomass, net photosynthetic rate, and antioxidant enzyme activities compared with Cd group, while reducing Cd content by 45.6% in leaves and 56.0% in roots, respectively. TEM observations also suggested that FeNPs may alleviate Cd-induced chloroplast damage. In this context, FeNPs_Cd group were therefore selected for further transcriptomic and metabolomic analyses. Integration analysis of metabolome and transcriptom…

title: Disease control potential of Mentha longifolia L. Hór-1 chemotype essential oil demonstrated against grapevine grey rot
abstract: Introduction Mint essential oils are promising agricultural antifungals as natural alternatives to chemical pest management. However, their phytotoxicity and volatility are challenging their application, which can be overcome by the use of adjuvants. In addition to formulation, the investigation of lesser-studied mint chemotypes may also lead to the development of novel and efficient fungicides due to the diversity of secondary metabolites of mint species. Materials and methods The antifungal and phytotoxic effects of the essential oil of Mentha longifolia L. Hó́r-1 chemotype were investigated in the present study using Vitis vinifera as a plant host and the grey rot causal fungus Botrytis cinerea as a pathogen. In addition, the effects of adjuvants on the above traits, as well as the essential oil-fungus interactions, were investigated in detail. Results The previously shown rare composition of M. longifolia L. Hór-1 essential oil was reinforced by the study, which detected significant amounts of thymol and carvacrol. The essential oil showed both fungistatic and fungicidal effects against B. cinerea in vitro . The fungicidal activity and the phytotoxicity of the essential oil against V. vinifera foliar disks were enhanced by the application of pine terpene-based or dioctyl sulfosuccinate emulsifiers. Fine-tuning of the formulation showed that 0.055% (v/v) essential oil in the…

Presence dynamics across film, virtual space, and social chatbot in an interactive installation
abstract: This article advances presence as a common variable for designing and evaluating multi-stage media experiences built with emerging technologies. As semiconductors make ever more objects function as media, a single experience increasingly spans several media. Yet presence has usually been studied one medium at a time, and the moments when it recedes have been treated as failures to be avoided rather than as part of the experience. The article develops an alternative account of presence through a practice-led interactive installation that unfolds a single narrative across three sequential stages: a projected film, a navigable virtual space, and a text-based conversation with a social chatbot. Analyzing the case through the notion of being digital, theories of presence, the Media Equation, and their foundations in evolutionary psychology, this article proposes presence dynamics: the way presence evolves across an extended, multi-stage experience that no single medium or session can account for. The concept brings together a time-varying view of presence with an account of the three dimensions of presence (physical, social, and self). The framework is specified as three testable propositions, advanced as hypotheses for subsequent work. First, Sequence: the shape presence traces depends on the ordering of stages, so reversing the order would not simply mirror the original path. Seco…

title: Dual-task graph attention learning for stress-responsive gene regulatory network inference in Panax notoginseng
abstract: Panax notoginseng is an important specialty crop and geo-authentic medicinal plant vulnerable to multiple stresses, with its stress responses regulated by complex gene regulatory networks. Limited species-specific regulatory evidence and sample size make systematic analysis of transcription factor (TF)-target relationships difficult. We developed a dual-task graph attention network (DTGAT) with a shared graph attention encoder and joint optimization of link prediction and expression reconstruction for regulatory relationship prediction. DTGAT was first evaluated in Arabidopsis thaliana for methodological validation. On the independent test set, link prediction achieved an AUC of 0.9106 and an AUPR of 0.8933, while expression reconstruction achieved an R² of 0.8375 and a PCC of 0.9152; link prediction outperformed the evaluated baselines. DTGAT was then applied to transcriptomic data from stressed P. notoginseng together with a homology-mapped prior network, yielding 55,108 high-confidence candidate regulatory edges. Promoter motif analysis further provided sequence-level support for 22 newly predicted candidate regulatory relationships associated with stress responses. Published experimental evidence supported the biological plausibility of the candidate MYB–CCoAOMT relationship. These findings highlight the utility of DTGAT for prioritizing stress-responsive regulatory candida…

title: Diabetes distress, social participation and social inclusion in Type 1 diabetes: a psychosocial framework
abstract: Purpose Diabetes distress in type 1 diabetes (T1D) is a widespread psychosocial problem that is clinically relevant but also a mental health and social inclusion problem and will be focused on here with a particular focus on adolescents and young adults. It has not been sufficiently theorised around its social implications. A psychosocial approach is suggested in this paper to understand the role of distress in social participation and feeling part of a group/society and provide a direction for psychosocial care. Design/methodology/approach This paper is grounded on the International Classification of Functioning, Disability and Health and is supported by theories of stress-coping, self-regulation and stigma and develops a conceptual moderated-mediation model and five testable propositions. Findings Diabetes distress can limit social participation by means of protective social withdrawal, which is the avoidance, restriction or concealment of social activity to manage glycaemic risk and the visibility of self-management, especially if diabetes perceived as stigma is expected. Withdrawal is presented as a reaction to the exclusionary conditions, rather than to the causes of the conditions. Relational support and safe disclosure are hypothesised to primarily affect the distress–withdrawal pathway, whereas environmental accommodation is hypothesised to primarily affect the withdraw…

title: EXPLAINING EMPLOYEE PERFORMANCE THROUGH DISCIPLINE AND COORDINATION: A PLS-SEM STUDY OF BEKASI REVENUE AGENCY
abstract: This study examines how work discipline and coordination relate to employees' self-reported performance at the Bekasi City Regional Revenue Agency. Drawing on coordination theory and the distinction between compliant work behaviour and task accomplishment, it re-examines a cross-sectional questionnaire survey of 30 employees drawn from an agency population of 100. The supplied manuscript reports descriptive summaries and a partial least squares structural equation model estimated with SPSS and SmartPLS. Mean scores were 4.82 for discipline, 4.81 for coordination, and 4.75 for performance on the reported five-point response scale. The reported positive paths to performance were 0.225 for discipline (t = 2.775) and 0.741 for coordination (t = 2.435), with an in-sample R² of 0.847. The larger coordination coefficient suggests that aligning tasks and information may matter especially in interdependent revenue administration, although the design cannot establish causal effects. An arithmetic audit also finds that the published discriminant-validity matrix does not reconcile with the path coefficients and R², while one reported p value is inconsistent with its t statistic. The contribution is therefore a bounded account of the two relationships and a transparent assessment of the evidence supporting them. Managers can use the pattern to review task handovers and procedural clarity, w…

title: Aorto-esophageal fistula after button battery ingestion in children: an early or a delayed complication?
abstract: Background Aorto-esophageal fistula (AEF) is a rare but potentially fatal complication of button battery ingestion in children. While traditionally considered an acute event, increasing evidence suggests a delayed onset, even after battery removal. However, the temporal pattern of AEF development has never been systematically characterized, and the duration of risk after ingestion remains unclear. Methods A structured literature review was performed following PRISMA principles, focusing on pediatric cases of AEF secondary to button battery ingestion. The primary outcome was the time between button battery removal and AEF onset. Secondary variables included demographic data, timing of battery removal, anatomical localization, and clinical outcomes. Results Fourteen pediatric cases were included. Among patients for whom the timing of battery removal was available, the median time from ingestion to battery removal was 14 h (IQR 5–16 h; range 4–24 h). Among patients in whom AEF developed after battery removal and the post-removal interval was available, AEF developed a median of 18 days after removal (IQR 9–21 days; range 9–35 days). The overall mortality rate was 43% (6/14). Conclusions AEF after button battery ingestion is predominantly a delayed complication and early battery removal does not eliminate risk. Need for prolonged vigilance and prompt evaluation of delayed warning s…

Germinated Kodo millet flour (GKMF) was used to replace 20% of the rice flour, and the standard rice flour-based product served as the control.

Hepatitis B Vaccine as a Primary Prevention Strategy for Cancer: Mechanisms, Outcomes and Model Extension
abstract: Vaccination against Hepatitis B can prevent liver cancer by preventing chronic infection of the liver. This paper reviews the role of hepatitis B virus (HBV) in hepatocellular carcinoma, cancer prevention via vaccination, and lessons learned from China's experience for other cancer-prevention programmes. HBV promotes cancer by inducing chronic inflammation in the host, integrating viral DNA into the host's DNA, and altering cell regulation through viral proteins. China's childhood vaccination programme has reduced infections among young children significantly. Extended data from the Qidong trial have also indicated a decrease in primary liver cancer; however, due to a small number of cancer cases, the exact extent remains unknown. Comparison with human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination shows that the biological principle can be applied to infections, but delivery needs to match the age and circumstances of the target population. China's addition of HPV vaccination to the national programme in 2025 is a policy change. Disease spread can be effectively prevented through timely vaccination, accessible medical services, and ongoing care for high-risk groups.

title: Perceived workplace discrimination and its impacts on leaders: latent class analysis
abstract: Purpose This study aims to identify distinct latent classes of perceived workplace discrimination among leaders and examine how different patterns of discrimination perception are associated with workplace attitudes and behaviors. Design/methodology/approach Using a mixture modeling approach, this study conducted latent class analysis with data from 3,351 leaders drawn from the 2022 Korean Women Manager Panel. The study examined predictors of latent class membership, including shadow labor culture, fairness of HR practices and top management leadership and compared organizational outcomes across the identified classes. Findings The findings revealed five distinct latent classes representing heterogeneous patterns of perceived workplace discrimination among leaders. The results demonstrated that organizational contextual factors significantly differentiated class membership. In addition, significant differences were found across the latent classes in organizational satisfaction and organizational commitment. However, leadership efficacy did not significantly differ across classes, suggesting that perceived workplace discrimination may influence organizational attitudes more strongly than leaders’ self-perceived leadership capability. Originality/value This study contributes to the human resource development and workplace discrimination literature by shifting attention from direc…

title: Micro brain drain: a conceptual explanation of scaling cognitive withdrawal into organizational capability vulnerability
abstract: Purpose Organizations may retain their employees and formal structures while gradually losing the cognitive participation required for collective learning and adaptation. This study introduces micro brain drain (MBD) as an emergent organizational process through which persistent and distributed cognitive withdrawal accumulates across interdependent organizational units and becomes consequential for organizational adaptation. Design/methodology/approach The study adopts a systematic literature review combined with an integrative conceptual synthesis. Following PRISMA-guided procedures, relevant peer-reviewed literature from Scopus and Web of Science was identified, screened and synthesized to examine cognitive withdrawal, organizational learning, collective sensemaking, knowledge integration and adaptive capabilities. The synthesis is used to develop a conceptual explanation of how micro-level cognitive withdrawal scales into an organization-level condition. Findings The synthesis indicates that MBD emerges when cognitive withdrawal becomes persistent, socially distributed and reinforced across interdependent organizational units. As MBD develops, it progressively constrains organizational interpretive capacity by narrowing distributed attention, reducing interpretive diversity and weakening collective sensemaking and knowledge integration. This erosion subsequently increases vu…

title: From implementation to doxa: strategic normalization as field restructuring in lean transformation
abstract: Purpose While strategy research has advanced understanding of implementation, enactment, participation and situated strategizing, less attention has been devoted to how strategic initiatives become enduring organizational realities. This study develops strategic normalization as a conceptual lens to explain how contested strategic interventions move beyond implementation toward taken-for-granted organizational practice. Design/methodology/approach The study adopts an interpretivist qualitative single-case design examining lean transformation within a Sri Lankan manufacturing organization. Drawing on 38 semi-structured interviews across multiple organizational levels and documentary evidence, the study retrospectively reconstructs the transformation as a process. Bourdieusian concepts of field, legitimacy, habitus and doxa are used to interpret how the strategic initiative moved toward becoming increasingly accepted and reproduced in everyday organizational life. Findings Interpreted through a Bourdieusian lens, the findings suggest that strategic durability emerged through a process involving disruption of the existing organizational order, restructuring of authority relations and participation mechanisms, production of strategic legitimacy, emerging habituation of strategic conduct and movement toward stabilization of the strategic logic as organizational common sense. Origina…

title: El Diálogo Empático como Estrategia Metodológica en Psicólogos en Formación
abstract: En el presente artículo se reflexiona sobre el papel de la empatía como estrategia metodológica en psicólogos en formación, construido por experiencias, relatos y vivencias en estudiantes universitarios. Se realizó un taller investigativo con 26 estudiantes de psicología de la Facultad de Estudios Superiores Iztacala, en el cual se realizaron actividades individuales y grupales donde reconocían sus emociones y sensaciones corporales al igual que la comprensión de las experiencias del otro. En la metodología se incluyó el uso de una silueta en blanco, triadas con los elementos de habla, escucha y observación, recursos artísticos y experiencias escritas, el contenido se analizó mediante categorías como contexto situacional, reacción emocional, sensación corporal, estrategias de afrontamiento y empatía. Los resultados mostraron que la escucha en las experiencias del otro generan respuestas emocionales y sensaciones corporales que están vinculadas con las vivencias propias. Las personas participantes destacaron la importancia en el tema de autoconocimiento y autorregulación emocional para poder acompañar al otro de manera genuina. El diálogo empático se relaciona con la confianza, apertura y la co-construcción de significados. Se concluye que la empatía es la base para un vínculo entre el conocimiento teórico y la experiencia del día a día, con una formación integral donde se recon…

title: Investigating prior experience and factors affecting vividness of Motor Imagery in people with Parkinson’s: a potential strategy with an unfamiliar name
abstract: Parkinson’s is characterised by motor symptoms, such as tremor, bradykinesia and problems with balance. Motor Imagery (MI) is a technique where people imagine movement without physically moving. It is a promising tool in motor rehabilitation in various clinical populations, including people with Parkinson’s (PwP). For MI interventions to be effective, people need to be able to vividly imagine movements, an ability that varies in the general population. This study utilised an online survey to examine the relationship between MI vividness scores and severity of Parkinson’s motor symptoms, as well as other factors such as depression and sports/musical ability and experience. Prior knowledge and experiences of MI were also explored. PwP were found to have significantly more vivid visual than kinaesthetic MI. However, no significant relationship/effect was found between MI vividness scores and Parkinson’s motor symptom severity, depression or musical/sports ability. While 78.5% of participants reported that they had previously used MI or something similar, most were unfamiliar with the name MI and 82.5% of participants reported wanting to know more about the technique. The results suggest MI is potentially suitable for PwP across different levels of motor symptom severity and previous expertise. The findings also highlight the need for resources about MI to raise awareness and expla…

title: Drivers of Strategy Implementation and Performance of Human Rights Organizations in Kisumu County
abstract: Purpose: The purpose of the study was to assess drivers of strategy implementation and performance of human rights organizations in Kisumu County. Methodology: This research used descriptive survey research design using both qualitative and quantitative approaches. The target population for this study were employees at all levels of the 21 HROs in Kisumu County. These included a total of 4,855 (Regional NGO Reports, 2024). All operating agribusiness registered by MSEA comprised the study sample. The Yamane model was used to obtain the sample size of 196 respondents. Descriptive statistics involved frequencies, means and standard deviation while inferential statistics were measured at significance level of 0.05. The analysis of a multiple linear regression model was used to test the significance of the influence of the independent variables on the dependent variable. Findings: The regression model revealed a strong positive relationship between the drivers and performance (R = 0.728), with the four drivers collectively accounting for 53.0% of the variation in performance (R² = 0.530; adjusted R² = 0.513). All four drivers had positive and statistically significant effects on performance: resource allocation (β = 0.322, p < 0.001), strategic communication (β = 0.286, p < 0.001), leadership commitment (β = 0.254, p = 0.001), and organizational culture (β = 0.218, p = 0.004). Uniqu…

title: Copper Nanocone Electrodes for Capacitive Pressure Sensing through Electric-Field Redistribution and Interfacial Modulation
abstract: Abstract Flexible capacitive tactile sensors are essential components for emerging human-machine interfaces, electronic skins, and wearable healthcare systems. However, the weak pressure-induced modulation of the electrode-dielectric interface in conventional planar configurations can limit the capacitance variation generated by small mechanical stimuli. Here, we develop a highly sensitive capacitive tactile sensor based on copper nanocone electrodes that regulate the local electric-field distribution and the pressure-dependent interfacial geometry. The nanocone arrays are fabricated through a two-electrode electrodeposition strategy, and their height and array density are systematically regulated to examine how electrode geometry affects field redistribution and pressure-induced interfacial capacitance variation. Finite element simulations reveal geometry-dependent stress and electric-field redistribution, while the measured structure-performance relationships indicate that nanocone geometry influences capacitive sensing through coupled electrical and interfacial effects. The optimized sensor achieves a sensitivity of 6.29 kPa–1 over 0–20 kPa, a minimum detectable load of 200 mg, a response time of 99 ms, and stable operation over 15,000 loading–unloading cycles. Airflow-pulse encoding of Morse signals demonstrates the detection of weak airflow-induced pressure changes without…

title: Effects of Suspension Stiffness, Vehicle Speed, and Road Roughness on Dynamic Loading of the Drive Axle Housing in a 1.25-Ton Light Truck
abstract: This paper investigates the effects of rear suspension stiffness on dynamic loading of the drive axle housing of a 1.25-ton light truck under random excitation, in accordance with ISO 8608:2016. A full-vehicle oscillation model was constructed to simulate dynamic loads over a speed range of 20–60 km/h for four road classes: B, C, D, and E. Two evaluation criteria were used: maximum dynamic load coefficient (Kdmax) and minimum dynamic load coefficient (Kdmin). The results show that road surface quality has a greater influence than speed and suspension stiffness. The traction reduction is high, while Kdmax increases from 1.05 to 2.02 (92.4%) when the road class changes from B to E at 60 km/h, and Kdmin decreases from 0.40 to 0.19 (52.5%). For road class E at 60 km/h, when the suspension stiffness increases from 0.5*C to 1.5*C, the Kdmax increases from 1.82 to 2.30 (26.4%), while the Kdmin decreases from 0.22 to 0.17 (22.7%). The worst case is for road class E with a stiffness of 1.5*C, where Kdmax = 2.30, corresponding to a dynamic load exceeding the static load by 130%, and Kdmin = 0.17, approaching the condition of loss of wheel contact with the road surface.
venue: International Journal of Automotive Manufacturing and Materials

title: Source Decomposition and Structural Changes in the Growth of China's New Energy Vehicle Sales
abstract: Based on the monthly "Operation of the Automotive Industry" reports released by the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology, this study constructs a 56-month dataset on China's new energy vehicle (NEV) market from January 2022 to August 2026. It applies a two-factor symmetric decomposition of market size and penetration rate, together with an incremental decomposition of domestic sales and exports, to identify the sources and stage-specific changes in NEV sales growth from the perspectives of product structure and sales destination. The results show that from 2023 to 2025, increases in the penetration rate accounted for 64.6%, 85.3%, and 63.9% of the annual sales increments, respectively, making penetration the main accounting source of NEV growth. From January to August 2026, the contribution of total automotive market size was −38.5 × 10,000 vehicles, while the contribution of the penetration rate was 144.2 × 10,000 vehicles, indicating that NEV sales growth did not result from an expansion of the overall automotive market. Over the same period, NEV exports increased by 192.8 × 10,000 vehicles, while domestic sales decreased by 87.1 × 10,000 vehicles; the export increment offset the decline in domestic sales. Sensitivity tests using reported cumulative values and aggregated monthly decompositions do not alter the main conclusions. The findings indicate that analyses o…

title: A Comparative Analysis of Three Quantitative Pricing Frameworks for SSE 50ETF Options: BS Analytical Model, CRR Binomial Tree Model and Monte Carlo Simulation
abstract: This study compares the effectiveness and feasibility of the Black-Scholes (BS) analytical model, the Cox-Ross-Rubinstein (CRR) binomial-tree model and Monte Carlo simulation of SSE 50 ETF European call contracts. With the help of the no-arbitrage condition, risk-neutral valuation and geometric Brownian motion are used to create these three models in Python with the same benchmark parameters and later compare their pricing accuracy, convergence rate and algorithmic efficiency, and their applicability to various applications. The numerical data shows that the three methods give almost the same option price: 0.0846 to the BS model, 0.0847 the 200-step CRR model, and 0.0843 the Monte Carlo simulation of 100, 000 paths. The BS approach is by nature simple and easy to use, but has some limitations. As the number of iterations increases, the CRR framework is inclined to the BS value and thus can be used in American style options. High-dimensional and path-dependent derivatives are best modeled using Monte Carlo simulation, whose accuracy depends on the number of simulated paths and the traditional model is not able to price American contracts directly. These results explain the tradeoff between accuracy, flexibility and computational cost in option pricing model selection.

title: Numerical Methods for Partial Differential Equations in Financial Derivatives Pricing: A Comparative Review from Classical Methods to Deep Learning
abstract: Pricing of financial derivatives can generally be reduced to solving partial differential equations (PDEs). Starting from the classical Black-Scholes framework, pricing models that better reflect market characteristics, such as stochastic volatility and jump-diffusion models, have been developed, and classical numerical methods, such as the finite difference method, have long dominated their solution. However, as the dimensionality of pricing problems rises, grid-based methods face a sharp growth in computational cost, the so-called curse of dimensionality, while deep learning methods such as physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) have recently offered new approaches to high-dimensional PDEs. This paper systematically reviews and compares classical numerical methods (finite difference, finite element and spectral methods) with deep learning methods in terms of convergence, computational efficiency and applicability, and discusses their suitability for free-boundary problems, such as the early exercise of American options, and for high-dimensional multi-asset pricing. A literature review combined with comparative analysis was adopted, and the methods were compared across numerical stability, computational complexity and dimensional adaptability. The analysis shows that classical methods rest on relatively mature convergence theory and produce stable results for low-dimensional…

title: Bridging institutional AI strategy and subject-level teaching practice: A school-level design framework for responsible AI-supported learning
abstract: The rapid growth of generative artificial intelligence (AI) in higher education has accelerated institutional investment in AI infrastructure, yet many universities continue to face difficulties translating institutional strategy into consistent subject-level teaching practice. This paper presents a School-level framework developed at an Australian university. The paper reports the design rationale, outputs and approved deployment model of the framework, including staff capability resources, configurable AI templates, disclosure mechanisms and governance processes. Informed by Educational Design Research and scholarship on organisational change in education, the paper argues that Schools can serve as meso-level environments that enact institutional AI strategy through resources and structures designed to support subject-level teaching practice. It contributes a meso-level governance model, six transferable design principles, and an operational framework intended to support responsible and human-centred AI-supported learning. Formal evaluation is planned following the pilot phase.

title: Beyond Porter: hybrid strategies, innovation, adaptive capabilities, and their impact on firm performance
abstract: Purpose In competitive environments, companies constantly seek new approaches and strategies to position themselves and compete successfully. Hybrid strategies provide a different, largely unexplored approach that is relatively opposed to Michael Porter’s well-known generic strategies. Hybrid strategies would yield better performance outcomes, especially in highly dynamic environments. The objective of this article is to empirically test this relationship using a conceptual model that analyzes how hybrid strategies, innovation, and adaptive capabilities affect firm performance in a particularly competitive environment. Design/methodology/approach Quantitative study based on questionnaires administered to companies in the dynamic Peruvian agro-export sector. The data were analyzed using structural equation modeling (SEM) and importance-performance map analysis (IPMA). Findings We found that hybrid strategies were preferred and used by all companies in the sample without exception, rather than Porter’s generic strategies. Furthermore, the results show that hybrid strategies have a positive and significant effect on firm performance. No mediating or moderating effects of innovation and adaptive capabilities were confirmed; however, both variables were essential in explaining performance. Research limitations/implications The study is limited to one geographical region and cross-se…

title: Content licensing strategy in AI–publisher coopetition: the role of asymmetric comparative advantages and citation intensity
abstract: Purpose This study examines strategic content licensing between a generative artificial intelligence (AI) platform and a digital news publisher in digital news markets, an important issue for understanding where AI platforms rely on publisher content while competing for user attention. It analyzes how citation intensity shapes licensing incentives, pricing, user diversion and welfare. Design/methodology/approach We develop a game-theoretic model of two-dimensional horizontal differentiation in which the AI platform has a comparative advantage in content integration and the publisher has a comparative advantage in factual accuracy. The model examines how citation intensity, hallucination risk, user preference correlation and per-use royalty jointly determine equilibrium outcomes. Findings Licensing between AI platforms and publishers arises from a trade-off between two countervailing forces: entry displacement and engagement expansion. Content licensing requires sufficiently high citation intensity; mutual gains additionally require low preference correlation. The pricing effects of citation intensity are nonmonotonic. Subscription prices can rise or fall depending on the strength of citation relative to royalty costs. User diversion is shaped by the balance between referral traffic expansion and direct substitution. Welfare improves only when engagement expansion dominates entr…
venue: Asia Pacific Journal of Marketing and Logistics

title: A Critical Analysis of Pop Mart's Marketing Strategy: From Blind Box Consumption to Sustainable Brand Community
abstract: China's trendy toy market has grown rapidly, with Pop Mart leading through blind box marketing. Yet this model, built on uncertainty and scarcity, is now challenged by tighter regulations and consumer fatigue. This study asks: (1) How does Pop Mart use psychological pricing, scarcity, and IP to attract consumers? (2) Why is its high-margin model under pressure from regulation and market saturation? Using a case study approach with PESTEL, STP, and 4Ps frameworks, this paper finds Pop Mart's success hinges on collectable psychology and the thrill of surprise, but China's Guidelines for the Operation of Blind Box Products (requiring probability disclosure and prohibiting sales to minors under 8) create structural challenges. To sustain growth, Pop Mart must move from one-time surprise consumption to building lasting brand communities by deepening IP content, communicating transparently, and managing long-term customer relationships. This research highlights ethical tensions in China's trendy toy industry and provides strategic references for brands operating at the intersection of behavioural marketing and regulatory compliance.
venue: Advances in Economics, Management and Political Sciences

title: Novel therapeutic strategy for interstitial cystitis: clinical efficacy evaluation of combined botulinum neurotoxin type A injection into the detrusor and pelvic floor muscle trigger points
abstract: Objective This study aimed to evaluate the preliminary efficacy and safety of combined botulinum toxin type A injection into the detrusor and pelvic floor trigger points in women with interstitial cystitis/bladder pain syndrome (IC/BPS) and concomitant pelvic floor muscle dysfunction. Methods This retrospective study analyzed IC/BPS patients hospitalized at the Urology Center of the First Affiliated Hospital of Xinjiang Medical University between January 2023 and January 2025 who underwent botulinum toxin type A injection therapy. All included patients had IC/BPS with concomitant pelvic floor muscle dysfunction, defined as elevated pelvic floor electromyographic resting activity and clinically identifiable pelvic floor tenderness/trigger points. Pelvic floor muscle dysfunction was a shared eligibility characteristic of both groups and was not used to define the comparison groups. Patients were retrospectively grouped according to the treatment strategy received in routine clinical practice: intradetrusor BTX-A injection alone (Intradetrusor-only group, n = 49) or combined intradetrusor and pelvic floor trigger-point BTX-A injection (Combined-treatment group, n = 58). Pre-and post-treatment follow-up data were evaluated, including changes in ICPI, ICSI, OABSS, pain scores, Physical Health (PH) and Mental Health (MH) scores, and psychological anxiety scores. title: Developing and Applying a Framework to Assess New Quality Productive Forces in New Energy Enterprises from a Supply Chain Integration Perspective
abstract: Assessing new quality productive forces from public reports is difficult because the available firm-level measures describe financial structure and workforce composition, not the coordination that runs across firms, and because a report that says nothing about a practice is easily misread as evidence that the practice is absent. This paper builds a diagnostic that treats such forces, for photovoltaic and lithium-battery manufacturers, as disclosed supply-chain integration practice. An integrative reading of measurement, integration and industry studies yields four dimensions and twelve indicators, each tied to one interface among internal functions, suppliers, customers and other partners, and each coded on a five-level scale of public evidence. The arithmetic is fixed before any score is read: a dimension score uses only the indicators that have evidence, a conditional total is reported only when at least 80 percent of indicators are scored and every dimension has at least two, and every unscored indicator is kept out of the total and inside an identification bound that places it at the bottom and then at the top of the scale. One coder applied the scheme to the 2025 reports of ten disclosure-rich manufacturers, scoring 114 of 120 firm-indicator cells and leaving six not assessable. The conditional totals run from 54.17 to 62.50, the knowledge dimension has the highest mean an…

title: Exploring game-based learning to advance teaching and learning in public health
abstract: Background There is a growing need to advance public health education through interventions that foster academic integrity, build professional confidence and future work-readiness, minimize teaching and learning fatigue, and remain efficient across educational modalities. Game-based learning (GbL) is a promising strategy to complement traditional teaching when well-informed, carefully planned, and supported by sustained engagement from both educators and students. However, empirical evidence on attitudes toward and experiences with GbL integration in public health education remains limited. This study examines public health instructors' and graduate students' perceptions and experiences of GbL, both as a broad pedagogical strategy and as a tool for teaching and learning about nature-based solutions, a novel concept in public health. Methods A qualitative descriptive study was conducted at the College of Public Health with course instructors and graduate students. Data were collected via 55 completed surveys, two focus groups, and 10 key informant interviews. Survey data were analyzed in Qualtrics, and qualitative data were analyzed thematically using MAXQDA. Results Participants reported their perceptions of and experiences with GbL in public health education and factors influencing its integration. Perceptions of GbL were largely positive, with participants acknowledging its r…

title: Editorial: Literacy in the age of artificial intelligence: research priority to realize learning futures
Evaluating Generative AI in Chemistry Prelabs: Efficiency Gains without Measurable Learning Benefits
abstract: Abstract The rapid adoption of generative artificial intelligence (AI) tools in higher education has raised questions regarding their impact on students’ information literacy (IL) and cognitive processes. In this study, we investigated how generative AI influences undergraduate students’ performance and perceptions in an inorganic chemistry prelaboratory assignment consisting in gathering and elaborating information relevant to the experiments. Second-year chemistry students completed two prelab tasks: one with generative AI support and one without AI. Students reported that generative AI support significantly reduced time dedicated to prelab elaboration. They also perceived AI-assisted tasks as easier and faster, rated AI-generated information as less clear and precise than traditional sources, and frequently expressed concerns about its reliability. However, no statistically significant differences were observed in instructor-evaluated scores between AI-supported and non-AI prelabs. These results indicate that students predominantly valued AI for efficiency. Interpreted through a Cognitive Load Theory lens, the reduction in time and search effort is consistent with a possible decrease in task-related logistical demands.

title: Deep learning–based individual segmentation and damage assessment of earthquake-damaged buildings: a case study of the old town of Beichuan county earthquake ruins
abstract: Introduction Addressing the technical demand for rapid and precise building segmentation and intelligent damage assessment after earthquakes, this study proposes a collaborative method based on improved YOLOv8 for individual building segmentation and damage assessment. Methods Using UAV imagery of the Beichuan old town ruins, we build a dual_task sample database and separately train segmentation and classification models via network improvements, under an integrated framework of image segmentation, individual extraction, and multi_view assessment. The segmentation model extracts building footprints and combines with DSM to build 3D constraint boxes for isolating individual buildings. We then use five_direction virtual camera imaging and the most severe damage criterion for automatic damage grading. Results Validation via high_accuracy 3D models and field surveys yields: (1) Under 300_epoch progressive training, both models converge stably. building.pt achieves mAP50(B)=0.934 and mAP50_95(B)=0.803, and assessment.pt attains Accuracy of 0.64, Precision of 0.58, Recall of 0.75, and F1_Score of 0.65, respectively, demonstrating effective handling of irregular building outlines and complex damage morphologies (2) A total of 64 target buildings are present in the study area, of which 61 are successfully identified and segmented by the algorithm, yielding an overall recognition succes…

title: Origin discrimination and screening of potential geographical origin markers for American ginseng based on metabolomics and machine learning
How do we know students have learned? Rethinking evidence, assessment and assurance of learning in the Age of AI
abstract: The rapid rise of artificial intelligence (AI) presents new challenges for educators striving to ensure learning can occur. Where higher education is making claims about graduate capability, we must ensure that our Assurance of Learning (AoL) architectures can support such claims. This symposium will introduce a systems-aware AoL architecture that aligns three interdependent layers: subject-level assessment design as evidence generation, program-level structures as mechanisms for longitudinal evidence integration, and institutional AoL frameworks as sites of interpretive judgement and capability claims. Through guided discussion the symposium will interrogate modes of learning, teaching and assessment that align with this model. We reframe AoL from a process of measurement and reporting to a system of evidencing. In doing so, it advances a future-focused agenda for institutional redesign, sector-wide reform, and research into evidence, inference, and capability in higher education environments where AI may now be fully embedded.

title: Data-Driven Analysis of C8 Olefin Epoxidation over TS-1 and Immobilized Peroxotungstate: From Experimental Catalytic Tests to Interpretable Machine Learning
abstract: Abstract Catalytic epoxidation of olefins with hydrogen peroxide has been recognized as an attractive route to produce epoxy compounds. In this work, an experimental dataset on the epoxidation of C8 olefins, including 1-octene, cyclooctene, trans-4-octene, and cis-4-octene, was generated for commercial titanium silicalite-1 (TS-1) and an immobilized peroxotungstate catalyst supported on a polymer matrix (A-PWx/PS). The catalysts were compared in terms of conversion, epoxide selectivity, epoxide yield, recyclability, TON, and TOF. TS-1 showed high activity toward 1-octene and 4-octenes, but its performance in cyclooctene epoxidation was strongly limited, with conversion not exceeding 7% after 6 h. In contrast, A-PWx/PS reached >99% conversion and >99% selectivity in cyclooctene epoxidation, with TON and TOFavg values of 266 and 44.3 h–1, respectively, and retained high catalytic performance over five consecutive cycles. To rationalize these trends, the experimental data were combined with substrate descriptors, including kinetic diameter, permanent dipole, and quantum-chemical parameters of the C═C bond, and analyzed using interpretable machine learning. SHAP analysis revealed that catalyst architecture, reaction time, steric accessibility, and C═C electron-donating ability determine the conversion–selectivity–stability balance. The results demonstrate that A-PWx/PS is a p…

title: ICG-AGLS: a competency graph-guided generative AI framework for interpretable learner-state modeling and adaptive learning support
abstract: Human learning is a dynamic cognitive process in which latent knowledge and competency states evolve through sequential interactions. However, existing generative AI learning-support systems often separate learner-state modeling, resource recommendation, knowledge-grounded generation, and pedagogical planning, limiting adaptive performance and interpretability. This study proposes ICG-AGLS, an interdisciplinary competency graph-guided adaptive generative AI learning support framework. It models learner states from historical interactions, projects them into a competency space, and constructs an interdisciplinary competency graph linking courses, concepts, resources, assignments, and competency dimensions. The framework integrates competency-gap-guided recommendation, graph-guided retrieval-augmented generation, adaptive reasoning routing, and multi-agent pedagogical coordination. Experiments on MOOCCubeX, OULAD, and EdNet demonstrate consistent improvements across learner-state modeling, recommendation, knowledge-grounded generation, and multi-agent planning. ICG-AGLS achieves an AUC of 0.871, Recall@10 of 0.812, ROUGE-L of 0.772, and a task completion rate of 0.839, outperforming representative task-specific baselines. These findings suggest that competency-structured latent-state modeling provides an interpretable computational bridge between evolving human learning states an…

title: Effects of gamified mobile learning on physical activity self-efficacy and fundamental motor skills among Chinese preschool children
abstract: Preschool children in urban Chinese-speaking contexts often face limited opportunities to practice fundamental motor skills because of cramped living spaces, scarce playgrounds, and high screen time. This study tested whether a 10-week gamified mobile learning intervention using augmented reality could improve fundamental motor skills and physical activity self-efficacy more effectively than standard kindergarten activities. A quasi-experimental design was employed with 240 children aged 4–6 years (120 in Chinese mainland and 120 in China's Taiwan region). Classes were assigned to either the experimental condition using the custom “Move & Win” app (AR overlays, points, badges, and adaptive feedback) or the control condition (regular teacher-led activities). Fundamental motor skills were measured with the TGMD-3, and self-efficacy with a pictorial scale. Mastery experiences were recorded automatically by the app. The experimental group showed significantly larger gains in both outcomes, with stronger motor skill improvements in Chinese mainland. Mediation analysis confirmed that mastery experiences explained the link between the intervention and self-efficacy gains. Post-test scores also exceeded regional normative data, with large effect sizes. These findings indicate that simple AR gamification offers a practical, low-cost way to overcome common environmental barriers and …

title: Teaching placebo analgesia to undergraduate students through a simulated clinical trial: a pedagogical approach to experiential learning in pharmacology
abstract: Background Although biomedical education is becoming increasingly theoretical and digitalized, hands-on practical exercises that actively engage students remain essential for enhancing knowledge acquisition. Understanding the methodology and functioning of clinical trials, the placebo response/effect and its physiological/biochemical basis are essential for biomedical students. In this study, we propose a practical exercise based on a simulated clinical trial in which students participate as both investigators and study subjects. Specifically, the analgesic and anesthetic effects of the EMLA® cream (prilocaine + lidocaine) were compared with those of the placebo and a moisturizing cream. Methods This educational research study employed a double-blind, randomized, controlled, parallel-group simulated trial design. A total of 499 undergraduate medicine and nursing students were randomly assigned, in a double-blind manner, to receive either the EMLA® cream, a placebo cream, or an unblinded comparator (moisturizing cream). Changes in five different sensory parameters (two low-threshold mechanical stimulations: von Frey and two-point discrimination tests; and three high-threshold mechanical and thermal stimulations: pinprick test, hot and cold plates) were assessed 60 min after treatment. Results EMLA® induced marked anesthesia and analgesia. Crucially, the placebo elicited robust a…

title: An explainable learning analytics approach for AI-supported early warning in higher education using frequent risk automata
Enhancing Plurigaussian simulation through neural truncation rules
abstract: Purpose Plurigaussian simulation (PGS) is a powerful approach in generating discrete stochastic structures of complex multiphase systems across a range of scales. Originating as an extension of truncated Gaussian simulation, PGS allows for the detailed representation of phase relationships and connectivity. A key element of PGS is the identification of truncation rules to dictate the geometric and facies relationships and traditionally involves a trial-and-error approach based on the physical characteristics of the modelled structures. The purpose of this study is to present an approach to learning such rules. Design/methodology/approach This study introduces the use of generative adversarial networks, specifically using the Wasserstein generative adversarial network with gradient penalty architecture, to automate and enhance the selection of truncation rules through a neural truncation rule. Findings By learning directly from the characteristics of the training data, this approach aims to bypass the limitations of manual truncation rule selection, offering a more efficient and precise method to replicate the desired structural features. Originality/value This study highlights the efficacy of generative machine learning in identifying suitable truncation rules for PGS, significantly reducing the uncertainty in truncation rule choice and enabling the accurate realisation of comp…

title: Teamwork as a learning practice: A framework for teamwork education
abstract: Teamwork drives transformative learning, fosters inclusivity and is critical for professional success. Yet, students and educators frequently struggle with it. Student experiences of teamwork vary widely across disciplines and programs, and many lack the foundational skills to collaborate effectively. Despite its importance and prevalence in assessment, teamwork education is often absent from curricula. Here we address this issue by reframing teamwork, not as a production process but as a learning practice. We introduce the Teamwork Learning Practice Framework, which is built on a natural landscape metaphor, and views teamwork as the ongoing, intrapersonal, functional, relational and reflexive processes through which people build awareness of themselves and others while working towards common goals. It positions collaboration as a means of achieving outcomes as well as a space for reflection, experimentation, and growth where people learn through and about working together within the broader structural, psychological, and relational institutional landscape. By focusing on various aspects of learning as a key element of teamwork, this framework offers a shared, consistent language across disciplines and programs, and a scaffold and practical resource for educators, program leaders, and institutions to provide the context and content for effective teamwork education. In doing so,…

title: "Engaging and exciting": Student perspectives on digital learning, authentic assessment and enabling pedagogy.
abstract: Students who see purpose or “find meaning” in coursework are more likely to achieve deep learning outcomes (Gee & Esteban-Guitart, 2019, p. 9); yet, there are limited examples which show how to engage learners in this way. Authentic assessment extends engagement through connection to aspirations, “challeng[ing] university students intellectually and creatively” (Australian Technology Network, 2020), and enhancing motivation through purposeful learning aligned to real-world contexts (ACEL, 2016). Enabling pedagogy advocates for purposeful learning connected to student goals (Stokes, 2023). Tai et al. (2022) observe authentic assessment provides opportunities for learners to blend “values […and] future aspirations” (p. 9), and showcase individual strengths and capabilities to demonstrate “distinctiveness” (p. 10). These approaches support design and delivery of meaningful assessment, encouraging student persistence and transformative learning outcomes. In our research, we investigated digital learning and authentic assessment framed through the lens of enabling pedagogy. Enabling pedagogy is an inclusive, strengths-based approach which focuses on student capabilities, facilitates understanding through dialogue, and supports learner agency at university (Bennett et al., 2018; Hattam et al., 2024; Stokes, 2014). Developed within university enabling programs (Fee-Free University Rea…

title: Deep learning image reconstruction at incremental weightings (20–80%) for high–resolution coronary CT angiography: a prospective image quality study
Applications of Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning in Financial Risk Management: A Review of Recent Research
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) are now widely used in credit, market, operational, liquidity, and systemic risk management, largely because they can handle large-scale, multi-source, and nonlinear data. This literature review draws on recent studies and public cases and groups the evidence by these five risk categories. It compares reported methods, data sources, evaluation practices, and regulatory issues. Credit scoring and fraud detection have advanced fastest. Market risk models increasingly rely on deep learning for volatility and return prediction, while liquidity and systemic risk remain difficult to model because extreme events are rare. Random forests, gradient boosting, and neural networks often outperform linear models on public datasets, yet their advantage is less stable in live business settings and stressed markets. Data silos, class imbalance, model degradation, weak interpretability, privacy risks, adversarial attacks, and model homogeneity continue to limit deployment. More work is needed on explainable AI, privacy-preserving learning, stress testing, and cross-institutional data governance, and validation on proprietary data remains necessary before wider use.
venue: Advances in Economics, Management and Political Sciences

title: Transformasi Digital dalam Manajemen Keuangan Perusahaan: Systematic Literature Review tentang FinTech, Efisiensi Keuangan, dan Pengambilan Keputusan
abstract: Aim: This article maps the evidence on FinTech and its enabling digital technologies, financial efficiency, and the quality of financial decision-making at the firm level, because evidence on the benefits, risks, and challenges of digital transformation is scattered across many technologies and contexts. Method: The study is a systematic literature review (SLR) guided by PRISMA 2020. Searches with 11 queries on a web search engine yielded 106 records; after removing 39 duplicates, screening, and eligibility assessment, 46 studies (published 2019–2026) were synthesised thematically. Results: Four patterns emerge. First, process-efficiency benefits (speed, errors, cost) are reported most consistently, but mostly in narrative reviews and perception studies. Second, improvements in decision quality are conditional on information quality and analytical capability. Third, effects on financial performance are mixed, delayed, and partly nonlinear. Fourth, risks (cyber and privacy, model bias and explainability, compliance, and organisational readiness) arise from the same technologies that deliver the benefits. Novelty: Primary firm-level evidence remains scarce, and topical and geographical imbalances are evident. The article proposes a value chain of technology, process, information, decision, and performance, together with five testable propositions.
venue: AL-IMAM: Journal on Islamic Studies, Civilization and Learning Societies

title: Machine learning and physical model derived Sentinel-2 vegetation indices for estimation of leaf area index: an approach to address optical data gaps
abstract: Accurate estimation of leaf area index (LAI) plays a crucial role in assessing crop growth and agricultural productivity. Sentinel-2 optical imagery enables accurate LAI estimation through vegetation indices (VIs), but its temporal availability is often limited by cloud cover and adverse weather, causing gaps in data availability. To overcome this limitation, this study proposes estimating Sentinel-2 VIs from Sentinel-1 synthetic aperture radar (SAR) data using machine learning methods. Our results indicate that while VIs obtained from Sentinel-2 data offer the highest accuracy in LAI prediction (R2 up to 0.88), VIs estimated from Sentinel-1 SAR parameters also perform well (R2 of up to 0.85), demonstrating their reliability when optical data are unavailable. In addition, LAI can be estimated without Sentinel-2 data by employing physically based approaches such as radiative transfer models. By integrating physically based model (PROSAIL) with machine learning algorithms, a hybrid framework is developed that improved prediction accuracy compared with the physical model alone, achieving R2 values up to 0.82, highlighting the effectiveness of this approach. The key contribution of this study is the synergistic use of Sentinel-1 SAR data for machine learning-based estimation of Sentinel-2 VIs and hybrid modeling to enable consistent and reliable LAI monitoring under limited optical…

title: An Overview and Applications of Uncertainty Quantification
abstract: The analysis and decision-making of scientific data and models have become increasingly important with the progress of data science, artificial intelligence, and computing. Although such analyses draw on available data, limited samples, measurement errors, missing data, and model assumptions all affect the results. In addition, many complex systems are inherently random. Therefore, in addition to prediction of a subject under study by a model, the uncertainty in the prediction must be studied. Uncertainty quantification (UQ) uses probability theory, statistics, and computational methods to study the sources of uncertainty and their magnitudes, and to study the effects of uncertainty in model results. This paper discusses sources of uncertainty in data, models, and randomness; uses confidence intervals, probability distributions, Bayesian methods, and Monte Carlo methods for UQ; and presents applications of these methods in healthcare, climate science, and artificial intelligence. UQ does not aim to make unknowns vanish; it makes model results more credible by describing the uncertainties in the results.

The impact of firms’ perception of economic policy uncertainty on inefficient investment decisions: evidence from China
abstract: Purpose Considering that economic policy uncertainty (EPU) may influence corporate investment decisions, this study aims to investigate the effect of perceived EPU on corporate inefficient investment and systematically examines the transmission mechanisms underlying this relationship. Design/methodology/approach Using textual analysis and empirical analysis methodologies, this study investigates how perceptions of EPU influence corporate inefficient investment and elucidates the underlying mechanisms. Findings The findings reveal that managerial overconfidence and agency problems play mediating roles in the relationship between perceived EPU and corporate inefficient investment. Specifically, perceived EPU mitigates inefficient investment by alleviating managerial overconfidence and agency conflicts. Further analysis demonstrates that the inhibitory effect of perceived EPU on inefficient investment is more pronounced in firms located in eastern areas of China. Originality/value This paper contributes to the existing literature in two aspects. First, from the perspective of firms’ perceived economic policy uncertainty, the authors extend the literature on the inefficient investment of enterprises. Second, while previous studies on the drivers of corporate inefficient investment have primarily focused on broad internal and external factors, this study delves into the mediating ro…

title: From Shastra to Storefront: A Critical Review of Classical Ayurvedic Sweets in Comparison with Market-Prepared Sweets
abstract: Background: Sweets have traditionally occupied an important place in Indian dietary, cultural, and religious practices. Ayurveda recognizes Madhura Rasa as nourishing and supportive of tissue development, while emphasizing moderation and individual suitability. In contrast, increasing consumption of commercially prepared sweets, refined sugars, and energy-dense foods, together with sedentary lifestyles, has contributed to the growing burden of obesity, diabetes, and other metabolic disorders. Objective: To review classical Ayurvedic principles of Madhura Rasa and sweet preparation and compare them with contemporary market-prepared sweets, with emphasis on Prakriti, Agni, Prakshepa Dravyas, and metabolic health. Methods: A structured literature review informed by PRISMA 2020 was conducted. Classical references were identified from Charaka Samhita, Sushruta Samhita, Ashtanga Hridaya, and Bhavaprakasha Nighantu using ESamhita. Contemporary evidence was obtained from scientific journals, research articles, and relevant electronic sources. Fourteen references, comprising seven classical Ayurvedic and seven contemporary scientific sources, were narratively synthesized. Results: Classical texts describe Madhura Rasa as nourishing and strength-promoting when appropriately consumed, while excessive intake is associated with Kapha and Meda accumulation, Agnimandya, Sthaulya, and Prameha.…
