title: Modeling echo chambers in LLM conversations: a neutrosophic framework for decomposing agreement, diversity and uncertainty
abstract: Introduction Large language models (LLMs) increasingly mediate how people encounter contested political, economic and social information. Existing analyses treat echo-chamber formation as a single, static bias, conflating whether a model agrees with the user, whether it presents one perspective or many, and whether it expresses uncertainty; they also cannot separate a model that reinforces the user's stance from one that counters it. We introduce a neutrosophic framework that decomposes echo formation into these components. The instrument measures conversational echo propensity in assistant output, not downstream belief change, selective exposure, or polarization. Methods Each conversational turn is represented as a triple 〈 T, I, F 〉: perspective Diversity ( T ) and expressed Uncertainty ( I ) as single-valued memberships on [0, 1], and stance Reinforcement F as a bipolar membership on [−1, 1] whose sign separates echo from counter-echo. This yields a closed-form EchoIndex on [−1, 3] with three independently varying additive terms. We apply it to an exploratory baseline over four commercial web products, then in a controlled experiment of 210 conversations and 1,260 turns crossing seven model configurations, three contested topics and two matched system-instruction conditions, with cluster-robust inference and a two-round human validation of 300 and 200 labeled turns. Results …

title: Uncertainty management responses in liminal mid-career transitions
abstract: Purpose Moving beyond viewing career transitions as discrete events, this study explores how mid-career individuals experience and respond to uncertainty during the unfolding, unscripted process of liminality during transitions. Design/methodology/approach Adopting a qualitative approach, 14 semi-structured interviews were conducted with mid-career individuals who navigated a voluntary career transition in the last five years. Findings The findings reveal that liminal phases are shaped by how an individual's agentic enactment (proactive versus reactive) intersects with the orientation of their transition-induced uncertainty (internal self-doubt versus external environment). This highlights distinct patterns of behavioral responses to uncertainty: regulation, receptiveness, resistance and reconstruction. Originality/value This research advances career scholarship by reframing uncertainty not as an inevitable background condition, but as an active phenomenon that must be actively managed during transitions. It provides a novel perspective on how individuals respond to uncertainty in different ways during mid-career transitions, illustrating when proactive mindsets empower individuals and when internal identity limits capacity for agency.

title: Uncertainty in Human–Machine Shared Driving and Takeover Decision-Making
abstract: In human–machine shared driving, takeover decision-making is affected by multi-source uncertainty from the environment, driver, and system. Existing studies lack integration of uncertainty modeling, evaluation, and the takeover process. This paper presents a focused review of recent literature from four aspects: uncertainty types, modeling methods, takeover decision-making process, and evaluation frameworks. It summarizes four sources of uncertainty: environment and perception, driver state, system and interaction, and situation. Modeling methods are grouped into probabilistic and Bayesian modeling, learning-based uncertainty quantification, cognitive modeling, and decision-theoretic methods. Research progress on pre-takeover risk prediction, takeover request timing, authority allocation, and trust calibration is reviewed. Current limitations include inconsistent evaluation metrics, poor cross-scenario generalization, and constraints on real-time deployment and explainability. Future work should strengthen multi-source fusion and online updating, human-adaptive takeover support, and standardized evaluation to improve the safety and timeliness of takeover decisions.

title: Optimization of aqueous extraction and antioxidant activities of crude polysaccharides from Hippophae rhamnoides L. fruit: protection against oxidative stress in Caenorhabditis elegans
abstract: Introduction Oxidative stress is a key contributor to chronic disease and aging, and natural antioxidants from edible plants are of growing interest as dietary protective agents. Hippophae rhamnoides L. (sea buckthorn) is a medicinal and edible plant rich in bioactive compounds, and its polysaccharide-enriched fractions have been reported to possess antioxidant properties. However, the extraction conditions and the in vivo antioxidant effects of these fractions remain insufficiently characterized. Methods The present work therefore optimized the aqueous extraction of a crude polysaccharide-enriched extract (HRPs) from sea buckthorn fruits and evaluated its antioxidant and oxidative-stress-protective potentials. Extraction conditions were first screened through single-factor tests, after which a three-level Box–Behnken design integrated with response surface methodology (RSM) was applied for further optimization. Results Under the optimized parameters (47 °C, 18.18 mL/g, 1.50 h), the polysaccharide yield reached 12.30%, consistent with the predicted value of 12.31%. The crude extract (HRPs) scavenged hydroxyl, superoxide, DPPH, and ABTS radicals in a concentration-dependent manner, though the effects were weaker than those of ascorbic acid ( p < 0.05). Optimization of Transparency and Accountability Structures in Algorithm-Driven Public Governance
abstract: Governance by algorithm is widely applied in the public sector for the purposes of distributing welfare, estimating administrative risks, regulating urban behavior, rationing public services, and enabling automated decisions. However, transparency and accountability mechanisms are often scattered in the technical, legal, and organizational dimensions. In this work, we present an empirical-computational approach to improving transparency and accountability designs within algorithmic governance architectures in the public sector. We construct a governance assessment dataset based on policy guidance, procurement requirements, data inventories, model cards, decision logs, explanation logs, appeal decisions, audits, and stakeholder review annotations. Our methodology combines natural language processing, rule-based compliance coding, accountability graph construction, supervised classification, risk scoring, and intervention simulation. Using PostgreSQL, Elasticsearch, Doccano, Neo4j, NetworkX, XGBoost, LightGBM, Optuna, and PyGAD, we analyze measures of disclosure completeness, explanation quality, procedure traceability, responsibility path consistency, appeal availability, correction timeliness, and audit resolution efficiency. We show that structural interventions increase the transparency completeness score from 0.642 ± 0.071 to 0.813 ± 0.058 (p < .001) and decrease the aggrega…

Structural optimization design of Sorting Robots Based on dynamic modeling and Genghis Khan Shark Algorithm
abstract: Introduction To address the lack of collaborative optimization of structural parameters and dynamic responses in a four-finger cable-driven sorting robot, a structural parameter optimization model based on dynamic modeling and the Genghis Khan shark algorithm is proposed. Methods A rigid-flexible coupled dynamic model is established using Lagrange’s equation of the second kind, explicitly depicting joint flexibility and rope-wheel transmission coupling. An adaptive Lévy flight perturbation mechanism is introduced to improve the global optimization ability of the Genghis Khan shark algorithm, forming a closed-loop optimization framework integrating modeling, solution, and feedback. Results The method has an inference time of only 48.62 m, with computational load controlled at 312.47 MFlops. The root mean square values of joint driving torques are as low as 8.93 N m. Maximum structural deformation is 0.32-0.41 mm, and maximum equivalent stress is 112.4-128.6 MPa, meeting aluminum alloy strength constraints. The fitness improvement rate reaches 46.5%-51.2%, and total hand mass is 2.75-2.96 kg. Discussion The proposed method effectively solves the coupling optimization problem between structural parameters and dynamic responses through the collaborative mechanism of dynamic modeling and the improved Genghis Khan shark algorithm, providing key technical support for robot structural …

title: FYN-associated NF-κB signaling in microglial pro-inflammatory activation following traumatic brain injury: an integrated single-nucleus transcriptomic and Mendelian randomization study
abstract: Objective Traumatic brain injury (TBI) induces secondary neuroinflammation characterized by pro-inflammatory microglial activation, but the molecular regulators involved in this process remain incompletely understood. Methods Two human single-nucleus RNA sequencing datasets and FinnGen R11 GWAS data were integrated using pseudobulk differential expression analysis and two-sample Mendelian randomization (MR) to prioritize microglia-associated candidate genes related to TBI. Functional validation was performed in LPS/IFN-γ-stimulated BV2 microglial cells using FYN-targeted siRNA, followed by Western blotting, ELISA, and immunofluorescence analyses. In vivo validation was further performed in a mouse TBI model to assess FYN-associated signaling and inflammatory responses. Results FYN was prioritized as a candidate gene based on its upregulation in TBI microglia and suggestive genetic evidence from MR. FYN knockdown reduced the expression of pro-inflammatory activation-associated markers (iNOS and CD86) and decreased the secretion of TNF-α, IL-1β, and IL-6. Time-course experiments showed that FYN phosphorylation preceded NF-κB p65 activation, while FYN knockdown reduced NF-κB p65 phosphorylation and nuclear translocation. In vivo experiments further showed alterations in FYN-associated signaling after TBI, accompanied by increased inflammatory responses and neurological impairment;…

Socio-Economic Assessment and Constraint Analysis of Hybrid Rice Growers under Conventional and System of Rice Intensification (SRI) Methods in Prayagraj, Uttar Pradesh, India
abstract: The present study was undertaken to assess the socio-economic characteristics, adoption pattern and major constraints faced by hybrid rice growers following conventional and System of Rice Intensification (SRI) methods. The study was based on primary data collected from individual hybrid rice cultivators in Prayagraj district of Uttar Pradesh during 2018–19. The socio-economic characteristics of the respondents were analysed in terms of age, education, farm size, farming experience, income, access to institutional credit, extension contact and other relevant factors influencing their decision-making and adoption of improved rice production practices. The level of adoption of major components of SRI and conventional rice cultivation was assessed, and the constraints perceived by farmers were identified and prioritised using a suitable graded-ranking technique. The findings indicated that socio-economic conditions played an important role in farmers’ decision-making, resource allocation and adoption of innovative rice production practices such as SRI. The SRI method was perceived as a resource-efficient approach owing to its potential for improved water management, efficient utilisation of farm inputs and enhanced productivity and farm income. However, farmers reported several constraints, including inadequate technical knowledge, higher labour requirements, difficulty in maintai…

title: Machine learning-integrated immunoinflammatory profiling facilitates diagnostic risk stratification for systemic lupus erythematosus
abstract: Purpose Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) often presents with significant phenotypic overlap with other autoimmune conditions, complicating accurate differential diagnosis. To address this clinical challenge, we developed a computational architecture integrating immunoinflammatory biomarkers to facilitate objective diagnostic risk stratification for SLE among symptomatic patients. Methods A retrospective observational framework was adopted, encompassing 1,950 individuals partitioned into 1,000 definitive lupus cases and 950 symptomatic non-SLE controls. To extract core distinguishing indicators, a bipartite screening methodology merging LASSO techniques with Boruta random forest evaluations was deployed. This isolated seven essential molecular targets: antinuclear antibodies (ANA), C-reactive protein (CRP), interferon-gamma inducible protein 10 (IP-10), tumor necrosis factor-alpha (TNF-α), interleukin-6 (IL-6), B-cell activating factor (BAFF), and anti-double-stranded DNA (anti-dsDNA). Among seven rigorously evaluated machine learning algorithms, logistic regression was selected as the primary diagnostic model due to its optimal balance of predictive robustness and interpretability in the internal validation cohort. This algorithm was translated into a graphical scoring index. Furthermore, to address potential incorporation bias, an autoantibody-independent cytokine-only panel…

REQUIREMENTS FOR DEVELOPING THE PERFORMANCE OF A SUSTAINABLE SYSTEM TO INCREASE WHEAT CROP PRODUCTIVITY
abstract: This study identified the requirements for improving the system through which modern agricultural technologies are disseminated to support sustainable increases in wheat productivity in selected provinces of central Iraq. A descriptive-analytical design was used. Data were collected by questionnaire from a stratified random sample of 274 agricultural extension workers drawn from a population of 950 employees in Baghdad, Wasit, Babil, and Karbala. The instrument contained 77 items covering five domains: planning and implementation, management, financing, research and development, and agricultural media. Respondents rated the overall requirements as high (weighted mean = 3.87). Agricultural media received the highest domain mean (3.92), followed by management (3.91), planning and implementation (3.89), financing (3.86), and research and development (3.79). The findings point to practical priorities that include systematic media planning, continuing administrative training, stable financing arrangements, stronger coordination among institutions, and greater support for research and development. Addressing these priorities may improve the capacity of the extension system to deliver relevant technologies to wheat producers.

title: Advances in the Application of Integrated PET/MRI in the Diagnosis and Treatment of Brain Tumors
abstract: Integrated PET/MRI possesses three core technical characteristics: simultaneous multimodal acquisition, complementary anatomical and metabolic information, and low ionizing radiation. It has outstanding clinical value in the precise diagnosis and treatment of brain tumors throughout the whole clinical pathway. This paper systematically reviews recent clinical studies on integrated PET/MRI and summarizes its application value in four major clinical scenarios for brain tumors: (1) Diagnosis and grading: combining tumor metabolic activity with fine anatomical morphology, the overall diagnostic accuracy reaches 92%; (2) Differentiation between recurrence and radiation necrosis: combined interpretation of multiple parameters achieves a diagnostic accuracy as high as 95%; (3) Planning of surgery and radiotherapy: accurate delineation of the Biological Target Volume (BTV), raising the postoperative neurological function preservation rate by 40% for patients with gliomas located in functional areas; (4) Dynamic therapeutic response monitoring: using a reduction of maximum standardized uptake value (SUVmax) greater than 40% combined with changes in the Apparent Diffusion Coefficient (ADC) as evaluation indicators, early treatment response can be detected 2 to 3 weeks earlier than conventional morphological MRI. At present, the popularization of this technology is restricted by high cost…

title: The Comparison of Multi-Armed-Bandit Algorithms in Movie Recommendation Systems
abstract: With the development of information technology, especially the Internet, people are rapidly moving from the era of information scarcity to the era of information overload. Recommendation systems have thus rapidly developed, which aims to find the optimization of the experience for users. The Multi-Armed-Bandit (MAB) algorithms belong to the category of reinforcement learning , always trying to optimize the balance between exploration and exploitation trade-offs. This fundamental principle successfully coincides the application of recommendation systems. By using a large number of real user ratings of movies as the data-set, this paper compares the performances of various MAB algorithms, ε-greedy, Explore-Then-Commit (ETC), Upper Confidence Bound (UCB), Asymptotically optimal UCB and Thompson Sampling (TS) in the movie recommendation system. Through the performance of different algorithms on the same data, it is concluded that the TS algorithm performs relatively optimally in improving the efficiency of the system. Since the basic principle of TS algorithm utilizes Bayesian inference, the balance of each selection trade-off can more probably be better than other algorithms. TS algorithm has a strong flexibility and can perform a better balance when facing different environments. In addition, the methodological framework of this paper can be drawn upon in more complex scenarios a…

title: Posthuman Engagements in Multi-Registered Writing
abstract: Abstract In this article, I analyze a spoken-word artistic engagement as a polyphonic piece of writing that exemplifies posthuman methods and their potential to create lived theory beyond the conventional constraints of academic work. The piece in question centers a story of migration and poses provocations on lived diasporic and queer experiences, engaging a method of fragmentation as a critical response to narrative homogenization. The posthuman methods in this paper trouble a singular understanding of authorial voice, rather foregrounding a polyphonous ensemble. The call-and-response format that takes place on the page and in the oral reading incorporated audio recordings, leaving/making space for silence, tears, rain, ocean, waves. This methodology links intertextual references and lived realities to form the polyphonous effect of movement, symphony, and debordering across space and time. The analysis of my creative piece shows how the inclusion of the non-human – in this case, water – decenters hegemonic human theorizing, moving instead towards posthumanist knowledge-making alongside embodied feminist and Indigenous epistemologies. As legacies of historical oppression perpetuate ongoing epistemic harms that delegitimize lineages of knowing, multiplicity and multi-registered writing offer methods for not only creative praxis but also academic writing as we seek to dismantle…

title: Multi-Factor Monte Carlo Actuarial Simulation and Financial Early Warning Research on the Cash Flow Risk of Real Estate Enterprises by Ownership Type
abstract: China's property market has undergone profound industrial restructuring in recent years. Against the background of continuous industry downturn, real estate developers with different ownership types have demonstrated notable divergence in their capacity to withstand external liquidity shocks. Traditional static financial early warning approaches often fail to capture dynamic volatility and tail risks faced by property firms. This study selects a sample of 87 A share listed real estate firms spanning 2018 to 2023. It separately calibrates four stochastic factors, including sales growth, financing cost, construction cost growth and debt maturity ratio for state owned, private and mixed ownership enterprises. A multi factor Monte Carlo cash flow risk model with 100 000 simulation paths is constructed to estimate the three year default probability, expected cash flow gap and 95% conditional tail expectation (CTE). The empirical results reveal that private developers suffer prominent default risks and severe tail losses, whereas mixed ownership enterprises maintain the most stable cash flow performance. By identifying the heterogeneity of corporate cash flow risks via simulation techniques, this research provides quantitative references for financial institution credit decisions, industry oriented regulation and internal liquidity management of real estate firms.

title: Histotripsy as salvage locoregional therapy for locally advanced, previously unresectable pancreatic adenocarcinoma following multi-modality treatment failure: case report
abstract: We present a case of locally advanced pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma following multi-modality treatment failure, where histotripsy was used as a salvage therapy that was followed by durable disease control. Locally advanced pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma that progresses despite systemic chemotherapy and radiation carries a poor prognosis and few locoregional treatment options, particularly once cumulative radiation dose to adjacent structures inhibits further irradiation. Histotripsy is a non-thermal, non-ionizing focused-ultrasound technique that mechanically ablates tissue through acoustic cavitation, without ionizing dose, heat, or surgical access. In this case, the patient is a 49-year-old male with locally advanced, unresectable pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma whose disease progressed through multiple lines of systemic therapy, two courses of radiation including ablative SBRT, and irreversible electroporation which was complicated by life-threatening hemorrhage. He underwent histotripsy as a salvage locoregional therapy, performed in an outpatient setting with prompt resumption of anticoagulation and systemic therapy. Following histotripsy and resumption of chemotherapy, serial imaging showed declining metabolic activity and regression of the histotripsy treatment zone with no new mass at the treated site, and durable local control at 16 months. This case illustrates …

title: Multi-omics data resource of pancreatic islet and β cell responses to pro-inflammatory cytokines
abstract: Abstract In type 1 diabetes (T1D), autoimmune responses and inflammation cause the death of pancreatic β cells, leading to the body’s inability to produce insulin and maintain glucose homeostasis. This process is at least in part mediated by pro-inflammatory cytokines, such as interferon (IFN)α, IFNγ, interleukin (IL)-1β, and tumor necrosis factor (TNF)α, which induce β-cell dysfunction and apoptosis. A deep understanding of the β-cell signaling and regulatory networks induced by these cytokines could lead to the identification of therapeutic targets to prevent T1D development. To study cytokine-mediated islets/β-cell signaling and regulatory networks, a variety of omics experiments have been conducted, including transcriptomics, epigenomics (DNA methylation, UMI-4C, ATAC-seq and ChIP-seq), proteomics (bottom-up, top-down, post-translational modification analysis), lipidomics, and metabolomics. The combination of these datasets can be instrumental in identifying signaling components and regulatory factors involved in β-cell stress/death. Here, we aggregated 70 (multi-)omics datasets from 23 studies spanning 14 years into a centralized location, providing a comprehensive resource for investigators seeking to reuse data to holistically study the impact of pro-inflammatory cytokines on β cells.

title: A multi-scale cross aggregation network for joint denoising and super-resolution of low-dose CT images
abstract: Introduction Low-dose computed tomography (LDCT) reduces radiation exposure but often introduces signal-dependent noise and spatially varying streak artifacts that obscure subtle anatomical structures. Existing restoration methods struggle to suppress these degradations while maintaining long-range anatomical consistency and recovering high-frequency details. To address these challenges, we propose MSCANet, a Multi-Scale Cross Aggregation Network for joint LDCT denoising and super-resolution. Methods MSCANet integrates three complementary components. The Token Fusion and Aggregation Block combines global structural context and local texture information through prototype-guided feature aggregation. Region-Aware Self-Attention models local contextual relationships with overlapping receptive fields, while the Multi-Scale Deformable Attention Module employs learnable sampling offsets to characterize irregular structures and spatially varying artifacts. We evaluated MSCANet on the public 3D-IRCADB and PANCREAS datasets at × 2 and × 4 scaling factors and compared it with nine representative image-restoration methods. An additional qualitative evaluation was conducted on a self-collected clinical CT dataset comprising 2,544 slices from 17 patients. Reconstruction quality was assessed using peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR), structural similarity index measure (SSIM), contrast-to-noise…

Digital leadership and corporate performance in tourism SMEs: a multi-mediator perspective
abstract: Purpose This research investigates the association between digital leadership and corporate performance among tourism small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs), considering organizational learning, digital talent and digital strategy as mediating capabilities. Based on dynamic capabilities theory (DCT) and the resource-based view (RBV), digital leadership is regarded as a higher-order capability linked to the development and coordination of these three capabilities. Design/methodology/approach Survey data were collected from 493 senior managers and supervisory-level employees working in SME travel agencies. Partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) was employed to evaluate the proposed multiple-mediator model. Findings Positive associations were identified between digital leadership and corporate performance, organizational learning, digital talent and digital strategy. The three organizational capabilities were also positively related to corporate performance, with each exhibiting a partial mediating role in the digital leadership–performance association. Practical implications The results suggest that tourism SMEs should prioritize the development of digital leadership. Managerial efforts should also emphasize ongoing organizational learning, digital talent development and an aligned digital strategy to coordinate digital transformation and support organiza…

title: Multi-Axis Design of Asymmetric Bilayer Nanocomposite PolyHIPEs for Interface Tissue Engineering
abstract: Abstract Spatially distinct requirements at tissue interfaces motivate scaffold designs that integrate regional differences into a single construct. Here, an asymmetric bilayer polymerized high internal phase emulsion (PolyHIPE) membrane was developed from photo-cross-linkable four-arm polycaprolactone methacrylate (4PCLMA) using coordinated molecular, formulation, and processing variables. The high-methacrylated network exhibited lower swelling in dichloromethane (133 ± 3% vs 159 ± 7%) and a higher compressive modulus (20.6 ± 4.2 MPa vs 6.6 ± 4.5 MPa) than the low-methacrylated network. For the bone-facing layer, 3 wt % nanohydroxyapatite increased pore diameter from 19 ± 10 to 28 ± 15 μm, compressive modulus from 0.28 ± 0.09 to 0.83 ± 0.24 MPa, and protein adsorption by 1.9-fold, while increasing human mesenchymal stem cell penetration relative to the nanohydroxyapatite-free formulation. For the soft-tissue-facing layer, increasing emulsification speed to 1000 rpm reduced pore diameter to 7 ± 4 μm without significantly altering stiffness. The selected layers differed 4-fold in pore diameter and approximately 14-fold in compressive modulus, with the latter determined over distinct strain intervals corresponding to their respective approximately linear regions. Consecutive casting and simultaneous photo-cross-linking produced a bilayer membrane that conformed to curved surfaces…

title: Adapting Kemp's Model for Research Management Set Up
abstract: What is new? This paper addresses the need to institutionalize research support at SVS Medical College, Mahabubnagar, by establishing a Research Management Unit (RMU) using Kemp’s instructional design model, tackling challenges like limited funding, low faculty research awareness, and administrative hurdles. Its originality lies in adapting an educational model (Kemp’s) to research management, providing a novel framework for medical institutions to enhance research culture and output. What was the approach? The research was conducted at SVS Medical College & Hospital, Telangana, India from January 2023 to August 2024, using Kemp’s nine-step instructional design model adapted for research management. The methodology involved a qualitative approach with stakeholder consultations (one-on-one discussions with 30 faculty heads), free listing, and pile sorting analyzed via Visual Anthropac software to identify challenges and solutions. Faculty feedback was collected using a five-point Likert scale questionnaire from 30 faculty members. Data sources included stakeholder responses, cognitive maps, and performance metrics like grant success rates and publication counts. What is the academic impact? The findings revealed key challenges in RMU establishment, including lack of research awareness, poor communication, low motivation, and negative perceptions, addressed through orientation wo…

A Review of Research on the Relationship Between Low Interest Rates, Financial Innovation, and Real Estate Bubbles
abstract: After the burst of the Internet bubble in 2000, the Federal Reserve reduced the federal funds rate to 1 % and maintained it for several years. At the same time, financial liberalization and asset securitization were spread around the world. Many economies accumulated real estate bubbles and eventually triggered a serious financial crisis. This paper is mainly based on literature review and supplemented by case comparison. Firstly, it combs the theoretical path of low interest rate and financial innovation affecting the real estate market, and then compares the two types of empirical research that support and question the "low interest rate fueling bubble". Then, taking the US subprime mortgage crisis as an example, it compares the macro indicators and cross-border capital flows during the bubble expansion period and the burst period, and summarizes the regulatory responses of various countries. The analysis shows that loose monetary policy is only a background condition for the formation of bubbles, not a sufficient condition; in the stage of crisis escalation, the lack of supervision and the role of cross-border capital flows are more critical. Incorporating these two opposing views into the analytical framework will help regulators better identify asset bubbles and coordinate monetary policy with macro-prudential tools.

title: Strategies for Enhancing Digital Financial Services Adoption to Strengthen Womenpreneur Competitiveness in Indonesia
abstract: The adoption of Digital Financial Services (DFS) in today’s era is a key factor in enhancing the competitiveness of Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs). However, the digital divide remains a challenge, particularly for women entrepreneurs in Indonesia, who face barriers in accessing, understanding, and optimally utilizing digital financial services. This study aims to formulate strategies to increase DFS adoption among women entrepreneurs to strengthen their business competitiveness in the digital era. This study employs a qualitative methodological approach by gathering information from stakeholders involved in the development of women entrepreneurs in Indonesia through in-depth interviews and case studies. The theoretical framework used includes the theory of innovation diffusion, the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM), and digital financial services. The research findings are expected to provide strategic recommendations for women entrepreneurs, the government, digital financial service providers, and other stakeholders in developing policies and initiatives that promote digital financial inclusion. Thus, this research contributes to enhancing the competitiveness of women entrepreneurs in Indonesia, accelerating the digital transformation of SMEs, and supporting more inclusive and sustainable economic growth.

title: Cost of Keeping Up: How Digital Lifestyle Comparisons Shift the Financial Rationality of Management Students
abstract: Abstract. The development of social media has changed how students compare themselves with others and make financial decisions. This study examines the effect of social comparison through social media on students’ financial rationality, directly and indirectly through consumptive behavior. Data were collected online and screened to include active students only. A quantitative explanatory approach was applied to 142 active students using a four-point Likert questionnaire (all items valid; Cronbach’s alpha 0.788–0.852), and mediation was tested with PROCESS Macro Model 4 (5,000 bootstrap samples). Social comparison positively affected consumptive behavior (B = 0.750, p < 0.001) and had a significant negative total effect on financial rationality (B = −0.493, p < 0.001). The direct effect (p = 0.050) and the effect of consumptive behavior (p = 0.058) were at the margin of significance, and the indirect effect was not significant (B = −0.218; 95% CI [−0.456, 0.001]). Consumptive behavior has therefore not been shown to mediate this relationship. The findings highlight the need for financial education that raises students’ awareness of digital lifestyle comparison. Abstrak. title: Graph-Based Financial Fraud Detection: A Property-Centric Survey of Static, Temporal, Cycle-Aware, and Generative Methods and Their Evaluation
abstract: Financial fraud is increasingly coordinated across multiple accounts and transactions, meaning that its evidence often lies in relationships between accounts, the sequence of events, and, in schemes such as money laundering and wash trading, closed loops of transfers rather than in individual records. This review examines graph-based methods for detecting such fraud, covering static and temporal graph neural networks, graph anomaly detection, cycle- and motif-aware methods, generative models, and the evaluation practices used to assess them. The review draws on 147 sources identified through a documented literature search protocol. Four findings emerge. First, no single method family performs best under all conditions: tree-based models remain highly competitive on feature-rich datasets, whereas graph-based and temporal models offer greater advantages when discriminative signals reside in relational structures or transaction sequences. Second, detecting cyclic laundering is fundamentally a representational problem: standard message-passing architectures have limited ability to capture cycle structures, while recent performance gains have been associated with representations that preserve the directed multigraph structure of transactions rather than simply increasing model complexity. Third, evaluation practices, including temporal leakage and threshold selection using test data…

title: “Then She Could Work as a Housewife”: Gendered Impoliteness and Institutional Distrust in Far-Right Online Discourse
abstract: Abstract This study examines online verbal attacks directed at a female judge during her nomination to Germany’s Federal Constitutional Court. Utilizing linguistic impoliteness models and critical discourse analysis, the paper analyses 3,173 YouTube comments from a highly engaged video. Findings reveal that attacks were driven by gendered delegitimization, focusing on accusations of intellectual inadequacy, moral unfitness, and failure to adhere to traditional gender roles. Additionally, anti-abortion discourse served as a primary moralizing frame to challenge the judge’s suitability. The analysis suggests these attacks mirror global far-right discourses concerning gender, morality, and institutional distrust. Ultimately, the study demonstrates how online impoliteness transforms legal disagreement into gender-based moral condemnation. By highlighting the systematic delegitimization of women in institutional authority, the research reveals how digital discourse reproduces gender inequality and contributes to broader processes of democratic erosion in different countries.

title: Maturation of venous inflow to the fetal right heart as reflected by the inferior vena cava reverse-flow fraction: preliminary reference ranges, disappearance of the reverse flow, and measurement repeatability between 18 and 39 weeks of gestation — a cross-sectional study
abstract: Abstract Background The atrial reverse flow in the inferior vena cava (IVC) is thought to reflect right ventricular diastolic filling. Most published indices rely on peak velocities, and the integral-based percentage of reverse flow was described in small series relative to forward flow, without one-sided centiles. We aimed to determine preliminary reference ranges for this fraction between 18 and 39 weeks and to assess changes in the frequency of disappearance of the reverse flow with gestational age in fetuses with normal findings at the examination. Methods Retrospective cross-sectional analysis of examinations performed in January–September 2026 by a specialist in fetal ultrasound and echocardiography. Pregnancies with maternal diabetes or hypertension and those with fetal anomalies were excluded. The fraction was defined as the percentage ratio of the velocity–time integral of the atrial reverse flow (A-IVC VTI) to that of forward flow (systolic and early-diastolic waves; IVC VTI). The analysis included 151 singleton pregnancies (18 + 3 to 38 + 6 weeks; one observation per pregnancy). Centiles were estimated by quantile regression with bootstrap confidence intervals; tracing repeatability was assessed on stored recordings. Results The fraction decreased with gestational age (Spearman rho = − 0.557; P < 0.001): median = 17.64 − 0.385 × GA, 90th centile = 23.77 − 0.425 × GA,…

title: Sanctions and financial networks: evidence from MENA CDS and sukuk markets
abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine how economic sanctions are associated with sovereign risk perceptions across selected Middle East and North Africa (MENA) economies, using sovereign credit default swap (CDS) spreads, dynamic models and descriptive financial-network representations. It also tests whether Islamic capital-market conditions, proxied by the Standard & Poor’s MENA Sukuk Index, moderate the sanction–sovereign-risk relationship under geopolitical stress. Design/methodology/approach The analysis combines descriptive distributional evidence, Granger temporal-predictability tests, a dynamic vector autoregressive moving average with exogenous variables/seasonal autoregressive integrated moving average with exogenous variables (SARIMAX) framework, correlation-based network analysis, an explicit Sanction × Sukuk moderation specification and CausalForest double machine learning (DML). The causal forest is conditioned on lagged CDS, the daily Geopolitical Risk (GPR) index, Cboe Volatility Index, Brent oil returns and Sukuk-market variables. Because sanctions are not randomly assigned, causal forest outputs are interpreted as model-based conditional treatment-effect estimates under selection-on-observables rather than as structural causal effects. Implementation of Green Accounting and Its Impact on Corporate Financial Performance in Indonesia: A Systematic Literature Review
abstract: Abstract. The adoption of Green Accounting has emerged as a response to the transition in financial reporting toward fulfilling the Triple Bottom Line principles (Profit, People, Planet). From a management perspective, however, the allocation of environmental costs is often viewed as an operational expense that can suppress short-term profitability—a view reflected in the mixed results found in previous empirical studies. This research aims to provide a comprehensive analysis of the impact of Green Accounting implementation on the financial performance of companies in Indonesia, while also examining the roles of Environmental Performance and Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) as supporting factors. The study employs a Systematic Literature Review (SLR) methodology, following the PRISMA 2020 guidelines, and utilizes a qualitative descriptive analysis approach through thematic synthesis. The findings indicate that, in the short term, the allocation of Green Accounting costs tends to have either no significant effect or a significantly negative effect on financial performance (ROA and ROE) due to the direct burden placed on ongoing operations. Environmental Performance (such as PROPER ratings) serves as an intervening variable, bridging the gap between environmental expenditures and tangible financial benefits, while CSR strengthens corporate legitimacy and reputation among sta…

title: Financial Performance Analysis Based on Vertical-Horizontal Methods and Financial Ratios at PT. Bosowa Berlian Motor Makassar
abstract: Abstract. This study aims to analyze the financial performance of PT Bosowa Berlian Motor Makassar for the 2023–2025 period, utilizing vertical analysis, horizontal analysis, and financial ratios. A descriptive quantitative approach was employed, drawing on secondary data—specifically financial statements—collected through documentation, literature review, and field research. The analysis incorporates liquidity, profitability, and solvency ratios. The findings indicate that the company’s assets are dominated by current assets, primarily vehicle inventory. The funding structure has shown improvement, evidenced by a decline in the debt ratio from 119.30% in 2023 to 96.93% in 2025, alongside a shift in equity from negative to positive. Nevertheless, revenue continued to decline throughout the observation period, and net profit in 2025 remained 0.18% below the 2023 level. While the current ratio rose to 86.40% and the cash ratio to 6.91%, current assets remain insufficient to cover current liabilities. Gross and net profit margins have remained relatively stable, whereas the return on investment fell to 1.41% by 2025. Overall, while the company’s financial performance reflects improvements in its funding structure and liquidity, these gains have not been matched by a proportional increase in revenue or asset productivity. title: From Linear Correlation to Tail Dependence: A Comparison and Selection of Methods for Measuring the Dependence of Financial Assets
abstract: Measures of dependence between financial assets are fundamental to portfolio risk assessment. This paper reviews the literature and summarises the mathematical foundations of Pearson's correlation coefficient, Spearman's rank correlation coefficient and Kendall's τ, highlighting their limitations in characterising non-linear dependence, heavy-tailed distributions and extreme co-movements. Building on Sklar's theorem, it introduces the key properties of copulas, commonly used copula families and tail dependence coefficients, and explains how copulas separate marginal distributions from the dependence structure. A comparison of conventional correlation measures and copula-based models highlights the latter's ability to represent asymmetric dependence and tail behaviour that scalar correlation measures may fail to capture. The paper also examines how correlation-based descriptions relate to copula models under elliptical assumptions. It then delineates the scope and limitations of both approaches, arguing that the choice of dependence measure or model should reflect the specific risk objective, rather than rely solely on statistical fit. Finally, it identifies promising directions for further research, including high-dimensional and time-varying copulas, with a view to improving the assessment of complex and evolving dependence in financial markets.

title: How Entrepreneurial Orientation Improves Financial Performance in SMEs: Insights from the Literature
abstract: This study examines the role of entrepreneurial orientation in improving the financial performance of Small and Medium Enterprises (SMEs) through a systematic literature review. Entrepreneurial orientation has become a strategic factor that enables SMEs to survive and compete in dynamic business environments. This study reviews previous empirical studies related to entrepreneurial orientation dimensions, including innovativeness, proactiveness, risk-taking, competitive aggressiveness, and autonomy, and their influence on SME financial performance. The review follows the PRISMA framework and collects articles from reputable international databases such as Scopus, ScienceDirect, and Emerald. The findings indicate that entrepreneurial orientation positively contributes to financial performance through increased innovation capability, market responsiveness, and competitive advantage. However, several contextual factors such as digital transformation, organizational culture, and environmental uncertainty also influence this relationship. This study contributes theoretically by synthesizing current research trends and practically by providing strategic insights for SME practitioners and policymakers.

title: Influence of LGAs' financial resource factors on the intention to adopt innovative financing instruments – evidence from Tanzanian local government authorities
abstract: Purpose This study surveys the influence of local government authorities’ (LGAs') financial resource factors on the intention to adopt innovative financing instruments among Tanzanian LGAs. Design/methodology/approach The study applies the Technology–Organisation–Environment (TOE) framework and uses a cross-sectional survey design. Data were collected from 255 respondents drawn from 26 Tanzanian LGAs and analysed using partial least squares structural equation modelling with SmartPLS 4. Findings The results show that all five predictors had positive and statistically significant effects on the intention to adopt innovative financing instruments. Budget allocation had a positive and significant effect (β = 0.094, p < 0.001), innovation cost reduction showed the strongest effect (β = 0.402, p < 0.001), organisational size was also significant (β = 0.243, p < 0.001), regulatory framework had a positive and significant effect (β = 0.107, p < 0.001), and top management support also significantly influenced intention (β= 0.296, p < 0.001). The model explained 54.1% of the variance in adoption intention. Research limitations/implications The study extends the application of the TOE framework in a public sector financing context by showing that technological, organisational and environmental factors jointly shape innovation intention among Tanzanian LGAs. However, the st…

title: Strategic Financial Management and Sustainable Corporate Performance Emerging Trends, Challenges and Opportunities in the Digital Economy
abstract: Strategic financial management plays a significant role in determining the financial stability, operational efficiency and long-term sustainability of modern business organisations. In the rapidly changing digital economy, organisations face challenges associated with technological disruption, financial uncertainty, global competition, changing investment patterns and sustainability requirements. Traditional financial management practices are increasingly complemented by digital technologies, data analytics, artificial intelligence and integrated financial planning systems. This conceptual research paper examines the relationship between strategic financial management and sustainable corporate performance, with particular emphasis on emerging trends, challenges and opportunities in the digital economy. The study explores financial planning, investment decisions, capital structure, working capital management, risk management and financial performance evaluation. It also considers how digital transformation and sustainable finance contribute to organisational competitiveness and long-term value creation. The research adopts a descriptive and conceptual approach based on secondary information, existing academic literature and established financial management theories. It develops an integrated conceptual perspective connecting strategic financial decisions, digital capabilities, f…

title: The Mediating Role of Competitive Advantage Between Financial Literacy, Entrepreneurial Orientation, and MSME Business Performance: A Systematic Literature Review
abstract: Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) are central to economic growth in emerging economies, yet their performance remains uneven and contested in the literature. Financial Literacy (FL), Entrepreneurial Orientation (EO), and Competitive Advantage (CA) are among the most frequently examined determinants of Business Performance (BP), but prior findings on the mediation role of CA are inconsistent and rarely integrated within a single FL-EO-CA-BP model. The objective of this study is to synthesize prior empirical evidence on these relationships, identify convergent and divergent patterns, and propose an integrated framework anchored in the Resource- Based View (RBV) and Dynamic Capability Theory (DCT). A Systematic Literature Review (SLR) was conducted on 50 peer-reviewed articles published between 2016 and 2025, retrieved from Scopus, Web of Science, and Google Scholar through structured keyword combinations and screened in three stages: title and abstract screening, full - text assessment, and quality appraisal. The synthesis shows that FL and EO exert predominantly positive effects on BP across diverse emergingeconomy contexts, that CA is consistently supported as an intermediate mechanism translating these antecedents into superior performance, and that divergent findings are largely explained by sectoral, geographical, and measurement differences. The study contributes…

title: DIGITAL PAYMENTS AND CONSUMER BEHAVIOR IN INDIA: ADOPTIODIGITAL PAYMENTS AND CONSUMER BEHAVIOR IN INDIA: ADOPTION, TRUST, FINANCIAL INCLUSION AND SPENDING IMPLICATIONS
abstract: India’s digital payments ecosystem has expanded rapidly, with the Unified Payments Interface (UPI) becoming a central channel for person-to-person and person-to-merchant transactions. Yet transaction growth alone cannot establish whether consumers feel secure, understand payment processes, receive effective support or experience better financial outcomes. This conceptual paper examines the behavioral factors that may influence the adoption and continued use of digital payments in India. Drawing on the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM) and the Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology (UTAUT), it synthesizes five principal drivers—perceived usefulness, Convenience/ease of use, Trust, Digital literacy and Social influence—and considers perceived risk as a potential barrier. It also discusses how low-friction payments may support convenience and recordkeeping while potentially making unplanned spending easier for some consumers. A Consumer-centered conceptual framework and propositions are developed for future empirical testing. The paper uses secondary contextual statistics reported by official sources and does not claim to present original survey data or statistically tested findings. It concludes that sustainable digital-payment adoption should be assessed through continued usage, confidence, accessibility, consumer protection and financial agency, rather than transact…

title: Dashboards and design Sprints: Humanising curriculum architecture at scale through holistic learning design
abstract: Managing curriculum transformation at scale to improve the student experience is a complex, systemic challenge. Traditional change efforts typically oscillate between broad institutional mandates and isolated course-level redesigns – leaving academics siloed and learners with fragmented learning pathways (Kumar & Rewari, 2022; McPhail, 2020). Without shared, iterative mechanisms to bridge macro programmatic intent and micro course delivery, universities struggle to deliver cohesive, industry-relevant graduate outcomes (Matthews & Mercer-Mapstone, 2018). This Pecha Kucha presentation demonstrates how a college-based Learning Design team shifted curriculum renewal from siloed, isolated innovation to systemic impact across 32 programs and 158 course redesigns, impacting over 2,000 students. Grounded in the Holistic Learning Design (HLD) framework, the initiative established a human-centered roadmap for scalable institutional practice built on three conditions: Illuminate the landscape: Creating shared visibility of the curriculum by deploying dynamic Power BI dashboards for whole-of-program transparency – enabling program teams to optimise curriculum efficiency, eliminate assessment redundancies, and structurally map graduate capabilities (Barker et al., 2024). Humanise the co-design: Facilitating opportunities for academics to make sense of the curriculum together through structu…

title: Instructional video use and design in tertiary music education: An exploratory survey of students and educators
abstract: Instructional videos are a widely used pedagogical tool within higher education in Australia, yet their use and design in tertiary music education is an area which remains largely unexplored. Given the central role of independent practice in music learning, instructional videos have considerable potential to support student learning beyond the classroom. This paper reports findings from the first phase of a sequential mixed-methods study investigating instructional video use and perceptions of effective instructional video design among tertiary music students and educators. The survey collected responses from 26 tertiary music students and 17 tertiary music educators. The quantitative data was analysed using descriptive statistics and the open text responses were analysed using thematic analysis. Participants identified several characteristics as important for instructional videos: clear explanations, appropriate video length, multimedia representations, and effective organisation. These findings broadly align with established instructional video design research while also highlighting the need for further investigation into music-specific instructional video design considerations. The findings provide an empirical foundation for subsequent interview and experimental phases investigating music-specific instructional video design.

The Learning Design Manifesto: What we value, resist and might build?
abstract: Learning design is increasingly central to higher education, yet practitioners continue to grapple with questions of identity, recognition and collective purpose. Building on previous ASCILITE conversations about professional standards for learning design, this working symposium builds upon previous symposia on this theme to move from questions about what learning designers do to what learning design stands for. Participants will be invited to co-author draft principles for a Learning Design Manifesto, articulating the values, commitments and purposes that should guide the field in a period shaped by generative AI, institutional reform, hybrid education and demands for scalability. Through short provocations based on existing research, guided group work and live synthesis, participants will develop, test and prioritise candidate principles.

title: The cost of trust: Human-centred learning design when the process gets fast
abstract: Designing an undergraduate systems thinking course in 2023 took months. Workshops, whiteboards, an academic drafting offline, iteration, constructive alignment, compliance, and endless box-moving on a digital canvas. One decision shaped the course: the learning designer judged 10 assessment submission points across 12 weeks excessive and argued to reduce them. The academic, who had taught the discipline for years, refused. Systems thinking concepts interlock, and a student who has not grasped one cannot proceed. The checkpoints were not overload; they were scaffolding. The design bent to the discipline, and the disciplinary expert was right. Generative AI could now compress much of that. It can propose a structure, recommend staggered low-stakes checkpoints for interdependent concepts, and draft the content beneath them. It might well have reached that assessment design faster. Learning designers are tempted to insist something irreplaceable is lost. Much of it is not: a considerable portion of that time was drag, and automating drag is a good outcome. The argument here is not that slowness was valuable. What mattered was less visible. Working on unfamiliar material, the learning designer frequently does not understand the subject. This is usually treated as a limitation. It is better understood as an instrument. The designer is an authentic novice, and their confusion is diagn…

title: The Impact of the "Competitive Neutrality" Rule in Regional Trade Agreements on China's State-Owned Enterprise Reform
abstract: As a benchmark of high-standard international economic and trade rules, the Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership (CPTPP) establishes a "competitive neutrality" framework governing state-owned enterprises through non-commercial assistance, transparency, and antitrust provisions. China has formally applied to join the CPTPP, yet its current State-owned enterprise (SOE) governance still lags the agreement's standards. This paper interprets the core provisions of competitive neutrality--including SOE definition, commercial considerations, non-commercial assistance, and transparency--through legal hermeneutics, combining textual and systematic interpretation. It then compares these international norms with domestic texts including but not limited to the Anti-Monopoly Law (2022 amendment) and the Fair Competition Review Regulations, to clarify the alignment benchmark. Through comparative and literature analysis, the paper assesses gaps between CPTPP requirements and China's SOE system and proposes tailored responses, such as building a unified information-disclosure platform, deepening competition-policy-based enforcement, and institutionalizing subsidy transparency. The conclusion holds that joining the CPTPP is not merely a rule game but an opportunity to push SOEs toward law-based, market-oriented transformation.

title: Between risk and reform: Learning designers’ experiences of institutional responses to GenAI in assessment
abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) has prompted universities to reconsider how assessment can remain meaningful, valid and fit for an AI-integrated future. While institutional responses to GenAI are often framed as technical, policy or academic integrity challenges, they are also deeply human organisational change challenges, shaped by competing logics of risk, reform, infrastructure and operational efficiency. Drawing on semi-structured interviews with 11 learning designers (LDs) from six Australian and New Zealand universities, the paper addresses the following research question: How do LDs experience and navigate institutional responses to GenAI in assessment in higher education? The analysis identified five interrelated themes: navigating strategic ambiguity and policy lag; mediating compliance-driven and integrity-focused responses; translating GenAI disruption into assessment reform; bridging AI infrastructure and pedagogical practice; and advocating for educational purpose within operational constraints. The paper contributes to current debates on GenAI and assessment by shifting attention from assessment tasks and technologies to the institutional conditions that shape assessment change. It argues that in addition to policy statements and enterprise AI platforms, sustainable responses to GenAI require coordinated professional development, curriculum governance p…

title: Revealing a multi-zone circumnuclear dust response in UGC 11487 through phase-resolved WISE W1--W2 diagnostics
abstract: Mid-infrared (MIR) flares trace dust reprocessing in obscured tidal disruption event (TDE) candidates, especially when the primary optical or ultraviolet flare is weak, missed, or strongly obscured. We investigate the phase-dependent W1--W2 evolution of the MIR-selected TDE candidate UGC 11487 (WTP14adeqka) and test whether its infrared behavior can be described by a single self-similar MIR response or requires a structured circumnuclear dust response. For the first time, we performed a phase-resolved analysis of the WISE/NEOWISE W1--W2 evolution of UGC 11487 (WTP14adeqka) over 2014--2024. We combined empirical W1--W2 timing, color, and flux diagnostics with phenomenological modeling and axisymmetric dust radiative-transfer calculations driven by hydrodynamically motivated fallback histories. We also constructed an aperture-matched ultraviolet-to-radio spectral energy distribution of the host galaxy. UGC 11487 exhibits a decade-long MIR flare characterized by a delayed and broader W2 response, color hysteresis, and systematic cooling from sim900 K to sim500--600 K. Observed-window positive-fluence centroids give a W2--W1 centroid offset of Δ t_ ̊m cent =224 d, corresponding to an effective differential response scale of 0.188 $, and the integrated IR energy is $(2.9--3.8) pc. The effective infrared luminosity reaches erg s -1 erg. A single fixed-color phenomenological component…

abstract: ABSTRACT This study aims to analyze the effect of earnings characteristics on the Market Value of energy sector companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX) during the 2016–2025 period. This research employs a quantitative approach with a causal associative research design. The study uses secondary data obtained from companies' annual reports and year-end closing stock prices. The sample was selected using purposive sampling, resulting in 687 firm-year observations. Earnings characteristics are classified based on the relationship among Net Income, Cash Flow from Operations, and Total Accruals, which are represented by dummy variables. Data analysis was conducted using the Weighted Least Squares (WLS) regression method with the assistance of IBM SPSS Statistics. The results indicate that earnings characteristics in categories D1 and D2 have negative and statistically significant effects on Market Value compared to the reference category, with regression coefficients of -0.335 (sig. 0.028) and -0.472 (sig. 0.030), respectively. In contrast, Net Income and Cash Flow from Operations have positive and statistically significant effects on Market Value. Simultaneously, all independent variables significantly affect Market Value, with a significance level of less than 0.001. The Adjusted R-squared value of 0.267 indicates that the research model explains 26.7% of the variati…

title: The relationship between Twitter uncertainty measures and stock market returns during the COVID-19 crisis
abstract: Purpose This paper aims to explore how uncertainty captured through social media, particularly Twitter, affects global stock markets during the COVID-19 crisis. It focuses on whether the Twitter economic uncertainty (TEU) and Twitter Market Uncertainty (TMU) indices contain information that helps explain market behaviour in periods of stress. Design/methodology/approach The analysis relies on daily data from January 2007 to May 2023. This paper combines linear and nonlinear Granger causality tests (Diks and Panchenko, 2006) with the BDS nonlinearity test, and a Dynamic Conditional Correlation-Generalized Autoregressive Conditional Heteroskedasticity (DCC-GARCH) connectedness framework is used (Gabauer, 2020) to capture the dynamic transmission of volatility between Twitter-based sentiment indicators and 13 international financial markets. Findings The results highlight strong nonlinear causal effects from Twitter-based uncertainty measures to market returns. TEU and TMU indices appear to drive fluctuations in stock returns, particularly during episodes of heightened uncertainty. The DCC-GARCH analysis shows that TEU-ENG and TEU-USA act as net transmitters of volatility to markets such as Japan, Ukraine, China, Germany and even Bitcoin. Research limitations/implications As the study focuses mainly on the COVID-19 crisis, future research could extend the analysis to other stress …

title: The irrelevant responses and stock liquidity: dual validation evidence from the Chinese stock market using machine learning and large language models
abstract: Purpose As China’s capital market advances toward higher-quality development, the quality of corporate information disclosure and the transparency of managerial communication have become central concerns for investors and regulators. This study examines the relationship between managerial irrelevant responses during site visits and stock liquidity, and further investigates the underlying mechanisms through which such responses affect market liquidity. Design/methodology/approach Drawing on Q&A records from site visits to A-share listed companies in China, this study constructs a quantitative measure of managerial irrelevant responses using machine learning techniques. In addition, online scoring based on a large language model (GPT-4) is introduced as a complementary indicator. Using regression analyses, we estimate the impact of irrelevant responses on stock liquidity and conduct mechanism and subgroup analyses to ensure robustness. Findings We find that managerial irrelevant responses are significantly negatively associated with stock liquidity. Mechanism analyses suggest that increased investor attention to financial issues reflects heightened uncertainty about firms’ future prospects, thereby exacerbating illiquidity. Integrating capacity building, ethical finance and market access for smallholder empowerment: evidence from Tebar Hewan Kurban (THK) programme in Indonesia
abstract: Purpose This study examines the trilogy of community empowerment – an integrated model combining capacity building, ethical profit-sharing finance and guaranteed market access – as implemented through Indonesia’s long-running Tebar Hewan Kurban (THK) programme to enhance economic outcomes among smallholder livestock farmers. Design/methodology/approach A qualitative single-case study examines 28 years of programme experience through semi-structured interviews with 100 partner farmers, 5 farmer group leaders and 3 programme managers, complemented by document analysis and field observations. Resource dependency theory provides the primary analytical framework. Findings Case-study evidence suggests that farmers participating in the integrated THK programme experienced substantial economic improvements. Farmers reported a 269% nominal income increase, livestock mortality reduction from approximately 10 to 2%, and 94% reduced reliance on moneylenders (self-reported). Programme-reported purchasing prices consistently exceeded middleman rates by 14–28%. Five formal propositions extend resource dependency theory into pro-poor agribusiness contexts. Research limitations/implications Single-case design, purposive sampling and absence of a comparison group limit causal inference. Findings should be interpreted as suggestive, theory-building evidence rather than causal impact estimates. Fu…

title: Competitive Advertising and Market Inefficiency in the Dairy Industry: A Dynamic Bargaining Approach Using the Beggar-Thy-Neighbor Index
abstract: Abstract This study examines inefficiencies arising from advertising competition in the dairy industry, with particular emphasis on the dynamics of advertising effects, the presence of negative cross-effects, and the role of coordination mechanisms among firms. The central issue is that advertising, rather than creating net demand, often leads to business-stealing competition and beggar-thy-neighbor effects. To analyze this issue, a dynamic advertising framework is developed that incorporates advertising carryover and saturation. Within this framework, each brand’s advertising has not only a positive direct effect but also a negative effect on its competitors’ demand. The research methodology compares three decision-making scenarios – non-cooperative behavior, complete cooperation, and Nash bargaining – and introduces the Beggar-Thy-Neighbor Intensity Index as a measure of competitive inefficiency. The model is calibrated for two products, milk and cheese, and six leading brands in the Iranian market, and is estimated over the 24-month period from April 2023 to March 2025. The results indicate that, in the milk market, moving from the non-cooperative scenario to complete cooperation increases total advertising by approximately 46 %, while simultaneously reducing the Beggar-Thy-Neighbor Intensity Index from about 2.0 to 1.0; total industry profit increases by approximately 1.2 %…

title: Salmonella risks in wet market poultry systems of Bangladesh: food safety challenges, control gaps, and implications for trade and public health
abstract: Abstract Foodborne Salmonella remains a leading cause of bacterial gastroenteritis globally, and poultry products are consistently identified as a major transmission vehicle. The risk is particularly pronounced in developing countries where informal poultry marketing systems dominate and hygienic processing infrastructure remains limited. In Bangladesh, the rapidly expanding poultry sector plays a critical role in ensuring affordable protein supply and supporting economic livelihoods, yet food safety governance within wet market systems remains a significant challenge. Available evidence indicates that Salmonella contamination occurs throughout the poultry value chain in Bangladesh, with live bird markets (LBMs) serving as major contamination hotspots due to bird aggregation, on-site slaughter, poor sanitation, and lack of cold-chain management. The increasing prevalence of multidrug-resistant (MDR) Salmonella further intensifies the public health burden by increasing the risk of treatment failure and complicating antimicrobial stewardship efforts. Beyond domestic health implications, persistent food safety deficiencies may also limit Bangladesh’s ability to comply with international microbiological standards required for poultry trade, particularly regarding Hazard Analysis and Critical Control Point (HACCP) implementation, traceability, and antimicrobial resistance (AMR) moni…

title: Notified but Hazardous Cosmetics: Examining Gaps in Post-Market Legal Liability
abstract: This study examines the normative gap between the cosmetic notification mechanism, which places initial responsibility on business operators, and the civil liability regime, particularly in cases involving discrepancies in the formulation of mercury-containing cosmetics discovered after the products have obtained notification numbers and entered the market. This study employs normative legal research using statutory, conceptual, and comparative legal approaches to examine the legal framework for consumer protection in Indonesia and functionally compare it with the cosmetic supervision and liability system in South Korea. The novelty of this research lies in positioning post-notification formulation discrepancies in mercury-containing cosmetics as the central issue of legal liability, examining the integration of consumer protection law, technical supervision, and health-related criminal law, and using actual judicial cases as the basis for normative evaluation. The findings indicate that the primary problem does not stem solely from a legal vacuum, but also from the lack of clarity regarding business operators’ obligations to continuously ensure the conformity, safety, and quality of cosmetic formulations after products enter the market. Furthermore, the interaction among the relevant legal regimes remains insufficiently integrated, potentially creating legal uncertainty in det…

title: From meaning to mastery: how psychological climate fosters eco-friendly employees and proactive service stars
abstract: Purpose This study aims to investigate how hotel employees’ psychological climate is associated with two discretionary behaviours: voluntary pro-environmental behaviour (VPEB) and proactive customer service performance (PCSP). The authors developed a moderated mediation model to explain the mediating mechanism of experienced meaningfulness and the moderating role of interdependent self-construal (InterSC) in these relationships. Design/methodology/approach Data were collected in two waves from 603 employees in Macau’s four- and five-star hotels. The hypotheses were tested using PLS-SEM and conditional mediation procedures in SmartPLS 4, supplemented by a hotel-cluster-adjusted path analysis. Findings Experienced meaningfulness mediated the relationships between psychological climate and both VPEB and PCSP. Its effect size was medium for VPEB and small for PCSP. InterSC strengthened these indirect relationships by moderating the relationship between psychological climate and experienced meaningfulness. Practical implications Luxury hotels can simultaneously achieve service and sustainability excellence by fostering a supportive psychological climate. Specifically, management can implement practices that foster meaningfulness while recognising differences in employees’ relational orientations. title: Promotion focus, growth i-deals and service creativity: a regulatory focus perspective
abstract: Purpose Given that content- and timing-based idiosyncratic deals (i-deals) are inherently heterogeneous across employees and contexts, this study shifts attention to motivation-oriented growth i-deals. Drawing on regulatory focus theory (RFT) and the ability–motivation–opportunity (AMO) model, the study seeks to examine the antecedents, outcomes, chain mediating paths and boundary conditions of growth i-deals. Design/methodology/approach Multiwave, multisource and multilevel data were collected from 600 frontline employees in 100 hotel and mall teams in China. A cross-level moderated mediation model was tested using multilevel path analysis in Mplus and 20,000 Monte Carlo simulations. Findings Four key findings have been obtained. First, promotion focus is positively associated with growth i-deals. Second, growth i-deals positively predict three AMO variables (creative self-efficacy, intrinsic motivation and perceived participation opportunity) that further promote service creativity. Third, team-level servant leadership moderates the main effect of promotion focus on growth i-deals. Finally, team-level servant leadership moderates the indirect effects of promotion focus on service creativity via the chain mediation path of growth i-deals and three AMO variables. The main effect and the indirect effects are stronger when team-level servant leadership is high rather than low. Pr…
