title: Design and Development of a WhatsApp Chatbot to Support Alumni Tracer Study Data Collection
abstract: Tracer study is an alumni-tracking activity conducted by higher education institutions to collect information about graduates after they complete their studies. This study aims to design and develop a WhatsApp chatbot to support the collection and management of alumni tracer study data. The development process included problem identification, requirements analysis, system design, implementation, functional testing, and user evaluation. The system supports WhatsApp-based interaction, student identification number (NIM) validation, conversation-history storage, database recording, and data management through an administrator dashboard. Black-box testing was used to examine the main system functions. Evaluation involving 30 alumni produced mean scores of 4.7 for ease of access, 4.8 for response speed, 4.5 for information clarity, and 4.6 for overall satisfaction. Based on the process durations reported in this study, manual data collection took approximately 5–7 days and involved three people, whereas the chatbot-assisted process took no more than one day and involved one administrator. These findings indicate that the application can support structured data collection and provide preliminary evidence of reduced processing time and administrative staffing. More detailed reporting of the evaluation instrument and time-recording procedure is needed before drawing stronger conclusion…

Design and fabrication of a multilevel phase grating via two-photon polymerization lithography for space-division phase-shifting incoherent digital holography
abstract: Abstract Grating-assisted space-division phase-shifting incoherent digital holography (IDH) allows a conventional image sensor to simultaneously record multiple phase-shifted holograms, enabling single-shot acquisition of complex-amplitude information. However, conventional binary grating configurations involve a trade-off between high diffraction efficiency and uniform optical-power distribution among the phase-shifted holograms. To address this issue, we propose a multilevel two-dimensional phase grating that generates four principal diffraction orders with high and nearly equal efficiencies. The phase distribution was optimized via simulated annealing while exploiting the grating’s rotational symmetry and periodicity to reduce computational cost. The calculated total diffraction efficiency of the four principal orders increased from 65.6% for the conventional binary checkerboard grating to 87.2% for the proposed multilevel grating. A 12 mm $$\times $$ 12 mm multilevel surface-relief grating was fabricated via two-photon polymerization lithography, after which a fabrication-aware design approach was introduced based on a spatially uniform bias phase to reduce intensity imbalance from fabrication-induced profile variations. Next, the fabricated grating was incorporated into an IDH system to simultaneously record four phase-shifted self-interference holograms. Finally, a comple…

title: Construction safety assessment for concrete gravity dams in cold regions: integrating DEMATEL-ANP and cloud model
abstract: Purpose The purpose of this study is to address the primary challenges in evaluating the safety status of concrete gravity dam construction. These challenges primarily consist of the complexity of the evaluation index system and the imprecision in describing random and uncertain information. The objective of this paper is to propose a new, integrated, comprehensive evaluation approach to overcome the limitations of traditional evaluation methods in determining indicator importance and handling ambiguous data. Design/methodology/approach This research proposes a comprehensive evaluation method integrating the Decision-Making Trial and Evaluation Laboratory (DEMATEL), Analytic Network Process (ANP) and a cloud model. Initially, a safety evaluation index system is to be established, encompassing human, environmental, management, quality and equipment factors. Second, DEMATEL analyses causal relationships between indicators, while ANP calculates their final weights. In conclusion, the construction safety level is determined using the cloud model’s three-dimensional digital eigenvalues. This approach is empirically evaluated through a case study of the Linhai Reservoir Dam Project in Heilongjiang Province. Findings Empirical research has identified a number of key factors that contribute to the safety of dam construction. These factors include the frequency of supervision, the statu…

title: Reallocating rural land for sustainable livelihoods: the impact of residential land reform on farmers' incomes in China
abstract: Introduction Rural residential land serves as a vital foundation for rural socioeconomic development, and reforming its utilization is crucial for farmers’ livelihoods and sustainable rural development. Methods To systematically evaluate the micro-level welfare effects of this land use transition, particularly the reform of the rural residential land system, this paper treats China’s pilot policy as a quasi-natural experiment. Using county-level panel data and a staggered difference-in-differences method, we assess the policy’s impact on farmers’ income and its underlying mechanisms. Results The results indicate that the reform of the rural residential land system significantly promotes farmers’ income growth. Mechanism tests suggest that this effect is achieved through the optimal allocation of both land and labor resources: first, the spatial optimization of land resources, which promotes the integration of agricultural industries; and second, the reallocation of household labor, which drives labor participation in non-agricultural employment while optimizing agricultural labor efficiency. Furthermore, the transfer of farmland exerts a significant positive moderating effect, amplifying the reform’s role in promoting farmers’ income growth. Discussion However, further analysis reveals disparities in welfare distribution, as the policy has raised urban residents’ incomes to a g…

title: A Potential Breaktrough? Examining the Direction of Agrarian Reform Following the Job Creation Law in Indonesia
abstract: Introduction: The Job Creation Law, as a regulation based on the omnibus law approach, introduces significant changes to Indonesia’s agrarian reform policy. Through new regulatory provisions and institutional arrangements, the law seeks to accelerate land management and improve the welfare of Indonesian citizens. However, several provisions have raised concerns regarding their compatibility with the principles of agrarian reform established under the 1960 Basic Agrarian Law. Purposes of the Research: This study aims to critically examine whether the changes introduced by the Job Creation Law constitute a breakthrough in Indonesia’s agrarian reform policy or risk diverting agrarian reform from its fundamental objectives of equity, justice, and the protection of people’s land rights. Methods of the Research: This study employs a normative legal research method using a statutory and conceptual approach. The research examines relevant laws and regulations, policy provisions, legal concepts, and secondary legal materials to assess the development, potential, and obstacles of agrarian reform following the enactment of the Job Creation Law. Results / Main Findings / Novelty/Originality of the Research: This study employs a normative legal research method using a statutory and conceptual approach. title: Multimodal Optical Anti‐Counterfeiting and Information Storage via Trap Manipulation Strategy in NaGdGeO 4 :Tb 3+ Long Persistent Luminescence Phosphors
abstract: ABSTRACT In response to the growing demand for information security, the development of multimodal optical anti‐counterfeiting and information storage technologies is of paramount importance. In this context, long persistent luminescence (PersL) phosphors have attracted extensive research interest due to their unique luminescent properties. Herein, a series of Tb 3+ ‐doped NaGdGeO 4 PersL phosphors were successfully synthesized and exhibited the typical emission of Tb 3+ . By employing two trap manipulation strategies, namely varying the concentration of the sole luminescent center, Tb 3+ , and introducing volatile Li + ions, the depth and distribution of traps were effectively regulated. This approach not only enabled tunable emission color from blue to green but also significantly prolonged the visually recognizable PersL. The phosphors exhibited versatile luminescent responses under various stimuli, including ultraviolet, x‐ray, heat, mechanical stress, and photostimulation. Based on the unique temporal and thermal dependencies of PersL, dynamic optical anti‐counterfeiting using Morse code patterns was demonstrated, achieving information encryption and decryption. Furthermore, an optical information storage system was constructed, which allows information writing with ultraviolet and reliable reading via either photostimulation or thermal stimulation. The PersL phosphors hav…

title: A Scalable Presodiation Strategy Enabling Dry‐Air‐Processable Hard Carbon Anodes for High Energy Sodium‐Ion Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT Hard carbon (HC) anodes hold promise for sodium‐ion batteries but are plagued by low initial Coulombic efficiency (ICE) stemming from irreversible sodium sequestration. Chemical presodiation offers a direct route to compensate this deficit, yet its translation to high‐loading electrodes is crippled by sluggish mass transport and air sensitivity of the sodiated product, a barrier to scalable manufacturing. Here, we break this impasse by synchronizing acoustic field enhanced transport with in situ interfacial engineering. Ultrasound‐driven microconvection and cavitation overcome diffusion limitations within thick electrodes, delivering ∼100% ICE within one minute, approximately twice as fast as conventional immersion. A five second quenching in sodium difluoro(oxalato)borate constructs a B/F‐rich hybrid interphase that not only passivates the highly reactive sodiated surface against dry‐air degradation, retaining >79% ICE after 6 h exposure, but also selfregulates subsequent solid‐electrolyte interphase evolution, suppressing impedance growth and stabilizing charge transfer kinetics. Practical pouch cells deliver 76% capacity retention over 700 cycles at 0.5 C/1 C and exhibit superior wide‐temperature adaptability from −40°C to 55°C. By resolving the coupled bottlenecks of kinetic inhomogeneity and environmental instability, this work establishes a scalable, dry‐air‐comp…

Extending the Strategy Tripod View to Explain Circular Economy Implementation in SMEs: A Systematic Review
abstract: ABSTRACT This study examines how interorganisational arrangements shape circular economy ( CE ) implementation in small‐ and medium‐sized enterprises (SMEs). Existing research identifies resource‐, institution‐ and industry‐related influences but insufficiently specifies how external arrangements condition their contribution to implementation. We systematically review 139 studies through the strategy tripod view's constituent perspectives and assess the strength of evidence supporting a system‐level extension. We develop circular value system architecture (CVSA), comprising connectivity, coordination locus and participation terms, and distinguish these attributes from resource access, deployment, capability augmentation and focal‐SME coordination burden. Seven proposition groups specify how arrangements may shape implementation across the three strategic paths. Along the resource path, deployment capability conditions the usefulness of external access, while coordination allocation shapes the SME's burden. Along the institutional path, environmental information exchange may condition the pressure–implementation relationship, depending on circular innovation orientation. Along the industry path, weaker bargaining positions may constrain implementation through less favourable participation terms. title: Influence of ROA, Working Capital to Total Asset dan Debt Ratio to Market Book Value in ASEAN Countries
abstract: This study aims to determine the influence of financial performance on the value of non-financial firms in ASEAN countries. In this study, financial performance is proxied by Return on Assets (ROA), the Working Capital to Total Asset, and the Debt Ratio, while firm value is proxied by the Market-to-Book Value (MBV). The data analysis technique employed is multiple linear regression. The study population consists of 223 firms, with a sample of 146 firms. The sampled firms are distributed as follows: 15 from Singapore, 11 from Indonesia, 17 from the Philippines, 33 from Thailand, and 70 from Malaysia. Data collection was conducted using purposive sampling. The results indicate that Return on Assets (ROA) significantly influences the Market-to-Book Value (MBV), as evidenced by a significance value of 0.002 (which is less than 0.05), suggesting a positive impact of ROA on MBV. The Working Capital to Total Assets (WCTA) ratio does not significantly influence the Market-to-Book Value (MBV), with a significance value of 0.757 (greater than 0.05). Similarly, the Debt Ratio does not show a significant influence on MBV, with a significance value of 0.911. The ANOVA significance value is 0.021, indicating that ROA, WCTA, and the Debt Ratio collectively influence the MBV. The R² value is 0.254, meaning that ROA, WCTA, and the Debt Ratio account for 25.4% of the variance in MBV, while the r…

title: Nivel de conocimiento sobre el cuidado de prótesis dentales en adultos del Mercado Municipal 24 de Mayo, Otavalo, Ecuador
abstract: Objetivo: identificar el nivel de conocimiento sobre el cuidado de las prótesis dentales en adultos que acuden al Mercado Municipal 24 de Mayo de Otavalo, Ecuador. Método: estudio cuantitativo, observacional, descriptivo y transversal. En enero de 2025 se aplicó un cuestionario de preguntas cerradas a una muestra no probabilística por conveniencia de 123 adultos. Resultados: el 91,9 % usaba prótesis. El 51,2 % refirió conocer muy poco sobre su cuidado y el 17,9 % lo desconocía. El 73,2 % aseaba la prótesis a diario, el 30,9 % solo acudía al odontólogo ante problemas y el 12,2 % refirió alguna enfermedad atribuida al mal uso. Conclusión: predomina un conocimiento insuficiente sobre el cuidado protésico, lo que justifica acciones educativas y controles periódicos.

Determinants of Market Channel Selection and Intensity of Participation Among Smallholder Chicken Farmers in Machakos County, Kenya
abstract: Chicken contributes to human protein and micronutrient intake, food security, and people’s livelihoods, leading to increasing demand worldwide. However, smallholder farmers often face challenges in choosing optimal markets to sell their chickens, contributing to inefficiencies in market participation and potentially leading to low income. This study examined the determinants of market channel choice and participation intensity among smallholder chicken farming households in Machakos County, Kenya. A multistage sampling technique was used to obtain primary data from 582 chicken farming households. The descriptive statistics showed the choice of village market hotels and restaurants market channel generated the highest returns, although most farmers relied on brokers and farm-gate consumer market channels. The selection equation model results of the multinomial endogenous treatment effect model revealed that age (dy/dx = -0.087, p < 0.01, and dy/dx = 0.108, p < 0.05), education (dy/dx = 0.517, p < 0.01), marketing experience (dy/dx = -0.050, p < 0.05, and dy/dx = 0.158, p < 0.01), flock size, (dy/dx = 0.182, p < 0.05, and dy/dx = 0.365, p < 0.01), hybrid chicken rearing (dy/dx = 0.572, p < 0.01, and dy/dx = 0.684, p < 0.01), group membership (dy/dx = 0.203, p < 0.01, and dy/dx = 0.379, p < 0.05) and use of smartphone (dy/dx = 0.124, p < 0…

title: Techno-economic assessment of commercial wind turbines for electricity generation in Nigeria
abstract: The main aim of the present paper is to examine the wind energy potential, as well as the performance and economic sustainability, based on mean monthly wind speed data collected from the Nigerian Meteorological Agency (NIMET) and previous scientific studies. In this study, the Weibull distribution function is used to analyze the characteristics of the wind resources of 32 locations in Nigeria. Besides, intensity of turbulence, wind power density (WPD), annual energy production (AEP), capacity factor (CF), cost of energy (COE), and payback period (PBP) were evaluated for six commercial Enercon wind turbines (E53/800, E82/2000, E70/2300, E82/2300, E82/3000, and E101/3000). Results showed considerable differences between seasons and across space. Jos and Obudu were found to possess significant wind energy potential, with mean wind speeds above 8.0 m/s and WPD greater than 300 W/m². In contrast, Delta, Edo, Bauchi, and Abia had very low wind energy potentials, having WPDs less than 10 W/m². The seasonal analysis indicated that about 80% of the selected regions had high wind energy potential during the rainy season, resulting in greater energy generation capacity and improved turbine performance. title: Multidimensional Flexibility in Sustainable Urban Logistics: Consumer Acceptance and Market Viability of E-Cargo Delivery
abstract: Abstract Sustainable urban logistics requires innovative solutions that reconcile operational efficiency and economic viability while complying with sustainable mobility requirements. This study investigates the role of multidimensional flexibility in enabling sustainable last-mile urban logistics, with a specific focus on electric cargo bikes used in last-mile urban logistics. Grounded in the Flexible Systems Management perspective, the analysis examines operational, social, and economic dimensions of flexibility, combining consumer perceptions with implications for logistics systems based on data from an online survey of 412 respondents in Italy. The results indicate a positive perception of goods deliveries by electric vehicles and high social acceptance, despite limited direct experience. Environmental benefits, particularly reduced pollution and noise, are widely recognised, especially among younger respondents and women. Regression analysis shows that environmental perception significantly enhances social acceptance, whereas operational barriers reduce it. However, environmental attitudes do not translate into a greater willingness to pay, confirming a persistent attitude–behaviour gap and highlighting that the economic viability of sustainable last-mile logistics cannot rely solely on consumer environmental preferences. Eco-labels emerge as the most effective incentive t…

title: Sectoral Debt-Service Exposure and Corporate Investment Under Global Monetary Tightening: Cross-Country Local Projections and Emerging-Market Financing Benchmarks
abstract: Standard floating-rate transmission models predict that monetary tightening depresses corporate capital formation more steeply in economies entering a hiking cycle with elevated non-financial corporate debt-service ratios and reprices shorter-maturity corporate obligations faster than household mortgages. Combining harmonized quarterly institutional sector accounts and Bank for International Settlements sectoral debt-service panels through mid-2026 with an external emerging-market financing benchmark across all 20 regions of Kazakhstan, we evaluate these predictions over the 2022–2025 tightening cycle. Local projections with country and quarter fixed effects and restricted wild cluster bootstrap inference uncover no statistically distinguishable conditional contraction gradient in real non-financial corporate fixed capital formation across 2021Q4 corporate debt-service exposures: at the four-quarter horizon (N = 206 across 16 economies), the interaction per 100-basis-point quarterly policy-rate increase and one-percentage-point initial exposure is -0.0158 log percentage points (country-clustered SE = 0.1127; wild cluster bootstrap p = 0.8732; inverted bootstrap 95% confidence interval [-0.2796, 0.1940]), remaining -0.0189 (bootstrap p = 0.8412) under full-rank Japan-only seasonal indicators, with 80% minimum detectable effects of 2.59 log percentage points per cross-country sta…

title: Analisis Reaksi Pasar Saham terhadap Pengumuman MSCI Annual Market Classification Review 2026
abstract: Studi ini dilakukan untuk menganalisis reaksi pasar saham terhadap pengumuman MSCI Annual Market Classification Review 2026 melalui volatilitas harga saham, Trading Volume Activity (TVA), dan Net Foreign Inflow (NFI). Penelitian menerapkan pendekatan kuantitatif melalui metode event study terhadap 54 saham konstituen MSCI Indonesia Investable Market Index (IMI). Peristiwa ditetapkan pada 24 Juni 2026 dengan jendela pengamatan lima hari perdagangan sebelum dan sesudah pengumuman. Pengujian dilakukan menggunakan paired-samples t-test dan uji Wilcoxon sesuai karakteristik data. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa volatilitas saham berbeda secara signifikan (p = 0,009) dan meningkat setelah pengumuman. TVA juga menunjukkan perbedaan signifikan (p < 0,001), tetapi mengalami penurunan. Sebaliknya, NFI tidak menunjukkan perbedaan signifikan (p = 0,756), meskipun rata-ratanya menjadi sedikit lebih negatif. Temuan ini menunjukkan bahwa perubahan volatilitas dan aktivitas perdagangan tidak selalu diikuti oleh perubahan transaksi bersih investor asing yang signifikan. Interpretasi hasil perlu mempertimbangkan keterbatasan penelitian, terutama keberadaan FTSE Russell Rebalancing pada 22 Juni 2026 yang berpotensi memengaruhi reaksi pasar selama jendela pengamatan.

title: From Wholesale Fuel Shock to Network-and-Tax Wedge: Industrial Electricity Tariff Component Dispersion and Manufacturing Output in Europe
abstract: When wholesale natural gas and power markets retreat from an acute supply shock, cross-country industrial electricity cost divergence persists as dispersion rotates from traded generation prices toward regulated grid charges and national fiscal wedges. Applying an exact variance–covariance decomposition across all 27 European Union Member States from 2017 to 2025, with semi-annual tax-wedge tracking through the first half of 2026, we document a structural reconfiguration of non-household tariff dispersion across three audited price definitions. In the benchmark medium-scale industrial consumption band (500 to 1,999 MWh annually), the share of cross-country tariff variance attributable to energy and supply costs fell from 57.26% in 2023 to 33.85% in 2025, whereas the regulated network variance share doubled from 6.54% to 13.03% and the net non-recoverable tax variance share reached 22.55%. Across 25 paired Member States in 2025, medium-consumption facilities faced unit network charges 21.85 EUR/MWh above large electro-intensive users alongside an additional 10.98 EUR/MWh net fiscal differential. Combining predetermined 2017–2019 sectoral electricity and gas intensities with a mutually exclusive panel of eight manufacturing divisions across 20 Member States (N = 1,182, 2017–2025) under country-by-sector, country-by-year, and sector-by-year fixed effects, we find a negative condit…

title: Evaluating human-like chatbot interaction in customer service: integrating anthropomorphism and conversational capability
abstract: The development of artificial intelligence (AI)-based technology has driven the development of rule-based chatbots into AI-based chatbots. This development is used by various companies to use AI chatbots as the frontline of customer service. Meeting user expectations for AI chatbots requires an evaluation model to measure chatbot quality. Based on the literature, chatbot evaluation models still focus solely on technical quality, even as AI chatbots are evolving towards human-like services. This research will explore the integration of the technical dimensions of information system success with a new dimension, namely Human-Like Chatbot Interaction (HLCI) as a higher-order construct of anthropomorphism and conversational capability. This quantitative study uses an explanatory research approach. Data were collected through a cross-sectional survey of users of the Veronika chatbot, owned by Telkomsel, an Indonesian telecommunications company. A total of 213 respondents had data ready for analysis using the Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) method in SmartPLS 4, namely the measurement model and structural model tests. The analysis results show that service quality is not significantly related to user satisfaction but has a direct effect on trust. Meanwhile, information quality, system quality, and human-like chatbot interaction are positively related to t…

title: Improving service quality in primary health care: Evidence from first-level health facilities
abstract: The quality of primary health care is a key factor in improving patient satisfaction and strengthening the performance of the health care system. Primary health care facilities play a strategic role as the first point of contact for the public in accessing health care services. This study analyzes improvements in primary health care (PHC) service quality. A scoping review using the Arksey and O’Malley framework was conducted. Eighteen articles from PubMed, ScienceDirect, Google Scholar, and SpringerLink were synthesized, focusing on service quality and patient satisfaction in PHC. Service quality, particularly SERVQUAL dimensions (reliability, responsiveness, assurance, empathy, tangibles), consistently dictates patient satisfaction. Key determinants span interpersonal factors (communication, staff attitudes), systemic elements (access, waiting time, care continuity), and technical quality (clinical competence). Strategies to elevate quality encompass patient-centered care implementation, system reform, service digitization, and staff competency enhancement. Healthcare administrators should prioritize comprehensive capacity-building, integrate digital health technologies, and evaluate systemic workflows to actualize patient-centered care and drive structural reforms. Unlike narrowly focused reviews, this study provides a novel holistic synthesis of interpersonal, technical, and…

title: Crafting the Digital Integrity: Ethical Governance in Service Delivery in the Identified Local Government Units
abstract: This study assessed digital integrity practices and ethical governance in public service delivery in the municipalities of Calubian and Leyte, Leyte, during Calendar Year 2025. It aimed to identify institutional, behavioral, and technological vulnerabilities as a basis for developing a long-term governance framework. Employing a descriptive-evaluative research design, the study gathered quantitative and qualitative data from 60 respondents comprising 10 government leaders, 20 local government employees, and 30 transacting clients. Data were collected through a validated four-point Likert-scale questionnaire and open-ended responses, which were analyzed using descriptive statistics and thematic analysis. Findings showed a high overall level of digital integrity practices, with a composite mean of 2.85. Front-end verification mechanisms (3.28) and transparency of transaction fees on digital platforms (3.42) were notable strengths. However, network downtime (2.22), limited real-time document tracking (2.35), and inadequate automated cloud backups (2.48) exposed critical technological weaknesses. Ethical governance likewise registered a high overall composite mean of 2.94. Honesty and anti-corruption obtained the highest rating (3.33), supported by automated payment systems (3.45) and reduced reliance on fixers (3.38). In contrast, responsiveness to citizen complaints and electroni…

title: Differential Regulation of Climate Modes on the Genesis Positions of Tropical Cyclones in Different Landing Areas
abstract: Abstract Tropical cyclone (TC) genesis positions have undergone marked shifts under climate change, yet the mechanisms driving changes across different landing areas remain unclear. Based on multiple datasets including the best track data from the China Meteorological Administration and ERA5 reanalysis, this study employs an integrated methodological framework to systematically analyze the migration of TC genesis positions and their differential responses to key climate modes across various landing regions along China’s southeastern coast from 1949 to 2024. The results indicate that genesis positions of landfalling TCs have shown a northwestward migration and clustering trend. Notably, this migratory trend is statistically significant for TCs landing along the southern China coast, resulting in a pronounced reduction in both the distance and time from genesis to landfall. El Niño–Southern Oscillation (ENSO), Pacific decadal oscillation (PDO), and Atlantic multidecadal oscillation (AMO) exhibit distinct regulatory effects on TC genesis positions across different landing regions. The AMO acts as the dominant controlling mode for TCs landing along the southern China coast, whereas the ENSO serves as the primary mode for those affecting the eastern coast. The PDO primarily modulates the zonal variation of genesis positions, with a stronger influence observed on TCs landing along th…

Effect of Spring Tibetan Plateau Snow Cover on the Frequency of Intense Tropical Cyclones over the Western North Pacific
abstract: Abstract Tibetan Plateau snow cover (TPSC) is recognized as a critical driver in modulating the regional atmospheric circulation. However, the critical role of TPSC in the frequency of intense tropical cyclones (ITCs) over the western North Pacific (WNP) remains poorly understood. Based on the observed and reanalyzed datasets during 1979–2023, this study reveals a seasonally lagged negative relationship between spring (March–April) TPSC and the frequency of ITCs over the WNP during the following peak season of ITCs (July–November). The analyses suggest that the sustainable hydrological effect of March–April TPSC enhances the upper-level convection heating and, in turn, intensifies the South Asian high until July–November. Then, the Rossby wave trains are excited, inducing a baroclinic structure with an anomalous upper-tropospheric cyclone and a lower-tropospheric anticyclone over the WNP. The resultant changes in the ITC-related dynamic factors, including enhanced vertical wind shear and suppressed midtropospheric vertical motion, create an unfavorable environment for the genesis of ITCs. Meanwhile, the low-level absolute vorticity and midlevel meridional shear of the zonal wind associated with the anomalous large-scale circulation further inhibit the intensification of tropical cyclones (TCs). Here, a physics-based statistical prediction model for the frequency of ITCs over th…

title: A STAT6 p.D419G variant causing severe multi-organ allergic disease: case report on a transformative response with dupilumab
abstract: Abstract Background Signal transducer and activator of transcription 6 (STAT6) gain-of-function (GOF) variants cause severe, early-onset multi-organ allergic disease through IL-4/IL-13-mediated type 2 immunity. We report a patient with a STAT6 p.D419G variant and her remarkable response to targeted therapy. Case presentation A 39-year-old woman of Middle Eastern origin presented with lifelong severe atopic disease beginning before age 2, including treatment-refractory atopic dermatitis, severe asthma requiring intubation, IgE-mediated food allergies, eosinophilic gastrointestinal disease, and recurrent infections. She demonstrated persistently elevated serum IgE (peak 16,000–17,000 KU/L and >5000 KU/L throughout her mid-thirties) and eosinophilia (peak 2.35 × 10⁹/L). Whole exome sequencing identified a heterozygous STAT6 variant (NM_001178079.2) c.1256A>G (p.D419G). Notably, brain MRI revealed vascular malformations in the circle of Willis, including hypoplastic vertebrobasilar arteries and persistent trigeminal artery. She required daily prednisone (average 20 mg) for years, resulting in cataracts and low bone mineral density. At age 34, dupilumab (300 mg subcutaneously every 2 weeks) was initiated, targeting the dysregulated IL-4/IL-13 pathway. Over five years of treatment, she achieved complete corticosteroid cessation, with her Eczema Area and Severity Index declining from …

title: Fruit Quality Response of Red Currant Cultivars to Different Soil Maintenance Systems
abstract: Soil maintenance practices may influence fruit development and quality in perennial crops. However, information regarding the response of red currant cultivars to different soil management systems under Romanian growing conditions remains limited. The study aimed to evaluate the influence of grass-cover and clean soil management on fruit quality of three red currant (Ribes rubrum L.) cultivars: ‘Jonkheer van Tets’, ‘Rovada’ and ‘Detvan’. The experiment was conducted in 2025 at Moara Domnească Experimental Base of the Research and Development Station for Fruit Growing Băneasa. The cultivars were evaluated under two soil maintenance systems: under grass cover (V1) and clean soil (V2). Fruit weight, height, diameter, firmness, soluble solids content (°Brix), pH and titratable acidity were determined. Experimental data were analysed using two-way ANOVA followed by Tukey's HSD test (p < 0.05). Cultivars responded differently to the two soil maintenance systems. The weight of 50 fruits ranged from 24.16 to 35.36 g under grass cover and from 29.09 to 32.86 g in clean soil. ‘Rovada’ recorded the highest fruit weight under grass cover (35.36 g/50 fruits), whereas ‘Detvan’ had higher fruit weight in clean soil. Firmness ranged from 0.26 to 0.42 kg/cm² under grass cover and 0.24 to 0.37 kg/cm² in clean soil. Soluble solids content ranged from 11.1 to 12.0 °Brix and 11.5 to 13.3 °Brix, res…

title: Household Food Demand in Riau Province, Indonesia: A Censored Demand System Approach Including Demographic Effects
abstract: Prices, expenditures, and demographic characteristics influence household food consumption patterns. This study examines household food demand in Riau Province, Indonesia, by estimating expenditure and price elasticities and assessing demographic effects across food groups. Data from 8,246 households in the 2023 National Socioeconomic Survey (SUSENAS), covering 13 food groups, were analyzed using a censored Quadratic Almost Ideal Demand System (QUAIDS) incorporating 18 demographic variables. The results show that expenditure elasticities are positive for all food groups, with FAFH, fruits, and meat showing relatively high responsiveness, while cereals show the lowest responsiveness. Uncompensated own-price elasticities are negative for all food groups, with meat and nuts exhibiting elastic responses. Almost all compensated cross-price and Morishima elasticities are positive, predominantly indicating substitution responses. Demographic characteristics also significantly influence household food demand. Female-headed households show higher tuber consumption than male-headed households, while postgraduate education is associated with higher consumption of eggs & milk, fruit, and FAFH. Food consumption patterns also differ significantly by occupation, marital status, and urban-rural location. These findings suggest that household demographic differences should be considered whe…

title: Response of Tomato to Indole-3 Acetic Acid-Based Bio-Stimulant Application Derived from Shallot Bulbs
abstract: Indole-3-acetic acid is a crucial phytohormone that regulates plant growth and development and is increasingly used as an active ingredient in biostimulants. This study aimed to evaluate the effects of an IAA-based bio-stimulant made from shallot bulbs on the growth, flowering, and yield of tomato (Solanum lycopersicum L.). The experiment used a Randomised Complete Block Design with different shallot bulb extract concentration applied at specific growth stages. Growth parameters, including plant height, and reproductive traits, such as flower cluster formation, fruit number, and yield, were systematically measured. Results indicated that applying shallot bulb extract enhanced vegetative growth compared to untreated plants. Plants treated with a low shallot bulb extract(2.5 mL/L) produced more flower clusters and fruits, leading to a notable increase in total yield. Conversely, higher IAA concentrations tended to suppress growth responses, demonstrating a dose-dependent effect of IAA on tomato physiology. These findings suggest that proper application of IAA-based bio-stimulants can effectively promote tomato growth and productivity. The study underscores the importance of optimising IAA concentration and application strategies to maximise the agronomic benefits of bio-stimulants while avoiding potential inhibitory effects. The results provide a scientific basis for developing s…

title: Design and Evaluation of an Integrated Electronic System for Prescription Management, User–Pharmacy Connectivity, and Drug Inventory Management in Libya
abstract: Reliable medicine searches depend on linking availability information to the stock committed to an order. Roshita was developed and evaluated in Libya to help users find nearby pharmacies with the required medicines and connect their orders to pharmacy inventory management. Requirements came from 150 questionnaire responses and interviews and observation in five Tripoli pharmacies. Development followed an Agile incremental approach. The system comprises three applications sharing Firebase services: an Android mobile application for users, a Windows desktop application for pharmacy management, and a React web application for administration. Backend transactions coordinate reservations, partial offers, invoices, collection, and internal insurance records. Evaluation covered functionality, integration, transaction integrity, access control, and performance. Functional and component integration tests passed in 26/26 user cases, 39/40 pharmacy cases, and 15/15 administrative cases. All 12 executed system integration scenarios passed out of 14 planned. Targeted tests confirmed single allocation of contested stock, prevention of duplicate invoices, and consistent terminal order outcomes; three pharmacy corrections passed retesting. A five-minute local-emulator workload reaching 25 virtual users recorded an order-confirmation P95 of 331.29 ms against a 3,000-ms limit, with a maximum of…

title: Application of Raman spectroscopy to the first actual fuel debris retrieved from the Fukushima Daiichi Nuclear Power Station Unit 2
abstract: Abstract Following the successful first trial retrieval of fuel debris from Unit 2 of the Fukushima Daiichi Nuclear Power Station (FDNPS), a Raman spectroscopic assessment was conducted to investigate the chemical states of the debris. The powdered fuel debris sample, prepared via a vibratory mill, was analyzed using micro-Raman spectroscopy and was compared with simulated debris synthesized under controlled conditions. The average Raman spectrum revealed characteristic bands corresponding to tetragonal ZrO₂, spinel-type oxides originating from stainless-steel structural components, and a cubic (U, Zr)O₂ solid solution. The Raman spectrum of the retrieved fuel debris differed significantly from that of uranium-containing particles (UP1) previously sampled from stagnant water at torus room of Unit 2 of the FDNPS, indicating that further sampling and analysis are required to fully understand the overall chemical complexity of the fuel debris. Raman spectroscopy proved effective for identifying oxidative products in the fuel debris, requiring only minimal sample amounts and no vacuum or coating pretreatments. This study highlights the method’s potential as a valuable tool in nuclear decommissioning efforts, especially for the characterization of uranium bearing compounds in fuel debris.

title: Pelvic fractures in dogs
abstract: The aim of this review article was to describe the most common surgical procedures used to treat pelvic fractures in dogs. Pelvic fractures account for approximately 25% of all fractures in dogs and are typically caused by high-energy trauma, most often road traffic accidents. In addition to skeletal injuries, concurrent trauma frequently affects the thorax, urinary system, and peripheral nerves. Pelvic fractures are classified by anatomical location as sacroiliac luxation or fracture, iliac wing fracture, iliac body fracture, acetabular fracture, ischial fracture, and pelvic floor fracture. Diagnosis is primarily based on radiographic examination. Treatment may be conservative or surgical. The majority of pelvic fractures (approximately 75%) are managed conservatively, with strict activity restriction, rest, and appropriate analgesic therapy. Around 25% require surgical intervention, most commonly for sacral fractures or sacroiliac luxations, iliac body fractures, and acetabular fractures. Surgical management is based on anatomical reduction and stable fixation. Among various implants, screws and reconstruction plates have the most favourable outcomes. Successful surgical management requires precise anatomical alignment, stable fixation, and early mobilisation. Postoperative care includes analgesic therapy, activity restriction, and follow-up radiographic examination 6–8 weeks…

title: Infliximab treatment affects serological expression of matrix metalloproteinases MMP-2 and -9 in Crohn's disease via extracellular vesicle-derived RAGE via the NLRP3 pathway
abstract: Background Matrix metalloproteinases MMP-2 and MMP-9 contribute to tissue remodeling and barrier dysfunction in Crohn’s disease (CD). Although infliximab modulates their serological levels, the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. This study investigated whether infliximab regulates serum MMP-2 and MMP-9 expression through extracellular vesicle (EV)-derived receptor for advanced glycation end-products (RAGE) and the NLRP3 inflammasome pathway. Methods Forty-two patients with active CD receiving infliximab induction therapy and 20 healthy controls were enrolled. Serum MMP-2 and MMP-9 levels were measured by ELISA at baseline and weeks 2, 6, and 14. Circulating EVs were isolated and characterized, and EV-associated RAGE was quantified. NLRP3 inflammasome activation was assessed in peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs). In vitro, healthy donor PBMCs were stimulated with patient-derived EVs in the presence or absence of a RAGE-blocking antibody or the NLRP3 inhibitor MCC950. Results Infliximab treatment significantly decreased serum MMP-9 levels (more markedly in clinical responders) while modestly increasing MMP-2 levels. EV-RAGE content was elevated in active CD and declined after infliximab, correlating positively with serum MMP-9. Infliximab also suppressed NLRP3 and cleaved caspase-1 expression as well as serum IL-1β. Patient-derived EVs induced NLRP3 activation, IL-1β s…

title: POLITICALLY CORRECT LANGUAGE AS A PRAGMATIC PHENOMENON: DISCURSIVE POWER AND SOCIAL MEANING
abstract: This paper examines politically correct (PC) language as a pragmatic phenomenon shaped by discursive power and the negotiation of social meaning. PC language is approached not as a set of lexical substitutions but as a communicative practice through which speakers construct identities, regulate social relations, and align with institutional or ideological norms. Drawing on pragmatic and discourse-analytical frameworks, the study investigates how PC language functions as a mechanism of discursive positioning and social regulation in the Romanian context. A qualitative pragmatic-discursive methodology is employed, with analysis focused on ten authentic examples from Romanian political, institutional, and social media discourse. The findings show that PC language can promote inclusion and reduce offense but may equally operate as a form of discursive power that shapes what can be said and how meaning is interpreted. The paper argues that PC language must be understood as a context-dependent pragmatic practice in which discursive power conditions both expression and interpretation.

title: THE MASKS OF POWER IN BATMAN ACROSS AGES FROM THE GREAT DEPRESSION THROUGH THE COLD WAR
abstract: Comics have long been considered low literature, and one of the main reasons they were classified as such was the audience they primarily targeted: the commoners, the ordinary middle- and lower-class citizens, rather than the elites or pretentious readers of sophisticated literature. Consequently, comics enjoyed greater popularity, appeal, and – therefore – distribution, which rapidly turned them both into reflections of the people’s needs, struggles, concerns, interests, and imagination, and efficient vehicles of wartime and patriotic State propaganda and manipulation. This tendency can be identified in the Batman comics and imaginary, and the purpose of this paper is to closely examine how this pop culture phenomenon has evolved from a medium of official propaganda in the Golden and Silver Ages of comics (mid 1930s – late 1960s) to an instrument for subverting state policies and discourse in the Bronze Age (the 1970s and first half of the 1980s). We shall focus on a brief history of thematic representations in the Batman comic books between 1939 and 1985, the theatrical serials from 1943 and 1949, and the television series from 1966-1968, and, at the same time, illustrate how character portrayals and evolutions articulate the paradigmatic shift driven by ideological changes at a global level and by the political, social, economic, and cultural practices within American societ…

title: Pengaruh Locus of Control, Financial Knowledge, dan Income terhadap Financial Management Behavior (Studi Kasus KSPPS BMT Yaqawiyyu Cabang Mranggen di Klaten Jawa Tengah)
abstract: Penelitian ini bertujuan menganalisis pengaruh locus of control, financial knowledge, dan income terhadap financial management behavior pada anggota pembiayaan KSPPS BMT Yaqawiyyu Cabang Mranggen, Klaten. Fenomena rendahnya perilaku pengelolaan keuangan meskipun tingkat literasi dan inklusi keuangan masyarakat terus meningkat menjadi dasar penelitian ini. Penelitian ini menggunakan pendekatan kuantitatif dengan metode purposive sampling terhadap 80 responden. Data diperoleh melalui kuesioner dan dianalisis menggunakan regresi linier berganda dengan bantuan SPSS versi 22. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa locus of control, financial knowledge, dan income secara parsial berpengaruh positif dan signifikan terhadap financial management behavior, dengan koefisien regresi masing-masing sebesar 0,210; 0,793; dan 1,464. Secara simultan, ketiga variabel tersebut juga berpengaruh signifikan, dengan nilai F sebesar 568,649 dan signifikansi p < 0,001. Nilai Adjusted R Square sebesar 0,956 menunjukkan bahwa 95,6% variasi financial management behavior dapat dijelaskan oleh ketiga variabel independen, sedangkan 4,4% sisanya dijelaskan oleh faktor lain di luar penelitian. Temuan ini diharapkan dapat menjadi referensi bagi KSPPS BMT dalam mengembangkan program edukasi keuangan dan strategi pembiayaan untuk meningkatkan kesejahteraan anggota.

title: Wireless sensor network-based real-time monitoring system for large ship airbag launching: design and field validation
abstract: Traditional monitoring solutions for airbag launching of large ships rely on mechanical pressure gauges with limited spatial coverage, slow response times (from several hundred milliseconds to a few seconds), and an inability to monitor dynamically changing attitude parameters during the launching procedure. This paper introduces a WSN-based real-time monitoring solution that combines IMUs and pressure sensors installed at strategic positions on the ship hull and airbags. The solution uses the hierarchical Zigbee mesh with edge computing nodes and the TDMA protocol to deliver real-time, high-speed communication with low end-to-end latency, even under challenging shipyard conditions. The Kalman filter fuses multi-sensor data to provide comprehensive monitoring of pitch, roll, heave displacement, velocity, and acceleration. In-field validation tests have been performed on cargo ships with 1500-2000 DWT capacities during the actual launching process at cooperating shipyards. The system achieves a sampling rate of 100 Hz for inertial data and 50 Hz for pressure data, end-to-end latency under 60 ms (95%), and measurement accuracy of ±0.3° for attitude angles and ±1.5% full scale for pressure measurement. Comparative analysis showed that the proposed system outperforms traditional mechanical gauges with a 75% reduction in spatial blind spots (60%→15% hull coverage), 20–100× faster te…

title: The Effect of Artificial Intelligence on Shopee Business Performance in Indonesia:
abstract: Purpose: This study examines the effect of Artificial Intelligence (AI) Applications on Business Performance among active Shopee sellers in Indonesia, considering Consumer Engagement, Consumer Attitudes toward AI, and Operational Efficiency as related variables. Research Method: This study employed a quantitative approach using an online questionnaire distributed to active Shopee sellers in Indonesia through purposive sampling. Data were analyzed using SmartPLS and Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM). Results and Discussion: The findings show that AI Applications significantly affect Consumer Engagement, Consumer Attitudes toward AI, Operational Efficiency, and Business Performance. Operational Efficiency also significantly affects Business Performance, while Consumer Engagement and Consumer Attitudes toward AI do not have significant effects on Business Performance. Implications: Shopee sellers can utilize AI Applications to improve operational efficiency and support business performance. Future research may examine other factors that influence business performance in e-commerce. Originality: This study contributes to the understanding of AI Applications and their relationship with business performance by examining operational efficiency and consumer-related variables among Shopee sellers in Indonesia.

title: Artificial Intelligence in Primary Health Care of the Kyrgyz Republic: Opportunities, Risks, and a Conceptual Implementation Model in a Resource-Constrained Health System
abstract: The rapid development of artificial intelligence (AI) technologies creates new opportunities for transforming primary health care (PHC), including risk stratification, early disease detection, clinical decision support, patient triage and referral optimization, medical documentation automation, and remote monitoring. However, most evidence on the effectiveness of these technologies originates from health systems with advanced digital infrastructures, limiting their direct transferability to resource-constrained settings. The aim of this study was to synthesize current approaches to AI application in PHC, assess their potential and limitations within the health system of the Kyrgyz Republic, and develop a context-adapted conceptual model for the phased integration of AI into primary health care. An analytical review of contemporary scientific literature and strategic documents addressing machine learning, predictive analytics, natural language processing, and generative AI in primary care was conducted. Organizational and digital prerequisites for AI implementation in the Kyrgyz Republic were analyzed separately. The analysis suggests that, in the Kyrgyz context, the most promising applications are not autonomous diagnostic systems but technologies that augment health professionals: automated risk-group identification, preventive and follow-up care support, intelligent triage, c…

Mental Health Initiatives and Leadership Approaches in Catholic Schools: Basis for Enhanced Management Policies
abstract: This study assessed the implementation of mental health initiatives and the manifestation of leadership approaches to inform enhanced management policies that strengthen school mental health programs. A quantitative descriptive-correlational research design was employed involving administrators and personnel from Catholic Educational Association of the Philippines (CEAP)-member Catholic schools in Western Visayas. Data were collected using a validated researcher-made questionnaire and analyzed using appropriate descriptive and inferential statistical tools. The findings revealed a high level of implementation of mental health initiatives and a high manifestation of leadership approaches. Ethical and Values-Based Leadership emerged as the most highly manifested leadership approach, while Guidance and Counseling Services ranked highest among the mental health initiative domains. Leadership approaches demonstrated a significant positive relationship with the implementation of mental health initiatives, with Transformational Leadership exhibiting the strongest association. Selected administrator profile variables, including age, highest educational attainment, attendance at local seminars and trainings, and school awards and recognition, showed significant relationships with mental health initiatives. title: RECONSTRUCTING THE ROLE OF THE JUSTICE COLLABORATOR WITHIN THE NEW ARCHITECTURE OF INDONESIA’S CRIMINAL JUSTICE SYSTEM
abstract: The status of justice collaborators in Indonesia currently relies solely on scattered and weakly hierarchical legal instruments, namely SEMA No. 4 of 2011, joint regulations issued by law enforcement agencies, and Law No. 31 of 2014, thereby creating uncertainty regarding the determination of their status and the granting of rewards. Since 2025, the architecture of the criminal justice system has changed through Government Regulation No. 24 of 2025, the new National Criminal Code (KUHP) and Criminal Procedure Code (KUHAP), as well as Law No. 3 of 2026 on the Protection of Witnesses and Victims. This study aims to analyze the normative status of justice collaborators within this new architecture and to formulate a reconstruction of their status. The study employs a normative legal method using legislative, conceptual, and case-based approaches, with qualitative-prescriptive analysis grounded in legal systems theory, fundamental legal values, and criminal policy. The results of the study indicate that the status of the “justice collaborator” has risen from “soft law” to “hard law,” but remains fragmented due to the overlap of terms such as “crown witness,” “perpetrator witness,” and “justice collaborator,” as well as the lack of a single, clear authority for designation. Ideally, the cooperative justice mechanism should be subject to judicial oversight, proportionality, and respe…

title: Effective perioperative management of Abernethy Malformation for complex congenital cardiac surgery utilizing zero-balance ultrafiltration
abstract: Abstract Abernethy malformation is a rare congenital vascular anomaly in which portal venous blood bypasses the liver and drains directly into the systemic circulation. As a result, splanchnic venous blood is not processed by the liver. Clinical manifestations include hyperammonemia causing hepatic encephalopathy, pulmonary arteriovenous malformations, primary pulmonary artery hypertension, and hepatic neoplasms. Herein, we describe the case of a three-year-old male with heterotaxy syndrome and complex congenital heart disease presenting for biventricular repair on cardiopulmonary bypass. He also had Abernethy malformation and a history of hepatic encephalopathy managed with intense medical therapy. Existing literature offers limited guidance on managing Abernethy malformation or hyperammonemia during cardiopulmonary bypass. We were concerned that the perioperative phase of surgery could acutely raise the ammonia to dangerous levels through blood transfusions and hemolysis due to prolonged time on the heart-lung machine and the excessive use of cardiotomy suction and vents using roller pumps. Therefore, a multidisciplinary team developed a comprehensive perioperative plan. This report describes careful monitoring and management across all perioperative phases, with an emphasis on cardiopulmonary bypass ammonia management through zero balanced ultrafiltration (Z-BUF). title: Research Ethics and Patient Confidentiality Challenges in Healthcare Management
abstract: In contemporary healthcare management, digital transformation, electronic health records (EHR), and Big Data analytics serve as a fundamental empirical basis for executing structural reforms, evaluating macro-level institutional metrics, and enhancing administrative efficiency across public and private medical domains. However, utilizing complex patient data in scientific research to optimize internal hospital processes, predict diagnostic trends, and drive strategic decision-making brings forth severe, multi-faceted ethical and legal dilemmas. The sensitive nature of medical data creates a sharp conflict between the rigorous requirements of global scientific progress and an individual's fundamental human right to privacy. The primary objective of this study is to systematically analyze the hidden risks of violating research ethics principles, examine structural data leaks, and critique the structural mechanisms for safeguarding patient confidentiality within the context of healthcare administration. This study employs a modern, dual-layered methodological framework consisting of a Systematic Literature Review (SLR) and Comparative Normative-Legal Analysis to ensure maximal academic objectivity and transparency. The application of artificial intelligence in large-scale high-end equipment manufacturing projects: the moderating effect on the relationship between corporate culture, advertising investment, and strategic management of Shandong SMEs
abstract: In view of the rapid development and penetration of artificial intelligence (AI) into the field of manufacturing, the strategic management of small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) in large-scale high-end equipment projects is undergoing a new transformation, yet previous studies have not taken artificial intelligence adoption as a boundary condition to examine the influence of corporate culture and advertising investment on strategic management effectiveness. Based on the Resource-Based View (RBV) and Contingency Theory, this study proposes a moderation model and tests it empirically. Questionnaires were distributed to 323 SME managers in Shandong Province, and hierarchical regression analysis and 5,000-resample bootstrapping were used to test the proposed model. The results show that all four hypotheses proposed in this study were verified. Corporate culture and advertising investment positively influence the effectiveness of strategic management. Artificial intelligence adoption plays a significant role in moderating these two relationships, and corporate culture is more important than advertising investment in this regard, since the interaction effect of corporate culture and artificial intelligence adoption on strategic management effectiveness is greater than that of advertising investment and artificial intelligence adoption. title: Techno-economic optimization of a grid-integrated hybrid renewable energy system with an EV charging station at a university campus​
abstract: Abstract The rapid expansion of electric vehicle (EV) adoption in developing economies, combined with the growing imperative to decarbonize campus energy systems, necessitates novel planning frameworks that reconcile grid-interactive microgrid design with probabilistic economic validation. This study presents a techno-economic planning framework for a grid-integrated hybrid renewable energy system (HRES) co-designed with an EV charging station at university campus​. Unlike prior studies that treat EV loads as static inputs, this work constructs a behaviorally-informed, regulated-charging EV load profile by characterizing the actual EV fleet accessible within the study area, yielding a demand model grounded in local mobility patterns. Four HRES configurations integrating PV arrays, WT, a Bio-Gen, BESS, and utility grid support are optimized through HOMER Pro. The optimal configuration achieves a NPC of $2,403,816 and a COE of $0.069/kWh at a RF of 70.04%, while attaining significantly reduced emissions of CO 2 , NO x , SO 2 , and CO compared to the more grid-reliant configurations (Cases III and IV), and demonstrating environmental performance akin to Case II. Critically, this study couples system-level optimization with a probabilistic Monte Carlo simulation framework consisting of 10,000 stochastic trials over uncertain techno-economic parameters to produce probabilistic finan…

Product quality and price alongside physical evidence in Hanasui lipstick purchase intention
abstract: This study examines associations of perceived product quality, price, and physical evidence with intention to purchase Hanasui lipstick at Toko Kawan Skincare, North Sumatra. The source study used a convenience sample of 96 repeat store customers, including 64 civil servants. Recruitment and eligibility verification were insufficiently documented. Reported OLS summaries gave F(3, 92) = 161.50, p < .001, and R² = .840. Product quality (B = 0.332, 95% CI [0.167, 0.497]), price perception (B = 0.187, 95% CI [0.012, 0.362]), and physical evidence (B = 0.417, 95% CI [0.169, 0.665]) had positive conditional associations. Their unique increments in R² were approximately .028, .008, and .019. VIFs of 4.433-6.856, overlapping and double-barreled items, and a Durbin-Watson statistic of .841 limit interpretation. The latter raises a concern about residual dependence in the recorded order but does not establish recruitment clustering. Conventional inference remains provisional because respondent-level data and recruitment metadata were unavailable for robustness checks. A regression sensitivity analysis gives an 80%-power benchmark of f² ≈ .0835 for one coefficient under independent errors. title: Hybrid CNN-LSTM model for urban air pollution forecasting: towards early warning systems for public health: a case study of Baghdad and Basra
abstract: Air pollution has become a critical issue in environmentally challenged regions due to rapid urbanization, especially in countries where forecasting tools remain underdeveloped. Despite the success of deep learning approaches in predicting air quality, there has been little research on multivariate forecasting of particulate matter in Iraqi cities using publicly accessible environmental information. This study proposes a CNN-LSTM architecture to predict the concentrations of PM₂.₅ and PM₁₀ the following day in Baghdad and Basra. Environmental data related to air quality, along with temperature, relative humidity, wind speed, and seasonal cyclical features, were used to generate multivariate time series with a 14-day lookback window. The proposed model was compared with an LSTM model and a conventional autoregressive integrated moving average model using 1,249 daily data samples collected from August 2022 to December 2025. The results reveal that the deep learning models outperformed the statistical baseline, and the LSTM approach exhibited the best generalization performance. A threshold-based pollution alert module was also implemented to demonstrate how continuous concentration forecasts can support operational air quality warning systems. The findings demonstrate the applicability of multivariate deep learning for short-term urban air pollution forecasting in data-constraine…

title: FORECASTING OF RISKS OF ADVERSE EVENTS IN DATA TRANSMISSION AND PROCESSING NETWORKS
Air quality index forecasting under seasonal and long-term environmental dynamics
abstract: The Air Quality Index (AQI) indicates air pollution levels and their associated risks to human health and the environment. Factors influencing AQI include temperature, humidity, wind, precipitation, air pressure, seasonal variations, changes in industrial and urbanization patterns, and major pollutants such as PM2.5, PM10, NO2, SO2, CO, and O3. This paper discusses AQI geography and timing, as well as the relationship between air pollution and climate systems. It gives special attention to seasonal fluctuations and regional differences in pollution, dispersion, radiative forcing, short-lived climate pollutants, deforestation, and urbanization. The study also addresses seasonal and long-term environmental variations that affect pollutant levels and AQI. The study recognizes the importance of AQI forecasting for pollution assessment, public information, health protection, resource allocation, enforcement, location ranking, trend analysis, and timely assessment. The assessment also highlights key challenges, including potential variation in pollutant locations, monitoring difficulties, data reliability, the lack of direct studies on air quality indexes, and limited validation for real-time applications. To develop efficient air-quality management plans and provide precise, trustworthy air-quality forecasts, it is crucial to understand these environmental and temporal factors.

title: Forecasting urban carbon monoxide concentrations using a hybrid ResNet transformer with STL decomposition
A transformer-based explainable machine learning framework for heterogeneous ESG risk and return prediction using text intelligence
abstract: Corporate ESG disclosure has shifted toward narrative form, yet vendor ESG ratings that most empirical work depends on show substantial disagreement across providers, and encoders dominant in financial text analysis inherit a 512-token ceiling that discards most of a typical 10-K. HET-ESGFormer combines hierarchical long-document encoding, heterogeneity-aware sparse expert routing conditioned on industry sector and firm size, and a dual-channel explanation layer subject to faithfulness verification. The framework is evaluated on 3,182 U.S.-listed firms over 2015 to 2024 using 10-K filings, sustainability reports, earnings call transcripts, and ESG-tagged news. Against nine baselines spanning econometric, dictionary-based, contextual encoder, sparse-attention, and time-series approaches, HET-ESGFormer reduces return RMSE from 0.0417 to 0.0389 and QLIKE from 0.148 to 0.128, with Diebold-Mariano tests rejecting equal predictive accuracy against every baseline after correction for multiple comparisons. The text channel's marginal contribution to downside risk prediction is materially larger than its contribution to return prediction, widening at longer forecast horizons, indicating that ESG narratives carry more information about risk than about expected return. Ablations reveal a decoupling between predictive skill and explanation faithfulness: removing the consistency regularizer…

title: Performance comparison of ML algorithms for liver disease prediction
abstract: Liver disease is a leading cause of mortality throughout the world. Numerous lives may be saved if it can be detected in its early stages. Therefore, early detection of liver disease is crucial. This study aims to find a reliable ML model that can predict liver disease development using demographic and clinical data. This research explores several ML methods and introduces the most promising ones, Random Forest (RF) and Light Gradient Boosting Machine (LightGBM), for classification. The Indian Liver Patient Dataset (ILPD) is preprocessed by encoding categorical data, imputing missing values, removing duplicates and noise, applying Min-Max scaling, and balancing the data with SMOTE; this yields a dataset of 583 cases with 11 clinical and demographic characteristics. Models are assessed using F1-score, recall, accuracy, and precision, with an 80:20 stratified train-test split. While the proposed LightGBM model achieves a 99.8% ACC rate, a 99.9% PRE rate, a 99.5% REC rate, and a 99.8% F1-score (F1), the experimental results show that the RF model achieves a 99.6% PRE rate, a 99.7% REC rate, and a 99.6% F1-score (F1). The findings confirm that the proposed models achieved high ACC and reliability in predicting liver disease, with LightGBM delivering the highest ACC and PRE.

title: Leakage-aware federated-style simulation for fraud risk prediction in AI-enabled FinTech platforms
abstract: AI-enabled FinTech platforms increasingly rely on automated fraud-risk prediction to secure high-volume digital payments, mobile-money transactions, and real-time financial services. However, fraud detection remains difficult because fraudulent transactions are rare, financial data are sensitive, and centralized machine-learning models may create privacy and data-governance risks. This study evaluates a leakage-aware and imbalance-aware federated-style simulation for fraud-risk prediction in AI-enabled FinTech platforms. The study does not implement FedAvg, cryptographic secure aggregation, differential privacy, or model-parameter exchange. Instead, the PaySim Synthetic Financial Dataset was partitioned into five simulated FinTech clients, local models were trained separately, and prediction-level aggregation was used to compare centralized and simulated decentralized learning settings. The experimental workflow included data-quality assessment, leakage-aware feature selection, feature engineering, class-imbalance analysis, centralized model development, threshold optimization, and federated-style model comparison. The results show that fraud cases represented only 0.0466% of all transactions and occurred only in CASH_OUT and TRANSFER operations. The best-balanced centralized model was the Improved Random Forest at a threshold of 0.33, achieving an F1-score of 0.3019. Federated…

title: Navigating complexity: applying machine learning to improve SWL outcome prediction
Spatial–temporal machine learning for traffic violation type prediction: a case study in Qatar
abstract: Although traffic violations are among the most significant factors contributing to road accidents, little research has focused on predicting specific types of traffic violations in Qatar and the Gulf region, where the number of vehicles has increased significantly in recent years. This work addresses this gap by proposing a machine-learning framework to solve fine-grained, multi-class prediction of traffic violation types on a large-scale dataset from Qatar. The dataset is extremely imbalanced and has a high-dimensional categorical space, with 97 original violation classes. We created a preprocessing pipeline to address these issues by filtering the 97 original codes to nine well-represented violation types while retaining 99.6% of the records. The final model uses 18 spatiotemporal features, including our zone violation entropy measure, which captures violation diversity in each enforcement zone. Five classifiers are evaluated with a strict temporal train–validation–test split, training-based encoding (to avoid temporal leakage), and balanced class weighting. Random forest's macro F1 score is 0.6184 and balanced accuracy is 0.7064, outperforming the linear and neural baselines. SHAP analysis shows that location-derived features account for ~74% of the model's predictive importance, while temporal features account for ~25%. title: A fragile reversible watermarking technique for medical imaging security using prediction error expansion and Canny edge detection
abstract: This paper develops a fragile, reversible watermarking technique to detect accidental and intentional alterations in DICOM medical images. A fragile method is adopted to detect any manipulation applied to medical images, while reversibility ensures the recovery of the original unaltered image at extraction. The proposed approach automatically segments medical images into Region of Interest (ROI) and Region of Non-Interest (RONI), extracts authentication data from the DICOM header, and generates a digital signature of the image. The method combines integrity and authentication data and inserts them into the edge areas within the ROI, implementing the Prediction Error Expansion (PEE) technique and Canny edge detection. During extraction, the embedded watermark and the original unmanipulated image are restored without knowing the pixel locations used to hide the watermark data. The method was assessed using twelve 16-bit DICOM images, including MRI and CT, with a 512x512 pixel size. The experimental results yielded an average PSNR of 97.19 dB and an average SSIM of 0.999996, with an average watermark length of 7835 bits per image. The proposed method also fully met the reversibility requirement by recovering both the original unaltered images and the embedded watermark data. title: A survey on intelligent transportation systems for accident detection and risk prediction using AI
abstract: The complexity of today's transportation networks has made road safety, accident detection, and risk management increasingly challenging. Intelligent Transportation Systems (ITS) offer a technological base to enhance transportation safety by incorporating sensors, communications, data processing, and intelligent decision-making. This review discusses the application of Artificial Intelligence (AI) for accident detection and risk prediction in ITS by examining information sources, methodologies, accident investigation, and associated challenges. It examines the use of machine learning, deep learning, computer vision, spatiotemporal modeling, and multimodal AI for accident detection, risk prediction, severity analysis, and active safety management. This review of studies suggests that collecting traffic, vehicle, road, environmental, geographical, historical, and driver-related information can improve understanding of collisions and support timely safety decisions. The review also highlights the importance of explainable and reliable AI that provides transparency, dependability, and accountability. However, the obstacles include data heterogeneity, model generalization, dynamic conditions, scalability, quick implementation, privacy considerations, security requirements, and compatible information systems. In conclusion, incorporating AI in ITS may have the power to shift road-saf…

Nab-paclitaxel-oxaliplatin-S-1 vs FOLFOX in locally advanced gastric cancer: Efficacy and postoperative disease-free survival prediction
abstract: BACKGROUND Locally advanced gastric cancer remains associated with a considerable risk of recurrence despite perioperative chemotherapy and radical surgery. Folinic acid, fluorouracil, and oxaliplatin is widely used, whereas nab-paclitaxel, oxaliplatin, and S-1 has shown potential antitumor activity in clinical practice. However, real-world comparative evidence between these regimens and postoperative tools for individualized disease-free survival (DFS) prediction remain limited. We hypothesized that clinicopathological and treatment-response variables could support postoperative recurrence risk stratification. AIM To compare the short-term response, long-term outcomes, and safety of the FOLFOX and P-SOX regimens in patients with gastric cancer. Using clinicopathological data, treatment response, and follow-up information, we applied least absolute shrinkage and selection operator Cox regression to select key factors associated with DFS and constructed a nomogram for predicting DFS at 18 months, 24 months, and 36 months. METHODS This retrospective study included 181 patients with advanced gastric cancer who received preoperative and postoperative chemotherapy followed by standard D2 radical gastrectomy. Clinical data were collected from two centers: Qinghai University Affiliated Hospital and Qinghai Red Cross Hospital. Among these patients, 113 received the P-SOX regimen, and 6…

title: A framework for integrating artificial neural networks and finite element analysis for shear strength prediction in unreinforced RC beam–column joints
abstract: Beam-Column joints (BCJs) are critical components in reinforced concrete (RC) buildings. These members experience excessive stress during seismic events, often resulting in catastrophic failures, particularly in RC buildings constructed prior to the introduction of seismic design provisions and lacking reinforcement in the BCJ zone. The study presents a machine learning framework to predict the shear strength of unreinforced BCJs using 7 input parameters. This study developed an Artificial Neural Network-Finite Element Analysis hybrid model (ANN-FEA-13), trained, validated, and tested on 4320 samples of BCJ failure generated through nonlinear analysis in ABAQUS. The data was divided into training (70%), testing (15%), and validation (15%) sets. The ANN-FEA-13 model achieved high prediction accuracy (R = 0.962) and was compared with experimental data from literature and the ACI 318 code, showing superior performance. The results were promising and demonstrated the effectiveness of the developed data-driven ANN-FEA-13 framework, which reliably predicts BCJ failure and supports ongoing efforts in resilience-based assessment and retrofitting of aging RC structures in seismic regions.

title: Influence of Provenance and Pre-Germination Treatments on Germination Capacity of Robinia pseudoacacia L. Seeds
abstract: Robinia pseudoacacia L. is a fast-growing tree species widely used in afforestation and land restoration. This study investigates the influence of seed provenance and pre-sowing treatments on germination capacity. Seeds were collected from four provenances in Romania (Căpâlna, Pârâul Ursului, Călan and Țagu) and subjected to four treatments: control, Germinoseed, Atonik and mechanical scarification. Germination tests were conducted under controlled laboratory conditions over 28 days. In addition, seed morphological traits (length, width and weight) were analyzed in relation to germination performance. The results revealed significant differences among treatments and provenances. Mechanical scarification resulted in the highest germination rates across all provenances, while untreated seeds showed the lowest values. Biostimulant treatments improved germination compared to the control, with varying effectiveness. A positive relationship between seed weight and germination capacity was observed, depending on the applied treatment. These findings highlight the importance of selecting appropriate pre-sowing treatments and seed sources to improve germination performance and support sustainable forest management, particularly in the context of increasing environmental variability.
