title: Postlandfall Persistence and Poleward Recurvature of Intense Western North Pacific Typhoons through a Track-Conditioned Moisture-Bridge Mechanism
abstract: Abstract Why some intense western North Pacific typhoons remain hazardous for 1–2 days after mainland China landfall whereas others weaken rapidly remains unresolved. This study examines that contrast using 1979–2020 Joint Typhoon Warning Center best tracks and ERA5 reanalysis fields. We combine prelandfall track-conditioned clustering, storm-centered event-level moisture budgets, a Helmholtz decomposition of integrated vapor transport, and a strength–persistence framework that separates antecedent inflow strength from fractional retention. The analysis focuses on the two near-coastal track classes that dominate mainland China landfall evolution. Recurving coastal storms retain stronger postlandfall south- and east-side inflow than northwestward coastal storms because the western North Pacific subtropical high, a southwesterly monsoon branch, and upper-level outflow remain more coherently phased across landfall. Consequently, recurving storms preserve a more persistent east-side transport pathway and larger absolute postlandfall moisture import even though their fractional retention is not larger. Cross-validated discrimination benchmarks show that landfall track variables account for most of the skill for inland persistence and poleward reach; adding the compact moisture-bridge proxy gives negligible incremental area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC). title: Effect of Ni-additive on jute stick charcoal-mediated carbon anode of Li-ion batteries
abstract: Li-ion batteries (LIBs) have gained popularity as a potential device for sustainable energy transition. Because of its simple and environmentally benign production, biomass-derived amorphous carbon is a viable anode for LIBs as a possible replacement for graphite. However, its performance is limited by structural deterioration and low conductivity. Therefore, developing low-cost biomass-derived carbon anodes with improved electrical conductivity and cycling stability is important for sustainable LIB applications. Here, slow pyrolysis has been used to produce amorphous carbon from jute stick charcoal. The jute sticks were pyrolyzed at 400 °C, and the structural characterization confirmed the successful formation of amorphous carbon with flake-like porous morphology. The resulting carbon was evaluated as an anode material in a full cell. After 500 cycles, this anode demonstrated a discharge capacity of 125.46 mAh/g and a Coulombic efficiency (CE) of 68.4% at 1C. In addition, Ni metal powder additives were added to improve cell performance. Ni considerably reduced the cell impedance and enhanced electrode conductivity. As a result, after 500 cycles, the Ni-added anode demonstrated improved performance with a discharge capacity of 148.02 mAh/g and a CE of 73% at 1C. Electrochemical investigations further indicated reduced cell resistance after Ni incorporation, demonstrating enhanc…

title: PoET²S: Folding a digital twin into validator selection for blockchain consensus in peer-to-peer energy trading
abstract: Blockchain platforms for peer-to-peer energy trading often add a digital twin that forecasts each meter's generation and demand. In most designs the twin only raises alarms, while validators are still chosen by stake or computation. The proposed scheme, PoET²S, incorporates the twin's evidence into validator selection: a node's weight is a stake-and-energy term multiplied by its Twin-Trust Score raised to γ = 2.5, so nodes that contradict the physical forecast quickly lose committee seats. A discrete-event simulator compares PoET²S (500 nodes, 15% Byzantine, 30 paired seeds) with seven classical baselines and three design points from recent work: a binary veto, an additive energy-and-trust score, and a linear (γ = 1) reputation weight. Detection is a near-tie: PoET²S catches 91.0% of attackers and the veto 91.7%. PoET²S raises more false alarms per catch by default (13.9 against 9.7) but matches the veto's catch rate at equal false-alarm cost. The malicious committee share is 10.8% under the veto, 3.8% under the linear weight, and 2.6% under PoET²S, and on 100 seeds the gain over the linear weight is 37% (Holm-adjusted p = 7.2 × 10⁻⁹). At 45% Byzantine nodes, the one-third fault bound fails in 64.4% of veto blocks and 2.4% of PoET²S blocks. Simulated commit latency (30.2 ms) is higher than for Proof of Stake and Delegated Proof of Stake, lower than for Practical Byzantine Fault…

Isolated Northern Hemisphere Cooling in an Idealized Model Promotes Ocean Carbon Storage and Glacial-like Ocean Features
abstract: Abstract Earth’s past glacial cycles are paced by orbital insolation changes, but internal climate feedbacks modulating atmospheric carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) are necessary to explain the full magnitude of glacial–interglacial climate variability. Identifying such feedbacks and linking them to orbitally paced forcing remains a challenge, impeding a comprehensive understanding of the glacial cycles. Orbital variations, determining the latitudinal distribution and seasonality of insolation, are primarily important for allowing the buildup of large Northern Hemisphere ice sheets. Meanwhile, the processes canonically understood to drive CO 2 drawdown and mediate ocean–atmosphere carbon partitioning are largely hosted in the far-flung Southern Ocean. This study explores the role of remote Northern Hemisphere temperature forcing in influencing Southern Ocean conditions that impact global ocean circulation and carbon content. In a set of idealized ocean–sea ice model simulations, we find that cooling air temperatures to glacial-like levels at the high northern latitudes (emulating the thermal effect of a large Northern Hemisphere ice sheet) drives a substantial CO 2 drawdown of 32 ppm—or 74% the magnitude of a simulation forced by globally glacial-like temperatures everywhere (43 ppm). title: Multipolar Light-Matter Coupling in Nanostructures: From Ultrafast Radiative Decay to Forbidden Molecular Transitions
abstract: We review optical responses in the nano-to-bulk crossover, where bulk translational symmetry no longer applies and the long-wavelength approximation (LWA) often fails. In this regime, the response must be treated nonlocal, and a self-consistent solution of Maxwell’s equations and the constitutive relation for excitonic polarization, with radiative boundary conditions, is required. We present a unified view based on internal-field resonance: when the internal-field profile is phase matched to quantized center-of-mass modes, radiative shifts and widths are reorganized in a mode- and size-selective way. After outlining the basics of the nonlocal formulation, we summarize theoretically predicted and experimentally observed phenomena that isolate nonlocal effects in nanostructures. Representative results include thickness-dependent level interchange, a nonmonotonic increase of linewidth with system size, ultrafast radiative decay down to 10 fs, and transitions that are forbidden in the LWA but allowed through internal-field coupling. We also note that the same nonlocal, self-consistent framework extends naturally to molecular scales, including molecule-plasmon systems and tip-enhanced spectroscopies, where structured near fields can activate nominally forbidden multipolar transitions. These connections show how a nano-to-bulk viewpoint can unify solid-state and molecular optical res…

title: Use of Geothermal Energy as a Renewable Source of Energy with the Help of Heat Pumps
abstract: Geothermal heat pumps are widely used for heating and cooling buildings. This technology is based on the principle of heat transfer between the ground and the building, significantly reducing electricity or fossil fuel consumption. In winter, heat from the ground is transferred to the building, and in summer, excess heat is returned to the ground. This closed-loop system not only provides a comfortable microclimate but also saves up to 50-70% of energy compared to traditional heating methods. This article discusses the operating principles, key technological solutions, as well as the environmental and economic aspects of using such systems. The focus is on heat transfer system types: vertical ground probes, horizontal collectors, and groundwater-based systems. Factors influencing configuration selection are analyzed, including geological conditions, available space, and the facility's heat load. It is emphasized that proper circuit calculation and design are key to long-term and efficient system operation. In conclusion, it is argued that integrating geothermal heat pumps into the energy systems of buildings and residential areas is a promising approach to decarbonizing heat supply, increasing energy independence, and achieving sustainable development goals. The widespread adoption of this technology will be facilitated by the development of a regulatory framework, government s…

title: Long-term dynamics and future trajectories of natural gas production: a global, regional, and Iranian assessment
abstract: Natural gas plays an important role in sustainable energy supply and future planning. This study examines trends in global natural gas production, Asia, the Middle East, and Iran, and outlines its outlook using several analytical methods. Annual data for the period 1970-2025 were examined using trend analysis and time series forecasting methods. The significance of trends was determined using the Mann–Kendall test, and the rate of change was determined using Sen’s slope estimator. Then, an ARIMA model was developed to forecast production up to 2035, and its accuracy was evaluated using RMSE, MAE, and MAPE criteria. The results showed that production increased in all four ranges and was statistically significant (p < 0.001). The Z-statistic values ​​were between 9.69 and 10.83. Sen’s slope estimates showed annual increases in production in the world, Asia, the Middle East, and Iran of 594.60, 295.04, 145.48, and 50.39 TWh/year, respectively. The ARIMA forecast also indicated that this increase would continue until 2035. Global production would increase from 41,964.71 TWh in 2025 to about 48,159.54 TWh. Production in Asia, the Middle East, and Iran in 2035 was also predicted to be about 18,096.72, 9,348.25, and 3,305.26 TWh, respectively. Simulation-based techno-economic evaluation of triboelectric and electromagnetic footstep energy harvesting
abstract: Abstract Footstep energy harvesters must be evaluated by stored energy, mechanical input, power-management losses, and cost rather than by open-circuit voltage alone. This study developed a reproducible simulation framework for comparing electromagnetic, triboelectric, and hybrid floor-tile energy harvesters under a common 7.0 J gross footstep-energy budget. A reduced-order two-dimensional Finite Element Method Magnetics (FEMM) model, coil/load optimization, rectifier modeling, mechanical-energy checks, and an upfront prototype component-cost model were used for the electromagnetic generator (EMG). A nylon/polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) contact-separation triboelectric nanogenerator (TENG) was audited for active area, air breakdown, parasitic capacitance, leakage, high-voltage (HV) rectification, and shared mechanical input. The balanced EMG design used a 28-magnet alternating-radial array, American Wire Gauge (AWG) 32 coil with 1226 turns, Schottky rectification, and a modeled gear-ratio-80 scenario, producing 0.5507 J per simulated step and 0.00331 J per step per USD. A unit-consistent Paschen calculation gave a 19.48 kV uniform-field limit for the 5 mm TENG case; the audited TENG stored 0.002382 J per cycle. title: Geopolitics of the Global Green Transition: Rethinking Azerbaijan's Energy Security
abstract: The accelerating global transition toward renewable energy frameworks and comprehensive decarbonization is structurally reconfiguring the international political economy. While shifting away from fossil fuels mitigates historical macroeconomic risks associated with hydrocarbon supply volatility and cartel-driven market manipulations, it simultaneously introduces novel structural vulnerabilities. These vulnerabilities manifest within the global energy architecture as nations transition from a reliance on liquid resource extraction to a dependency on rigid industrial supply chains, advanced technology, and geographically concentrated raw materials. This study aims to analytically deconstruct the structural transformation of the global energy security paradigm, critically evaluate the geopolitical implications of critical raw material monopolies, examine the rise of geo-economic protectionism, and comprehensively assess the strategic positioning of Azerbaijan as an emerging transnational green energy hub and corridor. A multidimensional analytical framework combining systemic economic analysis, comparative geo-economics, and institutional theory was employed. Empirical indicators and global energy supply chain data spanning from 2015 to 2026—sourced from the International Energy Agency (IEA) and the International Renewable Energy Agency (IRENA)—were synthesized alongside the natio…

Prospects of Integration Diplomacy of the Kyrgyz Republic as a Factor in Strengthening Political Stability: Scenarios and Recommendations
abstract: This study examines the prospects of the integration diplomacy of the Kyrgyz Republic as a factor in strengthening political stability. The relevance is determined by the transformation of the global architecture of international relations, increasing regional competition, and the need for small states to compensate for limited resources through participation in multilateral associations. The aim is to identify promising areas of Kyrgyzstan's integration diplomacy, propose scenario forecasts, and develop practical recommendations. The methodological framework includes comparative and institutional analysis, scenario forecasting, and content analysis of official documents. Results: Based on the analysis of Kyrgyzstan's participation in the EAEU, SCO, CSTO, and OTS, as well as taking into account the findings of researchers on political culture, ethnopolitics, political image, and bilateral relations, three scenarios for the development of integration diplomacy are proposed: inertial, adaptive, and proactive. The preference for the proactive scenario, involving a transition from passive adaptation to institutional leadership and the promotion of national interests, is substantiated. A set of practical recommendations has been developed for improving the institutional architecture, personnel training, communication strategy, and the use of chairmanship in regional organizations. First-Principles Calculations of the Magnetocrystalline Anisotropy Energy in Disordered Alloys Using Wannier-based Coherent Potential Approximation
abstract: We present a method for calculating the magnetocrystalline anisotropy energy (MAE) of disordered alloys using Green’s functions constructed from Wannier Hamiltonians within the coherent potential approximation (Wannier-CPA). The MAE of a disordered alloy system is obtained from the difference in thermodynamic potential between two magnetization directions, with the potential evaluated using the Luttinger–Ward functional. For validation, the MAE of Fe x Ni 1− x and Fe x Pd 1− x is calculated using both the Wannier-CPA method and the Korringa–Kohn–Rostoker (KKR) method combined with the CPA. The results obtained by Wannier-CPA are in good agreement with those from KKR-CPA, reproducing the composition dependence of the MAE and the characteristic behavior specific to each system. Furthermore, analysis of the in-plane MAE of Fe x Pd 1− x shows that it changes sign near x [Formula: see text] 0.425. This approach provides a route to evaluate the MAE of disordered alloys using Wannier Hamiltonians generated from various first-principles codes, while retaining the efficiency of Wannier interpolation.

title: Current perspectives on smart grid cybersecurity and critical infrastructure protection
abstract: The increasing convergence of renewable energy sources, information and communication technology, Internet of Things devices, smart meters, and phasor measurement units has enhanced the efficiency, reliability, and real-time operation of Smart Grids. However, this interconnected cyber-physical infrastructure has also increased cybersecurity vulnerabilities and attack surfaces. This paper reviews AI/ML-based security approaches for Smart Grid cybersecurity and critical infrastructure protection, focusing on major threats such as False Data Injection Attacks, Denial-of-Service attacks, Man-in-the-Middle attacks, spoofing, malware, and malicious command injection. The study examines existing protection mechanisms, including authentication and access control, intrusion detection, attack mitigation, secure communication, data protection, and privacy preservation. The study further discusses cyber-physical system protection, resilience, incident response, continuous monitoring, network segmentation, and AI/ML-based security approaches. A review of recent research highlights advances in anomaly detection, trust management, multilayer security, and intelligent threat detection. However, challenges remain in scalability, real-time processing, interoperability, adaptive defense, limited datasets, and real-world validation. title: Physicochemical characterization and FTIR analysis of pyrolysis oil derived from waste tires
abstract: Waste tire pyrolysis has emerged as a promising thermochemical conversion technology for recovering valuable liquid fuels while addressing the environmental challenges associated with end-of-life tires. For this purpose, tire-derived fuel was pyrolyzed in a fixed-bed reactor at varying temperatures of 560 °C, 565 °C, 580 °C, 590 °C, and 600 °C. The maximum pyrolytic oil yield was achieved at 600 °C, producing approximately 45.56% liquid, 22.44% gas, and 32% solid residue. Increasing the temperature improved oil yield while reducing gas output. The physicochemical properties analyzed for the pyrolytic oil include calorific value, viscosity, density, flash point, fire point, and elemental composition. Fourier Transform Infrared Spectroscopy (FT-IR) analysis revealed various functional groups, including alkanes, alkenes, aromatics, and carbonyl compounds, indicating a complex hydrocarbon mixture. Thus, this study aims to produce tire pyrolysis oil (TPO) and assess its suitability as an alternative fuel for IC engines through yield analysis and fuel property characterization.

title: The Free Energy of the Square Lattice Ising Model with Interactions Alternating in Horizontal and Vertical Directions
abstract: The free energy of the Ising model on the square lattice with alternating interactions in both horizontal and vertical directions is exactly derived. This model is distinct from the checkerboard Ising model. The result includes Onsager’s free energy as a special case, and also includes Lee–Yang’s free energy with an imaginary field, and relates these two solutions via continuous parameters. The result includes a generalization of Lee–Yang’s result to cases with four different couplings. It is also derived that each imaginary magnetic field iπ/2 applied to a lattice site corresponds to a single frustrated square in its dual lattice.

title: Existence and Uniqueness of Solutions for Initial Value Problems of First-Order Differential Equations with Nonlinear Riemann–Liouville Variable-Order Fractional Derivative Terms on the Half-Line
abstract: In recent years, numerous studies have addressed the existence of solutions to initial value problems for first-order differential equations that involve nonlinear terms of variable-order fractional derivatives. However, owing to the distinctive characteristics of variable-order fractional derivatives, these existing results cannot be directly generalized to nonlinear cases that incorporate nonlinear terms of such derivatives. Building upon established conclusions concerning Riemann-Liouville variable-order fractional derivatives and employing standard analytical techniques, this paper investigates the existence and uniqueness of solutions to the initial value problem for first-order differential equations with nonlinear terms of Riemann-Liouville variable-order fractional derivatives on the half-line. Finally, two illustrative examples are provided to illustrate the applicability of the results developed in the previous sections.

title: The Evolution of Web Design Principles: from Static Pages to Interactive Interfaces
abstract: Examines the historical development of web design principles, tracing the evolution from early static HTML pages to contemporary interactive user interfaces. The study aims to identify patterns across key stages of web design evolution and to determine how approaches to digital product design have shifted under the influence of technological progress. Particular attention is given to the proliferation of graphical web browsers, the introduction of Cascading Style Sheets (CSS) and JavaScript, the rise of mobile devices, and the emergence of frameworks for building single-page applications. The defining characteristics of the Web 1.0 and Web 2.0 eras, adaptive web design, and modern dynamic interfaces are explored. A hypothesis is proposed that design priorities have gradually shifted from the organization and presentation of information toward a focus on interactivity, ease of interaction, and the personalization of the user experience. The methodological foundation consists of an analysis of scientific publications, a comparative-historical approach, and the systematization and synthesis of information regarding the evolution of web technologies. The study proposes a qualitative typology of web design stages that reflects changes in page structure, implementation tools, and user interaction requirements. It was determined that technological innovations expanded design capabilit…

title: Beyond the Exit: Reimagining Transition as a Shared Design Process
abstract: Transition should not be treated as the final stage of special education. It should be understood as a shared design process that begins early, develops over time, and extends beyond a student’s exit from school. That requires schools to move from planning for students to designing with them. Families bring essential knowledge, students bring their goals and strengths, and community partners bring access to the systems and opportunities that remain after school services end.

Bond behavior and design challenges in GFRP reinforced concrete beams with research directions
abstract: Abstract Glass fiber-reinforced polymer (GFRP) bars are increasingly used as internal concrete reinforcement because of their corrosion resistance and non-magnetic properties. However, their lower stiffness, brittle behavior, diverse surface treatment options, and different bond mechanisms compared with steel bars complicate the design of anchorages, lap splices and detailing in general. This paper critically reviews the bond behavior of GFRP bars and compares the corresponding provisions of major international design guidelines. A structured literature search was conducted using the Web of Science database, from which 60 relevant publications were selected for detailed assessment. The review covers bond mechanisms and failure modes, bond stress–slip models, the effects of surface treatment, concrete properties and confinement, development and lap-splice length, bent-bar detailing, and long-term bond performance. The findings show that surface properties are among the most influential parameters governing bond strength, but their effects are not adequately represented by the limited surface coefficients used in current design provisions. Therefore existing development-length equations are generally conservative, particularly for modern GFRP products and well-confined reinforcement, although unconservative predictions may occur under certain conditions. Most guidelines rely on e…

title: Some Contributions to Multiple-Variable Cyclic Inequalities
abstract: In this paper, we propose two general theorems concerning inequalities in several variables, subject to flexible parametric constraints: the first presents a new sum-type inequality, while the second introduces its product-type counterpart. These results find natural applications in the study of cyclic inequalities. A wide range of examples is provided to illustrate the applicability of our approach, complemented by four additional theorems that further expand the analytical framework.

When Pixels Persuade: Virtual Influencer Content Appeals, Credibility, and Generation Z Purchase Intention
abstract: This study investigates how the emotional, rational and authenticity appeals of virtual influencer (VI) content, together with VI credibility, shape Generation Z purchase intention through perceived content value and consumer engagement. An online survey was conducted among Indonesian Generation Z Instagram users who had been exposed to Lil Miquela’s Calvin Klein content, and the proposed model was estimated using partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS-SEM). The results reveal that rational appeal, emotional appeal and VI credibility are positively associated with perceived content value, whereas authenticity appeal shows no significant relationship. Perceived content value is positively related to consumer engagement, which in turn is positively related to purchase intention. Perceived content value mediates the relationships of rational appeal, emotional appeal and VI credibility with engagement, and engagement mediates the link between perceived content value and purchase intention. The study extends advertising value and source credibility perspectives to non-human endorsers by demonstrating that message characteristics and source evaluations operate jointly in VI marketing. For practitioners, the findings highlight the importance of informative, emotionally relevant and credible VI content. The cross-sectional, single-influencer and single-brand design li…

BASTARD, BELOVED AND THE POLITICS OF NAMING: MASKS AND POWER IN ROBIN HOBB’S REALM OF THE ELDERLINGS
abstract: This article examines the politics of naming in Robin Hobb's Realm of the Elderlings, arguing that personal names in this fantasy cycle function not as neutral identificatory tags but as semantic, symbolic, and ethical structures that shape character identity, narrative trajectory, and reader interpretation. Adopting an interdisciplinary framework grounded in literary onomastics and semiotics, with narratological, philosophical, and gender-theoretical perspectives employed as supplementary interpretive lenses, the study focuses on the two central figures of the series, FitzChivalry Farseer and the Fool, whose successive names — FitzChivalry, Fitz, the Bastard, Changer, Tom Badgerlock, Beloved for the former, and the Fool, Amber, Lord Golden, Beloved for the latter — trace parallel arcs of legitimacy, marginality, performance, and transformation. Rather than treating naming as a decorative feature of world-building, the analysis positions it as a structural device through which Hobb negotiates questions of authority, gender, kinship, and selfhood. The study opens by situating Hobb within a broader tradition of onomastic scholarship on fantasy fiction, noting that while naming in Tolkien, Le Guin, and Martin has received sustained critical attention, Hobb’s naming systems remain comparatively underexamined despite their scale and complexity across sixteen novels organized into fi…

TRANSLATING POWER: AI, MEDIATION AND THE IMAGINARY OF MANIPULATION IN ACADEMIC CONTEXTS
abstract: The growing use of generative artificial intelligence in academic writing and translation is changing not only the speed of textual production but also the ways in which linguistic authority is constructed and perceived. In multilingual academic contexts, AI systems translate, reformulate, and refine texts according to dominant conventions of academic English. Such assistance may widen access to international communication, yet its fluency can also make the interpretative choices embedded in the resulting text less visible. This article examines AI-mediated Romanian-English academic translation as a site where linguistic assistance, symbolic power, and the imaginary of manipulation intersect. The study approaches translation as mediation rather than neutral transfer. It asks how AI may reshape lexical authority, epistemic stance, and stylistic identity, how these changes influence the perceived legitimacy of academic discourse, and when unobtrusive mediation may acquire a potentially manipulative effect. The theoretical discussion connects translation studies with scholarship on symbolic power, academic stance, and sociotechnical imaginaries. Methodologically, the article adopts a conceptual qualitative approach supported by three illustrative Romanian-English micro-analyses. These examples are not treated as a representative corpus and do not support statistical generalisation…

title: Bebidas vegetales de almendra y avena frente a la leche de vaca en la salud dental: revisión narrativa
abstract: Objetivo: analizar la evidencia sobre el impacto de las bebidas vegetales de almendra y avena en la salud dental frente a la leche de vaca. Método: revisión narrativa de 15 documentos indexados en PubMed y SciELO sobre composición nutricional, potencial cariogénico y erosivo de la leche y sus alternativas. Resultados: la leche de vaca no endulzada mostró bajo potencial cariogénico y se asoció con menos caries. Las bebidas vegetales fueron heterogéneas, con calcio y vitamina D dependientes de la fortificación y frecuentes azúcares añadidos. Las bebidas de almendra endulzadas fueron más cariogénicas que la leche bovina. No se hallaron estudios dentales sobre la bebida de avena. Conclusión: el efecto de las bebidas vegetales sobre los dientes depende de sus azúcares y de su fortificación mineral.
venue: Sanitas. Revista arbitrada de ciencias de la salud

title: Scalability Scope and Limitations of Potential Innovations and Renewable Energy Sources to Sustain Small Holder Farming Families and Various Ecosystems in India-Local to Global Relevance
abstract: The soil, water and air pollution are posing a huge threat to soil, underground water aquifers, oceans, various ecosystems, food chain, human, animals (land, aquatic both), various species health and our environment. Efficiently recapturing carbon emissions through agroforestry, increasing area under forests along with increasing the use of renewable sources in hybrid mode can put a halt on this pattern. Biogas/Biofuels along with necessary engine changes, can control vehicular carbon emissions to a great extent. There is need to increase use of vermi-compost, in-situ crop residue management techniques, green manuring, farm yard/poultry manures, pulse-cereal intercropping/diversification, eco-friendly integrated pest management techniques, biodegradable plastic, jute bags and use of crop residue biochar, sunflower seed husk and its biochar as a bioremediation to treat industrial waste with heavy metals. A new and innovative eco-friendly Parkash Bioherbal water reservoir is proposed. Neem, Moringa oleifera and seaweed products can be used as biopesticides, bioinsecticides, biofertilizers to enhance crop growth in an organic way. The technologies and implementation to minimize and treat industrial/domestic waste at source before discharge into the marine system are urgently required so as to enhance the oceans’ capacity to maintain carbon cycle.

title: Petrochemical export taxation as energy-industrial policy in Iran: a product-specific value-chain analysis
abstract: As a hydrocarbon-rich economy, Iran faces an energy-policy challenge in deciding whether to export oil and gas feedstocks as basic petrochemical products or convert them into higher-value materials. Iran’s petrochemical exports remain concentrated in basic and intermediate products, while downstream exports are limited. Using a descriptive-analytical design, documentary analysis, financial scenario analysis, and a comparative policy case study, this article examines the evolution of Iran’s petrochemical tax and export-duty policy from 2021 to 2025. The findings show that the initial approach sought to reduce the attractiveness of exporting basic and intermediate products by removing tax exemptions or imposing export duties. Evidence from the quantitative analysis reveals a structural imbalance between export volumes of raw materials (US$11.24 billion) and upstream and intermediate petrochemicals (US$11.43 billion) and the exports of downstream industry, which stood at US$0.36 billion in 2018. Import volumes of downstream industry were about US$0.56 billion and thus exceeded its export volumes. Policy projections for the modified tariff system generated about US$200 million in revenue. Taxes and tariffs can only support value chain upgrading if there is downstream capacity, comparative advantage, market demand, technological capability, and justifiable economies of scale. A comp…

title: Preoperative dual-energy computed tomography radiomics for prognosis of advanced gastric adenocarcinoma
abstract: BACKGROUND Gastric cancer remains a major global health burden. Many patients are diagnosed at an advanced stage and remain at high risk of recurrence despite curative-intent surgery. Although pathological tumor-node-metastasis (pTNM) staging is the cornerstone of prognostic assessment, patients within the same stage often show heterogeneous outcomes, suggesting that additional tumor biology-related information is needed to refine prognostic assessment. Dual-energy computed tomography (DECT)-derived iodine maps reflect tumor perfusion and vascularity, and radiomics can quantify subtle intratumoral heterogeneity. We hypothesized that iodine-map-based DECT radiomics, integrated with clinical factors, could improve individualized prognostic predictions in resectable advanced gastric adenocarcinoma. AIM To develop and validate DECT radiomics-based models for disease-free survival and overall survival prediction in resectable advanced gastric adenocarcinoma. METHODS This retrospective study included 175 patients with advanced gastric adenocarcinoma who underwent radical gastrectomy and were divided into training (n = 122) and validation (n = 53) groups. Radiomic features were extracted from venous-phase-blended images and iodine maps. Prognostic models based on pTNM staging, clinical factors, radiomics signature (Rad-score), and combined clinical-radiomics features were developed an…

title: Holographic Data Storage Devices: from Principles to Engineering Reality
abstract: Examines the fundamental principles of holographic data storage devices: volume recording, Bragg selectivity, and multiplexing methods. The classes of materials (photorefractive crystals, photopolymers), their advantages and limitations are analyzed. Contemporary challenges are discussed: cross-talk, energy efficiency, and scalability that hinder the mass adoption of the technology.

title: Cepillos dentales eléctricos frente a manuales en la higiene bucal: revisión narrativa de la evidencia
abstract: Objetivo: analizar la evidencia que compara la eficacia de los cepillos dentales eléctricos y manuales en la higiene bucal. Método: revisión narrativa con búsqueda en PubMed y SciELO de revisiones sistemáticas, ensayos clínicos y estudios clínicos en español o inglés; se analizaron 15 documentos. Resultados: las revisiones sistemáticas y los ensayos clínicos mostraron que los cepillos eléctricos, sobre todo los oscilantes-rotatorios, eliminaron más placa y redujeron más la gingivitis que los manuales, con diferencias modestas. El beneficio se observó en niños, adolescentes y personas con discapacidad, pero no fue consistente en pacientes con ortodoncia fija. Ambos fueron seguros para los tejidos. Conclusión: el cepillo eléctrico ofrece una ventaja moderada; la elección debe individualizarse según la destreza, las necesidades clínicas, el costo y la adherencia.

title: Automatic Termination Strategy of Inelastic Neutron-scattering Measurement Using Bayesian Optimization for Bin-width Selection
abstract: Currently, an excessive amount of event data is being obtained in four-dimensional inelastic neutron-scattering experiments. A method for automatic bin-width optimization of multidimensional histograms has been developed and recently validated on real inelastic neutron-scattering data. However, measuring beyond the equipment resolution leads to inefficient use of valuable beam time. To improve experimental efficiency, an automatic termination strategy is essential. We propose a Bayesian-optimization-based method to compute a stopping criterion that can support online decisions on whether to continue or terminate an experiment. In the proposed method, the bin-width optimization is performed using Bayesian optimization to efficiently compute the optimal bin widths. The experiment is terminated when the optimal bin widths become smaller than the target resolutions. In numerical experiments using real inelastic neutron-scattering data, the optimal bin widths decrease as the number of events increases. Even the optimal bin widths for data downsampled to 1/5 are comparable with the resolutions limited by the sample size, choppers, and so on. This implies excessive measurement of the inelastic neutron experiments for the moment. Moreover, we found that Bayesian optimization can reduce the search cost to approximately 10% of an exhaustive search in our numerical experiments.

Collaborative policing model: A community human resource strengthening strategy for crime prevention in Bandar Lampung’s urban residential areas
abstract: High property crime rates in the residential areas of Bandar Lampung City, combined with the unsustainability of previous security programs, demand adaptive crime prevention strategies. This study aimed to propose an exploratory collaborative policing model based on strengthening community human resources. Employing a quantitative survey with an accidental non-probability sampling design, data were collected from N = 467 residents across Bandar Lampung City. Exploratory Factor Analysis (EFA) using Principal Axis Factoring and Varimax rotation was conducted on 25 indicator items to map construct dimensionality. The EFA extracted eight main factors cumulatively explaining 63.88% of the data variance. Notably, the dimensions of technology & community collaboration (19.28%) and community virtual engagement (12.60%) accounted for the largest proportion of shared variance among the measured indicators (31.88% combined), reflecting shifting engagement preferences toward digital platforms among surveyed residents, who were predominantly under 25 years old. Based on these empirical response patterns, this study proposes an exploratory Community Human Resource-Based Collaborative Policing Model that integrates informal and formal agencies through communal digital channels, supported by the core pillars of collective efficacy, communication capacity, and digital literacy. The research imp…

title: Multi-objective reinforcement-learning simulation for co-optimizing resource circularity and environmental performance in circular manufacturing
abstract: More regulations require manufacturers to enhance material circularity and reduce their environmental footprint simultaneously; however, it remains unclear whether these two objectives align, and if so, in which domain. A discrete event simulation model for a remanufacturing plant operating multiple production lines with environmental performance measures at the process level is defined as a multiobjective Markov decision process, which is then solved using a preference-conditioned actor–critic technique, employing feasibility masking for the precedence and capacity constraints and adaptive sampling between the surrogate model and the full-scale simulator. Two life cycle accounting methods have been used: Boundary A (cut-off) and Boundary B (avoided burden). The environmental burden reveals three regimes, synergistic, trade-off, and inverted, characterized by transition points in secondary-material input levels at 0.38 and 0.61 for Boundary A and at 0.47 and 0.78 for Boundary B; sweeps with fixed ratios validate these transition points. One conditionally generated network accounts for 87.4% of the non-dominated solutions of eleven scalarized agents using 9.1% of the simulation budget allocated to them, and the switching strategy reduces the number of simulation calls needed to reach the reference hypervolume by 27.7%. A screening based on the unit-cost criterion limits the join…

H-VSAF: a verifiable and privacy-preserving federated learning framework for secure remote healthcare monitoring
abstract: The sensitive patient data handled by remote healthcare monitoring systems requires reliable, secure learning methods. Federated learning enables collaborative healthcare analytics without storing raw medical data centrally. However, existing techniques still suffer from issues including privacy leakage, untrusted aggregation, and frequent device outages. In this work, we propose H-VSAF, a privacy-preserving, verifiable, and lightweight federated learning system for healthcare environments. H-VSAF uses linear homomorphic hashing, Bloom filter-based online authentication, Shamir secret sharing, Diffie-Hellman key generation, and single-mask Secure Aggregation to ensure secrecy, precision, and resilience. The security analysis provides informal guarantees against gradient inference, aggregation tampering and deletion, and forged dropout claims under the threat model and cryptographic assumptions above. We experimentally evaluate H-VSAF on healthcare datasets and demonstrate that it achieves model accuracy within 0.2-0.8% of standard federated learning while decreasing client compute cost by up to 32% and communication overhead by 28% compared to traditional secure aggregation methods. Moreover, the framework is resilient to 40% client dropouts and introduces verification latency < 35 ms each round. The results clearly show that H-VSAF provides a credible and practical platform fo…

title: Global value chains, domestic value creation, and firm performance: machine learning evidence from Vietnam
abstract: This study examines the impact of domestic value added and participation in global value chains (GVCs) on firm performance, based on a sample of 287 observations from listed companies across five key industries in Vietnam's Southeast region during 2020-2024. Three machine learning methods, Ridge Regression, Random Forest, and Gradient Boosting, are applied to estimate the influence of each independent variable on firm performance. Ridge regression produced the best estimates of firm performance among these three model types, based on the lowest RMSE (4.97), MAE (2.78), and R-squared (0.57). This suggests that the relationship between GVC-related attributes and firm performance is largely linear and additive. Among the individual predictors, lagged profitability was the most important single predictor of current performance, followed by GVC activity. Notably, domestic added-value predicted firm performance more strongly than foreign added-value. Greater GVC activity therefore does not necessarily translate into stronger firm performance. Instead, firms appear to perform better when global engagement is combined with strong internal capabilities and substantial domestic value creation. Firm size, financial leverage, technological capability, and logistics efficiency also statistically explained variation in firm performance.

title: Comparative evaluation of milling machine tooling fixtures using finite geometry and finite element methods
abstract: Fixture layout directly affects workpiece stability during milling, but checking several possible locator arrangements with finite element analysis can be time-consuming, especially at the initial design stage. This study examines a milling machine angle plate fixture using a two-stage Finite Geometry (FG) and Finite Element Analysis (FEA) procedure based on the 3–2–1 locating principle. Three locator configurations were developed from the fixture geometry and first assessed using finite geometry. The Effective Support Area and Kinematic Stability Index (KSI) were used to assess the geometric stability of each arrangement, with MATLAB used to carry out the required geometric calculations. The KSI values obtained for Configurations 1, 2, and 3 were 0.01214, 0.01033, and 0.00772, respectively. Configuration 3 was consequently selected for structural assessment. The selected configuration was then analyzed in ANSYS Mechanical under a 10 kN distributed machining load. A maximum von Mises stress of 48.322 MPa and a maximum deformation of 0.015394 mm were obtained. The results show that the geometric assessment provided a means of screening the three locator arrangements before the more detailed finite element analysis was carried out. The study therefore demonstrates the use of FG as a preliminary assessment stage, followed by FEA for structural verification of the selected fixture …

title: Intelligent visual perception beyond classification: a survey of deep learning and foundation models
abstract: Intelligent visual perception has advanced from traditional image classification to thorough comprehension of objects, scenes, relations, spatial context, and semantic information. This paper surveys the development of intelligent visual perception, particularly focusing on DL and foundation models. This section provides a comprehensive overview of visual recognition, detection, segmentation, and scene understanding, including key methods such as convolutional neural networks, recurrent neural networks, attention mechanisms, encoder-decoder architectures, generative models, and Vision Transformers. The study also explores feature attribution, visual attention, visual reasoning, and multimodal vision-language models, which combine visual and text information for tasks such as visual question answering, captioning, and visual generation. This study examines recent foundation models incorporating vision-language architectures for their transferability, contextual understanding, and generalized perception capabilities. The study also discusses challenges related to computational efficiency, environmental variability, data requirements, robustness, explainability, and real-time deployment. Finally, it contrasts current developments to identify new approaches to scalable, interpretable, multimodal, and human-centric visual intelligence systems.

title: A hybrid heuristic–reinforcement learning method for multi-table join optimization in cloud-native databases
abstract: Multi-table join optimization in cloud-native databases faces challenges of storage-compute separation, resource elasticity, and runtime cost variation that classic optimizers cannot handle, which drives the need for methods able to adjust their decision boundaries according to the runtime behavior of the underlying cloud infrastructure. The proposed hybrid architecture freezes the stable sub-components of an IKKBZ-GOO heuristic seed plan into a structural freeze mask that constrains the learning algorithm throughout training, rather than being discarded after a single warm-start iteration. The mask works together with a state-aware cost function whose single state-dependent parameter is updated online. Two further components complete the design: a logistic gate trained on production telemetry, and a regression containment strategy that falls back to the heuristic plan when the learned plan underperforms. Training converges in 6.4 hours on one 16-vCPU compute node without GPU acceleration. The method was evaluated on the Join Order Benchmark, TPC-H, and TPC-DS, with PostgreSQL running on an eight-node Kubernetes cluster with object-store-backed shared storage. It achieves a geometric mean speedup of 1.38-fold on JOB, 1.28-fold on TPC-DS, and 1.07-fold on TPC-H, produces a query plan in 4.6 to 6.4 ms, returns median latency to within 5% of its pre-scaling value within 22 seconds…

title: Deep transfer learning and radiomics synergy for enhanced lung cancer classification on CT scans
abstract: Lung cancer remains one of the leading causes of cancer-related mortality worldwide, making accurate and timely detection essential for improving patient outcomes. Computed tomography (CT) is widely used for lung assessment; however, manual interpretation can be affected by inter-observer variability and subtle imaging characteristics. This study proposes an automated three-class lung CT classification framework that integrates deep transfer learning with quantitative lung-region features. EfficientNet-B7, initialized with ImageNet-pretrained weights, was employed to extract high-level deep representations from CT images. In parallel, lung Regions of Interest (ROIs) were automatically segmented, from which four quantitative descriptors were extracted: Skewness, Kurtosis, GLCM Contrast, and GLCM Homogeneity. The standardized lung-ROI features were subsequently concatenated with the EfficientNet-B7 deep feature representation using a feature-level fusion strategy and classified into Normal, Benign, and Malignant categories. Experimental evaluation on the held-out test set demonstrated an overall classification accuracy of 96.36%, correctly classifying 106 of 110 CT images. The proposed fusion framework achieved macro-averaged Precision, Recall, F1-score, and Specificity of 94.39%, 90.87%, 92.39%, and 97.53%, respectively. Furthermore, one-vs-rest ROC analysis yielded AUC values o…

title: Making Sense of Society: Exploring Senior High School Students’ Lived Experiences in Learning Araling Panlipunan
abstract: Araling Panlipunan plays an important role in developing learners’ understanding of society, history, culture, governance, citizenship, and contemporary social issues. Beyond acquiring factual knowledge, students are expected to interpret social realities, examine multiple perspectives, develop critical awareness, and connect classroom learning with their everyday experiences as members of communities and society. This qualitative phenomenological study explored the lived experiences of Senior High School students in learning Araling Panlipunan at Dimanayat Integrated School in Barangay Dimanayat, San Luis, Aurora, Philippines. Specifically, it examined how learners experienced classroom discussions, collaborative activities, inquiry-oriented tasks, contextualized lessons, and engagement with social issues, as well as the challenges and meanings they associated with learning the subject. Participants were selected through purposive criterion sampling, while data were gathered through semi-structured individual interviews and analyzed using reflexive thematic analysis. The proposed thematic analysis generated five interconnected themes: (1) Seeing Society Beyond the Textbook, (2) Finding Relevance Through Local and Everyday Experiences, (3) Learning Through Dialogue and Multiple Perspectives, (4) Wrestling With Complex and Contested Social Issues, and (5) Becoming More Socially …

title: Navigating Dual Responsibilities: Work-Life-Learning Balance Among Master in Business Administration Students in Northeastern College
abstract: Balancing employment, graduate education, and personal responsibilities has become a growing challenge for working professionals pursuing advanced degrees in public administration. This phenomenological study explored the lived experiences of Master in Business Administration (MBA) students at Northeastern College, Santiago City, Philippines, in managing work-life-learning balance. Guided by Husserlian phenomenology, the study sought to understand how graduate students navigate competing professional, academic, and personal demands while sustaining academic performance and personal well-being. Purposive sampling was employed to select fifteen MBA students who were simultaneously employed in government agencies, local government units, educational institutions, and private organizations. Data were gathered through semi-structured, in-depth interviews and analyzed using Colaizzi's seven-step phenomenological method. Findings revealed five essential themes: (1) navigating competing professional and academic responsibilities; (2) strategic time management and prioritization; (3) institutional and family support as catalysts for persistence; (4) psychological resilience amid multiple role demands; and (5) graduate education as a pathway toward professional advancement and public service excellence. Participants described balancing multiple responsibilities as challenging yet transfo…

title: Preparing Students in Technical Fields for the Application of Machine Learning Technologies
abstract: Examines the theoretical and practical aspects of preparing students of technical specialties to apply machine learning technologies in educational activities. The relevance of the study is обусловлена by the rapid development of artificial intelligence and the need to develop competencies among future specialists that enable them to use machine learning methods for analyzing educational data, predicting learning outcomes, personalizing educational trajectories, and automating individual pedagogical processes. The main components of student training are considered, including mathematical, algorithmic, programming, analytical, and project-based components. A step-by-step model for competency development is proposed, incorporating the study of machine learning fundamentals, data processing, model development and evaluation, solving practical educational problems, and developing students' own intelligent projects. Examples are provided of using linear regression to predict learning outcomes, classification to identify students at academic risk, and clustering to form groups of students with similar educational characteristics. The necessity of developing not only technical skills but also an ethical culture for the responsible use of intelligent technologies among students is substantiated.

title: Understanding Students’ Perceptions of Gamified Science Learning: A Descriptive Analysis of Teams Games Tournament in Environmental Pollution Education
abstract: Students’ perceptions provide important insights into how cooperative game-based learning is experienced in science classrooms; however, descriptive evidence concerning these perceptions in environmental pollution education remains limited, particularly in Indonesian junior high schools. This study examined Grade VII students’ perceptions of science learning through the Teams Games Tournament (TGT) model, focusing on instructional attractiveness, group participation, game-based activities, perceived ease of assessment tasks, and the relevance of learning content to everyday life. A descriptive quantitative survey with a cross-sectional, post-instruction design was conducted involving 120 students from four Grade VII classes at SMP Negeri 1 Turi, Lamongan, during the second semester of the 2021/2022 academic year. Data were collected using a ten-item questionnaire with a five-point Likert scale and analysed using descriptive statistics. Expert evaluation indicated that the questionnaire achieved a validity score of 91.13%, categorized as highly valid. The findings revealed generally positive student perceptions of TGT-based science learning. The highest proportion of agreement (74.17%) was observed for the statement concerning the attractiveness of group work and game activities, followed by the perceived relevance of environmental pollution content to everyday life (70.00%). title: Learning to Learn at the Graduate level: A phenomenological Exploration of Academic Adaptation and Pedagogical Experiences among MAEd students
abstract: Graduate education requires students to move beyond routine academic participation toward more independent, reflective, and self-directed learning. This phenomenological study explored how Master of Arts in Education (MAEd) students at Northeastern College experienced academic adaptation and developed learning skills within graduate-level pedagogy. The inquiry focused on how students adjusted to advanced academic expectations, managed competing responsibilities, engaged with research-oriented tasks, and responded to teaching practices that shaped their learning. Data were gathered through semi-structured interviews with purposively selected MAEd students and analyzed through phenomenological thematic procedures. Participants described both positive and negative experiences. Challenges included time pressure, academic writing difficulties, research anxiety, demanding readings, and balancing work and family responsibilities. Positive experiences included greater independence, stronger critical thinking, improved research competence, reflective practice, and increased confidence as professionals. The findings suggest that graduate pedagogy becomes more meaningful when it promotes active inquiry, scaffolded academic support, reflective learning, and flexible but rigorous engagement. The study highlights the importance of supporting MAEd students not only in mastering course content…

title: Digital Text-Based Learning as an Innovative Approach to Enhancing Critical Reading Literacy in Higher Education
abstract: In the twenty-first century, cultivating critical reading literacy is essential for university students navigating complex digital information. This study investigates the impact of Digital Text-Based Learning (DTBL) on advancing undergraduate students' critical reading proficiencies. Employing a pre-experimental one-group pre-test and post-test design, the research involved twenty-five students in an eight-week structured digital intervention. Data derived from measuring five distinct cognitive indicators were analyzed through paired sample testing and effect size calculations. The findings reveal a statistically significant enhancement in analytical capabilities, generating a remarkably large effect size. Interactive digital tools, such as collaborative annotations and lateral reading, successfully shifted habits from passive to active reading. The most growth occurred in identifying main ideas and evaluating arguments. While formulating evidence-based responses grew, it remained challenging primarily due to academic vocabulary constraints. Ultimately, integrating dynamic digital texts with explicit pedagogical frameworks successfully empowers students to critically evaluate modern information landscapes.

title: Integrating the Lesh translation model in e-learning to foster students’ numeracy skills
abstract: Although the Lesh Translation Model (LTM) has proven effective in addressing students' difficulties in translating mathematical ideas across representations, its application has so far been limited to face-to-face learning and its effectiveness when integrated into structured e-learning environments to improve students' numeracy skills has not been widely studied. This study aims to examine the effectiveness of integrating LTM into an e-learning platform (E-Numerasi) in enhancing students' numeracy skills compared to conventional instruction. This research uses a quasi-experimental pretest-posttest control group design and involves 119 eighth-grade students from two public junior high schools in Kuningan Regency, West Java, who were divided into an experimental group (n = 61) and a control group (n = 58). T-tests confirmed the equivalence of initial numeracy skills between the two groups prior to the intervention (p = 0.832). After the intervention, the experiment group obtained a significantly higher posttest mean score (M = 74.46) than the control group (M = 63.88), t(117) = 4.962; p < 0.001, supported by a moderate Normalized Gain (0.39) and a very large effect size (Cohen's d = 0.91). These results indicate that integrating the Lesh Translation Model into e-learning is significantly more effective in improving students' numeracy skills than conventional instruction.

Deep Q-network path planning with stratified sampling and prioritized replay
abstract: Deep reinforcement learning (DRL) has been widely adopted for mobile robot path planning in unknown and complex environments. However, existing DRL-based approaches suffer from two main limitations: sparse reward, which provides meaningful feedback only at terminal states, and experience heterogeneity, which reduces the efficiency of uniform sampling from the standard experience replay buffer due to the diversity of transition qualities stored within it. To tackle both issues at once, we propose SS-PER-DQN, a novel path-planning approach in which stratified sampling and a prioritized experience replay mechanism are incorporated into the Double Deep Q-Network. The memory buffer is divided into three priority layers based on temporal-difference error levels, with a dynamically varying sampling ratio between layers, and importance-sampling compensation to balance the sampling-distribution bias. A densely shaped reward function is additionally employed to expedite early exploration in the presence of sparsely rewarded actions in the environment. Experiments performed on Grid World and ROS Gazebo simulations show that the SS-PER-DQN is able to successfully plan paths at success rates of 94.5% and 89.0%, with a 24.5% and 21.8% reduction in path lengths, respectively, when compared to the traditional DQN algorithm, after convergence in approximately 53% fewer training episodes. abstract: The twenty-first century has brought significant changes that have transformed educational systems worldwide. Rapid technological advancement, digital transformation, globalization, demographic shifts, artificial intelligence, public health crises, and evolving societal expectations have created complex challenges for educational institutions. These conditions require educational leaders to adopt strategic leadership practices that strengthen organizational resilience, encourage innovation, and promote institutional sustainability. This study presents a systematic literature review and thematic synthesis examining the relationship among strategic leadership, innovation, organizational resilience, and sustainability in educational contexts. Relevant scholarly studies were systematically identified, screened, and analyzed using academic databases, including Scopus, Web of Science, Google Scholar, and other scholarly sources. Guided by a systematic review approach and thematic analysis, the selected literature was examined to identify recurring patterns and emerging insights. The synthesis revealed five major themes: (1) increasing uncertainty and complexity in educational institutions; (2) strategic leadership as a driver of organizational adaptability; (3) innovation and digital transformation as catalysts for resilience; (4) collaborative governance and stakeholder engagement a…

abstract: As a renewable alternative to fossil fuels, the production of bioethanol and biochemicals from lignocellulosic biomass has drawn significant interest. For biochemical conversion, pretreatement is the most crucial step, which removes biomass recalcitrance to improve cellulose’s accessibility for enzymatic saccharification and fermentation. This study investigated the potential of dilute sulfuric acid pretreatment of waste rice straw to produce building-block sugars and bioethanol. The study focused on optimizing several key parameters, including dilute acid concentration (60 mM), pretreatment time (30 minutes), pretreatment temperature (120°C), and liquid-to-solid ratio (5:1). This study also compared the efficiency of dilute acid pretreatment of rice straw with conventional dilute alkali and organosolv pretreatment techniques. The results showed that dilute acid pretreatment effectively dissolved a significant amount of hemicellulose under these circumstances, retaining 97.96% of cellulose in the solid substrate, which led to 64.28% glucose yield in enzymatic saccharification. The rice straw structure underwent morphological changes (i.e., cell wall rupture and changes in crystallinity) as the result of acid pretreatment, which were confirmed using SEM and XRD techniques. title: Stochastic Model for Optimal Control of Water Resource Treatment under Random Disturbances
abstract: This study addresses the problem of optimal control of water resource treatment under stochastic uncertainty and random external disturbances. A mathematical model describing the dynamics of water pollution is developed in the form of a stochastic differential equation, which accounts for the influence of random environmental factors on the treatment process. The corresponding optimal control problem is formulated using a quadratic performance functional that characterizes the trade-off between minimizing the pollution level and reducing the costs associated with water treatment. The stochastic Pontryagin maximum principle is applied to derive the necessary optimality conditions for the control strategy. A numerical example is presented to demonstrate the applicability of the proposed model and to evaluate the resulting optimal control strategy under stochastic disturbances. The obtained results demonstrate the potential of the proposed approach for developing environmentally sound and economically efficient strategies for water resource management under uncertainty.

title: AI-driven multi-objective optimization of CNC machining parameters for enhanced surface finish and tool life
abstract: AI-driven CNC machining optimization requires balancing surface quality and productivity while avoiding unsupported integration of independently collected machining data. This study proposes a leakage-controlled, surrogate-assisted framework using two open datasets: a 27-condition turning surface-quality dataset and a 968-observation milling tool-life dataset comprising 14 tools. The datasets were analyzed independently, with no row-wise fusion or DOC–ADOC mapping. Cutting speed, feed rate, and depth of cut were used as controllable turning variables, while milling sensor and metadata features were used separately for remaining useful life (RUL) prediction. The selected Ridge surface model achieved LOOCV MAE = 0.1077, RMSE = 0.1383, and , while nested validation yielded , indicating limited out-of-sample generalization. The no-cycle RUL model achieved MAE = 23.44 cycles, RMSE = 31.39 cycles, and under leave-one-tool-out validation. NSGA-II significantly outperformed equal-budget random search in normalized hypervolume (0.7711 vs. 0.7421). Because the surrogate surface was statistically limited, continuous optimization was treated as exploratory. Final selection was therefore anchored to measured Pareto-efficient turning conditions. Equal-weight TOPSIS selected , , and , with measured and , as the balanced practical recommendation.

title: Constraint internalization through parametric reconstruction: A legality-aware framework for geometric optimization problems
abstract: Geometric optimization problems such as \(PA + k \cdot PB\) are commonly solved using reflection methods, projection techniques, or calculus-based optimization. In elementary treatments, these approaches often assume that signed algebraic expressions directly represent non-negative geometric distances across the entire real domain. When the variable extends beyond the traditional geometric boundary, this implicit assumption fails, creating what we describe as a representation legality gap. In this paper, we propose a parametric reconstruction framework that internalizes geometric admissibility constraints into the algebraic representation. Rather than partitioning the variable domain through piecewise case distinctions, we introduce an admissible auxiliary scaffold parameter \(L \ge x\) to decompose the objective function into a geometrically legal core path and an algebraically compensating residual. The auxiliary parameter \(L\) cancels identically in the reconstructed representation, ensuring global validity across \(\mathbb{R}\). title: Optimization and Automation as Efficiency Drivers: From Corporate Operations to Intellectual Property Management
abstract: In the context of the digital transformation of the economy, optimization and automation of business processes are becoming key factors in improving the efficiency of corporate governance. The article examines the relationship between the introduction of intelligent systems and the growth of operational efficiency using the example of two areas: automation of corporate operations and management of intellectual activity results. Based on the analysis of practical cases of the implementation of intelligent management systems in Russian companies, including the experience of large retail chains, the contradictory effects of large-scale algorithmization of managerial processes are revealed. Standardization and improvement of average operational efficiency indicators at the initial stages of digital transformation are accompanied by risks of leveling the unique competencies of managers and reducing the adaptability of organizations to changes in the external environment. The paper proposes a model of phased digital transformation, including inventory of business processes, implementation of SLA metrics, automation of time tracking, and formation of an intellectual property management system. title: Integrated genetic and phenotypic characterization of doubled haploid lines in onion (Allium cepa L.)
abstract: Abstract Accurate identification of haploids, doubled haploids (DHs), and diploids is a critical step in the successful implementation of DH technology. This study aimed to establish a reliable framework for ploidy identification in onion by integrating flow cytometry, simple sequence repeat (SSR) marker analysis, stomatal characterization, and morphological evaluation, while assessing the potential of stomatal traits as a rapid and cost-effective screening approach. Flow cytometric analysis successfully distinguished haploid, diploid, and mixoploid regenerants based on nuclear DNA content, whereas SSR markers were used to confirm the homozygous nature of DH plants. Polymorphic SSR markers produced single-band profiles in DH plants, in contrast to the heterozygous banding patterns observed in donor plants, validating the genetic identity of DH regenerants. Significant differences were detected among haploid, DH, and diploid plants for all evaluated stomatal traits. Stomatal length, width, and index increased with increasing ploidy level, with diploid plants exhibiting the highest values, DH plants showing intermediate values, and haploid plants displaying the lowest values. Conversely, stomatal density showed a negative association with ploidy level, with haploid plants exhibiting the highest stomatal density and diploid plants the lowest. abstract: BACKGROUND Sodium taurocholate cotransporting polypeptide deficiency (NTCPD) causes persistent hypercholanemia and neonatal cholestasis, but its genotypic and phenotypic spectrum across ethnicities and geographic backgrounds remains poorly characterized. AIM To characterize the genetic architecture, biochemical trajectories, and genotype-phenotype correlations of NTCPD in a multi-ethnic pediatric cohort. METHODS In this case cohort study, we analyzed 125 patients with genetically confirmed NTCPD from Kunming Children’s Hospital (2020-2025). Longitudinal biochemical parameters were tracked, and multivariable regression was performed to assess genotype-biochemical relationships, adjusting for age, ethnicity, and geographic location. RESULTS The cohort comprised 69 male and 56 female patients (83 homozygous, 25 heterozygous, and 17 compound heterozygous). The c.800C>T variant was present in all compound heterozygotes, together with 11 additional variants (four likely pathogenic variants and seven variants of uncertain significance). The cohort comprised 73 Han and 52 individuals from ethnic minority groups, predominantly Yi and Hui, distributed across 15 prefectures. Biochemical profiles indicated self-limiting hypercholanemia, with total bile acid levels declining from 178.8 ± 60.9 µmol/L (0-2 months) to 141.2 ± 77.9 µmol/L (> 4 months, P = 0.0002). title: Probabilistic-temporal modeling of network security monitoring subprocesses for multi-stage attacks in IoT networks
abstract: Timely detection of a multistage cyberattack in an IoT network depends on the chosen monitoring architecture, execution time, and the transition behavior of subprocesses within that architecture. This paper introduces a probabilistic temporal model to evaluate an NSMS for both known and unknown multi-stage attacks. First, we introduce a conceptual monitoring architecture that organizes streaming-data processing, temporal analysis, attack classification, attack prediction, and response selection. The recurrent neural networks in the architecture form the basis of the implementation framework and are neither trained nor empirically analyzed. The evaluated contribution represents the NSMS subprocesses as a continuous-time Markov chain, where each state corresponds to a monitoring task and each transition rate is estimated from the respective mean processing time. We develop state-probability equations and use a specialized software tool to estimate the stationary probabilities and successful anomaly-detection probabilities. Numerical evaluations examine how delays in preprocessing, syntactic construction, encoding, classification, and prediction affect monitoring effectiveness. title: Multi-agent generative AI ecosystems for cyber-physical systems in Industry 5.0
abstract: Cyber-Physical Systems (CPSs) are increasingly being implemented in critical industrial infrastructure, where complexity and interdependence are rising, posing significant cyber and operational risks. Traditional anomaly detection algorithms can be ineffective in capturing temporal dynamics, relational dependencies, and interpretable response requirements. The present paper proposes a multi-agent generative AI system to detect CPS anomalies and provide decision support by combining temporal feature encoding, relational modeling as graphs, supervised learning, and reasoning with an LLM. The architecture consists of detection, diagnosis, planning, governance, and human-in-the-loop validation agents. The framework is tested on the SWaT benchmark data. Findings indicate that the Autoencoder, LSTM, and 1D-CNN are more effective in terms of raw detection metrics, whereas the Random Forest provides more interpretable and agent-readable evidence to support the post-detection decision. Analysis of features and sensor family suggests the relevance of relational dependencies in characterizing anomalies. The multi-agent layer converts selected anomaly predictions into context-dependent explanations and governance-filtered recommendations to aid operator review, response planning, and process resilience. Overall, the framework supports transparent and human-supervised CPS anomaly management…

abstract: Purpose: This study examines the influence of sales promotion content, content attractiveness, and user-friendliness on financial decision making through imitation intention among social media users in Indonesia, particularly in the context of influencer marketing for Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) in the food and beverage sector. Data are collected through an online questionnaire using a five-point Likert scale and purposive sampling. Data analysis employs Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) using SmartPLS. Results and Discussion: The study proposes that sales promotion content, content attractiveness, and user-friendliness influence imitation intention and financial decision making. Imitation intention is also expected to influence financial decision making and mediate the relationships between promotional content characteristics and financial decisions. These relationships will be evaluated empirically. title: Peran Financial self-efficacy dalam Memoderasi Literasi Keuangan Digital, Herding behavior, dan Perilaku Keuangan Mahasiswa
abstract: This study aims to analyze the influence of digital financial literacy and herding behavior on financial behavior, as well as to examine the role of financial self-efficacy as a moderating variable. The study sample consisted of economics education students from State University of Malang and State University of Surabaya. Data were collected using questionnaires. A quantitative approach was employed, utilizing multiple linear regression and Moderated Regression Analysis (MRA). The results indicate that digital financial literacy has a positive and significant effect on financial behavior, whereas herding behavior has a negative and significant effect. Moderation analysis reveals that financial self-efficacy strengthens the impact of digital financial literacy on financial behavior and weakens the impact of herding behavior on financial behavior. These findings suggest that enhancing digital financial literacy can foster better financial behavior, while the tendency to follow others' financial decisions can diminish the quality of financial behavior.

title: Financial Development, Foreign Direct Investment, Government Expenditure and Economic Growth in Sub-Saharan Africa: A Joint-Effect and Causality Analysis
abstract: Financial development, foreign direct investment (FDI) and government expenditure are well-established drivers of growth but are rarely studied together. This study examines their joint effect on economic growth in 45 Sub-Saharan African countries over 2002–2021, using correlation analysis, pairwise Granger causality tests and a six-step hierarchical fixed-effects panel regression with country-clustered standard errors. The predictors are jointly significant (F(6, 659) = 10.71, p < 0.001), though within-country explanatory power is modest (within R² = 0.089). Broad money (β = −0.097, p < 0.001) and interest rate spread (β = −0.017, p < 0.001) reduce growth, gross capital formation raises it (β = 0.081, p = 0.011), and domestic credit, FDI and government consumption have no significant contemporaneous effect; in a lagged specification FDI raises growth one year later (β = 0.078, p < 0.001). Granger tests show broad money and interest rate spread are bidirectionally related to growth, private credit is demand-following, and gross capital formation and government consumption Granger-cause growth without feedback. Growth within SSA economies responds to intermediation efficiency and productive investment rather than financial depth, and the FDI dividend materialises with a lag.
