title: Socio-Demographic and Political Factors Associated with Attitudes Toward Electoral Reform in the Philippines, Indonesia, and Mexico
abstract: Public evaluations of electoral reform are shaped by social position, political affiliation, and assessments of electoral institutions. Objective: This review examines socio-demographic and political factors associated with attitudes toward electoral reform in the Philippines, Indonesia, and Mexico. A narrative thematic synthesis was conducted using 24 publication records designated in the author-supplied extraction worksheet. The evidence included quantitative studies, qualitative and descriptive studies, legal and institutional analyses, and secondary research. Perceived fairness, institutional trust, and representation were distinguished from expressed support for or opposition to reform. Evidence from Indonesia foregrounds political information, representation, and party or leader cues; Mexican studies emphasize partisanship, electoral integrity, and institutional trust; Philippine research contributes primarily institutional and voter-information context. Education appears relevant where measured, whereas chronological age and income are insufficiently assessed for robust cross-national comparisons. The evidence remains uneven in geographic coverage, study design, and outcome measurement. title: The Role of Trust and Local Presence in Selling IT Outsourcing Services in the United States Market
abstract: The United States market for information technology outsourcing combines intense competition with long, multi-stage procurement, making price and technical skills weaker predictors of who wins a contract than they once were. This paper examines how trust and local presence shape the outcome of business-to-business deals for software development services in that market. The analysis draws on the management practice of a vendor that employs around 3500 people and sells primarily to clients in the United States and Canada, and it treats anonymized deal episodes as the empirical material. The argument develops in three steps. The first step maps the barriers that define the market, where buyers expect a provider to understand their business quickly and to work as if it were an internal team. The second step explains why clients reward the provider they trust the most, even when a cheaper option exists, and it shows how expertise, flexibility, and risk reduction combine into a single perception of dependability. The third step describes the shift toward an onshore model and a local office, opening segments that an offshore provider cannot reach and increasing conversion rates in large enterprise deals. title: Tensões entre mercado global, identidade nacional e reerguimento de fronteiras
abstract: Contemporary international relations reveal a scenario increasingly shaped by tensions between the integrative logic of the global market and the identity-driven forces fueling nationalism. Across the world, a renewed emphasis on physical and symbolic borders emerges as a reaction to the economic, cultural, and political uncertainties associated with globalization. This contradictory movement reflects the simultaneous advance of two historical vectors: on one hand, the consolidation of transnational flows of capital, technology, and information; on the other, the resurgence of discourses around sovereignty, economic protection, and cultural exclusion. While corporations and multilateral institutions extend their influence beyond nation-states, governments adopt defensive strategies based on restrictive immigration policies, trade barriers, and the reinforcement of national identities. This ambivalence highlights the crisis of the post-Cold War liberal global order, challenging ideals of interdependence and international cooperation. Moreover, the rise of populist leaderships in different contexts amplifies the political use of borders as symbols of control and autonomy in response to a perceived global inequality. Existing research has widely examined these factors in isolation, whereas rare attention has been given to their combined direct, mediating, and moderating relationships grounded in the dynamic capabilities view, ecological modernization, and feminist institutionalism theories across the EU member states. Hence, this study primarily aims to examine the direct association among the outlined factors. Secondly, it examines the mediating role of circular economy between digitalization and sustainable market competitiveness, the mediating role of circular economy between green finance and sustainable market competitiveness, and the mediating role of green finance between digitalization and circular economy. title: An Investigation of Market Invariance for the Tokyo Stock Exchange
abstract: ABSTRACT We test the invariance‐of‐bet hypothesis from Kyle and Obizhaeva (2016) for the Tokyo Stock Exchange (TSE). The pooled regression coefficients of the logarithm of the number of trades on the logarithm of the product of volume and volatility range from 0.663 to 0.665, close to the theoretical value of two‐thirds predicted by the invariance‐of‐bet hypothesis. Using the TSE as a relatively clean benchmark, we further examine when the empirical two‐thirds relation deviates from its theoretical prediction. We find that deviations become more pronounced during extreme market conditions, for stocks facing more binding tick‐size constraints, and around the market open and close. Our results also suggest that measurement errors in transaction data can contribute to deviations from the two‐thirds relation.

title: Sustainability‐Related Information and Secondary‐Market Corporate‐Bond Spreads: Disclosure, Verification, and Contractual Commitment
abstract: ABSTRACT This study examines whether observable disclosure environments are associated with secondary‐market pricing in a global sample of corporate bonds containing a sustainable‐classified subset. Using corporate bonds from LSEG Workspace, the analysis relates option‐adjusted spreads to three dimensions of sustainability‐related information architecture: disclosure, external verification, and contractual commitment. Disclosure is negatively associated with option‐adjusted spreads in cross‐sectional specifications, but issuer fixed‐effects and within‐between estimates indicate that this association is primarily between issuers rather than within issuers. The principal zero‐versus‐positive Disclosure comparison has observed support among nonclassified bonds; classified bonds have no zero‐Disclosure observations. Moreover, the Disclosure Index ranges from 0 to 2 among nonclassified bonds and from 3 to 5 among classified bonds in the support sample, preventing a like‐for‐like comparison across classification groups at a common index value. Verification is positively associated with spreads in conventional joint specifications but is insignificant when recorded classification is included; its positive values occur exclusively among classified bonds in the support sample. Contractual commitment has sparse support. These findings describe conditional associations for outstanding bon…

title: Intermediate-Layer Governance and the Coupling of an Effective Market and a Proactive Government: A Mechanism-Based Analysis of Practices in the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area
abstract: Within the broader context of the "One Country, Two Systems, Three Legal Systems" framework, the cross-border flow of production factors among Guangdong, Hong Kong, and Macao has long faced a dual dilemma: high institutional convergence costs and the risk of market failure when governance remains laissez-faire. This paper argues that intermediate-level governance represents a third pathway to resolve this dilemma and achieve an effective synergy between an efficient market and an active government. Building upon transaction cost theory and drawing on the core institutional innovation practices within the Guangdong–Hong Kong–Macao Greater Bay Area, this study examines the mechanism and practical outcomes of intermediate-level governance, identifies the barriers to deepening such governance, and proposes pathways for improvement, thereby providing empirical insights for governance innovation in diverse institutional environments.

abstract: A mass circumcision social service initiative serves as a form of community-based healthcare, bringing essential medical services closer to the public. This activity, which provides circumcision services through a collaboration between professional organizations and the local government, was held to commemorate the 62nd National Health Day in 2026. It took place on November 14, 2026, in Bonto Tinggi, Tondong Kura Village, Tondong Tallasa District, Pangkep Regency. The event was organized by the Pangkep Regency branch of the Indonesian National Nurses Association (PPNI) in partnership with the Pangkep Regency Health Office. The initiative successfully delivered mass circumcision services, representing a joint contribution from professional organizations and the local government toward public healthcare. This cross-institutional collaboration serves as a vital approach to supporting the delivery of community-based health services.

title: PROVISION OF THE “PERSONAL ASSISTANT” SOCIAL SERVICE TO PEOPLE WITH INTELLECTUAL DISABILITIES
abstract: Relevance. The development of social services that support independent living and the participation of people with disabilities in community life is an important aspect of transforming Ukraine’s social support system. Personalized assistance is particularly important for adults with intellectual disabilities, who may require individualized support with daily activities, communication, and social interaction. Aim. To analyze the implementation of the personal assistant social service for people with intellectual disabilities, using the activities of the Shliakh Dobra (“Path of Goodness”) civic organization in the Uman territorial community as a case study, and to identify the organizational conditions needed for its further development. Methods. The study draws on an analysis of documents and materials from the organization’s practical activities, a comparative analysis of project implementation stages in 2024–2026, and a qualitative synthesis of documented experience in personal assistance. The empirical basis consists of information on assistant recruitment, the number of people receiving support, the organization of assistance, and service coordination. Quantitative indicators are treated as measures of project implementation rather than as results of a standardized effectiveness assessment. Results. The findings reveal the gradual development of personal assistance practices…

title: Evolution of a hospital-integrated online consultation service: a five-year descriptive study of utilization, expenditure, and insurance coverage
abstract: Abstract Background Online medical services are increasingly integrated into routine healthcare delivery, but evidence on the long-term evolution of hospital-integrated online consultation services remains limited. This study described changes in utilization, clinical scope, patient age distribution, expenditure composition, and medical insurance coverage over five years. Methods This retrospective repeated cross-sectional study used administrative outpatient data from a tertiary specialist hospital between 2021 and 2025. Annual utilization, age distribution, expenditure composition, and payment mechanisms were examined descriptively. An exploratory interrupted time-series analysis assessed changes in the monthly proportion of online consultations following the institutional implementation of expanded medical insurance mobile payment in June 2024. Results Online consultations increased from 62 in 2021 to 29,842 in 2025, accounting for 9.5% of total outpatient visits, while participating clinical specialties increased from 4 to 18. Across the full study period, in-person and total outpatient activity decreased by 13.8% and 4.7%, respectively, with most of the decline occurring in 2022. During the more comparable period from 2023 to 2025, online, in-person, and total outpatient activity increased by 58.3%, 3.0%, and 6.6%, respectively. The medication share of online-associated ex…

Context-aware forecasting of inter-firm competitive dynamics with graph learning and multi-agent reasoning
abstract: Abstract The evolution of competitive dominance in technology-intensive industries is shaped by complex interactions among research activity, media visibility, strategic disclosures, public attention, and market signals. Understanding these dynamics is critical for strategic intelligence, yet existing predictive models often treat firms as isolated entities and provide limited support for contextualizing long-horizon firm-to-firm competitive forecasts. Here, we introduce an integrated framework that captures the relational nature of market competition by extending our prior Bayesian Multivariate Time-series Graph Neural Network with a newly designed, post hoc, lookahead-free multi-agent reasoning layer. The framework infers inter-firm relational dependencies endogenously from multimodal signals to forecast latent firm competitiveness and pairwise competitive gap trajectories with quantified predictive uncertainty. To evaluate strategic plausibility, specialized persona-driven language model agents critique the forecasted trajectories across technological, financial, and regulatory lenses using retrieved evidence. Evaluated under a rigorous date-based temporal protocol with strictly withheld test horizons, the framework consistently outperforms competitive structural baselines and yields well-calibrated prediction intervals. When applied to thirty leading AI-oriented technology …

title: Forecasting Respiratory Syncytial Virus Activity Using Seasonal ARIMA Models: Evidence from CDC Weekly Surveillance Data
abstract: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) imposes seasonal operational pressure on paediatric care and hospital healthcare systems. This study evaluates whether weekly RSV test percent positivity data from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) National Respiratory and Enteric Virus Surveillance System (NREVSS) can support short-term forecasting of RSV transmission activity. The national weekly surveillance dataset spanning 3 January 2015 to 27 June 2020 was analyzed with four forecasting approaches: seasonal autoreggressive integrated moving average (SARIMA), non-seasonal autoregressive integrated moving average (ARIMA), exponential smoothing (ETS), and a seasonal naive benchmark model. Model predictive performance was validated via a 52-week chronological holdout sample and rolling-origin forecasts for 1–4 week ahead horizons. Multiple evaluation metrics were adopted, including root mean square error (RMSE), mean absolute error (MAE), symmetric mean absolute percentage error (sMAPE), directional accuracy, and peak-timing error. Exploratory time-series analyses verified prominent annual seasonality and short-term serial dependence embedded in RSV percent positivity time series. Among all candidate models, SARIMA yielded the smallest RMSE and MAE on the holdout dataset, and exhibited relatively robust performance as the forecast window extended. The overall findings demon…

title: Short-Term Forecasting of Weekly Dengue Cases in Singapore Using ARIMA and Fourier-ARIMA Models
abstract: In this paper, a clear case-only forecasting model is developed on weekly basis. Dengue in Singapore based on official surveillance data between 2012-W01 and 2026.W17. The paper questions whether the number of cases routinely reported can be useful on their own. Short-term warning information in cases when external covariates are not available or are delayed. Dengue Fever and Dengue Haemorrhagic Fever cases were aggregated on a weekly basis, converted with log(1 + cases), tested to be stationary, and modelled using Autoregressive Integrated Moving Average (ARIMA). And Fourier-ARIMA specifications. Candidate models were compared through residual diagnostics, information criteria, and recursive one-week-ahead validation on the final 10% of the series. ARIMA(4,1,0)+Fourier(2) was selected because it balanced point accuracy, residual adequacy, and parsimony. In the 75-week test period, the model achieved MAE of 11.6 cases and RMSE of 16.0 cases, while 90% prediction interval coverage was 80%. The framework is therefore potentially useful as interpretable and timely surveillance decision support for early warning and preparedness, but it should be combined with field intelligence and future calibration work.

The Role of Risk‐Neutral Moments in Forecasting Future Realised Variance: An International Perspective
abstract: ABSTRACT This paper estimates the predictability of future realised variance for eight stock markets using US‐listed proxy ETFs, based on their risk‐neutral variance, skewness, and excess kurtosis. Our evidence shows that risk‐neutral variance and skewness have a positive relationship with future realised variance, while excess kurtosis has a negative relationship. Results from various statistical tests for model comparison indicate that incorporating second and higher‐order risk‐neutral moments from specific market proxies, as well as aggregated moments across market proxies, into the HAR‐RV model enhances the predictability of future realised variance. The inclusion of these moments provides additional information, significantly improving forecasting power and reducing extreme underestimation. Moreover, portfolio allocation exercises demonstrate that these improvements can translate into economically meaningful certainty‐equivalent return gains.

BriefCensus: A short metering campaign that chooses permanent monitors for rooftop photovoltaic fleet estimation and forecasting
abstract: Most rooftop photovoltaic (PV) systems report no live generation, so operators estimate fleet output from a few monitors, yet the metering needed to choose those monitors remains unclear. BriefCensus chooses permanent monitors from a short temporary metering campaign. Its forward greedy search matches the capacity-weighted ratio of the campaign set with no fitted weights, so the estimate needs no refit when a monitor fails. Its outage filter removes campaign rows with under half of the capacity reporting, because such rows otherwise reward survival during data outages. A logged confirmation run on 16 UK regions, without the filter, passed its rule at four weeks and kept 0.68 of the one-year selection gain. With the filter, added after that run, four weeks kept 0.82 on 12 regions of unread systems and cut the error by 27% against random monitors at k = 10. An Australian hold-out agreed. In the retrospective forecast experiment, the largest gains from monitor selection occurred at 0.5 h and 1 h. The simulated campaigns support testing a one-month metering campaign in the field. Keywords: Rooftop Photovoltaics, Fleet Estimation, Reference Systems, Monitor Selection, Measurement Campaign, Short-Term Forecasting.

title: A Physically Interpretable Dual‐Encoder Cross‐Attention LSTM for Water Level Forecasting in Dam–Tide Interaction Systems
abstract: ABSTRACT Predicting the water level in real time in regulated tidal rivers is challenging because upstream dam releases and downstream tidal fluctuations act simultaneously, with their relative dominance shifting within an event. Attention‐based deep learning models for such systems have generally either mixed all forcings within a single encoder, meaning no forcing‐level attribution can be recovered, or distributed attention across variable–lag pairs in a self‐attention stream. This makes it impossible to read the relative influence of two named physical forcings. This study proposes a dual‐encoder cross‐attention long short‐term memory (LSTM) framework that separates the forcings at the encoder level rather than the attention level. Dam discharge and tidal stage are encoded by dedicated bidirectional long short‐term memory (BiLSTM) encoders. Attention is then applied at two levels: temporal cross‐attention with a per‐horizon query and channel attention normalized over the two forcings. When applied to the Gahwa River Basin, which is subject to releases from the Namgang Dam and tidal forcing from Sacheon Bay, the framework was evaluated across 12 flood events using event‐based cross‐validation. Predictions from 1 to 12 h ahead were benchmarked against those from a single‐encoder LSTM. The two models performed comparably at short lead times. Beyond 5–6 h, however, the baseline …

title: Hybrid Seamless Seasonal‐to‐Annual Forecasting for the Wind Energy Sector Over the Americas
abstract: Abstract Wind power generation is sensitive to atmospheric variability across seasonal to annual timescales, creating demand for climate information that is both skilful and temporally consistent. Here we develop a hybrid seamless seasonal‐to‐decadal forecasting framework for annual wind speed over the Americas. The hybrid system combines dynamical predictions from seasonal and decadal forecast systems with a statistical multilinear regression model driven by four large‐scale ocean–atmosphere variability indices. Temporal consistency is achieved by constraining decadal ensemble members according to their agreement with updated seasonal predictions, avoiding discontinuities when transitioning across forecast horizons. Results show that the hybrid framework provides skilful wind predictions in key wind energy regions of the Americas, including the Great Plains and northeastern Brazil, and in some cases outperforms dynamical‐only forecasts, while preserving forecast continuity across timescales. These findings demonstrate the potential of combining seamless dynamical predictions with statistical post‐processing for wind energy climate services.

title: Regime-Gated Feedback Adaptive Conformal Prediction for Financial Forecasting
abstract: Financial prediction intervals must respond to volatility clustering and abrupt shifts in forecast-error distributions. We propose regime-gated feedback adaptive conformal inference (RG-ACI), which combines volatility-normalized nonconformity scores, rolling calibration, a single online miscoverage-rate state and a causal short-to-long volatility-ratio gate. Building on the finance-specific score normalization of Chen et al., the method couples a retrospective coverage correction with an ex-ante volatility signal without introducing a second error-feedback state. On 20 simulated heavy-tailed, autoregressive stochastic-volatility paths with multiple regime transitions, RG-ACI attains 0.895 mean coverage and 0.894 crisis-period coverage at a nominal 90% target with low between-path dispersion, while volatility-normalized rolling calibration remains the most efficient interval in width and interval score. Component ablations separate the effects of error-rate adaptation, the volatility gate and feedback gain, and quantify the calibration–efficiency tradeoff of each. The contribution is an explicitly causal, single-state integration of feedback and regime gating together with a transparent analysis of its tradeoffs under designed distribution shifts.

title: Multicollinearity Problem in Prediction of Egg Albumen Index and Some Regression Methods
abstract: Research on Japanese quail (Coturnix coturnix japonica) eggs examined factors affecting albumen index prediction and evaluated the multicollinearity problem among egg quality traits. The study included egg weight, egg width, egg length, shape index, and Haugh unit as explanatory variables for predicting albumen index. Correlation analysis results showed a high positive relationship (r=0.85) between egg weight and egg width and a high negative relationship (r=−0.91) between egg length and shape index. Variance inflation factor (VIF) values ranging from 1.41 to 30.30 indicated the presence of strong multicollinearity within the dataset. To overcome the effects of multicollinearity, principal component regression (PCR) and penalty-based regression methods including Ridge, LASSO, Liu, and Elastic Net were applied. PCR analysis showed that the first two principal components explained 75% of the total variance, demonstrating the effectiveness of dimension reduction. Ridge regression stabilized coefficient estimates by retaining all variables, whereas LASSO controlled model complexity through coefficient shrinkage. Liu regression provided stable coefficient estimates under correlated variable structures, while Elastic Net combined L1 and L2 penalties to regulate coefficient selection. The comparison of model performance criteria demonstrated that PCR, Ridge, and LASSO regression model…

title: Applications of Deep Learning Algorithms in Protein Structure Prediction and Design
abstract: The three-dimensional configuration of a protein is important for its biological function, which is crucial in biological study and drug development. The progress of deep learning has greatly improved the prediction of protein structures. Especially, the AlphaFold series has increased the prediction precision and extended its use in the simulation of biomolecular complexes and drug discovery. This paper describes the latest progress in protein structure prediction and antibody design based on deep learning. The emphasis is on the enhancement and efficiency of the template-based method and the AlphaFold series. Furthermore, the practical applications of these methods in antibody engineering and drug discovery are illustrated by considering specific examples such as AbEgDiffuser for simultaneous sequence and structure design, and AlphaFold3 for the choice of covalent ligands. Experimental data indicate that deep learning can precisely forecast the protein structures and effectively improve the design and screening of potential substances, thereby offering new possibilities for rational drug design. In the future, more research should concentrate on predicting the conformational changes of proteins, designing novel antibody frameworks from scratch, and obtaining multiple drug-like properties at the same time.

Machine-learning-assisted prediction and optimization of tensile strength in particulate-filled polymer composites
abstract: Abstract Particulate-filled polymer composites (PFPCs) are characterized by high specific strength, good formability, and considerable design flexibility, making them key materials for rapid tooling in aerospace equipment manufacturing. In this study, metal-powder/resin composites were investigated, and a tensile-strength dataset comprising 45 independent experimental conditions was established. Three machine-learning regression algorithms, namely linear least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression, k-nearest neighbors (KNN), and support vector regression (SVR), were employed to develop tensile-strength prediction models. A fixed outer five-fold cross-validation procedure was used to obtain out-of-fold (OOF) predictions, while hyperparameters were selected through inner five-fold cross-validation within each outer training fold; a genetic algorithm (GA) was subsequently used to further optimize the SVR hyperparameters. The OOF RMSE, MAE, and R² values of SVR were 1.67 MPa, 1.32 MPa, and 0.882, respectively, and those of GA-SVR were 1.54 MPa, 1.21 MPa, and 0.901. With increasing particle volume fraction and particle size, the tensile strength initially increased and then decreased, whereas ball-milling time had a relatively limited effect. title: Physics‐Constrained Recurrent Prediction of Fatigue Stiffness Degradation in Composite Laminates Under Constant‐Amplitude and Two‐Stage Variable‐Amplitude Loading
abstract: ABSTRACT Composite structures are susceptible to fatigue damage under complex cyclic loading, and accurate prediction of stiffness degradation is important for structural condition assessment and life management. In this study, constant‐amplitude and two‐stage variable‐amplitude fatigue tests were conducted on four carbon‐fiber composite laminate configurations. A physics‐constrained sequential‐learning framework, termed PI‐LSTM‐VA, is developed for full‐curve stiffness degradation prediction. The model predicts a nonnegative degradation intensity and integrates it over an endpoint‐independent logarithmic cycle coordinate. A parameter‐supervised switch module represents additional posttransition degradation while preserving stiffness continuity. On four held‐out variable‐amplitude specimens, specimen‐mean MAE and RMSE were 0.008238 and 0.010016, respectively. RMSE decreased by 21.8% relative to the shared constrained baseline and by 39.2% relative to direct LSTM. Repeated specimen partitions confirmed lower average error, although dispersion increased and some predictions worsened. Separate five‐fold constant‐amplitude holdout tests yielded specimen‐mean RMSE of 0.015918 across 38 specimens and supported applicability within the investigated domain.

title: A Multi‑Objective Metaheuristic‑Driven Feature Selection Method for Body Fat Prediction
abstract: Accurate estimation of body fat percentage (BFP) is essential for obesity assessment and cardiovascular risk management. However, conventional anthropometric methods lack sufficient precision, while specialized body composition analyzers entail high costs that limit their widespread clinical adoption. This study proposes a multi‑objective metaheuristic‑driven feature selection framework that integrates an artificial neural network (ANN) with the Non‑Dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm II (NSGA‑II) to optimize both predictive R2 and feature parsimony for BFP estimation. The proposed methodology is evaluated on a benchmark dataset comprising 252 individuals with 13 anthropometric predictors. A comprehensive baseline assessment is conducted using 16 machine learning algorithms, including six linear and ten non‑linear models. The hybrid ANN‑NSGA‑II framework identifies an optimal subset of six features, achieving a root mean square error (RMSE) of 3.4962 and an R‑squared (R²) value of 0.8311. These quantitative outcomes demonstrate that embedding a multi‑objective metaheuristic selection mechanism within an ANN architecture enables substantial dimensionality reduction while maintaining robust predictive performance. The proposed approach provides a cost‑effective and computationally efficient alternative for BFP prediction using only fundamental anthropometric measurements, thereby…

title: Genomic prediction of feed conversion ratio and breast muscle protein content across dietary protein regimes in Arbor Acres broilers using Genomic Best Linear Unbiased Prediction (GBLUP), BayesB, and Reproducing Kernel Hilbert Spaces (RKHS) models to diss
abstract: This study conducted genomic prediction of body weight gain and breast protein content in 500 Arbor Acres broilers across dietary protein regimes (18%, 21%, 24% CP) and water stress conditions (well-watered, moderate stress, severe stress). Birds were phenotypes for body weight gain, breast protein content, lysine, and methionine. Genotyping-by-sequencing generated 42,567 SNPs. Four genomic prediction models (GBLUP, BayesB, RKHS, BayesCπ) were evaluated using five-fold cross validation. RKHS achieved the highest prediction accuracies for breast protein (r=0.85) and body weight gain (r=0.72). a training population of 150-200 individuals were sufficient (r>0.65). eight QTL were identified, with overlapping but distinct positions on chromosomes 1A and 7A for yield and protein, suggesting tight linkage rather than pleiotropy. Genomic selection reduced cycle length from 5 to 2 years and improved cost efficiency by 45-52%. Top RKHS with 200 training individuals effectively improves breast protein without compromising yield under stress. It is recommended that NAPRI implemen genomic selection targeting QTL on chromosomes 1A and 7A, with RIL-289, RIL-089 and RIL-124 advanced as dual purpose lines.

title: Effect of Data Augmentation and Membership Functions on ANFIS-Based Tensile Strength Prediction of FDM-Printed PETG Parts
abstract: Fused deposition modeling (FDM) enables the fabrication of complex polymeric components; however, the tensile performance of printed parts is strongly influenced by processing conditions and can be difficult to predict when only a limited number of experimental observations are available. This study investigates the use of linear interpolation-based data augmentation combined with an adaptive neuro-fuzzy inference system (ANFIS) for predicting the tensile strength of FDM-printed polyethylene terephthalate glycol-modified (PETG) specimens. Layer thickness, infill density, and nozzle temperature were investigated using a Taguchi L9 experimental design, with three specimens fabricated for each condition and their mean tensile strength values used as the reference dataset. The experimental data were augmented in MATLAB using linear interpolation to generate datasets containing 200, 400, and 600 samples. Gaussian ANFIS models with three membership function configurations (M222, M333, and M444) were subsequently developed using 60/40, 70/30, and 80/20 training/testing ratios. Model performance was assessed using R2, MSE, and MEP, and a multi-criteria performance index was employed to determine the optimum configuration. The results showed that increasing the number of membership functions generally improved prediction accuracy, whereas increasing the augmented dataset size did not ne…

title: A comparison of machine learning models and established grading scales for hospital mortality prediction in non‐traumatic subarachnoid haemorrhage
abstract: Abstract Introduction Existing severity grading scales show limited ability to guide decisions in subarachnoid haemorrhage (SAH). Machine learning (ML) offers a promising alternative. We compared ML models against established scales—World Federation of Neurosurgeons (WFNS), Fisher, Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) and Acute Physiology and Chronic Health Evaluation (APACHE) IV—for predicting hospital mortality in Intensive Care Unit (ICU) patients with non‐traumatic SAH. Methods We collected relevant data from adults with non‐traumatic SAH admitted between January 2011 and March 2025. Two multivariable prognostic models were developed and compared across logistic regression (LR) and three ML algorithms (random forest [RF], artificial neural network [ANN] and eXtreme Gradient Boosting). Model 1 included demographics, GCS, radiographic findings, vasospasm, 5‐day interventions and APACHE IV scores, whereas Model 2 omitted APACHE IV. Model performance was assessed with area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) and area under the precision‐recall curve. Results Among conventional scales, APACHE IV discriminated best (AUROC 0.871, 95% CI 0.839–0.902), followed by GCS severity (0.804), WFNS (0.780), and Fisher (0.540). Model 1 achieved AUROCs ranging from 0.916 to 0.935 (ANN AUROC 0.935, LR AUROC 0.928), significantly outperforming individual admission scales. For Model 2 …

Strength–stiffness coupling mechanism governing grout‐rock interface performance and anchorage capacity
abstract: Abstract Interfacial shear strength ( τ p ) and shear stiffness ( k s ) at the grout‐rock interface (GRI) are key parameters governing load transfer and pull‐out resistance of fully grouted rock bolts. This study systematically investigates the shear behavior of the GRI under four grout material conditions, namely early high‐strength cement (EHC), EHC with 5% silica fume (SF), EHC with 10% styrene‐acrylate emulsion (SA), and EHC with 20% SA. Direct shear tests combined with digital image correlation (DIC) are conducted to characterize the macroscopic shear response and localized deformation of the interfaces. (1) The direct shear tests show that the incorporation of SF increases τ p from 7.7 to 9.1 MPa and k s from 15.5 to 22.5 GPa/m, whereas the addition of SA reduces these parameters to 7.3 MPa and 10.5 GPa/m at 10% SA and further to 5.7 MPa and 5.7 GPa/m at 20% SA; (2) The DIC results reveal that interfacial shear stiffness is closely associated with the extent of the localized deformation on the grout side. The deformation‐zone thickness decreases from 2.5 mm for EHC to 1.5 mm for EHC with 5% SF, but increases to 4.0 and 5.0 mm for EHC with 10% and 20% SA, respectively. A stiffer grout therefore results in stronger deformation localization and a higher k s , whereas a more deformable grout broadens the shear zone and reduces k s . Development of a School Partnership Management Training Module to Improve the Managerial Capacity of Senior High School Principals in Sekadau Regency
abstract: This study aimed to develop a valid, practical, and effective school partnership management training module to strengthen senior high school principals' managerial capacity in Sekadau Regency. It was motivated by low partnership management competence: all 21 principals were categorized as “Poor” or “Very Poor,” particularly in program implementation (45.2) and supervision and evaluation (42.8). This research and development design used a mixed-methods approach adapted from the five-stage ADDIE model: Analysis, Design, Development, Implementation, and Evaluation. Participants included five principals for interviews, seven for a focus group discussion, two expert validators, five principals for a limited trial, and ten for a broader trial. The module was evaluated using a four-point Likert-scale instrument. Quantitative data were analyzed using mean scores, N-Gain, and a paired-samples t-test; qualitative data were analyzed through the interactive model of Miles, Huberman, and Saldaña. The findings indicated that the module was valid, with feasibility scores of 82.3% from material experts, 79.5% from language experts, and 81.7% from instructional media experts, all “Very Feasible.” Its practicality score was 84.2% (“Very Practical”), with readability (88.0%) and ease of use (86.0%) as its strongest features. Effectiveness was demonstrated by an increase in the mean score from 48.…

title: No change in skeletal muscle oxidative capacity biomarkers after 6 weeks of twice‐weekly single‐leg cycle interval training in young active adults
abstract: Abstract Interval training (INT) of sufficient frequency, intensity and duration can increase biomarkers of skeletal muscle oxidative capacity in humans. Studies typically involve three to four sessions per week; however, the effect of reduced training frequency on this response is unclear. Most studies also do not include a non‐exercise control (CON) condition to account for the potential influence of extraneous, uncontrolled factors. We employed a single‐leg, counterweighted cycling model to investigate the effect of twice weekly INT for 6 weeks on biomarkers of skeletal muscle oxidative capacity including mitochondrial content and fibre capillarisation. Sixteen healthy active adults (6 males, 10 females; 22 ± 3 years; peak oxygen uptake: 36.1 ± 6.1 mL kg −1 min −1 ) performed INT with one leg and their contralateral limb served as a CON. INT involved 4 × 5‐min bouts at an intensity of 50%–60% W peak , interspersed with 2.5 min of recovery at 20% W peak . Muscle biopsy samples obtained from the vastus lateralis of both legs before and after the intervention revealed no differences in the primary outcome measure, citrate synthase maximal activity ( P = 0.350, time × leg interaction). There were also no differences in multiple markers of mitochondrial protein content or capillarisation (all P > 0.05), except NDUFB8 protein content, which increased post‐training in the INT leg o…

title: Mutation of Dengue Virus Envelope Protein and Mechanism of Cross-Host Transmission
abstract: Dengue virus spreads worldwide. Mosquitoes of the Aedes genus pass it to humans. The virus poses big risks to global public health. Its envelope protein, E protein, controls three key viral behaviors. It lets viruses recognize host cells, fuse cell membranes and live through changing environments. Most adaptive non-synonymous mutations appear on the gene that makes E protein. These amino acid changes reshape the protein’s 3D structure. This change lets dengue jump across different host species. This paper sorts out E protein structures and sites where mutations often happen. It explains how single amino acid changes affect virus heat resistance, receptor binding speed and intracellular replication. Mutated E proteins help viruses escape mosquito immune defenses. They also help viruses survive stress inside mammalian cells. This paper builds a full molecular path to explain how dengue shifts between mosquitoes and people. Current research has clear limits. Few studies measure how multiple mutations work together. Lab cell models cannot copy real infection environments. Long-term tracking of wild virus strains is rare. This work improves theories about dengue’s evolution in two hosts. It picks out key adaptive mutation sites. It offers theory support for epidemic early warning, broad-spectrum vaccine design and new antiviral drug research.

title: Biomechanical Load Characteristics, Injury Mechanism, Prevention and Intervention of Proximal Hamstring in Badminton Racket-Side Forward Lunge
abstract: The badminton racket-side forward lunge is a special step frequently used in the front court. During the landing buffer phase of this action, the proximal hamstring bears a relatively large centrifugal traction load, which is likely to cause tendon injury at the ischial tubercle, limiting daily activity and sports performance. This article systematically reviews the biomechanical load characteristics of the proximal hamstring during the badminton racket-side forward lunge, analyzes its specific injury mechanism, summarize and analyze the existing prevention and intervention strategies. The results showed that: in the landing buffer stage of the badminton racket-side forward lunge, the large flexion of the hip and knee joint form the bidirectional traction stress concentration effect on the proximal hamstring; Long term unilateral load accumulation and dislocation of the hip and knee motion sequence will further increase the risk of local injury; resistance and eccentric training and landing movement technology correction are the main damage prevention and control measures at present, and various external equipment can be used as auxiliary intervention measures. The existing research has some limitations, such as insufficient measured data, difficulty matching laboratory conditions to real-life badminton competition scenarios, and lack of long-term tracking. In the future, more …

title: Molecular Mechanism of Alzheimer's Disease: Aβ -amyloid protein deposition, abnormal phosphorylation of tau protein and neurofibrillary tangles
abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is a prevalent neurodegenerative disorder that seriously endangers the physical and mental health of the elderly population. Currently, the molecular pathogenic mechanism of this disease has not been fully elucidated, and there are limitations in clinical treatment methods, making it difficult to curb the progression of the disease at its root. This article systematically analyzed the interactive effects of the three core pathological mechanisms in AD, namely Aβ deposition, excessive phosphorylation of Tau protein, and neuroinflammation, and reviewed the advantages and disadvantages of traditional interventions, nano-delivery carriers, and nasal administration as new treatment technologies. The results show that the pathological process of AD is dominated by a multi-dimensional interactive network, and the APOE4 gene and chronic neuroinflammation play a key role in upstream regulation. Simply removing pathological proteins cannot stop disease progression, while targeted precise intervention such as p-tau217 and ceRNA regulatory networks show significant potential. This study clarified the multi-factor interwoven pathological regulatory mechanism of AD, complemented the cognitive limitations of single pathological research, and provided theoretical support for the development of early screening markers and precise targeted treatment. The causal relations…

title: The Molecular Mechanism of HIF-2α-Mediated ADRN-MES Phenotypic Transition Under Hypoxia in Neuroblastoma Cells
abstract: Neuroblastomas are usually located in an area with poor oxygen supply inside the tumour; such an environment may promote metastasis and other serious behaviour in children. Tumor cells can switch between adrenergic and mesenchymal states to affect the clinical outcomes of young children.Hypoxia causes changes in the shape of cancer cells, the whole molecular signal pathway is still not known, and essential regulators that control these switches at different stages of cell growth have not been identified, Therefore,many crucial regulatory circuits still need to be studied. Based on the data of hypoxic cell lines, genetic knockdown assays and various molecular diagnostic methods were used to identify the metabolic pathways that cause structural changes in neuroblastoma under oxygen deprivation. HIF-2α is a switch that changes the expression pattern of the adrenergic signature genes into a mesenchymal one. PRRX1 and NOTCH3 are the secondary mediators that can decrease the production of native adrenergic mRNAs and promote the activation of a pro-tumorigenic mesenchymal feedback loop via HIF-2α. Currently, all of them are still at the level of laboratory cell culture and have not been validated by living mouse experiments or histopathological tests of real human tumour tissue. In the future, new technologies and a new biological model of rodents will be introduced into clinical tria…

title: Dual‐Mechanism Suppression of Posterior Capsule Opacification by an MMP2/9‐Responsive Sulforaphane‐Eluting Intraocular Lens
abstract: ABSTRACT Posterior capsule opacification (PCO) is the most frequent complication of cataract surgery and is driven by the epithelial‐mesenchymal transition (EMT) of residual lens epithelial cells (LECs). The current standard of care, Nd:YAG laser capsulotomy, is reactive and carries well‐documented complications, underscoring the need for proactive pharmacological prophylaxis. Drug‐eluting intraocular lenses offer a localized delivery platform. Here, we developed a sulforaphane (SFN)‐eluting intraocular lens (GelMA‐SFN@IOL) by integrating SFN‐loaded gelatin methacryloyl (GelMA) microparticles onto the IOL haptics. The GelMA carrier was designed to respond to MMP‐2/9, which were upregulated in PCO‐associated capsular tissues. In vitro, MMP‐2 enhanced SFN release from GelMA‐SFN microparticles, supporting enzyme‐responsive release behavior. In TNFα‐stimulated HLE‐B3 cells, SFN suppressed LEC migration and EMT marker expression, accompanied by increased autophagic activity and reduced MMP‐2/9 expression. These findings suggest a potential feedback mechanism whereby SFN‐mediated MMP downregulation could reduce enzyme‐promoted carrier degradation and release as the pathological signal subsides. In a rabbit PCO model, GelMA‐SFN@IOL preserved capsular clarity and reduced aberrant LEC proliferation over 28 days, with no obvious histological abnormalities in the examined ocular tissues. …

title: Synergistic Mechanism of Functional Foods Rich in Active Peptides in Tumor Immunotherapy
abstract: Given that traditional tumor therapy is associated with recurrence risk and immunotherapy is limited by the tumor immune microenvironment, alternative adjuvant approaches are urgently needed. In this context, active peptide-functional foods have emerged as promising auxiliary resources, yet their synergistic anti-tumor mechanisms are still not well understood, necessitating further research. In this paper, the dual functions of active peptides in direct tumor suppression and bidirectional regulation of immunity were analyzed. The synergistic principle of inducing immunogenic cell death and activating systemic anti-tumor immunity was elucidated by Gramicidin S and its light-controlled derivatives. Four types of synergistic methods, including molecular modification, light-controlled administration, combination therapy, and nanocarriers, were summarized. It was pointed out that these peptides had problems such as lack of preparation standards and only stopping in vitro experiments. This study clarified the mechanism of active peptide combined with immunotherapy, and provided theoretical support for the development of anti-tumor active peptide food. The existing in vivo pharmacological data are insufficient, and the Immunogenic cell death (ICD) regulatory pathway can be further analyzed in the future, so as to improve the in vivo efficacy and standardized production research and pr…

title: STRENGTHENING THE CAPACITY OF THE BORNEO WASTE BANK THROUGH COMMUNITY-BASED OUTREACH IN THE BANJAR SERASAN NEIGHBORHOOD, PONTIANAK
abstract: The Borneo Waste Bank, which was established in 2014, has played a role in supporting waste reduction while also boosting community engagement. However, its management appears to be suboptimal, as the Waste Bank still faces challenges related to organizational governance and human resource capacity. These two aspects need to be addressed so that the Waste Bank’s management can improve in the future. The community service activity was conducted using a participatory outreach method, meaning that the material presented was not merely one-way communication; rather, the community was actively involved in discussions and in identifying issues. The activity was carried out in three stages: preparation, implementation, and evaluation. During the evaluation phase, the team distributed a questionnaire before and after the activity concluded, covering four main points: the level of understanding of the educational material, willingness to implement the material, an assessment of the activity’s benefits and expectations for the program’s sustainability, and gathering direct feedback for planning future activities. The results of the activity showed that the implementation process went as expected, with active participation from the community. All four aspects assessed by the team showed improvement. A particularly significant improvement was seen in understanding of the material, which ro…

title: The Key Role and Potential Molecular Mechanism of HER2 (ERBB2) in Breast Cancer: A Bioinformatics Analysis Based on the TCGA-BRCA Database.
abstract: Breast cancer is one of the most common malignant tumors in women, with the HER2-positive subtype exhibiting strong invasiveness and poor prognosis. ERBB2, a key encoding gene of HER2, plays a crucial role in the development and progression of breast cancer, and its molecular mechanisms still require further in-depth analysis. This study, based on the TCGA-BRCA database, integrated transcriptome expression data, clinical information, and survival data to comprehensively analyze the molecular characteristics related to ERBB2. Differential expression analysis identified 334 significantly expressed genes, and GO and Hallmark pathway analyses revealed that they are mainly involved in the ERBB2 signaling pathway, estrogen response, and lipid metabolism. Further PPI network construction and module analysis revealed that ERBB2, GRB7, STARD3, PGAP3, and MIEN1 form a highly cohesive core functional module. Based on survival analysis, there is some correlation between ERBB2 expression and patient survival. The present study sheds lights on the synergistic interactions between ERBB2 and co-amplified genes in breast cancer, indicating that they may be involved in the synergistic progression of breast cancer and metabolic reprogramming. The results serve as a reference for the research of molecular mechanism of breast cancer that is positive to the HER2 receptor and screening for potential …

title: SiC-embedded 3D carbon network microspheres derived from spray-dried granules for tunable microwave absorption
One Carbon Matters: Conformational Bending Stabilizes Ferroelectric Nematic Order and Enables Domain‐Modulated Antiferroelectric Smectic C Order
abstract: ABSTRACT Molecular design of ferroelectric nematics has primarily focused on optimizing highly polar rigid mesogenic cores, whereas the role of flexible aliphatic segments in regulating molecular conformation and polar ordering remains insufficiently understood. Here, we show that exchanging the positions of a methylene group and the ether oxygen within the linkage between a polar rigid core and an aliphatic tail (Ar‐O‐CH 2 ‐ versus Ar‐CH 2 ‐O‐) reshapes the molecular conformational landscape and profoundly influences the stability of the ferroelectric nematic (N F ) phase. Molecules with a stronger preference for bent, pear‐like effective geometries exhibit significantly enhanced N F stability, accompanied by reduced splay and bend elastic constants in the apolar nematic phase, and lower apparent activation barriers for dipolar reorientation. Further elongation of the flexible segment introduces competing packing motifs and gives rise to a domain‐modulated antiferroelectric smectic C (SmC AF ) phase. These findings establish conformational bending as a molecular‐shape parameter for controlling hierarchical ferroelectric and antiferroelectric liquid‐crystalline order, bridging the design principles of conventional bent‐core layered ferroelectrics with emerging rod‐like fluid ferroelectric materials.

title: Dissipation‐Decoupling‐Reorganization: Three Layer Response and Energy Matter Decoupling in the Urban Boundary Layer to Anthropogenic Heating
abstract: Abstract Coherent structure contributions to momentum, sensible heat, and CO 2 fluxes after anthropogenic heating were examined based on seven level turbulence observations from the Beijing 325 m meteorological tower. A three layer vertical structure was identified according to the 2017 data set: a near surface dissipation layer (8–15 m) marked by reduced CO 2 transport efficiency, organized coherent structures decreased significantly; a decoupling layer (47–80 m) characterized by divergent responses in the ejection and sweep contributions to heat and CO 2 fluxes; and an upper reorganization layer (200–280 m) featuring with recovered transport efficiency and a profile inflection point. This three layer pattern is most clearly expressed in 2017. Data from 2016 to 2015 show simplified two layer (decoupling and reorganization) without a distinct dissipation layer, indicating that the complete three layer response depends on background meteorological conditions. Our results provide a vertically explicit framework for understanding anthropogenic perturbations to urban turbulence transport process.

Layer‐by‐Layer Solvent‐Free Additive Manufacturing Enabling Controllable Ultrathick Electrode Coating for Lithium‐Ion Battery
abstract: ABSTRACT Dry electrode manufacturing is emerging as a transformative strategy for sustainable lithium‐ion battery production, yet achieving ultrathick electrodes with homogeneous microstructures, efficient electron transport, and high electrochemical utilization remains a fundamental challenge. Here, we report a solvent‐free, layer‐by‐layer additive manufacturing strategy that enables architecturally controlled ultrathick cathodes through molecular‐level coupling between reduced graphene oxide (rGO) and binder. During roll‐to‐roll hot pressing, molten binder infiltrates the rGO framework to form a continuous conductive binder network, uniformly bridging NMC811 particles to enhance particle adhesion, suppress binder aggregation, and establish efficient electronic percolation. This strategy enables precise control of electrode thickness (300–1000 µm) and areal loading (20–100 mg cm − 2 ) while eliminating solvent‐induced structural defects. The resulting multilayer cathodes, comprising up to five sequentially deposited layers, deliver a specific capacity of 230 mAh g − 1 at 0.1 C and an areal capacity of ∼10 mAh cm − 2 . The nearly linear increase in areal capacity with layer number demonstrates homogeneous conductive networks and efficient electrochemical utilization throughout the electrode thickness. Electrodes with ∼50 mg cm − 2 loading retain 9 mAh cm − 2 after 50 cycles. Th…

Spatially robust pixel‐based mapping of biotic stress in Pinus nigra using unmanned aerial vehicle multispectral imagery and Random Forest
abstract: Abstract BACKGROUND Biotic stress threatens forest health, creating a need for rapid monitoring methods that complement field surveys. This study compared four original multispectral bands, five vegetation indices, and their combination for segmentation‐free, pixel‐based Random Forest mapping of healthy and unhealthy Pinus nigra canopies in Bingöl, Türkiye. Field and laboratory observations confirmed Dothistroma spp . and Tomicus spp . within the stand. RESULTS Unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) imagery with a ground sampling distance of 2.31 cm was evaluated using identical five‐block spatial cross‐validation partitions comprising 113 georeferenced trees (55 healthy and 58 unhealthy), each represented by mean predictor values from a manually delineated within‐crown sampling polygon. The combined model achieved the highest pooled overall accuracy (98.23%; Kappa = 0.9646). The vegetation‐index model achieved 97.35% accuracy and the highest area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (ROC‐AUC, 0.9991), with Optimized Soil‐Adjusted Vegetation Index (OSAVI) showing the greatest mean permutation importance. Exact McNemar tests detected no significant differences among models (all P = 1.000). The vegetation‐index model was retained as a parsimonious alternative to the combined model and fitted using 200 reference polygons to generate the operational map. Cross‐validated perform…

title: Charging schedule as a design variable for active harmonic filter sizing in unbalanced low-voltage networks: when do optimisation and V2G add value?
Timed Elastic Band based trajectory planning and MPC based adaptive cruise control for car-like autonomous vehicle
abstract: This paper presents a hierarchical control architecture for a car-like autonomous vehicle. Lateral motion is handled by a Timed Elastic Band (TEB) local planner that repeatedly optimizes a short-horizon waypoint band, while steering is generated by a Pure Pursuit controller tracking the optimized local path. Longitudinal behaviour is governed by a model predictive control (MPC) based adaptive cruise control (ACC) that regulates speed and inter-vehicle distance in free-driving and car-following modes, explicitly respecting acceleration and braking limits and enforcing a minimum safety distance. Safety is addressed through constraint-aware planning and control: the TEB optimization penalizes proximity to obstacles and violations of lane boundaries using smooth penalty terms that support stable gradient-based updates, while the MPC-ACC embeds hard bounds and distance constraints to prevent unsafe following. The integrated stack is evaluated in representative driving scenarios, including lane keeping and car-following, and is benchmarked against the MathWorks Path Following Control System (PFCS) reference model to quantify tracking behaviour and constraint compliance under identical conditions.

Job Rotation as a Human Capital Strategy and Perceived Employee Performance in the Ghana Armed Forces
abstract: Objectives Job rotation is widely promoted as a human capital strategy, yet survey evidence from African armed forces is scarce. Anchored in Human Capital Theory, this study examines how three rotation-related dimensions of career mobility in the Ghana Armed Forces (GAF), namely military education and training, personnel transfers and peacekeeping deployments, are associated with perceived employee performance (productivity), and which implementation challenges personnel perceive Methods A cross-sectional questionnaire survey was administered to 390 serving personnel drawn from the Army, Navy and Air Force Results Personnel rated training and education most favourably (M = 4.04), peacekeeping missions moderately (M = 3.39), and personnel transfers at the scale midpoint (M = 2.95), with items on the transparency and fairness of transfers rated below neutral. In a multiple regression the three dimensions jointly accounted for 34.7 percent of the variance in perceived performance (R² = .347). Only training and education were significantly associated with performance (β = .57, p < .001); personnel transfers (β = −.04, p = .469) and peacekeeping deployments (β = .07, p = .184) were not. Insufficient career counselling (M = 3.89), long periods in a single role and the priority of institutional needs over personal career growth were the most strongly endorsed implementation challenges…

title: Digitalisation, Eco‐Innovation and SME Internationalisation: A Dynamic Capabilities Perspective
abstract: ABSTRACT This study integrates the digitalisation and dynamic capabilities literature to examine the relationship between digitalisation, eco‐innovation and internationalisation in small and medium‐sized enterprises (SME). Using data obtained from 300 SME owner‐managers operating in the United Kingdom, the findings suggest that digitalisation positively impacts eco‐innovation and consequently the nature of internationalisation activities. In addition, there is a moderating effect of internationalisation experience on the relationship between eco‐innovation and internationalisation. These findings highlight the pivotal role of eco‐innovation, digitalisation and international experience in enabling SMEs to thrive in international markets. Furthermore, the study offers empirical evidence of how SMEs dynamically develop digital resources, and internationalisation is an outcome of building such capabilities. The implications for practice and future research avenues are examined.

title: Leveraging Industry 5.0 for Sustainable Waste Valorization Planning: A Novel Decision‐Support Framework for Barrier‐Strategy Prioritization
abstract: ABSTRACT Accelerating urbanization and increasing waste generation pose significant challenges to sustainable development and underscore the need to effectively implement waste valorization systems. This study addresses critical gaps in thorough barrier and Industry 5.0‐integrated strategy identification for implementing sustainable waste valorization systems. This study develops an innovative decision‐making barrier‐strategy analysis tool, which extends Step‐wise Weight Assessment Ratio Analysis (SWARA) and Measurement of Alternatives and Ranking according to COmpromise Solution (MARCOS) within an Interval Type‐2 Trapezoidal Fuzzy Set (IT2TrFS) environment to capture a wider range of uncertainty for more accurate analysis. IT2TrFS‐SWARA facilitates holistic evaluations of implementation barriers, while IT2TrFS‐MARCOS prioritizes Industry 5.0‐oriented strategies. To validate this model, a case study of implementing advanced incineration‐based medical waste valorization was conducted. The results indicated “Inefficient process design for energy recovery mechanism” as the most significant barrier and “Integrate renewable energy as an energy source” and “Provide wearable safety‐monitoring IoT devices for workers” as most pivotal mitigation strategies. This tool can be extended to other urban sustainability domains, which support Industry 5.0‐enabled policy interventions for sustai…

title: A ordem e o caos: transições de poder na história antiga e medieval
abstract: The transition of power in Ancient and Medieval History was marked by dynamics of order and chaos that shaped civilizations and social structures. In Antiquity, political changes often occurred through military conquests, the collapse of empires, and the rise of new leaderships, as seen in the Persian, Roman, and Greek empires. Stability, often illusory, was disrupted by internal wars, popular uprisings, and external invasions. In the medieval period, the fragmentation of power after Rome's fall led to decentralization and feudalism. In this context, vassalage relationships and the Church's influence played central roles in political and social reorganization. The struggle for hegemony among European kingdoms, Muslim expansion, and the Crusades exemplified how distinct forces shaped power transitions in this era. Thus, the history of these two periods is a narrative of continuous reconfiguration, where stability was often preceded or followed by chaos and instability.

abstract: ABSTRACT Qur'an memorization learning in nonformal education requires instructional strategies that promote accurate recitation, memorization fluency, long-term retention, and learner motivation. This article aims to examine educators' instructional strategies for improving the quality of Qur'an memorization through three interconnected dimensions: planning, implementation, and evaluation. The study employed a qualitative literature review approach with descriptive qualitative analysis through a literature search conducted in October 2026 using Google Scholar, Garuda, and DOAJ. The review analyzed seven relevant scholarly articles published between 2023 and 2024. The synthesis identifies three essential dimensions of effective instructional strategies. First, learning planning involves assessing learners' initial abilities, establishing realistic memorization targets, selecting appropriate methods, and designing evaluation procedures. Second, instructional implementation integrates tahsin, talaqqi, wahdah, and muraja'ah with individualized guidance, motivational reinforcement, and active learner participation. Third, learning evaluation emphasizes memorization accuracy, fluency, tajwid compliance, retention, and continuous formative feedback. The discussion also highlights the importance of family involvement and supportive learning environments in strengthening memorization pr…

title: Marketing Communication Strategy Through Social Media Content based on Local Wisdom to Increase the Added Value of Indonesian Coffee Brands (Study on Conservation Coffee Brands Based on Local Wisdom)
abstract: The coffee industry is a significant sector in Indonesia, contributing to both domestic production and consumption. However, challenges such as declining production due to climate change, limited agricultural land, and increasing global competition have encouraged coffee businesses to adopt more innovative marketing strategies. One emerging approach involves social media marketing communications that incorporate local cultural values and traditional knowledge. This study aimed to explore the social media marketing communication strategies employed by Indonesian coffee businesses, particularly those incorporating local wisdom, and examine their implications for brand value. A descriptive qualitative approach employing a holistic single-case study design was adopted. Data were collected through semi-structured interviews with consumers and coffee business owners who actively incorporated local wisdom-based content into their marketing strategies. The findings indicated that such content fostered emotional connections with consumers, enhanced brand awareness and engagement, and strengthened brand loyalty. These findings highlight the strategic potential of integrating local cultural values into social media marketing communications to enhance brand differentiation, strengthen perceived brand value, and support long-term business sustainability in Indonesia's coffee industry

title: Traceability as a Quality Cue: How Consumers Respond to Product‐Level Information
abstract: ABSTRACT Food supply chains have become longer, more fragmented and less visible to the people at the end of them, leaving consumers unable to verify the safety, provenance and ethical credentials of what they buy and firms unable to demonstrate them credibly. Against this background of growing supply chain complexity and consumer uncertainty, we examine whether traceability information functions as a quality cue in meat consumption and how it influences purchase intentions. Focusing on electronic identification (eID)‐enabled lamb traceability in Australia, we employ a multi‐study, mixed‐method design. Study 1 ( n = 10) explores consumer perceptions through in‐depth interviews. Study 2a conducts a pilot, whereas Study 2b uses a Facebook A/B field experiment to test behavioural responses in a natural setting. Study 3 ( n = 402) applies an online experiment to test a moderated mediation model. Qualitative findings show generally favourable attitudes, linking traceability to quality, safety and assurance. Whereas the field experiment shows no significant behavioural effect, the controlled experiment demonstrates that traceability increases purchase intention via perceived product quality, with stronger effects for highly involved consumers. Findings suggest that traceability can serve as a strategic, institutionally verified quality signal but that its effectiveness is conditional…

title: SAÚDE MENTAL DOS PROFISSIONAIS DE ENFERMAGEM: A PRÁTICA DO AUTOCUIDADO COMO ESTRATÉGIA DE MELHORIA
abstract: A saúde mental dos profissionais de enfermagem tem recebido atenção diante das condições de trabalho marcadas pela sobrecarga, pressão emocional e contato frequente com o sofrimento humano. Este trabalho tem como objetivo analisar de que forma a prática do autocuidado contribui para a melhoria da saúde mental dos profissionais de enfermagem e identificar estratégias utilizadas para promover o bem-estar mental desses trabalhadores. Trata-se de uma revisão integrativa da literatura, com abordagem qualitativa e caráter descritivo e exploratório. A busca dos estudos foi realizada na Biblioteca Virtual em Saúde (BVS), entre maio e julho de 2026. Como resultados foram analisadas 13 publicações, os achados apontaram que a sobrecarga, as jornadas extensas e as condições inadequadas de trabalho estão relacionadas ao estresse ocupacional e ao desgaste emocional dos profissionais. Entre as práticas de autocuidado identificadas, destacam-se a atividade física, o descanso, o relaxamento e o apoio social. As estratégias individuais apresentaram contribuições para o bem-estar mental, especialmente quando associadas ao suporte institucional e à melhoria das condições de trabalho. Conclui-se que o autocuidado contribui para a promoção da saúde mental dos profissionais de enfermagem. Sua associação com medidas institucionais de acolhimento, apoio psicológico e condições adequadas de trabalho fav…

title: Valoración actuarial del reaseguro no proporcional en seguros de automóviles: Aplicación de la tarificación del Burning Cost
abstract: En el mercado asegurador es fundamental contar con mecanismos para mitigar los riesgos asociados a la intensidad de los siniestros. En este proceso interviene un agente clave, el reasegurador, quien proporciona cobertura ante eventos inesperados. En este contexto, el presente trabajo aborda la modalidad no proporcional de los contratos de reaseguro, en particular Excess Loss y Stop Loss, centrándose en su tarificación mediante la metodología Burning Cost. Asimismo, se aplican distintas técnicas de triángulos de run-off para analizar la sensibilidad en la estimación de la prima de reaseguro. El estudio se basa en una cartera real (modificada) de seguros de automóviles perteneciente a una aseguradora con reconocimiento a nivel nacional.

title: POLA ASUH ORANG TUA DAN PERILAKU SIBLING RIVALRY PADA ANAK USIA DINI: TINJAUAN LITERATUR
abstract: ABSTRACT Sibling rivalry in early childhood is manifested through jealousy, competition for parental attention, quarrels, and rivalry between siblings. This study aims to (1) analyze the relationship between parenting styles and sibling rivalry behavior and (2) examine parenting styles and family factors associated with such behavior. This article employs a structured literature review guided by the PRISMA 2020 reporting principles. The literature search was conducted in October 2026, covering publications from 2012 to 2025, and analyzed 18 relevant publications consisting of empirical studies, reviews, and meta-analyses. The findings were synthesized using a narrative-comparative approach. Meta-analytic evidence indicates that authoritative parenting is negatively associated with sibling conflict (r = −0.201), whereas neglectful, inconsistent, permissive, and authoritarian parenting styles are positively associated with it. Other studies highlight the importance of differential parental treatment, age gaps, child characteristics, autonomy support, and parental mediation of conflicts. Publications on family education further reinforce the implications of communication, family interaction, and prosocial behavior development, although they do not directly examine sibling rivalry. These findings suggest the need for warm and consistent parenting that is fair and responsive to chil…

title: Bacterial DnaK Promotes CHIP‐Mediated GPX4 Degradation: A Bone‐Targeted DNAzyme–Nanozyme Strategy for Repair of Infected Bone Defects
abstract: ABSTRACT Staphylococcus aureus infection impairs bone repair, but how bacterial proteins disrupt osteogenic progenitors remains unclear. The bacterial chaperone DnaK promotes glutathione peroxidase 4 (GPX4) degradation in bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells (BMSCs), accompanied by lipid peroxidation, ferroptotic injury, and impaired osteogenic differentiation. GPX4 protein turnover increases without a change in Gpx4 mRNA abundance. A candidate E3‐ligase screen identifies the C terminus of Hsc70‐interacting protein (CHIP) as a mediator of this response. Catalytically inactive CHIP attenuates DnaK‐associated K48‐linked GPX4 ubiquitination, while CHIP knockdown preserves GPX4 and osteogenic proteins in primary BMSCs. To target bacterial DnaK and host oxidative injury, a bone‐targeted deoxyribozyme (DNAzyme)–nanozyme platform (DMPA) combines a dnaK ‐targeting DNAzyme with manganese hexacyanoferrate, polydopamine, and alendronate. In infected cultures, DMPA reduces bacterial dnaK transcript and DnaK protein abundance and improves BMSC redox balance and matrix mineralization. In a mouse model of infected tibial defects, DMPA promotes bone regeneration. These findings link bacterial DnaK to host GPX4 degradation through CHIP and establish a bone‐targeted DNAzyme–nanozyme strategy that combines bacterial DnaK suppression with redox regulation to promote repair of infected bone defects.

title: Rethinking Paradoxical Tensions in the Transition Toward Circular Business Practices: A Systematic Literature Review
abstract: ABSTRACT As central actors in the transition toward a circular economy, firms face multiple tensions when implementing circular business practices, often resulting in paradoxical situations. Although paradox scholars increasingly call for a systems perspective to capture the full complexity of wicked problems, the extent to which systems thinking informs research on paradoxes in firms' transition toward circular business practices remains unclear. We address this gap through a systematic literature review of 42 peer‐reviewed articles published between 2018 and 2025 and indexed in Scopus and Web of Science. We examine the implicit assumptions underlying the reviewed studies, drawing on the three core elements of systems: hierarchy, interconnections, and emergence. To structure the analysis, we classify paradoxical tensions across four analytical levels—macro, interorganizational, organizational, and individual. Based on recurring patterns in the literature, our review identifies four implicit assumptions that constrain a more systemic understanding of paradoxes in firms' circular transition: (1) Paradoxes largely exist in isolation from one another and (2) remain stable over time, (3) within the organizational level, strategy is the key element shaping paradoxes, and (4) individual actors, and their perceptions and experiences of paradoxes, play a limited role in shaping firms' …

title: An In Situ Amorphous Thermoconversion Strategy for Macroscopic Glass Heterojunctions
abstract: ABSTRACT Heterojunction fabrication has long been constrained by the stringent lattice‐matching requirements between dissimilar components, limiting the accessible material combinations and processing routes. Here, we report an amorphous thermoconversion strategy for constructing hybrid glass heterojunctions in situ. In this approach, structural competition among liquid phases derived from distinct metal–organic hybrid halide crystal structures generates divergent luminescence across amorphous phases, giving rise to a new family of halide glass heterojunctions. These hybrid halide glasses display excitation‐dependent and time‐gated persistent luminescence that is color‐tunable across a 160 nm wavelength window, a property that enables direct optical visualization and confers broad photonic versatility. Beyond their optical attributes, the resulting macroscopic glass heterojunctions exhibit well‐defined mechanical rigidity and arbitrary processability, supporting spatially resolved fluorescence and persistent luminescence outputs alongside one‐dimensional (1D) optical waveguiding at losses that surpass those of state‐of‐the‐art crystalline counterparts. Therefore, this work delivers the demonstration of macroscopic heterojunctions in halide supramolecular glasses and establishes a scalable route to multi‐channel, low‐dimensional optical waveguide for information storage and encr…

title: Divergent Smoke Transport and Subseasonal Responses Under Uncertainty in Smoke Injection Height in the 2017 Pacific Northwest Event
abstract: Abstract Wildfire smoke injection height (IH) is closely linked to aerosol vertical distribution, long‐range transport, radiative effects, and aerosol‐meteorology interactions. The Unified Forecast System coupled with the second‐generation NASA GOCART aerosol scheme currently lacks explicit plume‐rise parameterization, confining biomass burning emissions to the boundary layer. This treatment misrepresents extreme events like the 2017 Pacific Northwest (Pacific Northwest event) wildfires, which injected smoke into the upper troposphere and lower stratosphere. We used idealized sensitivity experiments within fully coupled subseasonal‐to‐seasonal (S2S) configurations to examine differences in smoke evolution among simulations with prescribed IHs (surface‐to‐500 hPa and surface‐to‐200 hPa) and the default boundary‐layer injection. Our results demonstrate that simulations with elevated injection better reproduce lofted smoke layers and associated long‐range transport pathways. Crucially, we find that simulations with different IHs show pronounced, delayed divergences in coupled meteorological fields. While aerosol and atmospheric differences among the simulations are modest in the first 2 weeks, they become more pronounced during weeks 3–4. By this period, simulations with varied prescribed IHs show substantial local differences in near‐surface temperature (ranging from −7.7 to +8.3…
