title: A Quasi-Experimental Study to Assess the Effectiveness of a Virtual Reality Distraction Technique on Reducing Pain During Painful Procedures Among Children in a Selected Hospital
abstract: Pain during procedures is a common and distressing experience for hospitalised children. Repeated needle procedures, venepuncture, intravenous cannulation, injections, wound care and other brief interventions may produce fear, anticipatory anxiety and behavioural distress, which can make cooperation more difficult. Virtual reality (VR) distraction uses an immersive digital environment to direct attention away from the procedure and may reduce the amount of attention available for pain processing. This review examines the theoretical basis, clinical use and research evidence for VR distraction in children undergoing painful procedures and presents a practical quasi-experimental framework for assessing its effectiveness in a selected hospital. Evidence from randomised and quasi-experimental studies suggests that immersive distraction can reduce self-reported pain and, in many settings, observable distress. The likely benefit is influenced by age, developmental level, previous procedural experiences, type and duration of procedure, headset acceptability, content preference and the quality of usual care. A proposed study can compare pain scores in an experimental group receiving age-appropriate VR distraction plus routine care with a comparison group receiving routine care alone. Pain should be measured using an age-appropriate validated scale, while demographic and procedural char…

title: The Digital Commons and the Infrastructural Power of Generative AI
abstract: Abstract The use and construction of generative AI reshape how information flows in society and who controls it. This paper investigates these changes and assesses their potential repercussions for the future of our shared information infrastructure. The findings elucidate an emergent social dilemma in which the use and construction of generative AI tend to degrade and compete with our existing infrastructure, while also layering atop the commons new infrastructure that is, by its current design, centralised and mediated. Yet, alternative futures that preserve the collective nature of our infrastructure remain possible. As a first step toward such futures, this paper concludes by exploring interventions to promote a decentralised and unmediated generative commons.

title: Far-red light can power biological nitrogen fixation in cyanobacteria
abstract: Abstract Nitrogen fixation is one of the most energetically expensive biological reactions shaping the biosphere. Here, we demonstrate that some heterocyst-forming cyanobacteria can perform this process solely with low-energy far-red light, after undergoing a light acclimation response known as far-red light photoacclimation (FaRLiP). Although FaRLiP has been shown to drive oxygenic photosynthesis beyond the visible spectrum in some cyanobacteria from shaded terrestrial habitats, it was unknown whether it could also support growth in nitrogen-poor environments. In this study, we focused on heterocyst-forming, nitrogen-fixing cyanobacteria carrying FaRLiP genes from various habitats. Based on transcription, protein, and enzymatic activity assays, we demonstrate that FaRLiP does support growth in the absence of combined nitrogen sources. This includes a strain lacking far-red Photosystem II, though it was energy-limited and required additional sugar input. Bioinformatic analyses revealed that this reduced FaRLiP gene cluster variant is transcribed in nitrogen-fixing symbiotic cyanobacteria in natural environments. Together, these results indicate that nitrogen fixation can be powered by low-energy photons, likely facilitating cyanobacterial growth in resource-limited microbial mats as well as shaded symbiotic environments. The Effect of Balance Funds and Regional Original Revenue on Regional Financial Performance through Capital Expenditure in Medan City
abstract: Regional autonomy demands local fiscal independence, where Local Own-Source Revenue (PAD) and Balancing Funds are expected to drive Regional Financial Performance, with Capital Expenditure as a mediator. This study aims to analyze the direct and indirect effects of Balancing Funds and PAD on Regional Financial Performance through Capital Expenditure in Medan City. This explanatory quantitative research uses Medan City Government time series data from 2007-2024. The path analysis method was applied using EViews software. The results reveal that PAD positively and significantly affects Capital Expenditure and Financial Performance. Conversely, Balancing Funds have a negative and significant effect on Financial Performance and an insignificant effect on Capital Expenditure. Capital Expenditure positively affects Financial Performance but fails to mediate the relationship between the two independent variables and Financial Performance. In conclusion, fiscal independence through PAD is the primary lever for financial performance, while reliance on central transfers potentially weakens it.

title: The Effectiveness of Problem-Based Learning in Enhancing ‎Science Literacy ‎Skills and Conceptual Understanding in Science and ‎Social Studies among ‎Sixth-Grade Elementary School Students ‎
abstract: Problem-based learning (PBL) is frequently proposed to strengthen scientific literacy and conceptual understanding, but small school-based comparisons require careful interpretation. This study describes a non-equivalent-group, pretest–posttest comparison involving 38 sixth-grade students from two public elementary schools in Bogorejo, Blora, Indonesia. Nineteen students in one school received PBL-oriented instruction and 19 students in another school received conventional instruction. The revised analysis uses aggregate figures available in the original report; individual-level records and the original statistical output were unavailable for verification. Reported posttest means were higher in the PBL-school group than in the comparison-school group for scientific literacy (78.16 vs. 62.37) and conceptual understanding (80.00 vs. 64.21), with a descriptive difference of 15.79 points for each outcome. The source report also listed normalized gains of 0.709 vs. 0.490 and 0.727 vs. 0.516, respectively; these gains could not be reproduced without individual data and a documented calculation procedure. Because the original inferential tables do not validly establish an independent between-school effect, statistical significance is not asserted in this revision. The observed pattern is compatible with the pedagogical rationale for PBL but cannot isolate an intervention effect from s…

title: Predicting awareness of where facility-based abortion services can be accessed among women in Ethiopia using explainable machine learning
abstract: Abstract Access to safe abortion care remains a significant public health concern in low- and middle-income countries, where unsafe abortion contributes substantially to maternal morbidity and mortality. In Ethiopia, although abortion is legally permitted under specific circumstances and facility-based abortion services are available, awareness of where these services can be accessed remains limited. Evidence on predictors of such awareness remains scarce. Therefore, this study aimed to predict women’s awareness of where facility-based abortion services can be accessed in the community and identify its key predictors using nationally representative data. Data from 8,894 women participating in the 2019 Performance Monitoring for Action (PMA) Ethiopia survey were analyzed. The data were stratified into development (80%) and independent test (20%) sets. Within each training fold, imputation, categorical encoding, Boruta feature selection, and SMOTENC were performed before model fitting to minimize information leakage. Eight supervised machine learning algorithms were developed and compared using repeated stratified 10-fold cross-validation with five repeats. Grid-search hyperparameter tuning was performed for the selected model using the development data. title: Myhill–Nerode Quotient Learning for Continuous Observation–Action Spaces via Kernel Maximum Mean Discrepancy
abstract: Model-free identification of the minimal world-model of a bounded agent in a POMDP has been made tractable in the finite setting by Myhill–Nerode quotient learning: a permutation G-test on fixed-policy continuation histograms clusters histories into continuation-equivalence classes. With continuous observations and actions the continuation alphabet is infinite and the G-test is undefined. We extend quotient learning to 𝒪 × 𝒜 ⊆ ℝ^(d). Histories are keyed by coarse quantile bins; for every pair of bins the continuation laws are compared with a kernel maximum mean discrepancy (MMD) permutation test on raw continuation vectors under Benjamini–Hochberg control, and bins whose test does not reject are merged by union–find. We (i) identify the estimator’s target—the bin-level continuation quotient—and give conditions under which it coincides with the latent quotient of index n; (ii) prove an alphabet-free trajectory bound N = O (Blog (B/δ)/ε_(MMD)² + B²log (1/δ)) for an analysed variant (T) with one window per trajectory, in which the alphabet size |𝒞| of the finite bound is replaced by the MMD separation ε_(MMD); and (iii) characterise finite-sample behaviour as a resolution effect: distinctions below the test’s detection scale are merged, so the returned size depends on the bin count B and the sample budget. Penguatan Keterampilan Berpikir Komputasional Murid Kelas V melalui Pendekatan Pembelajaran Mendalam pada Mata Pelajaran IPAS
abstract: Padatnya topik yang diberikan pada murid kelas V, terutama pada mata pelajaran Ilmu Pengetahuan Alam dan Sosial (IPAS) menyebabkan murid cenderung menghafal untuk menguasainya. Akibatnya keterampilan berpikir untuk memecahkan masalah menjadi rendah. Kegiatan pengabdian kepada masyarakat ini bertujuan untuk menguatkan keterampilan berpikir komputasional murid kelas V di SD Negeri 1 Tonja melalui pendekatan pembelajaran mendalam pada mata pelajaran IPAS. Metode pelaksanaan pengabdian dilakukan melalui pembelajaran interaktif dan pendampingan praktik langsung dengan empat pilar berpikir komputasional, yaitu dekomposisi, pengenalan pola, abstraksi, dan algoritma. title: Enhancing AI Feedback Systems: Lessons Learned from a RAG Implementation Study
abstract: This study investigates the impact of Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) on graduate students' perceptions of AI-generated feedback in a cyber-social learning environment. Using a non-equivalent cohort comparison quasi-experimental design, the research compared survey responses from Fall 2023 (n=96) and Spring 2024 (n=86) before and after implementing RAG. Participants engaged in iterative project cycles involving AI feedback, peer reviews, and instructor evaluations. Results revealed significant improvements in perceived feedback quality (p < .001, d = 0.41) and usefulness (p < .001, d = 0.51) following RAG implementation, while perceptions of actionability remained unchanged (p = .68, d = -0.05). Hierarchical regression analyses identified educational level as a positive predictor of quality and usefulness perceptions, whereas age and location negatively predicted actionability, and educational level positively predicted it. These findings suggest that RAG enhances the contextual relevance and perceived value of AI-generated feedback, particularly for advanced students. However, the lack of improvement in actionability highlights a persistent challenge in AI feedback systems. The study recommends integrating RAG with human support and developing targeted interventions to improve feedback literacy and implementation, especially for less advanced students and older learners.

title: Real-time cognitive load estimation from language in interactive learning environments
abstract: Abstract Cognitive load is a foundational construct in learning. Yet, most adaptive educational systems continue to depend on behavioral traces or physiological instrumentation to infer learners’ mental effort, limiting their scalability and ecological validity in open-ended learning contexts. This paper introduces a language-based framework for turn-level, real-time, and non-invasive cognitive load regulation in interactive learning environments. We present the Cognitive Load Estimate from Language (CLEL). This metric synthesizes eight linguistically grounded indicators into a unified estimate of cognitive load derived directly from learners’ written explanations. Building on this metric, we develop the Cognitive Load-Adaptive Multi-Agent Tutor (CLAMAT), a multi-agent instructional architecture in which specialized LLM-based agents coordinate adaptively through a cognitive-load-aware orchestration mechanism. Empirical evaluation with undergraduate learners performing explanatory tasks shows a strong association between CLEL and self-reported mental effort. Teacher evaluations favour CLAMAT feedback in clarity, helpfulness, and perceived adaptivity. Students also show an overall pre–post score improvement after receiving feedback from both systems, although the design does not isolate their respective contributions to learning. title: Deep learning identification of SST teleconnections driving early-winter North Atlantic climate
PENERAPAN MODEL PROBLEM BASED LEARNING UNTUK MENINGKATKAN KEMAMPUAN NUMERASI MURID PADA PEMBELAJARAN MATEMATIKA MATERI SATUAN PANJANG DAN BERAT KELAS III SD
abstract: Penelitian ini bertujuan meningkatkan kemampuan numerasi murid melalui penggunaan Problem Based Learning (PBL) dalam materi satuan panjang dan berat pada pelajaran Matematika kelas III sekolah dasar. Penelitian ini dilakukan dengan metode Penelitian Tindakan Kelas (PTK) yang dilakukan selama dua siklus dengan murid berjumlah 30. Setiap siklus memiliki alur pembelajaran yang sama yaitu perencanaan, aksi, pengamatan, dan refleksi. Data dikumpulkan melalui tes, observasi, dan dokumentasi selama pembelajaran. Hasil penelitian yang didapat memperlihatkan terdapat perkembangan hasil penilaian murid siklus I senilai 2.331 dari maksimal skor 3.240 atau 71,94% berkategori cukup, yang berkembang pada siklus II yaitu senilai 2.694 atau 83,15% berkategori baik. Nilai rata-rata pada aspek kognitif berkembang dari 72,67 menjadi 83,33. Perkembangan aspek-aspek yang dinilai dalam penelitian ini mengungkapkan bahwa penggunaan model pembelajaran PBL dapat memberikan hasil yang baik dalam pembelajaran Matematika materi satuan panjang dan berat. Model PBL dinilai mampu menjadi solusi bagi murid dalam mencerna konsep matematika, menyelesaikan masalah sehari-hari, diskusi, dan masalah kontekstual lainnya. Maka dari itu, PBL dinilai memiliki potensi dalam meningkatkan kemampuan numerasi murid sekolah dasar.

title: Islands in the Machine: A Systematic Geographic Assessment of Insular Territories in Video Games
abstract: Islands occupy a privileged position in human imagination and in the geography of the real world. As circumscribed, ecologically distinct, and often isolated territories, they concentrate geographic diversity into bounded spaces that invite exploration, narrative, and control. These same qualities make islands recurrent settings in video games, where the island serves simultaneously as a spatial container, a design convenience, and a cultural signifier. Yet despite the ubiquity of island environments in interactive media, no systematic attempt has been made to assess how faithfully video games represent the specific geographic properties that define insular territories. This paper presents the first comprehensive geographic analysis of island representation in video games. Drawing on a catalogue of 125 titles spanning multiple genres, platforms and release decades, a seven-block variable framework is developed, covering insularity, geomorphology, climate, hydrography, biogeography, human elements, and spatial scale, and computing an Island Geographic Fidelity Index (IGFI) for each title. Restricting the main analysis to 96 genuinely insular games and using 28 continental titles as a comparative reference, a mean IGFI of 42.2 (SD = 10.8) is found on a 0–100 scale, with Microsoft Flight Simulator 2024 serving as a benchmark reference at 98.8. Results show that insularity recognit…

title: Discrimination of ranges of closely related RNA targets using CRISPR-based detection assay developed using machine learning-based optimization
abstract: Abstract Early detection and identification of pathogen strains are crucial for mitigating infectious disease threats, including those posed by closely related zoonotic variants. A key limitation of current molecular detection approaches is their narrow focus on individual targets, which can delay recognition of outbreaks caused by closely related but non-identical pathogens. Here we report a two-channel CRISPR/Cas13a detection assay capable of discriminating between SARS-CoV-2 and a panel of twelve closely related zoonotic sarbecoviruses using a compact duplex assay format. Guide RNA sets with tunable specificity were designed using a two-stage machine learning pipeline: initial candidate filtering with a pre-existing RuleFit model, followed by retraining on 382 sarbecovirus-specific in vitro data points to refine the mismatch threshold from 4 to 6 mismatches for target exclusion. The optimized assay achieved proof-of-concept three-way classification of synthetic RNA targets into: (1) SARS-CoV-2, (2) the closest known near-neighbor BANAL-236, and (3) remaining zoonotic near-neighbors, with a limit of detection of 15–150 fM for synthetic RNA targets. This approach provides a practical framework for surveillance-oriented detection that identifies not only a specific pathogen but also its closest relatives, provided that system-specific validation and model retraining are include…

title: Improvement in phase-C students’ writing skills of pantun following the implementation of differentiated instruction within a deep learning approach
abstract: This study examined changes in Phase-C elementary school students’ pantun writing skills following the implementation of differentiated instruction within a Deep Learning approach. The study employed a quantitative approach using a one-group pretest–posttest design involving 30 fifth-grade students at Al Kautsar Islamic Elementary School in Krian, Sidoarjo. Data were collected through pantun writing assessments, classroom observations, and documentation. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, the Shapiro–Wilk test, a paired-sample t-test, and N-Gain analysis. The findings showed an increase in the mean pantun writing score from 68.40 on the pretest to 84.70 on the posttest, representing a mean improvement of 16.30 points. The paired-sample t-test indicated a statistically significant difference between pretest and posttest scores (p < .001), while the N-Gain score of 0.52 indicated moderate improvement. These findings suggest that students’ pantun writing skills improved following the implementation of differentiated instruction within a Deep Learning approach. However, because the study did not involve a comparison group, the observed improvement cannot be attributed exclusively to the instructional intervention. The findings provide preliminary empirical evidence regarding the implementation of differentiated instruction in pantun writing instruction.

Results: BPW Ar Risalah is effective as a benefit distributor (distributive effectiveness): targeting is perceived as accurate, distribution is generally on time with one compensated delay, and monitoring is conducted periodically according to the type of beneficiary. Social assistance of IDR 500,000 per month, scholarships of IDR 1,500,000 per semester, and income of IDR 1,500,000 per month contribute to meeting living needs, education, and income stability, with job creation as the most transformative benefit. However, transformative effectiveness cannot yet be fully concluded: beneficiaries' understanding of the concept and mechanism of productive waqf remains limited, the benefit amounts are supplementary, and monitoring does not yet measure impact. abstract: Abstract Investment decision-making is a challenging problem in financial engineering, particularly when investors are presented with multiple investment options. The decision paths become more complex in the space of digital assets, where investors are faced with a huge number of assets to select from, before even deriving optimal allocations. Within virtual space, the market for cryptocurrencies is gaining traction among investors, especially due to its potential for substantial returns and diversification. However, the market for cryptocurrencies presents unique challenges due to its inherent volatility and uncertainty, underscoring the need for a robust and structured investment framework to guide decision-making. Noting this gap in the literature on cryptocurrency investment, we introduce an innovative two-phase framework for cryptocurrency portfolio construction, designed to address the complexities and uncertainties inherent in cryptocurrency markets. In a two-phased analysis, we start with a Robust Ratio Data Envelopment Analysis (RR-DEA) to screen and preselect the most efficient cryptocurrencies from a pool of available assets, followed by the application of a Robust Goal Programming (RGP) optimization procedure to allocate weights based on the investor’s risk preferences, return targets, and other relevant financial goals. The two-phased framework ensures that the fi…

title: OPTIMIZATION OF BATH TEMPERATURE FOR ELECTRODEPOSITED NiFeWMoMn HIGH-ENTROPY ALLOY THIN FILMS
abstract: In this study, NiFeWMoMn high-entropy alloy thin films were successfully synthesized using the electrodeposition method by varying the bath temperature. The structural, morphological, corrosion, magnetic, and compositional properties were systematically investigated using X-ray diffraction (XRD), Field-emission scanning electron microscopy (FESEM), Energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS), electrochemical tests, and Vibrating-sample magnetometry (VSM). XRD analysis confirmed the formation of a solid solution with a refined crystalline structure, showing the smallest crystallite size and lower dislocation density at 75 ∘ C. FESEM images revealed uniform and dense surface morphology at this temperature, while EDS confirmed the presence of all intended elements with a more balanced atomic distribution. Electrochemical corrosion studies showed that the sample coated at 75 ∘ C exhibited the lowest corrosion rate and the highest polarization resistance, indicating superior corrosion resistance. Magnetic measurements showed that coercivity increased with temperature 75 ∘ C was identified as the most favorable temperature for achieving a uniform coating, improved corrosion resistance, controlled magnetic behavior, and enhanced structural properties.

title: Integrated population genomics and phenotypic analyses reveal geographic structure and signatures of recent positive-selection underlying insecticide resistance in Anopheles arabiensis from The Gambia, West Africa
abstract: Abstract Insecticide resistance in malaria vectors is spreading, with newly identified resistance markers raising operational challenges and threatening malaria reduction. Anopheles arabiensis is an important vector in The Gambia; however, the molecular basis of its insecticide resistance remains poorly understood. We observed signals of population structure between coastal and inland An. arabiensis populations in The Gambia, indicating restricted gene flow likely influenced by environmental variation. Pyrethroid and DDT resistance were widespread. However, the prevalence of both phenotypic and genetic insecticide resistance differed between coastal and inland populations. For instance, the Vgsc-L995S and Vgsc-L995F substitutions conferring pyrethroid and DDT resistance were more frequent in coastal populations and were associated with markedly higher phenotypic resistance to these insecticides. We also identified increased frequencies of copy number variation at Cytochrome P450 (Cyp6aa/p, Cyp9k1) and carboxylesterase (Coeae2-7 g) metabolic resistance markers in coastal An. arabiensis. Some observed gene amplifications were unique to Gambian coastal populations, suggesting their independent evolution. Furthermore, we found evidence of genomic regions under recent positive selection on chromosomes 2L:37,282,152-37,298,202 and 3R:28,590,243-28,602,280 with more pronounced selecti…

title: HierWoodNet: HierStyle multi-scale semantic style transfer method for Chinese woodblock painting
abstract: Abstract Woodblock painting, a traditional Chinese intangible cultural heritage, is known for its vivid colors and distinctive textures. However, modern lifestyles and declining cultural inheritance have led to risks of style loss and discontinuity. AI-based image style transfer offers a promising avenue for preserving and creating woodblock art. However, existing methods struggle with semantic feature extraction, style consistency, and color modeling in this domain. To address these challenges, we propose a hierarchical woodblock style transfer network. Our approach introduces a Content-Aware Positional Encoder based on the Transformer architecture, which enhances multi-scale feature representation and global structural perception. This helps preserve content during style transfer. We further present a HierStyle Encoder that learns rich, hierarchical style features from data, enabling fine-grained control over the transfer process and improving semantic and textural coherence. A progressive decoder integrates multi-stage upsampling with cross-layer connections to preserve semantic structure while injecting detailed style features. Finally, the ChromaNova Color Decoder dynamically optimizes color representation through a multi-dimensional color loss function that considers both color contrast and distribution differences. Quantitative experiments show that our method achieves t…

title: A specialized microbiome enriched in nitrification and halogen cycling potential resolved from multi-omics investigation of a Caribbean suboxic and acidic marine sinkhole
abstract: Abstract Background The Luymes Sinkholes, located on the Luymes Bank northwest of Saba, represent a unique marine environment characterized by distinct biogeochemical gradients. Most noticeable is an acidic (pH ≈ 6.25) and suboxic (O2 < 60 µmol/kg) submerged ‘lake’ at ~ 220 m depth exhibiting extreme deviations from standard oceanographic patterns, including elevated inorganic carbon, nitrate, and phosphate, and a lower temperature (20.3 ºC vs 26.4 ºC). To determine how the microbiome within the submerged acid lake adapted to these unique conditions, we collected 59 coupled samples of size-filtered (0.22 µm) planktonic microbes for shotgun metagenomics and solid-phase extracted dissolved organic matter for untargeted metabolomics from 21 stations at depths ranging from 2 to 600 m during a 10-day research cruise in December 2019. Results We identified a distinct microbial community within the submerged acid lake different from the non-acidic sinkholes, with increased abundances of Nitrospinota , Thermoproteota , Planctomycetota , and Actinobacteriota . We also found three enriched classes of dissolved compounds within the submerged acid lake: (1) large, (2) low-polarity, and (3) halogenated metabolites, including iodides and halobenzoic acids. Correlations between microbial taxa and metabolite classes show potential links between nitrifying archaea and halogenated compound cycli…

abstract: Pemberdayaan ekonomi jemaat melalui pelayanan gereja membutuhkan pengelolaan yang terarah dan berkelanjutan, bukan hanya penyediaan bantuan dan fasilitas usaha. Penelitian terdahulu telah membahas pemberdayaan ekonomi melalui pengembangan potensi lokal, bantuan modal, pelatihan, dan pemanfaatan aset gereja. Namun, kajian yang mengintegrasikan fungsi pengelolaan program ekonomi berbasis pasar dengan faktor pendukung, penghambat, dan dampaknya terhadap pemberdayaan ekonomi jemaat masih terbatas. Penelitian ini bertujuan menganalisis pengelolaan Pasar Obor, mengidentifikasi faktor pendukung dan penghambat, serta menganalisis dampaknya terhadap pemberdayaan ekonomi jemaat di GKI Ekklesia Klasaman, Kota Sorong, Papua Barat Daya. Penelitian menggunakan pendekatan kualitatif deskriptif dengan pemilihan informan secara purposif. Data dikumpulkan melalui wawancara, observasi, dan dokumentasi, kemudian dianalisis secara deskriptif. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa pengelolaan telah mencakup fungsi perencanaan, pengorganisasian, penggerakan, dan pengawasan, tetapi belum terintegrasi secara optimal karena keterbatasan pedoman operasional, pendampingan usaha, dan evaluasi perkembangan peserta. Crop Load Management of Plums Using 1-Aminocyclopropane Carboxylic Acid (1-ACC)
abstract: Excessive fruit set in European (Prunus domestica L.) and Japanese (Prunus salicina L.) plum trees necessitates thinning to optimize crop load, enhance fruit quality, and reduce manual hand thinning. This study evaluated the efficacy of the ethylene precursor 1-aminocyclopropane-1-carboxylic acid (1-ACC) as a chemical thinning agent for the European plum cultivar ‘Vibrant’ and the Japanese plum cultivar ‘Early Golden’. Treatments were applied at full bloom (FB) and at the fruitlet stage (8-10 mm diameter) using 1-ACC concentrations of 150, 300, and 450 mg·L⁻¹. Horticultural measurements included crop load, yield, fruit size distribution, fruit quality, phytotoxic effects, and crop value. Applications of 1-ACC effectively reduced crop load, with FB applications producing greater thinning responses than fruitlet-stage applications. Increasing application rates resulted in decreased yield and crop value, while average fruit weight increased. No hand thinning was required in both years of the study due to poor pollination in the ‘Early Golden’ orchard and atypical fruit drop unrelated to 1-ACC treatments following early fruit development in the ‘Vibrant’ orchard; therefore, commercial thinning was not required. Thinning responses varied by cultivar and application timing, underscoring the importance of cultivar-specific thinning strategies. Ethylene evolution following 1-ACC applic…

title: Relationship Between Perceived Stress and Student Incivility Among College Students: A Cross-Sectional Study
abstract: Student incivility has become an increasing concern in higher education because of its adverse effects on classroom climate, teaching effectiveness, and students' academic experiences. Psychological stress has been recognised as a potential factor influencing uncivil behaviour. This study evaluated the relationship between perceived stress and student incivility among college students and investigated whether perceived stress significantly predicts student incivility. A quantitative, cross-sectional research design was followed, and data were collected from 219 college students using structured questionnaires measuring perceived stress and student incivility. Descriptive statistics, reliability analysis, Pearson's correlation, and simple linear regression were performed using Jamovi. A statistically significant positive relationship was identified between perceived stress and student incivility. Regression analysis showed that perceived stress significantly predicted student incivility, although it explained only 4% of the variance in uncivil behaviour. Significant gender differences were observed in both perceived stress and student incivility. Rather than presuming an automatic, uniform progression from student stress to behavioural misconduct, this study provides a nuanced, methodologically transparent evaluation that underscores the sensitivity of stress–incivility dynamics…

title: The Monitoring Paradox: Why Oversight Mechanisms Fail to Predict PPP Infrastructure Projects Performance in Kenya
abstract: Purpose: The study explored role of project monitoring mechanisms in enhancing performance of Public-Private Partnership (PPP) infrastructure projects in Kenya. Policy puts a lot of emphasis on the need for monitoring along the project lifecycle; however, many PPP projects continue to display inefficiencies pointing towards weak monitoring systems. Materials and Methods: Data were collected from 252 respondents representing government agencies, private consortia, and project management units across 103 PPP projects. Regression analysis was used to test relationship between project monitoring mechanisms and project performance. Findings: Project monitoring had a statistically significant but weak positive influence on project performance (β = .014, p < .005). The positive but not so profound effect suggests that the monitoring frameworks that exists are largely compliance-oriented rather than the one that drives performance in the project environment. Implications to Theory, Practice and Policy: The study recommends institutionalizing real-time monitoring, feedback systems, and adoption of digital data tools to strengthen accountability within PPP infrastructure projects in Kenya. To anchor these measures, the Public Private Partnerships Act, 2021 and the regulations around privately funded public infrastructure should be amended to create a performance-based monitoring making i…

abstract: Abstract Background The reintroduction of exercise pulmonary hypertension (EPH) to the pulmonary hypertension (PH) definition by the European guidelines underlines the importance of examining the hemodynamic response to exercise during right heart catheterization. Because the standard exercise modality of cycle ergometry (CE) is not universally accessible, we compared its hemodynamic effects with those of dynamic single-arm exercise (AE) in patients undergoing right heart catheterization (RHC). Methods 50 consecutive patients with indication for RHC were enrolled. Hemodynamic parameters were assessed at rest, followed by randomized exercise periods with an intervening rest phase. Thermodilution was used to determine cardiac output. The intensity of the AE was patient-determined, whereas CE was conducted at a fixed work rate ranging from 10 to 50 watts, based on the patient’s physical status. Oxygen uptake (VO₂) was estimated using the reverse Fick principle to compare relative exercise intensity between modalities. EPH was defined by an mPAP/cardiac output slope > 3 mmHg·L⁻¹·min⁻¹, and exercise-induced left heart disease by a rise in PAWP from ≤ 15 mmHg at rest to > 25 mmHg during exercise. Results Mean pulmonary arterial pressure increased by 12 mmHg with CE compared to 3 mmHg with AE (p<0.001), pulmonary artery wedge pressure increased by 5 mmHg versus 2 mmHg (p<0.001), cardi…

title: The Effect of Financial Literacy and Financial Planning on the Financial Control Ability of MSMEs
abstract: Financial control is a critical managerial function for MSME sustainability because it enables owners to compare actual outcomes with plans, identify deviations, and take corrective action. This study examines the associations of financial literacy and financial planning ability with financial control ability among MSMEs. A cross-sectional quantitative survey was conducted using purposive sampling of 91 MSME owners or managers who completed 24 five-point Likert items. Variable scores were calculated as item means and analyzed using multiple linear regression, supported by reliability assessment, residual diagnostics, and HC3 robust standard errors. Mean scores for financial literacy, financial planning, and financial control were 4.615, 3.892, and 4.369, respectively. Financial literacy (B=0.332; β=0.331; p<0.001) and financial planning (B=0.317; β=0.655; p<0.001) were positively associated with financial control. The model was significant, F(2,88)=136.829; p<0.001, with R²=75.67%. However, financial control reliability was low (α=0.424), and residuals were non-normal. The findings suggest that financial planning has a stronger standardized association with financial control than financial literacy, although interpretation should remain exploratory because of measurement-quality limitations and the observational design.

abstract: Differences in financial service use between urban and rural areas suggest that the expansion of financial technology (fintech) does not necessarily lead to meaningful inclusion. This study synthesizes the roles, benefits, barriers, and policy priorities of fintech for rural communities through a systematic literature review and narrative thematic synthesis of ten core publications from 2021–2025. A reconciled selection flow reports 309 records, 102 duplicates, 95 records excluded during screening, 56 reports not retrieved, 46 reports excluded after eligibility assessment, and ten included studies. The literature suggests that digital payments and financial services may reduce geographical and transaction-cost barriers, while their effects on poverty, productivity, and welfare are highly context- and design-dependent. Most available evidence is national-level or conceptual; direct rural household-level evidence remains limited. Recurring barriers include connectivity, financial and digital literacy, trust, data security, and product suitability. The synthesis proposes a sequenced policy agenda encompassing digital infrastructure and local agents, practice-oriented literacy, context-sensitive services, consumer protection, and outcome-based evaluation. The evidence does not justify a universal numerical claim about poverty reduction.

abstract: This study examines institutional perspectives on youth digital vulnerability in Lampung Province, Indonesia, focusing on problematic information, cyber financial fraud, and community-based prevention. Using a qualitative descriptive approach, data were collected through face-to-face, semi-structured interviews with purposively selected representatives from 13 organizational units across provincial and municipal government, police, territorial defense, social resilience, and digital-governance institutions. Documented interview records were analyzed thematically and contextualized using policy and connectivity documents, alongside provincial cyber-governance evaluations covering 2022–2025. The analysis generated four themes: youth vulnerability within an unequal digital environment; problematic information and cyber financial fraud as converging risks; a layered institutional response and its implementation constraints; and a proposed community-based youth digital resilience model. Institutional informants linked youth digital vulnerability to unequal connectivity, uneven information-verification capacity, and limited digital-safety awareness. Problematic information and cyber financial fraud were described as distinct but related risks that may exploit trust, emotion, urgency, and limited verification. Density of Subminimum Wage Usage and Labour Market Consequences for Workers with Disabilities in the United States
abstract: Section 14(c) of the Fair Labor Standards Act allows for workers with disabilities in the United States to be paid below the federal minimum wage. Using Current Population Survey data and 14(c) certificate employment data from the U.S. Department of Labour, this article investigates whether the density of 14(c) employment has labour market spillovers for workers with disabilities. Logistic regressions suggest individuals with disabilities living in states with more active 14(c) certificates are less likely to be participating in the labour force and to be employed. Regional concentrations of 14(c) certificates may be related to weakened regional differences in bargaining power of workers with disabilities. JEL Codes: J14, K31, J31

title: Characterization, Epidemiology, and Host Range of Alternaria solani f. sp. lactucae , the Causal Pathogen of Alternaria leaf spot of lettuce
abstract: An undescribed leaf spot disease was first seen on lettuce grown in coastal California in 2023. Caused by a species of Alternaria , the symptoms were round to irregular, gray green to brown leaf spots having concentric rings; these symptoms were distinct from those of other known foliar diseases of lettuce in the state. Inoculation experiments showed that 15 different cultivars of iceberg, romaine, green leaf, red leaf, and butterhead lettuce types were susceptible. When 22 non-lettuce crops in seven plant families were inoculated, this Alternaria sp. caused disease on only endive, potato, and tomato. Conidial morphology of the lettuce pathogen resembled that of the potato early blight pathogen, A. solani . When an A. solani isolate from potato was inoculated onto potato and lettuce, the potato developed severe early blight, but the lettuce remained symptomless. In 8- to 11-month-old Petri plate cultures, the lettuce Alternaria sp. isolates formed microsclerotia; when inoculated onto lettuce, the microsclerotia caused the leaf spot disease. Whole-genome sequencing and calculation of average nucleotide identity indicated that the lettuce Alternaria sp. and A. solani isolates clustered together, although the lettuce isolates were distinct from the potato pathogen and represented a new forma specialis , A. solani f. sp. lactucae , within the A. solani species complex. abstract: The global transition from fossil-fuel-based electricity systems to renewable energy sources is essential to achieving sustainable development and reducing grid dependency. This study investigates residential energy consumption behavior within a solar-battery-grid architecture using the proposed GridSolarMatch framework. System monitoring data were obtained through a dedicated data logger operating with Module Version No.: LSWS_01_2421_SS_00_00.00.00.06, ensuring high-resolution and reliable time-series measurement of solar generation, battery operation, and grid interaction. GridSolarMatch employs a transparent, rule-based dispatch strategy that prioritizes solar energy utilization, regulates battery charging and discharging via explicit state-of-charge (SOC) dynamics, and uses the grid as a fallback resource during energy deficits. Time- of-Use electricity tariffs are incorporated to evaluate tariff-aware operational behavior without relying on forecasting or computationally intensive optimization solvers. The result demonstrates effective battery buffering, reduced grid dependency during peak tariff periods, and controlled SOC cycling that preserves battery longevity. abstract: Background: Turmeric (Curcuma longa L.) is a globally significant spice, also referred to as the “golden spice.” India is the world’s largest producer of turmeric, accounting for 80% of the global production. Turmeric is utilized in the preparation of food, as a colouring agent in textiles and as a component of confectionaries and medicine. Turmeric is also employed to treat human and animal diseases due to its antimicrobial and anticancer properties. The plant is susceptible to a variety of fungal, bacterial, viral and nematode diseases. Leaf spot, which is caused by Colletotrichum capsici, is the most significant fungal disease. It results in a substantial decrease in yield as a result of the loss of photosynthetic area. Methods: The growth of C. capsici, the influence of light sources on growth and sporulation, the utilization of carbon and nitrogen sources and the effect of organic manure extract on growth were all examined in this experiment. Result: The maximum radial mycelial growth was achieved on potato dextrose agar and potato dextrose agar plus host leaf extract media, with diameters of 90.00 and 87.00 mm, respectively. title: Forecasting volatile electricity prices in the Australian National Electricity market using machine learning
abstract: Abstract The growing integration of variable renewable energy Sources have intensified price volatility in the Australian National Electricity Market (NEM), creating operational challenges for market operators, traders, and battery energy storage systems (BESS). Short-term electricity price forecasting is important for arbitrage, market operation, and participation in ancillary services such as Frequency Control Ancillary Services (FCAS). The evaluation presents a Comparative evaluation of eight forecasting models: Autoregressive Integrated Moving Average (ARIMA), Seasonal Autoregressive Integrated Moving Average with Exogenous Regressors (SARIMAX), linear regression, exponential smoothing, XGBoost, Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks, and Prophet with and without an exogenous demand regressor, using historical price data from New South Wales (NSW). Five-minute-ahead forecasting performance is assessed across selected stable, volatile, and rapidly fluctuating periods. XGBoost achieves the lowest mean validation MAE (0.040) and highest mean validation $$R^2$$ (0.949) among the evaluated models, and retains the best performance on the held-out test set. The findings support the use of market information in the evaluated forecasting models.

title: Formation of State Policy on Professional Orientation as a Factor in Mitigating the Personnel Shortage in the Labour Market
abstract: This study compared career guidance in Kazakhstan with Germany and Finland and identified policy implications for improving education–labour market links. It combined documentary analysis, cross-national comparison, media content analysis and a survey of 42 respondents in Kazakhstan. Germany emphasised employer participation and workplace-integrated vocational training, while Finland provided continuous guidance across educational and employment transitions. Kazakhstan has adopted elements of both models, but coordination, labour market alignment, training options and school-based guidance remain limited. Survey findings also indicated gaps in school guidance provision. Stronger coordination among schools, employers, and employment services could improve continuity and employment relevance.

title: Festa e mercado
abstract: No presente texto discutimos a política dos eventos festivos e da produção de seus públicos. A partir de uma abordagem etnográfica, cruzamos o acompanhamento de festas universitárias LGBTQIA+ em São Carlos, município do interior do estado de São Paulo, com os megaeventos de Madonna e Lady Gaga realizados no Rio de Janeiro, tomando-os como situações privilegiadas para observar transformações nas formas de organização, consumo e ocupação da cidade em uma leitura mais sistêmica. Argumentamos que esses eventos integram a paisagem urbana contemporânea e são simultaneamente espaços de consumo e acontecimentos públicos, com relações de interdependência. Embora incorporem práticas inclusivas, que envolvem o reconhecimento da democratização do acesso e das diferenças, a naturalização dos processos econômicos de profissionalização, empresarização e segmentação dos públicos para viabilização do lucro, rearticula desigualdades. Demonstramos que a ampliação do acesso dos públicos não elimina as diferenciações e hierarquias, que reaparecem nas formas de trabalho, nos modos de circulação das pessoas, nas possibilidades de consumo e nas dinâmicas dos espaços. title: Inclusive Agribusiness Models for Smallholder Farmers: Value Creation, Market Integration and Equitable Benefit Sharing
abstract: Inclusive agribusiness is increasingly proposed as a means of connecting smallholder farmers to remunerative markets while improving the distribution of benefits within agricultural value chains. Yet participation, commercial upgrading and equity are analytically distinct outcomes, and improvements in one do not reliably secure the others. This critical narrative review examines the institutional designs, value-creation mechanisms and distributional consequences of contract farming, producer organisations, coordinated value chains, sustainability certification and digitally mediated market services. Peer-reviewed theoretical, observational, quasi-experimental, experimental and review evidence was assessed with attention to selection, counterfactual validity, contract governance, heterogeneity and geographical transferability. The evidence indicates that coordinated marketing can reduce transaction costs, support quality upgrading and improve access to inputs or information. Nevertheless, observed income gains are contingent on crop characteristics, procurement reliability, bargaining conditions and who is able to enter and remain in a scheme. Stronger causal evidence exists for particular contractual and information interventions than for the broader claim that inclusive business models routinely reduce inequality. Commercial standards may provide price or market advantages whi…

title: Do guard dogs really need protecting? Tibetan perspectives and practices of Tibetan Mastiff conservation after the market collapse
abstract: Following the collapse of the Tibetan Mastiff (TM) market in China in the mid-2010s, conservation of the breed has become a laissez-faire field dominated by competing grassroots actors. Drawing on twenty-four months of multi-sited ethnography in Tibetan pastoral communities, breeding farms, and enthusiast networks, this article compares how Tibetan intellectuals, enthusiasts, and pastoralists in Machu (Gansu) understand whether TMs need conservation, who should be responsible for it, and by what method. Because the TM is neither a wildlife species nor a standardised breed, what stakeholders seek to sustain is a working pastoral lineage and the interspecies lifeway through which guarding capabilities are cultivated. I argue that these positions are best distinguished through three concepts routinely conflated in everyday speech: guarding, protection, and conservation. Tibetan intellectuals use the TM as a metaphor for Tibetan dispossession but rarely offer practical proposals. Tibetan enthusiasts, despite claiming Tibetan custodianship, equate conservation with protection through controlled breeding farms, reproducing the paternalistic rescue logic critiqued by Abu-Lughod. Pastoralist conservationists in Machu instead seek to restore the conditions in which guard dogs can guard once again, although certain pastoral dog-keeping practices such as long-term tethering and misconcept…

title: Digital Platform Entrepreneurship, Gendered Care Responsibilities and Labour Market Inclusion in India
abstract: Women’s labour force participation in India remains persistently low, shaped not only by limited employment opportunities but also by the unequal distribution of unpaid domestic and caregiving work. This study examines the role of women-led platform entrepreneurship in promoting an inclusive labour market by addressing the care burden and enhancing female labour force participation. It asks how digital transformation has enabled platform entrepreneurship, how platform entrepreneurship shapes women’s entry and terms of participation, whether platform entrepreneurship accommodates, relieves or intensifies care, how it relates to inclusive growth, and what constraints limit these outcomes. The paper adopts a conceptual and analytical approach, drawing on existing literature and descriptive analysis of Time Use Survey (TUS), 2024. It compares gender differences in participation and average time spent per participant in employment, unpaid domestic and caregiving activities across sixteen major states: Andhra Pradesh, Assam, Bihar, Gujarat, Haryana, Himachal Pradesh, Karnataka, Kerala, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Odisha, Punjab, Rajasthan, Tamil Nadu, Uttar Pradesh and West Bengal. The findings indicate that the gender gap is associated with unequal allocation of unpaid work as much as with differential access to employment, with notable variation across states. title: Market Penetration of a Premium Dairy Brand through General and Modern Trade: Exploratory Field Evidence from Pune, India
abstract: A premium dairy brand entering an established city market has to win over two very different people: the neighbourhood retailer in general trade (GT) and the shopper in modern trade (MT). This paper reports an exploratory field study of Sid’s Farm, a dairy brand that sells on laboratory testing and quality, carried out during a two-month on-the-job training placement in Pune (May–July 2026). I draw on a recorded retailer funnel from Wakad (53 retailers approached), a brand-availability audit of those same 53 outlets, and field observation of customer interactions, freezer merchandising and two sampling activities at a modern-trade store in Baner. Reading the evidence through Ansoff’s market-penetration logic, the AIDA model and retailer relationship management, I find five things. First, 77.8% of interested retailers (21 of 27) placed a first order, yet only 39.6% of everyone approached did. Second, 13 of the 21 first-order retailers (61.9%) were recorded as reordering, while 6 had stopped. Third, Govind and Amul were present in 94.3% and 88.7% of audited outlets, so entry means competing for shelf space that is already taken. Fourth, the main GT barriers were price, demand uncertainty, margin and cold-chain-related spoilage, while MT shoppers pushed back on price, loyalty and low visibility. Fifth, high-protein curd and paneer drew stronger interest in a fitness-adjacent store…

abstract: Background Community learning centers ( Pusat Kegiatan Belajar Masyarakat , PKBM) are Indonesia’s main providers of second-chance upper-secondary (Package C) education, yet little is known about how their learning services develop learners’ 21st-century skills. This study examined whether learning service quality develops learners’ critical thinking, creativity, collaboration, and communication (4C skills) directly or through tutor competence. Methods A cross-sectional survey was completed by 354 final-level Package C learners drawn by proportional geographic stratification from 4,530 learners in urban, coastal, and highland PKBMs in South Sulawesi, Indonesia. Adapted, expert-reviewed instruments measured the three constructs, and data were analyzed with partial least squares structural equation modeling using 5,000 bootstrap resamples. Results The measurement model met reliability and validity criteria, and full collinearity tests indicated that common method bias was unlikely. Learning service quality predicted tutor competence (β = 0.545, p < 0.001), and tutor competence predicted 4C skills (β = 0.548, p < 0.001), whereas the direct effect of service quality on 4C skills was not significant (β = 0.170, p = 0.146). title: CONTENT MARKETING DIMENSIONS AND CUSTOMER PATRONAGE OF QUICK-SERVICE RESTAURANTS IN CALABAR, NIGERIA
abstract: This study examined the effect of content marketing on customer patronage of quick-service restaurants (QSRs) in Calabar, Cross River State, Nigeria. Specifically, it assessed the effects of informational content marketing, visual content marketing and social media content marketing on customer patronage. A cross-sectional survey design was adopted, and primary data were collected from customers of purposively selected QSR outlets using a structured questionnaire. The sample size was determined using the Topman formula, resulting in 369 questionnaires being administered, of which 328 were returned and found usable, representing a response rate of 88.9%. The data were analysed using descriptive statistics and multiple linear regression with the Statistical Package for the Social Sciences (SPSS). The regression model was statistically significant (F = 35.640, p < .001), explaining 24.8% of the variation in customer patronage (R² = .248). The findings revealed that informational content marketing (Beta = .163, p = .010), visual content marketing (Beta = .288, p = .001) and social media content marketing (Beta = .372, p = .002) each had a positive and statistically significant effect on customer patronage. Social media content marketing recorded the strongest relative contribution, followed by visual and informational content marketing. The study concludes that content marketing is…

State Capacity and Environmental Regulation: The Case of Air Pollution in La Oroya, Peru (1922–1927)
abstract: This study evaluates the Peruvian state’s resolution of the La Oroya emissions conflict (1922–1927), assessing whether it demonstrated state capacity by incorporating environmental considerations and effectively implementing the measures adopted. Using a historical-institutional approach based on the qualitative analysis of historical sources—bulletins and reports of the Corps of Mining Engineers of Peru (CIMP), established in 1902 to manage mineral resources, official bulletins of the Ministry of Development, and secondary literature—the analysis applies Carpenter’s concept of bureaucratic autonomy (legitimacy, organizational capacity, and political differentiation) to examine the CIMP’s role during its first decades. The results show that, despite its political support, legitimacy, and technical capacity, the CIMP’s bureaucratic autonomy was constrained on the criterion of political differentiation. Its Report on La Oroya’s Emissions (1926) identified the problem and proposed technical solutions, but the CIMP lacked the authority to enforce them: the Cerro de Pasco Copper Corporation complied only partially, installed filters only between 1936 and 1942, and purchased much of the affected land at low prices. In La Oroya, the resolution favored corporate interests over environmental and community concerns, reflecting Peru’s broader trend of prioritizing economic growth over env…

title: Physiological and clinical comparison of two high-frequency oscillatory ventilation with volume guarantee strategies in preterm infants with respiratory distress syndrome
abstract: Abstract Objective: To compare the physiological performance and clinical outcomes of two high-frequency oscillatory ventilation with volume guarantee (HFOV-VG) strategies in preterm infants born at less than 30 weeks of gestation. Methods: In this retrospective cohort study, 88 preterm infants born at less than 30 weeks of gestation received either a low-VThf/high-frequency strategy (oscillatory frequency 15–17 Hz; measured VThf/kg 1.5–1.9 mL/kg; n=61) or a high-VThf/standard-frequency strategy (oscillatory frequency 10–12 Hz; measured VThf/kg 2.0–3.0 mL/kg; n=27). Minute-level ventilator and paired arterial blood gas data were analysed. Clinical outcomes included moderate-to-severe bronchopulmonary dysplasia (BPD), mortality, and duration of invasive mechanical ventilation. Results: A total of 267,786 ventilator observations and 825 paired blood gas observations were analysed. PaCO₂ was comparable between strategies (50 [44–56] vs 49 [43–57] mmHg; p=0.67). The low-VThf/high-frequency strategy was associated with lower FiO₂ requirements, reduced oscillatory pressure variability, and shorter invasive mechanical ventilation (10 [6–21] vs 24 [12–39] days; p=0.0005). title: Effect of ultrasonic vibration frequency on material removal mechanism and surface finishing performance of additively manufactured fuel nozzles during abrasive flow machining
abstract: Additively manufactured aerospace fuel nozzles possess complex internal channels and superior structural integration; however, their practical application is restricted by poor surface quality caused by powder adhesion and the balling effect during additive manufacturing. Ultrasonic-assisted abrasive flow machining (UAAFM) provides a promising solution for improving the surface integrity of such complex components, while the influence mechanism of ultrasonic parameters on abrasive flow behavior and material removal remains insufficiently understood.In this study, a coupled acoustic–flow–particle numerical model was developed to investigate the effect of ultrasonic vibration frequency on the machining characteristics of additively manufactured fuel nozzles. The transient interaction among ultrasonic excitation, abrasive flow behavior, and particle transport was analyzed based on a turbulence model, non-Newtonian abrasive medium model, and Lagrangian particle tracking method. The effects of ultrasonic frequencies ranging from 25 to 80 kHz on velocity distribution, dynamic pressure, wall stress, and abrasive particle motion were systematically investigated. title: Scalp high‐frequency oscillations differentiate neonates with hypoxic–ischemic encephalopathy with and without electroencephalographically confirmed seizures
abstract: Abstract Objective Hypoxic–ischemic encephalopathy (HIE) is a leading cause of neonatal seizures, but seizure detection is challenging when continuous electroencephalography (EEG) is unavailable and neonates undergo only a single routine EEG. Biomarkers derived from routine EEG may aid identification of neonates with seizures. We investigated whether scalp high‐frequency oscillation (HFO) rates derived from the first eligible routine EEG (1) differentiate neonates with HIE with and without seizures; and (2) contribute to seizure classification alongside established clinical, neurophysiological, and imaging biomarkers. Methods We retrospectively analyzed routine scalp EEG recordings from 33 term neonates with HIE (17 with seizures, 16 without), obtained at a mean postnatal age of 4 ± 3 days. The mean analyzed EEG duration was 38 ± 14 min in neonates with seizures and 36 ± 20 min in those without. HFO rates in sleep segments were quantified using a validated automated detector. Results Scalp HFO rates were significantly higher in neonates with seizures than in those without (.12 ± .11 vs. .03 ± .02 HFOs/min/channel, adjusted p = .02). An HFO rate threshold of .07 HFOs/min/channel optimally discriminated neonates who had seizures from those who did not (area under the curve [AUC] = .81). title: Dual-axis genetic regulation of iron homeostasis links to metabolic diseases
abstract: Abstract Iron homeostasis is essential for physiological function and is implicated in multiple complex diseases, yet its shared genetic architecture with metabolic disease remains incompletely understood. Here, we analyzed genome-wide association study summary statistics for five iron-related traits: serum ferritin, total iron-binding capacity, transferrin saturation, liver iron concentration, and spleen iron concentration. Using genomic structural equation modeling, we identified two genetic dimensions, termed F1 and F2, that capture distinct patterns of variation across these traits. F1 showed stronger enrichment for iron-response and storage-associated signals, whereas F2 was more closely related to iron transport and tissue iron distribution. Transcriptome-wide association and Mendelian randomization analyses prioritized candidate genes associated with each dimension. Their genetic relationships with obesity and type 2 diabetes also differed, suggesting that genetically defined components of iron regulation may have distinct relationships with metabolic disease risk. We further applied the pleiotropic analysis under the composite null hypothesis (PLACO) to identify loci with potential pleiotropic associations between iron-related traits and complex diseases. From Thermal Thresholds to Temporal Response: A Dual‐Dimension Framework for Lithium‐Ion Battery Safety
abstract: ABSTRACT Lithium‐ion batteries (LIBs) face a persistent safety challenge from thermal runaway (TR), a catastrophic failure triggered by exothermic chain reactions under abuse conditions. Despite extensive progress in material‐level thermal stabilization, most strategies remain confined to raising temperature thresholds, overlooking the temporal dimension of TR progression. This review introduces a temperature–time dual‐dimensional framework that unifies TR mechanisms, characterization techniques, and mitigation strategies. We first elucidate the TR process and put forward key parameters. Meanwhile, a thermal–electrochemical–chemical (TEC) coupling model is constructed that reveals three intervention windows: decoupling (temperature‐prioritized), interruption (time‐prioritized), and containment (system‐level). We then survey characterization methods across material and cell levels, followed by a critical assessment of temperature‐ and time‐domain strategies, ranging from thermally stable materials to smart electrolytes, PTC collectors, and self‐responsive separators. We construct a design space that map strategies by their ΔT and Δt effectiveness, highlighting the trade‐off between temperature stability and time responsiveness. Finally, we outline three strategic frontiers, that is, multifunctional materials, machine learning‐enabled prediction, and self‐reporting/self‐healing s…

title: Contact-End-Voltage Analysis of Anisotropic Charge Transport in a Mo/MoSe2 Layered Heterostructure
abstract: Abstract Understanding anisotropic charge transport in two-dimensional layered heterostructures is important for vertical electronic devices. Here, we examine in-plane and cross-plane transport in a Mo/MoSe2 heterostructure with a designed nanoarchitecture. The in-plane resistivity changes by less than 5% between room temperature and liquid-helium temperature, consistent with transport dominated by the metallic Mo layers. Contact-end-voltage measurements across contacts of different widths are used to estimate lead and interfacial contributions to the measured cross-plane resistance. For this sample, the resulting cross-plane resistivity is approximately 103 times larger than the in-plane resistivity. The cross-plane resistivity decreases by approximately a factor of three from room temperature to liquid-nitrogen temperature, which is inconsistent with simple thermally activated transport through intrinsic MoSe2 states. Large-area contacts exhibit linear current–voltage behavior, whereas reduced-area contacts exhibit nonlinear behavior. These observations are consistent with contributions from localized conductive pathways in the large-area geometry and barrier-limited transport in the reduced-area geometry. The results demonstrate a contact-end-voltage approach for examining anisotropic transport in an individual layered heterostructure while accounting for contact and lead co…

title: Spatiotemporal Weather Variability Modelling for Mango Yield Forecasting Using Machine Learning Techniques
abstract: This study developed and evaluated a machine-learning framework for forecasting mango yield in two mango-growing areas of Tamil Nadu, India: Periyakulam (Theni district) and Krishnagiri district. Annual rainfall, minimum and maximum temperature, relative humidity and mango-yield observations were compiled for 2010–2023 in Periyakulam and 2015–2023 in Krishnagiri. The resulting dataset included 114 district–variety–year observations covering six mango varieties. Descriptive assessments of inter-annual weather variability were combined with Pearson correlation analysis, analysis of variance (ANOVA) and a lightweight one-dimensional convolutional neural network (1D-CNN) regression model. Model performance was assessed using a 70:30 training–validation split and five-fold cross-validation, with Random Forest, Support Vector Regression and multiple linear regression as comparators. Yield differed significantly among varieties (F = 10.465, p < 0.001), whereas the district main effect was not significant (F = 0.406, p = 0.525). Validation root mean square error (RMSE) ranged from 3.12 to 3.94 kg/tree in Periyakulam and from 2.98 to 4.01 kg/tree in Krishnagiri. Across the two districts, validation correlations ranged from 88.65% to 95.64%. title: Prediction of soil selenium content and model optimization for a watershed in the Taihang Mountains based on machine learning models
abstract: Abstract Accurate spatial prediction of soil selenium (Se) in mountainous regions is constrained by limited field sample sizes and unreasonable model validation strategies, which complicates co‑management of selenium‑rich agricultural production and heavy‑metal ecological risk mitigation. In this work, we investigated a metamorphic mountain watershed on the eastern Taihang Mountains, Hebei Province. A total of 107 topsoil samples were collected, and 17 soil geochemical indicators were measured. Two geostatistical models (ordinary kriging, OK; regression kriging, RK) alongside four machine-learning algorithms: Elastic-Net, radial-basis-function support vector machine (RBF-SVM), Honest Random Forest (Honest RF), and XGBoost were benchmarked. We adopted a dual nested cross-validation scheme to separate model-fitting performance from spatial extrapolation capacity. The results indicated that our spatial‑block cross‑validation avoids inflated accuracy caused by random sample division. Among all competing models, Honest RF achieved the optimal performance, exhibiting minimal residual spatial aggregation and stable predictive performance for unmeasured watershed areas. title: Dynamic blood glucose trajectory is 28-day all-cause mortality in critically ill patients with heart failure: A survival prediction analysis
abstract: Background Heart failure (HF) is a global public health issue. Blood glucose influences HF progression, but research on its dynamic changes and mortglity remains limited. Objective This study aimed to investigate the association of baseline admission blood glucose and its dynamic changes with all-cause mortality in patients with HF. Methods This retrospective cohort study used data from MIMIC-IV and a tertiary hospital. We identified distinct glycemic trajectories using group-based trajectory modeling (GBTM) and assessed their association with 28-day all-cause mortality via Cox proportional hazards models and restricted cubic spline analysis (RCS). Machine learning models were applied to evaluate the predictive value of glycemia. Results A total of 6142 patients from the MIMIC-IV database and 391 local patients were included. Results showed that five dynamic blood glucose trajectory groups were identified. Among them, the moderate-to-high and high-level groups exhibited elevated mortality risk [HR (95% CI): 1.546 (1.231–1.942); 1.572 (1.140–2.168)]. Incorporating blood glucose trajectories into predictive models moderately improved the predictive performance for outcomes, and the Deepsurv model demonstrated better predictive accuracy and stability. Conclusion Although current retrospective design limits causal inference and warrants prospective validation, the present study pro…

title: Machine Learning-Based Prediction of Tumor Recurrence or Progression in Patients with Non-Functioning Pituitary Adenomas
abstract: Abstract Background Despite advances in surgical technique, postoperative tumor recurrence or progression (R/P) remains a major challenge among patients with clinically non-functioning pituitary adenomas (NFPA). Reliable tools for individualized R/P risk stratification are limited. Objective To develop and evaluate machine learning (ML) models that integrate clinical, immunohistochemical, and radiomic features based on preoperative MRI towards predicting tumor R/P in patients with NFPA who underwent pituitary surgery. Methods We retrospectively analyzed data of patients with NFPA who underwent their first pituitary operation at Massachusetts General Hospital between 2005–2019, had preoperative postcontrast MRI images available, and ≥3 months of follow-up and conducted an exploratory multimodal modelling analysis. Supervised ML models combining clinical and radiomic features were then trained to predict R/P and were internally evaluated using cross-validation. SHAP analysis was used to identify predictors of R/P. Results 537 patients met inclusion criteria (median age: 58 yr, range: 18–92 yr; 59% male). Overall, 120 patients (22%) experienced R/P during a median follow-up of 74 months. Median R/P-free survival was 170 months. Pareto optimization of BEMU traction battery capacity and recharging infrastructure
abstract: Abstract The increasing integration of the energy and transport sectors requires efficient solutions for electrifying rail networks. Battery-powered trains (battery electric multiple units - BEMUs) offer a promising alternative to full electrification, but their range is limited by the current state of battery technology and recharging infrastructure. This study presents an optimization model that simultaneously optimizes the recharging infrastructure and traction batteries of the trains, enabling a system design based on BEMU power demand and timetable data. The model considers various factors, including route topology, timetable, charging infrastructure, and battery aging. A case study of a non-electrified mountain line considering two combinations of optimization targets and a case study for a long-distance line with partial electrification demonstrate the flexibility of the model and its applicability for different optimization tasks. The optimization results provide insights into the optimal dimensioning of charging infrastructure and batteries, considering factors such as heating ventilation and air conditioning (HVAC) demand, end-of-life capacity, discrete power of charging infrastructure, and battery replacement. title: Boosting Oxygen Transport with Nanoporous Graphdiyne for High‐Capacity Li−O 2 Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT Li−O 2 batteries have attracted extensive attention due to their potential to achieve several times higher energy density than Li‐ion batteries. However, the actual discharge capacity and rate performance still fall short of practical requirements, as cathodes made of dense carbon black particles hinder the fast diffusion of O 2 deep into the cathode during discharge, thus severely limiting cathode utilization. In this work, we introduce graphdiyne (GDY) into the cathode to accelerate O 2 transport. GDY is a two‐dimensional material with intrinsic nanopores that allow O 2 molecules to pass through. When incorporated into carbon‐black cathodes, GDY particles forms pathways of low diffusion resistance that facilitate O 2 diffusion deep into the cathode. The accelerated O 2 transport, which is supported by gas permeability measurement, enhances the discharge capacity of the battery by over 4 times to 10.36 mAh cm −2 , equivalent to 950 mAh g −1 (Li2O2+carbon) . Characterization of the discharged cathode reveals that GDY introduction substantially changes the growth of the discharge product, lithium peroxide, promoting its formation both in the form of larger particles and deeper throughout the cathode, thereby contributing to higher discharge capacity. Our findings demonstrate a new strategy for accelerating mass transport to improve cathodes utilization, and ultimately r…

title: Scalable Capacity‐Constrained Power Diagrams via Compressed Optimal Assignment
abstract: Abstract Power diagrams with prescribed capacities are widely used in geometry processing, including blue‐noise sampling, remeshing, and constrained clustering. The problem can be viewed as a semi‐discrete optimal transport problem and is commonly discretized by dense sampling into a capacity‐constrained assignment between n samples and m sites. Since this assignment is repeatedly solved in Lloyd‐type optimization, its efficiency is crucial to scalability. We propose an exact algorithm for the resulting discrete capacity‐constrained assignment problem. Unlike general‐purpose minimum‐cost flow solvers, which treat the input as an abstract graph, and entropic‐regularized approximations, which sacrifice exactness, our method exploits the asymmetry m ≪ n between sites and samples, performing augmentations on a compressed auxiliary graph with only m + 2 nodes while maintaining point‐level transfer costs using priority queues. We prove that augmenting paths in the full residual network can be projected to bounded‐length walks on the auxiliary graph, yielding an O(nm 2 log n) running time and near‐linear scaling in the number of samples for fixed m. Experiments on synthetic data and geometry‐processing tasks show that our method achieves one or two orders of magnitude speedup over classical algorithms while preserving exact optimality for the discrete transport problem, enabling effic…

Carbon Sequestration in Agricultural Soils through Agronomic Interventions: A Review
abstract: Agricultural soils are simultaneously a source of greenhouse gases, a reservoir of organic carbon and a foundation for crop production. Rebuilding soil organic carbon (SOC) through agronomic management is therefore attractive, but sequestration must be distinguished from temporary carbon storage, surface redistribution and displacement of emissions outside the field. This review critically synthesizes evidence on the processes that govern SOC accumulation and stabilization, and evaluates residue management, conservation tillage, cover crops, diversified rotations, organic amendments, integrated nutrient management, agroforestry, water management and rehabilitation of degraded soils. Plant-derived inputs, microbial transformations, mineral associations and aggregation jointly determine whether newly supplied carbon persists. Evidence from meta-analyses indicates that cover cropping and sustained organic inputs often increase SOC, whereas claims of large climate benefits from no-tillage alone require caution because sampling depth, bulk density and operational history influence the apparent response. The article further examines trade-offs involving nitrous oxide, methane, crop yield, competition for water and nutrients, and biomass availability in smallholder systems. title: Carbon fluxes in rhodoliths, coraliths and artificial substrates on tropical reefs
abstract: Abstract Understanding how calcifying benthic systems contribute to short-term carbon dynamics helps assess their role in shallow tropical ecosystems under environmental change. We compared day-to-night relative patterns of net organic carbon production and net calcification in three contrasting functional units from the Colombian Caribbean: rhodoliths, spherical free-living colonies (coraliths) of the coral Siderastrea radians , and colonized artificial substrates mimicking the rhodolith shape. In situ incubations were conducted during morning, afternoon, and nighttime periods under natural environmental conditions. We observed significant variation among incubation periods and across all functional units, with higher daytime net organic carbon production and calcification and reduced or negative nighttime values. Rhodoliths exhibited the highest daytime rates of both net organic carbon production and net calcification and the greatest morning-to-night contrast in net calcification (11.6-fold). Colonized artificial substrates showed the greatest contrast in net organic carbon production (5.37-fold) and consistent nighttime net CaCO₃ dissolution, whereas corals exhibited comparatively lower daytime rates and more moderate contrasts.
