Protein Dynamics Modulates Excitonic Coupling in the Water-Soluble Chlorophyll-Binding Protein
abstract: Abstract We investigated the internal dynamics of the water-soluble chlorophyll-binding protein (WSCP), an important model system for light harvesting in photosynthesis, by combining all-atom molecular dynamics (MD) simulations with quasielastic neutron scattering (QENS) experiments. Dynamic structure factors simulated using MDANSE show excellent agreement with WSCP QENS spectra, thus capturing the relevant picosecond protein motions and revealing that WSCP pigment–pigment distances and their relative transition dipole orientations deviate from crystallographic values and, more significantly, are characterized by rather broad distributions in the solution state at physiological temperatures. Illustrative excitonic calculations demonstrate that realistic structural fluctuations can lead to measurable variations in excitonic coupling and, consequently, affect spectroscopic features of the WSCP pigment dimer. Within limitations of the classical MD simulation, the results show that a combination of MD simulations with QENS experiments can provide a validated route to link protein dynamics with spectroscopic observables in WSCP and, in perspective, in similar pigment–protein systems.

title: Pre‐Branching Conversion of Bio‐Diols via Methanol‐Mediated Cascade Coupling for Sustainable Aviation Fuels
abstract: ABSTRACT Sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) is indispensable for aviation decarbonization. Nevertheless, conventional SAF syntheses from biomass‐derived alcohols suffer from tedious reaction pathways, energy‐intensive post‐isomerization, and inadequate control of alkane branching. Herein, we propose a novel “pre‐branching” strategy for high‐quality SAF production: C 2 ‐C 4 bio‐based vicinal diols convert into C 4 ‐C 6 branched alcohols over CuMgAlO x in supercritical methanol, integrating dehydrogenation, cross‐aldol condensation, pinacol rearrangement, and in‐situ hydrogenation; subsequent oligomerization and hydrotreating further upgrade C 4 ‐C 6 alcohol intermediates into branched C 8 ‐C 16 alkanes for aviation applications. With ethylene glycol as a model substrate, a maximum 77.9 C% yield of C 4 ‐C 6 alcohols was achieved. In situ spectroscopy and 13 C isotope labeling reveal that Cu + /Cu 0 sites catalyze (de)hydrogenation, MgO promotes C─C coupling via cross‐aldol condensation, acidic AlO x sites induce 1,2‐alkyl migration of vicinal diols for skeletal branching, and methanol serves as an in situ hydrogen donor. Subsequent oligomerization over Amberlyst‐35 and hydrotreating over Ni/Al 2 O 3 deliver an 83.3 C% toward C 8 ‐C 16 iso‐alkanes, affording a 64.9% overall carbon yield from ethylene glycol. Without post‐isomerization, the SAF features a ‐65°C freezing point and robu…

title: Controlling Semi-Crystallinity in P3HT for Efficient Perovskite Solar Cells and Low-Power Applications
abstract: Abstract Poly(3-hexylthiophene) (P3HT) is a promising low-cost, hole-transport material for stable, scalable perovskite solar cells (PSCs). However, the performance of P3HT-based PSCs is often limited by suboptimal charge transport associated with disordered molecular aggregation and packing in solution-processed P3HT films. Here, we demonstrate a solvent-controlled strategy to regulate the molecular ordering and morphology of P3HT in MAPbI3-based PSCs. Chloroform and dichlorobenzene (DCB), selected for their different boiling points and evaporation rates, are combined to tune solvent evaporation during P3HT film formation. The optimized CHCl3/DCB (4:1) blend produces a compact, ordered film with reduced crystallite misorientation, yielding a champion PCE of 17.1% without additional interfacial passivation or modification of the P3HT hole-transport layer. The optimized processing conditions were also used to fabricate PSC modules with active areas up to 36 cm2. Under outdoor sunlight, a 36 cm2 module delivered an output power of approximately 0.1 W, while module-scale devices powered commercial low-power electronics under indoor illumination. Long-term ambient dark-storage measurements showed retention of ∼80% of the initial PCE after one year using a simple paraffin−acrylic encapsulation strategy. These results demonstrate that solvent-controlled molecular ordering and film mo…

title: Mango Anthracnose: New Sources of Resistance and Effect of Temperature on Disease Severity in Mangifera spp.
abstract: Anthracnose caused by Colletotrichum spp. is a major postharvest disease that can rot mangoes within 8 days, affecting overseas shipment. In this study, eight Mangifera species ( M. casturi , M. indica , M. lalijiwa , M. laurina , M. odorata , M. zeylanica , M. sylvatica , and M. rubropetala ) and seven M. indica varieties (‘Totapuri’, ‘Nam Doc Mai’, ‘Maha Chanok’, ‘Kensington Pride’, ‘Keitt’, ‘Sunny’, and ‘Irwin’) were inoculated with C. asianum and evaluated for 25 days for anthracnose severity at two different temperatures, 11 and 25°C. Anthracnose severity was significantly lower at 11°C than at 25°C. Significant differences were observed in disease severity among the eight species tested. M. casturi exhibited the lowest anthracnose severity (6.1%). Among M. indica varieties, ‘Sunny’ exhibited the lowest anthracnose severity (21.6%), followed by ‘Keitt’ (21.9%). Cold treatment for 15 days helped to reduce anthracnose severity between 25 and 70% for M. lalijiwa , M. laurina , M. sylvatica , and M. zeylanica , and M. indica varieties (‘Sunny’, ‘Irwin’, ‘Maha Chanok’, ‘Totapuri’, and ‘Nam Doc Mai’). On the other hand, anthracnose severity increased after cold treatment for 15 days for M. casturi , M. odorata , M. rubropetala , ‘Keitt’, and ‘Kensington Pride’ by 62-fold. Overall, tolerance to mango anthracnose in the wild species M. casturi and in the variety ‘Sunny’ is reporte…

title: Distribution of VC1-like ribAB sequences and vicine-convicine across the genus Vicia: evolutionary implications
abstract: Abstract Background Many Vicia species contain vicine and convicine (VC), which limit the use of faba bean and some vetches in food and feed. The first step in VC biosynthesis in V. faba is shared with the riboflavin pathway and attributed to VC1 as the major gene and RIBA2 as a minor gene, both being members of the multicopy ribAB family. Since riboflavin is ubiquitous in living organisms but VC is not universal even in Vicia , we examined the distribution of VC1 and VC production in the genus. Methods Three accessions of each of 33 Vicia species were grown in glasshouse conditions to provide fresh seeds for VC analysis and leaves for DNA analysis. VC was analysed by standard (U)HPLC methods. PCR was used to amplify fragments of the VC1 / ribAB gene for sequencing, and these sequences were used as a proxy for the gene to create a phylogenetic tree. COX1 and ITS2 sequences were used for examining the nucleotide diversity in the genus. Results VC and DNA sequences consistent with VC1 were found only in members of subgenus Vicia . One member of this subgenus, V. lathyroides , carried an apparently intact VC1 sequence but produced no detectable VC. Convicine was found only in species that had vicine. VC1/ribAB sequences outside of subgenus Vicia showed fewer non-synonymous substitutions than those from subgenus Vicia , whereas synonymous variation was similar between groups. Concl…

title: HIGH-EFFICIENCY TRIPLE-INPUT DC–DC CONVERTER WITH OPTIMIZED DESIGN FOR RENEWABLE POWER SYSTEMS
abstract: Small renewable sources such as photovoltaic strings, fuel cells and batteries rarely share a common voltage, and none of these sources comes close to the 120 V bus expected by many auxiliary loads. A triple-input high step-up direct current to direct current (DC–DC) converter is reported here for exactly that situation. The circuit uses one switched-capacitor branch and three inductor–switch cells fed from 12 V, 24 V and 18 V, and was sized for 120 V at 2 A into a 60 Ω load, roughly the rating of an electric vehicle auxiliary rail. Duty ratios of 0.90, 0.80 and 0.85 set the three gains at 10, 5 and about 6.7. Each inductor (0.27 mH, 0.48 mH and 0.3825 mH) was chosen for the same 0.4 A current ripple, and a 22 µF capacitor holds the output ripple under 1 V at 100 kHz. Losses were estimated term by term: conduction and switching in every metal–oxide–semiconductor field-effect transistor (MOSFET), forward drop and reverse recovery in the diodes, copper and core loss in the inductors, equivalent series resistance (ESR) loss in the capacitor, and gate-drive power. The simulated total loss was 3.5 W with V1 alone and 5.75 W with all three inputs, i.e. 98.56% and 97.66% efficiency at 240 W, and the change of output voltage between no load and full load was 1.67%. In the triple-input case, 3.4 W of the 5.75 W was lost in the MOSFETs and diodes, so the switching devices, and not the in…

title: Multi-stage optimal allocation of power system resources using a combination of deep reinforcement learning and chance-constrained programming
abstract: Abstract With a high proportion of renewable energy integration, power system resource allocation faces the challenge of co-optimizing long-term dynamic uncertainties and probabilistic security constraints. Traditional deterministic programming and stochastic optimization methods struggle to balance economy, flexibility, and security. This paper constructs a multi-stage resource optimization allocation method that combines Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) and Chance Constrained Programming (CCP). To address the problem that resource allocation is difficult to adapt to the evolution of system state during long-term planning, a dynamic decision-making environment including new energy, energy storage, demand response, and network regulation resources is constructed. The Soft Actor-Critic (SAC) algorithm is used to learn the nonlinear mapping between state and configuration actions to achieve multi-stage in-distribution adaptability during rolling stages. For the problem of insufficient safety constraints in the configuration strategy, the CCP mechanism is applied to convert the new energy output error and load fluctuation into probabilistic safety constraints. Economic optimization and safety control coordination are achieved through risk feedback and Lagrange multiplier updates, and combined with the rolling deduction mechanism, the subsequent resource allocation path is continu…

title: Climate-driven peak squeeze threatens a rare deadwood moss (Buxbaumia viridis) in Türkiye
Segmented maximum power point tracking for photovoltaic systems using variable-step perturb-and-observe and predictive fuzzy PID control
abstract: Photovoltaic maximum power point tracking (MPPT) faces a trade-off between rapid dynamic response and accurate steady-state regulation. This study proposes a segmented MPPT framework that uses large-step perturb-and-observe (P&O) control for coarse tracking outside a normalized voltage range of 0.75Uoc-0.90Uoc and prediction-assisted fuzzy PID control for fine regulation within this range. The framework was evaluated through MATLAB/Simulink simulations, threshold-sensitivity and hysteresis analyses, partial-shading tests, and outdoor hardware experiments. Under irradiance and temperature variations, the proposed method reduced tracking time by up to 79.9 % and dynamic power overshoot by more than 98 %, while maintaining tracking errors below 0.18 %. Threshold-sensitivity analysis confirmed the 0.75/0.90 range as an effective operating interval, achieving 100 % relative tracking efficiency, while hysteresis reduced switching events by 70.27 %. Under partial-shading conditions, tracking efficiencies of 99.23 % and 98.80 % were achieved. Outdoor experiments further verified real-time mode switching and demonstrated improved energy harvesting. Overall, the proposed segmented control framework enhances both dynamic and steady-state MPPT performance with low computational complexity, making it suitable for embedded photovoltaic applications.

OPTIMIZING THE INSULATION LAYER FOR ENERGY EFFICIENCY IN BUILDING FACADES
abstract: This paper examines the role of shape optimization in improving the thermal performance of building facades. The study investigates whether modifying the internal interface between brick and expanded polystyrene (EPS) insulation can enhance seasonal thermal performance without increasing material usage. A two-dimensional steady-state heat diffusion model is solved using a finite-difference scheme. The interface is parameterized by a cubic polynomial under a strict volume-preservation constraint, and optimal shapes are determined through a discrete search. Results indicate that interface geometry affects heat transfer differently across seasons: redistribution of insulation changes thermal resistance under summer conditions, while in winter it alters conductive heat pathways. Overall, geometric redistribution can influence seasonal thermal response while keeping total material volume constant. Without insolation, however, the winter optimal geometry increases heat loss, so the winter result applies to peak-insolation conditions only.

title: Knowledge and attitude toward energy and environmental sustainability in Islamic schools around Indonesia’s capital
A 360° Survey on Reconfigurability of HPC Storage Systems for Efficient I/O
abstract: High-performance computing (HPC) storage and I/O software stacks have been challenging to configure due to multiple software layers, interdependencies among those layers, and the number of parameters to tune within each layer. The storage stack has become increasingly complex with the ever-growing sets of new software and hardware. In addition, there is a shift in HPC applications from modeling and simulations (mod-sim) to AI training and inference. While several efforts focused on tuning I/O parameters of write-heavy simulation workloads, configuring I/O for random and read-heavy AI applications has still been in progress. Although the HPC storage stack could be reconfigured to meet these diverse write and read requirements, finding optimal I/O configurations for even a single application is a challenging task. This survey proposes a taxonomy of HPC storage and I/O system configurations and reconfigurability for bringing a consensus to the I/O parameters that are tunable by clients (i.e., users and applications). In this paper, we survey I/O tuning and optimization, harnessing the HPC I/O system configuration knowledge from the past decade. This paper can serve as a primary source of information for HPC I/O researchers and developers to design and optimize novel tuning strategies that improve storage and I/O system reconfigurability and performance.

In Vitro Cell Culture Evaluation of Camel Milk Biocompatibility as a Storage Medium for Avulsed Teeth: A Preliminary Investigation
abstract: ABSTRACT Background The long‐term success of replanting an avulsed tooth depends fundamentally on preserving the viability of the periodontal ligament fibroblasts and associated mesenchymal stem cells adhering to the root surface. When immediate replantation is unfeasible, an appropriate physiological storage medium is required to prevent cell death. Aim This study aims to evaluate the efficacy of camel milk variants as an interim storage medium for maintaining the viability and metabolic activity of human periodontal ligament fibroblasts (HPLFs) and human bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells (hBMMSCs). Materials and Methods HPLFs and hBMMSCs were cultured and subsequently incubated in various experimental media: fresh unprocessed camel milk, filtered fresh camel milk, commercially pasteurized camel milk, and commercially pasteurized whole bovine milk. Dulbecco's Modified Eagle Medium (DMEM), normal saline, tap water, and dry storage served as experimental controls. Cellular viability and metabolic dynamics were quantitatively and qualitatively assessed at 1, 3, and 24 h utilizing MTT assays, Alamar Blue assays, and Live/Dead fluorescent confocal microscopy. Results Unprocessed camel milk, particularly the filtered variant, induced a distinct hypermetabolic response (> 150% viability relative to controls) at the 1‐ and 3‐h intervals. At the 24‐h mark, filtered unprocessed camel m…

abstract: Silicon Photonics offers petabyte-per-second PB/s data rates for future data links. Electrical crosstalk must be minimized for density. Discrete Mach-Zehnder Modulators are needed in silicon-based integrated photonic circuits. Building the traveling-wave electrode Coplanar strip line (CPS) and coplanar waveguide (CPW) and improving recalculation reduced crosstalk and improved system efficiency. Cutting-edge software like COMSOL Multiphysics and MATLAB was used to develop a configuration with a shared-ground coplanar waveguide (CPW) with minimal separation between the traveling wave electrode and compact dimensions, resulting in minimal interference, roughly -70dB, compared to (-21dB) for the CPS layout standard. At speeds beyond 50 Gbps, the enhanced CPW with shared-ground design ensures signal integrity and with a Bit Error Rate (BER) of 10-15 and the assured 50-ohm impedance ensures maximum interoperability with high-speed communication systems

Tri-level hybrid electric bus scheduling under time-of-use tariffs for cost-effective public transportation
abstract: Abstract The deployment of electric buses requires coordinated fleet scheduling and charging management to maintain passenger services while controlling infrastructure and electricity costs. This study proposes a Tri-Level Hybrid Electric Bus Scheduling under Time-of-Use tariffs (TLH-EBS-TOU) framework that combines Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) for global exploration, Rule-Based Scoring Large Neighborhood Search (RBS-LNS) for schedule restructuring, and Mixed Integer Linear Programming (MILP) for neighbourhood repair. A TOU-aware charging-time selection procedure coordinates charging expenditure with battery-energy requirements, compatible-charger availability, deadheading, and prescribed passenger departures. The framework is evaluated on a Madurai transportation network comprising 810 scheduled passenger trips per day and compared with standalone MILP, PSO, and RBS-LNS. The reported baseline solution uses 149 electric buses and 15 chargers, with an annualized total cost of ₹30.86 crore, representing a 4.85% reduction relative to standalone PSO. Bus capital, charger capital, electricity, and deadheading costs decrease by 5.77%, 4.81%, 3.54%, and 3.70%, respectively. Under the modelled conditions 48.00% of the required 37,885kWh per day charging capacity is allocated to the most economical time of day to charge. The results of these tests illustrate the possibilities of co…

title: Optimized droop control-based load flow analysis for islanded AC microgrids with electric vehicle integration
abstract: Abstract Microgrids have become a crucial element of modern power systems with increasing penetration of distributed energy resources and require an accurate load flow analysis (LFA) to determine the steady state operating conditions of Microgrid. In islanded configurations, traditional LFA methods are less effective due to the absence of a reference bus. In this type of network, the bus voltage, network frequency, and coupling between droop-controlled distributed generator (DG) introduce additional nonlinear characteristics that are not addressed by conventional LFA formulations. This paper presents an optimized droop control-based Modified Gauss–Seidel (MGS) method for LFA in AC islanded microgrids (IMGs) with integration of static electric vehicle (EV) load models in which voltage and frequency are treated as operating variables due to IMG operation. A bio-inspired optimization is employed to obtain suitable DG droop coefficients with the objective of network loss minimization and maintaining voltage and frequency in an acceptable range with improved DG power sharing. The proposed approach is evaluated on 6-bus and 33-bus AC IMG test networks under diverse static EV load scenarios and is compared with alternative optimization approaches. The optimized droop coefficient achieves active power loss reduction of 23.35%, 10.57%, and 18.97% for EV-1, EV-2, and EV-3 load models, re…

title: Functionalized Clay-Based Ion-Selective Membranes for Modular Moisture-Electric Generation
abstract: Abstract Moisture electric generators (MEGs) offer a mechanical and thermal-gradient-free route to sustainable electricity. However, they are constrained by low power density, poor durability, and irreversible dehydration. Here, a modular MEG is developed by integrating a nanofluidic ionic conductor (a functionalized kaolinite clay membrane), a replaceable moisture source (a PVA-based hydrogel), and an integrated evaporator (exfoliated V2O5). Raw kaolinite expanded via urea intercalation was functionalized with hygroscopic ZnO nanoparticles and sulfonated PVA (Ek-sPVA-ZnO) to create ion-conducting lamellar nanofluidic membranes. At 80% relative humidity (RH), the Ek-sPVA-ZnO membrane exhibited a conductivity of 4.18 mS cm–1, nearly 6800-fold higher than unmodified Ek-PVA. The optimized device with PVA(Ag)-Gel as the ionic source and V2O5 as the evaporative layer delivered an open-circuit voltage of ∼630 mV, a short-circuit current of ∼45 µA, and a peak power density of 1.2 mW m–2 (at 82% RH). Modular replacement of the desiccated hydrogel restored performance across multiple cycles. Assembly of 84 MEG units scaled voltage and current outputs to 23 V and 76 µA, respectively. Beyond ambient air, the device generated electricity directly from moist solids such as soil, fruit, and skin, demonstrating utility as a self-powered moisture and physiological sensor, including respiration…

title: Stem Cell Cardiomyocytes Maturity Evaluation With Electric Cell-Substrate Impedance Sensing
abstract: Abstract Real-time monitoring of the contractile behavior of pluripotent stem cell-derived cardiomyocytes (PSC-CMs) remains a significant challenge, although the demand for mature cardiomyocytes and PSC-CMs with successfully achieved maturity for transplantation and drug screening is substantially increasing. Therefore, reliable, non-invasive, labor-free, and real-time monitoring tools are essential for evaluating the functional beating behavior of PSC-CMs. In this study, we demonstrated that the electric cell-substrate impedance sensing (ECIS) method can be used to monitor the beating rhythm of PSC-CMs in real time without disrupting their culture environment. The results revealed impedance-based contractile signals of PSC-CMs, corresponding to contraction and relaxation dynamics. By statistically analyzing these electrical readouts, we extracted key functional features that suggest partial functional maturation. These functional features can provide quantitative insight into the physiological state of PSC-CMs during culture period. Immature PSC-CMs exhibit irregular rhythm patterns, low contraction amplitudes that may be associated with weak contractile force, and spontaneous beat rates. As the cells remained on the chip, more regular beating patterns and more stable beat rates were observed, suggesting a partial transition toward functional maturation. This approach can cont…

title: EFFECT OF AIR MASS FLOW RATE ON THE PERFORMANCE OF AN EARTH AIR HEAT EXCHANGER USED IN COOLING THE ELECTRIC MOTOR OF AN OIL PUMP: A NUMERICAL INVESTIGATION
abstract: Elevated temperatures in electric motors significantly contribute to diminished efficiency and a reduced lifespan. An EAHE can be utilized as an efficient cooling method to lessen this issue. This study designed a theoretical model of a 3-phase, squirrel-cage induction motor using ANSYS 2024/FLUENT software. The motor was connected to an underground pipe 4 m deep. This research numerically investigated several design parameters, including the effect of air mass flow rate, pipe diameter, outlet condition, and required cooling load. The study utilized 90 m of PVC (polyvinyl chloride) earth-air heat exchanger (EAHE) pipes with an inlet temperature of 50°C, based on the climatic conditions of Nasiriyah, southern Iraq. The results showed that raising the air mass flow rate reduces the electric motor temperature. The observed reduction in the maximum motor temperature was approximately 11.00%, 11.51%, and 11.85% for pipe diameters of 6, 4, and 3 in, respectively. This shows that the smaller the diameter, the greater the ratio of reduction, and this results in increased system efficiency. An EAHE is effective in its use, bringing the electric motor temperature down, which leads its performance to an increase in efficiency and increases its life

title: Adoption-Stage-Based Content Strategy for Business-to-Business Industrial Marketing: A Case Study of an Indian Industrial Manufacturer's Business Development Product Portfolio
abstract: Business-to-business (B2B) industrial organisations often possess strong engineering capability but limited structured marketing communication, which can leave genuinely useful products under-recognised by the very dealers and customers who already have access to them. This paper presents a case study of an applied content-strategy project carried out within the Business Development (BD) function of a large Indian industrial engine and power-generation manufacturer (referred to here as "the Company" for confidentiality), over an eight-week internship period. The study addresses three BD product portfolios – Product C (engine and genset maintenance offerings), Product B (a telematics and remote-monitoring device), and Product A (a pre-launch fuel additive) – for which no structured, stage-aware communication approach previously existed. Drawing on Rogers' Diffusion of Innovation theory, the Dynamic Staged Adoption Model, and literature on fear-of-missing-out (FOMO) driven consumer behaviour, the study develops and applies an integrated practitioner framework, termed the Who-How-What framework, which maps the customer's adoption category (Who), the product-adoption behaviour expected at each stage (How), and the communication trigger required to move the audience forward (What) across a five-gate adoption journey. Applying this framework across the three product portfolios result…

title: FUNCTIONAL ASSESSMENT AND IMPROVEMENT OF A CONTROL STRATEGY FOR AUTOMATED PART SORTING ON A DIDACTIC WORKBENCH USING A SIEMENS S7-1200 PLC
abstract: This article presents the functional evaluation and improvement of a control strategy for automated part sorting on an AUAPL4000 modular educational workbench. The platform integrates a Siemens SIMATIC S7-1200 programmable logic controller (CPU 1214C DC/DC/DC), industrial sensors, pneumatic actuators, and a conveyor belt driven by a direct current motor. The strategy initially implemented was developed in Ladder logic in TIA Portal V17 and subjected to 90 experimental cycles with manual feeding, in which 90 correct sortings were recorded. For the observed proportion, the exact 95% confidence interval was 95.98% to 100%, a result restricted to the experimental conditions evaluated. The functional analysis identified limitations associated with the use of fixed timing, the conveyor stop sequence, and actuator interlocking. Based on the physical characterization of the workbench and the verification of the input and output mapping, an event-driven sequential strategy was developed, grounded in sorting memorization, exclusive actuation of the actuators, and confirmation of the advance and retract positions and of the passage of the parts through the discard chutes. The results demonstrate the workbench's potential for practical industrial automation activities and indicate the need for experimental validation of the improved strategy in future studies.

title: Comprehensive diagnosis and surgical treatment of nodular nontoxic goiter: clinical experience and improved surgical strategy
abstract: Background. Nodular goiter is one of the most common thyroid pathologies found in both endemic and non-endemic regions. The frequency of thyroid nodules, according to various authors, reaches 30–50 % among the adult population, and in women this pathology is observed several times more often. The purpose of the study was to improve the outcomes of surgical treatment for nodular nontoxic goiter through a differentiated approach to choosing the volume of surgery and reducing the frequency of postoperative complications. Materials and methods. The study included 186 patients divided into control and main groups. The main group used ultrasound with elastography, fine needle aspiration biopsy, as well as a developed algorithm for selecting the volume of surgery and new surgical instruments. The study was approved by the local ethics committee of the Bukhara State Medical Institute named after Abu Ali ibn Sino (Protocol No. 124 dated March 12, 2024). The study was conducted in accordance with the principles of the World Medical Association Declaration of Helsinki (1964, with subsequent amendments). Results. A comparative analysis showed that the use of comprehensive diagnostics increased the accuracy of the preoperative assessment of nodules (sensitivity 91.4 versus 78.2 % in the control group), reduced the number of unnecessary radical operations and reduced the incidence of complic…

title: Association between embolic protection strategy and distal embolization during Jetstream atherectomy for calcified femoropopliteal lesions
MENTAL HEALTH MANAGEMENT IN THE WORKPLACE: ADAPTING TO THE NEW NR-1 AS A STRATEGY FOR ORGANIZATIONAL INCLUSION
abstract: Mental health in the workplace is no longer exclusively a corporate well-being issue and has become a legal requirement in Brazil. This paper analyzes how companies can structure mental health management in the workplace to comply with the new wording of Regulatory Standard No. 1 (NR-1), in force since May 26, 2026, which mandatorily includes psychosocial risks in the Risk Management Program (PGR). The research is qualitative and exploratory-descriptive in nature, developed through bibliographic and documentary research. The results show that Brazil recorded a historic high in sick leave due to mental disorders, with significant economic impact, and that the origin of illness lies mostly in work organization, not in individual weaknesses. It is concluded that effective compliance with the standard requires cultural change, leadership training, and integration between areas, going beyond documentary conformity.

title: Mapping methodologies: Exploring visual narratives of identities, families, and power with immigrant‐origin and marginalized youth
abstract: Abstract Mapping methodologies offer a versatile and innovative approach to understanding the complexity of youth identities, families, and communities, while also attending to the systems of power, privilege, and marginality in which they are embedded. Mapping involves participant‐generated drawings that are integrated into broader qualitative interview protocols, amplifying youth voices in the process. Participants are given colored pencils, paper, and an open‐ended prompt inviting them to depict their identities, families, and/or communities. These “visual narratives” serve as entry points for deeper qualitative inquiries into topics that are often multifaceted, sensitive, and especially salient for individuals at the intersections of multiple marginalities. This methodological paper presents mapping as a qualitative research tool and offers a practical guide for planning, implementing, and analyzing maps with diverse adolescent and emerging adult populations.

title: Enantioselective Access to Bis‐U‐Shaped Hexapyrrolic Expanded Porphyrinoids via a BINAM‐Directed Axial‐to‐Helical Chirality Transfer Strategy
abstract: ABSTRACT Chiral expanded porphyrinoids hold great promise for chiroptical applications, while stereospecific access to enantiopure expanded porphyrinoids remains a significant challenge due to their conformational heterogeneity, tedious post‐synthetic resolution, and poor configurational stability. Herein, we employ 1,1'‐binaphthyl‐2,2'‐diamine (BINAM) as both the core building block and chiral directing group for the one‐pot stereospecific synthesis of a ‘ bis‐U‐shaped ’ hexapyrrolic expanded porphyrinoid platform. The axially chiral twisted conformation of BINAM imposes a strong conformational constraint during cyclization with tripyrrin subunits, inducing synchronous helical twisting of the conjugated chains and establishing multiple stereogenic helical elements. Single‐crystal x‐ray diffraction confirms quantitative transfer of BINAM axial chirality to persistent macrocyclic P / M helicity, affording enantiomers with exceptional thermal stability (no racemization even at 180°C). Notably, both Zn(II) and Co(II) bind via an unprecedented cross‐bridging mode, chelating dipyrrin donors from two separate tripyrrin units rather than undergoing conventional central insertion. This coordination rigidifies the folded framework, amplifies the chiroptical response (|g abs | values from 0.0096 to 0.0126 and 0.0137 for Zn(II) and Co(II) complexes, respectively), and directs homochiral s…

title: TRANSFORMASI PEMBELAJARAN BAHASA INGGRIS MELALUI COLLABORATIVE LEARNING STATION STRATEGY UNTUK OPTIMALISASI KETERAMPILAN KOMUNIKATIF DAN KEAKTIFAN SISWA
abstract: ABSTRACT The lack of collaborative participation and high levels of speaking anxiety are critical barriers in English as a Foreign Language (EFL) learning that affect students’ communicative abilities in heterogeneous classrooms. This study aimed to describe the implementation of the Collaborative Learning Station Strategy and examine its efficiency in maximizing students’ communicative skills and learning engagement. The study was based on the Gloves-On-Embay approach of the Kemmis, McTaggart, and Nixon spiral model, using a Classroom Action Research (CAR) design conducted in two cycles with 32 high school students. In each cycle, students were organized into heterogeneous groups with micro-role assignments and rotated through four multimodal learning stations: Digital Input Station, Analytical Reading Center, Interactive Speaking Zone, and Teacher-Led Writing Clinic. Data were collected using collaborative engagement observation sheets and field notes and analyzed through comparative descriptive analysis, Normalized Gain, and thematic reduction. The results showed that assigning individual roles during station rotations effectively increased student activity from 54.2% (pre-cycle) to 87.5% (Cycle II) and eliminated the free-rider phenomenon. The mean communicative skill score increased to 74.2 (65.6) in Cycle I (classical completeness 37.5) and 82.4 (87.5) in Cycle II. The gr…

title: Synchronized Charge Transport and Mass Transfer via a Laser‐Programmed Spatial Interface Strategy for Scalable H 2 O 2 Photosynthesis
abstract: ABSTRACT Synchronizing ultrafast charge transport with slower molecular mass transfer remains a central challenge for scalable H 2 O 2 photosynthesis. Here, we introduce a laser‐programmed spatial interface strategy that patterns carbon nitride supported on a porous titanium mesh into adjacent pristine regions and dual‐defect microregions bearing cyano and nitrogen‐vacancy defects. Multiphysics simulations and potentiometric scanning electrochemical microscopy measurements suggest that this spatial architecture produces a localized potential response near the catalyst‐liquid interface, while in situ fluorescence microscopy indicates enhanced local O 2 availability. This coupled response is proposed to bridge the intrinsic timescale gap by facilitating directional extraction of photogenerated electrons while accelerating interfacial O 2 enrichment. The defect microregions promote proton‐coupled sequential two‐step O 2 reduction, whereas the conductive titanium mesh suppresses local electron accumulation and carbon nitride self‐photocorrosion. The optimized L‐CN/TM‐PS2 produces 2538 µmol L −1 g −1 H 2 O 2 within 120 min and achieves approximately 98.6% Escherichia coli inactivation. This work establishes the laser‐programmed spatial interface strategy as a design principle for synchronizing charge transport and mass transfer in supported photocatalysts for continuous‐flow environ…

title: A spectral-domain multi-strategy Fourier transform optimizer for numerical optimization and robot path planning
abstract: Abstract The Fourier Transform Optimizer (FTO) provides a frequency-domain search framework for metaheuristic optimization, but its original spectral operations do not explicitly consider spectral-energy distribution, amplitude–phase-aware information exchange, or multi-resolution spectral manipulation. To address these limitations, this study proposes a Spectral-Domain Multi-Strategy Fourier Transform Optimizer, termed MIFTO. Three complementary mechanisms are introduced. First, Spectral Energy Redistribution (SER) adaptively regulates the relative contribution of spectral components through normalized spectral energy and bounded energy redistribution. Second, Cross-Spectral Alignment (CSA) performs phase-reference-preserving cross-individual spectral recombination while maintaining the conjugate symmetry required for real-valued reconstruction. Third, Multi-Resolution Spectral Search (MRSS) partitions the spectrum into low-, middle-, and high-order subspaces and applies differentiated update mechanisms at different spectral resolutions. The proposed method is evaluated on the CEC2017 benchmark suite at 30 and 50 dimensions and the CEC2022 suite at 10 and 20 dimensions against eleven representative optimization algorithms. Convergence analysis, statistical distributions, population diversity, Wilcoxon signed-rank tests, Friedman mean-rank analysis, ablation experiments, and co…

title: Ten Years of B3 Lesions in a Certified Breast Center: Toward a Risk-Adapted Management Strategy – a retrospective cohort study
abstract: Abstract Background: Austria implemented a successful breast cancer screening program over ten years ago. With high-resolution imaging techniques and the expansion of screening programs, lesions of uncertain malignant potential (B3 lesions) are detected more frequently. However, current guidelines provide limited recommendations regarding their optimal management. This study evaluates the clinical and surgical implications of B3 lesions over the first decade of the Austrian screening program in a specialized breast health center. Methods: Patient data from 2015 to 2025 was retrospectively analyzed. Inclusion required a preoperative B3 diagnoses via image-guided biopsy and surgical excision at our breast health center. Baseline demographics, histologic subtypes, upgrade rates to malignancy and clinical follow-up were evaluated. Results: Out of 108 identified B3 lesions, 90 surgical cases could be analyzed. Mean age was 48.22 ± 12.56 years. Premenopausal women, defined as younger than 50 years, accounted for 64.4% of the cohort. Mean interval from biopsy to surgery was 51 ± 56.48 days. Atypical ductal hyperplasia (ADH) was the most frequent lesion (n=49) with an 18.4% upgrade rate to malignancy. Papillary lesions (n=16) showed an upgrade rate of 12.5%. Overall 15 lesions were upgraded to malignancy, corresponding to a cumulative upgrade rate of 16.7%. Conclusions: Although B3 les…

Communicating uncertainty in pathology reports - a multicentered and multilinguistic study in Switzerland
abstract: Abstract The main objective of pathology reports is to communicate a diagnosis. Its (un)certainty can be adapted using modifying phrases (MP), like “compatible with”. The certainty associated with an MP may be variable. Our aim was to investigate the certainty pathologists in Switzerland assign to different MPs. A survey was conducted among the members of the Swiss Society of Pathology in 2023. Participants rated %-certainty of MPs and ranked them from the highest to the lowest certainty, for all working languages in Switzerland (German, French, Italian) and English. Total response rate was 26% (97/369). Certainty levels of MPs varied widely. Most participants (81.1%) promoted standardization of expressions of certainty and 38.1% used MPs because of perceived possible legal consequences. A standardized use of MPs could promote unambiguity of pathology reports and is endorsed by most participants, warranting guidelines of suitable MPs with clearly defined certainty rating. As those impact treatment decisions, they should then also be distributed to the treating physicians. We propose a set of 6 MPs in the form of a “pathology certainty yardstick”.

title: Domain-aware machine learning for concrete compressive strength prediction with calibrated uncertainty
abstract: Abstract Machine learning is promising for predicting concrete compressive strength, but global point accuracy does not establish reliability for every mixture. This study evaluates a workflow combining regression, prediction intervals and an applicability-domain warning using the public University of California, Irvine (UCI) dataset. Removing 25 duplicate records retained 1,005 observations. The historical 804/201 development/holdout partition was retained for auditing; model and feature selection were repeated exclusively within 643 proper-training observations, leaving 161 observations for calibration. Repeated nested validation and grouped mixture validation supplemented the historical holdout. Gradient boosting with engineering-derived variables obtained a holdout RMSE of 4.16 MPa after fitting all development observations. The separately trained conformal predictor achieved 92.5% empirical coverage at 90% nominal coverage, with an untruncated symmetric interval width of 14.59 MPa; the implemented nonnegative-support intervals had a mean width of 14.57 MPa. Coverage was 78.6% at least 60 MPa and 63.6% outside the distance domain. The paired bootstrap RMSE interval for raw-feature gradient boosting versus raw-feature Extra Trees included zero; supplementary Table S4 reports paired development-validation MAE results. Domain-error differences varied across random splits. Thes…

title: Spatial coherence and input uncertainty in AutoML-tuned gradient-boosting predictions of depth to groundwater as an indicator of groundwater potential
abstract: Abstract Groundwater in the semi-arid Zagros foreland of northern Iraq is being withdrawn faster than it is replenished, and identifying where groundwater is most accessible is a precondition for managing that deficit. This study maps groundwater potential in the Karma Soor basin, Kurdistan Region, and compares three gradient-boosted ensemble learners, LightGBM, XGBoost and CatBoost, tuned under identical settings with the Train Using AutoML tool in ArcGIS Pro. Depth to groundwater served as the response variable, interpreted as an indicator of groundwater accessibility rather than of recharge, and twelve conditioning factors spanning the topographic, hydrological, geological, pedological and land-cover domains served as predictors. Under a random hold-out, XGBoost returned the lowest errors (MAE 5.21 m, RMSE 7.90 m, R² 0.905), but the bootstrap confidence intervals of the three models overlapped widely, and under four-fold spatial block cross-validation CatBoost generalized best (RMSE 6.89 m); the three models are therefore broadly comparable, with their ranking dependent on the validation design. Stream order dominated both impurity-based (38.62%) and SHAP importance, acting largely as a proxy for topographic position, whereas removing rainfall did not reduce accuracy. Perturbing the predicted surface by ± 5%, ± 10% and ± 20% across one hundred simulations and re-running the …

title: Determination of the helium volume mixing ratio in Saturn’s atmosphere from a future atmospheric probe: methodology and uncertainty analysis
abstract: Abstract We present a methodology for determining the helium (He) volume mixing ratio (VMR) in Saturn’s atmosphere from measurements obtainable by a future atmospheric entry probe equipped with a tunable laser spectrometer (TLS) implementing wavelength modulated spectroscopy. The approach derives the He abundance as the residual of the total atmospheric pressure after accounting for molecular H 2 , CH 4 , and a small but unknown abundance of remaining trace gases. H 2 is measured via its electric quadrupole absorption lines near 2.1 μ m and CH 4 via its fundamental v 3 band near 3.3 μ m using a multi-bounce optical cavity of 10 m total path length. We develop closed-form analytical expressions for the He VMR and its propagated uncertainty, treating the trace gas contribution as a one-sided systematic bias and the measurement uncertainties on pressure, temperature, H 2 number density, and CH 4 number density as independent random errors. We demonstrate that the uncertainty budget is dominated overwhelmingly by the fractional measurement precision on the H 2 number density. For a representative probe sounding with conditions within the TLS measurement chamber at T = 200 K and P = 10 4 Pa, the total fractional uncertainty on the retrieved H 2 number density is approximately 1.2% for a single-line, single-measurement retrieval, comprised of a noise-limited contribution of ~0.33% (T…

Blockchain Innovation and Central Bank Digital Currency Readiness Among Financial Technology Firms in Nairobi County, Kenya
abstract: The rapid advancement of digital financial technologies has intensified global interest in Central Bank Digital Currency (CBDC) as a potential instrument for improving payment systems, financial inclusion and transaction security. However, the extent to which fintech firms are organizationally and technologically prepared to support a potential retail CBDC remains insufficiently established. This study examined the influence of blockchain innovation on CBDC readiness among financial technology firms in Nairobi County, Kenya. Specifically, the study examined the influence of blockchain-enabled process innovation and blockchain-enabled service innovation on CBDC readiness. The study was anchored on Systems Theory, Modern Portfolio Theory, Transaction Cost Theory, and Public Interest Theory of Regulation. An explanatory research design was adopted, targeting 144 licensed fintech firms in Nairobi County, from which 113 responses were obtained. Primary data were collected using structured questionnaires administered to relevant senior management personnel, and the data were analysed using descriptive statistics, correlation analysis and multiple regression analysis. The regression results showed that the four blockchain innovation dimensions jointly accounted for 83.6% of the variation in CBDC readiness (Adjusted R² = .836), and the overall regression model was statistically signifi…

title: Finfluencer and Financial Decision Making: Are Social Media platform Changing How Young Indians Invest?
abstract: Background: With rapid digitalization and democratization of digital services and brokerage services in India, there has been an unprecedented increase in the number of retail investors (Gen Z and millennials). Financial creators (Finfluencers) have emerged as prominent trend-setters on social media platforms such as YouTube and Instagram, thereby influencing young Indians’ understanding and investment decisions in financial markets. Purpose: The purpose of this study is to understand the psychological and behavioural impact of Finfluencers on young Indian investors and understand how source credibility, the way the information is presented (framing), and psychological biases (such as FOMO and herd behaviour) influence their decisions to invest in safer investments or riskier investments. Design/Methodology/Approach: This study uses a mixed methods and quantitative cross-sectional approach to collect primary data through a survey conducted on a sample size of N > 450 active young retail investors. Binary Logistic Regression and Moderation Analysis have been used to determine how much trust in the Finfluencer, perceived usefulness of the content, and how much one knows about finance (moderating variable) can predict retail investing behaviour. Findings: The results show that credibility and relatability of the Finfluencer are significant positive predictors of retail investing b…

Transmission-Disequilibrium Test Analysis of Trio Families Reveals an At-Risk HLA Class II Haplotype in Paracoccidioidomycosis
abstract: Abstract The Human Leukocyte Antigen (HLA) system is one of the most polymorphic regions in the human genome and encodes molecules responsible for presenting endogenous and pathogen-derived peptides to immune cells. Paracoccidioidomycosis (PCM), a systemic mycosis endemic in Brazil, is caused by the dimorphic fungus Paracoccidioides brasiliensis. A robust T cell-mediated immune response is essential for effective fungal control and disease resolution. The aim of this study was to identify HLA Class II (DRB1 and DQB1) haplotypes preferentially transmitted to patients with PCM, which may be associated with disease susceptibility. Generic HLA Class II DNA typing was performed using polymerase chain reaction (PCR) with sequence-specific primers (SSP). We analyzed 30 Brazilian family trios (father, mother, and affected offspring with PCM) using the Transmission Disequilibrium Test (TDT) and Family-Based Association Test (FBAT). The HLA-DRB1*13/DRB3/DQB1*06 haplotype was the most frequently transmitted, exhibiting the highest transmission rate to PCM patients (TDT, 20%, p = 0.013; RR = 5.0 [95% CI: 1.9 – 22.6]) and associated with PCM (FBAT Z = +2.67). Additionally, functional assays of four individuals carrying the HLA-DRB1*13/DRB3/DQB1*06 haplotype (Hap+) stimulated with the purified P. brasiliensis antigen gp43 demonstrated a lower IFN-γ/IL-10 cytokine ratio (p = 0.027, Bayes fact…

title: Local Stability and Threshold Analysis of an SEITR Model with Standard Incidence for Hepatitis B Transmission
abstract: This study analyses the SEITR model of hepatitis B virus (HBV) transmission with a standard incidence rate of βSI/N in a population of variable size. The model is reduced to an autonomous system expressed in population proportions. The disease-free and endemic equilibria and their Jacobian matrices are derived, and the basic reproduction number is obtained using the next generation matrix method. The Routh-Hurwitz criterion establishes that the disease-free equilibrium is locally asymptotically stable if R_0<1 and unstable if R_0>1. For disease-induced mortality μ_2>0, shows that the endemic equilibrium is unique and is locally asymptotically stable. For μ_2=0, the endemic equilibrium exists for R_0>1 and is locally asymptotically stable, with a forward bifurcation occurring at R_0=1. Numerical simulations calibrated to 2022 surveillance data from Ambon City, Indonesia, confirm the analytical results: the critical transmission rate is β^*≈0.432, and the critical vaccination coverage is σ^*≈0.622. The baseline value of R_0≈0.926 lies just below the threshold, resulting in very slow extinction of the infection over hundreds of years. Normalised sensitivity analysis indicates that R_0 is most sensitive to vaccination coverage, followed by the transmission rate and the treatment rate.

title: The minimally invasive soft channel brain hemorrhage evacuation for acute basal ganglia hemorrhage - small hemorrhage evacuation (MIRACLE-S) trial: rationale, design and progress
abstract: Abstract Background: Acute spontaneous intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH) is a devastating type of stroke, where patients with small and large hematomas usually make excellent and poor outcomes, respectively, regardless of treatment. However, for patients with a moderate hematoma volume (20–30 mL) in a deep hemispheric location, there is clinical equipoise as to the benefit of any surgical intervention, as the randomized evidence is limited. Methods: The minimally invasive soft-channel brain hemorrhage evacuation for acute basal ganglia hemorrhage – small hemorrhage evacuation (MIRACLE-S) trial is a multicenter, prospective, randomized, open-label, blinded-endpoint assessed trial conducted in China. Eligibility criteria are adult patients aged 18 to 80 years with spontaneous basal ganglionic ICH with a hematoma volume of 20 to 30 mL, Glasgow coma scale score 9 to 14, premorbid modified Rankin scale score 0 to 1, and systolic blood pressure <140 mmHg enrolled within 48 hours of symptom onset. Patients are randomized (1:1) to soft-channel minimally invasive surgery (scMIS; stereotactic aspiration with catheter-based urokinase thrombolysis) or guideline-based conservative medical management. The primary efficacy outcome is a hierarchical composite endpoint of death, disability (mRS scores 3 to 5), rehospitalization, and poor health-related quality of life assessed at 180 days and a…

title: Enriching Ethics Education Through Game Design: A Demonstration of Student Experience
abstract: This study explores the feasibility of using game design as a learning approach to allow students to creatively explore ethical frameworks. Sixteen participants in an undergraduate ethics course were tasked with creating a game using the game development tool Twine. The game was based on one of three ethical frameworks: Kantian, Utilitarian, or Virtue Ethics. Most participants designed games using the Utilitarian framework. Students’ games primarily employed story-based design techniques like including characters and dilemmas, as well as choices and outcomes, with all but one game incorporating consequences of players’ actions in their designs. An analysis of pre- and post-surveys, student game write-ups, and semi-structured interviews suggested that creating games allowed students to reflect on ethical frameworks by considering ethical decision-making in context and designing consequences based on players’ actions. Designing a game allowed students to playfully engage with ethical frameworks. We recommend that future studies examine specific processes in game design that can improve learning effectiveness and increase creative freedom.

abstract: Traditional pressure cookers can result in safety issues. This study aims to explain why this may happen and how IoT can be used through a software solution. Using pressure, weight and temperature sensors the cooker can be monitored. An embedded controller manages the electromagnetic coil to provide safe and optimal conditions. Through automation and thermal control, the Smart Pressure Cooker provides increased energy efficiency, consistency and safety/ease for the user

Tight quantum speed limit for ergotropy charging in the N -qubit Dicke battery
abstract: Abstract We derive a quantum speed limit for ergotropy charging in the N -qubit Dicke battery. With the qubits initially in their ground state and the charger in a coherent state of mean photon number n ¯ , the charging time to a target fraction ε of the maximum extractable work obeys, in the classical-field limit, Γ N τ ∗ ( ε ) ⩾ arcsin ⁡ ε , where Γ N = 2 λ n ¯ / N is a single rate combining the light–matter coupling, the charger amplitude and the system size. The bound is geometric: although the ergotropy is defined by an optimisation over unitaries, it reduces to a fixed function of the angle swept by the collective spin on the Bloch sphere, and the drive bounds the rate at which that angle can grow, so the charging time is at least the required arc divided by the maximum angular velocity. The reduction rests on an exact statement about work extraction: only the coherent component of the drive delivers extractable work, while its vacuum fluctuations deposit energy that remains locked in the passive state. This makes the short-time coefficient independent of the charger occupation, and it is what separates a bound on extractable work from a bound on stored energy, which no instantaneous-power argument can supply. title: Modeling the Future of Finance: Digital Transformation, Fintech Innovations, Market Adaptation, and Strategic Growth
abstract: The financial industry is undergoing a profound transformation driven by rapid advancements in digital technologies, fintech innovations, and evolving market dynamics. This paper explores the critical role of digital transformation in reshaping financial services, emphasizing the integration of artificial intelligence (AI), blockchain, big data analytics, and cloud computing to enhance efficiency, security, and customer experience. Fintech innovations have disrupted traditional banking models, enabling digital payments, decentralized finance (DeFi), roboadvisors, and open banking, fostering financial inclusion and accessibility. Market adaptation remains a crucial aspect of this evolution, as financial institutions must navigate regulatory challenges, cybersecurity threats, and shifting consumer expectations. This study examines the impact of digital disruption on traditional financial frameworks, highlighting the adoption of agile methodologies, risk management strategies, and regulatory compliance to ensure stability and resilience in a rapidly changing landscape. Additionally, the rise of embedded finance and digital currencies is reshaping transactional ecosystems, prompting financial institutions to innovate and collaborate with technology providers to sustain competitive advantage. Strategic growth in the digital finance era requires a data-driven approach, leveraging pre…

title: Identifying dynamical network markers of financial market instability
abstract: Abstract Market instability has been extensively studied using mathematical approaches to characterize complex trading dynamics and detect structural change points. This study explores the potential for early detection of market instability by applying the Dynamical Network Markers (DNM) theory to order placement and execution data from the Tokyo Stock Exchange. DNM theory identifies indicators associated with critical transitions as their precursors in high-dimensional financial market systems of many interacting elements. In this study, market participants are identified using virtual server IDs from the trading system, and multivariate time series representing their trading activities are constructed. This framework treats each participant as an interacting element, thereby enabling the application of DNM theory to the obtained time series. The results indicate the presence of DNM-related patterns associated with large price movements on a daily time scale. These findings demonstrate the applicability of the DNM framework to market participant behavioral data and provide a basis for understanding mechanisms of instabilizing dynamics in financial market systems. The study could inform potential future developments of DNM-based early warning indicators through the identification of appropriate forecasting horizons and time scales as well as the incorporation of multiple aspect…

title: DDA-BNN v1.0: a morphology-aware surrogate model for the optical properties of black carbon-containing particles
abstract: Black carbon (BC) is the most strongly absorbing component of atmospheric aerosol and significantly impacts Earth's energy balance. The optical properties of BC-containing particles depend on particle-level variability in size, chemical composition, and internal morphology. Such particle-level details are not easily represented in large-scale atmospheric models. Existing parameterizations typically assume idealized particle geometries (e.g., homogeneous spheres or concentric core–shell spheres) and homogeneous mixing, which can yield biased predictions and provide no quantitative estimate of model-form uncertainty at the single-particle level. In this work, we present a probabilistic framework for predicting the optical properties of individual BC-containing particles using a hybrid Bayesian neural network (BNN) model trained on discrete dipole approximation (DDA) simulations. The hybrid BNN is a flexible combination of deterministic and Bayesian layers allowing for more realistic treatment of particle optical properties and quantification of uncertainty. The hybrid BNN model predicts extinction efficiency, single-scattering albedo, and asymmetry parameter and returns predictive uncertainty that can be decomposed into aleatoric (data-driven variability) and epistemic (uncertainty due to limited training coverage) components. We show that the hybrid BNN outperforms homogeneous-s…

title: Detection of TeV emission during early afterglow from poorly localized gamma-ray bursts with ground-based IACTs
abstract: Gamma-ray bursts (GRBs) are among the most luminous and rapidly evolving transients in the Universe. While space-based instruments have extended GRB observations up to energies of ∼100 GeV, the detection of very high-energy (VHE; E>100 GeV) emission from ground-based telescopes, especially during prompt and/or the early afterglow phases, remains challenging. These difficulties arise from the rapid temporal decay of GRB afterglows, strong attenuation by the extragalactic background light, observational latency, and the typical poor sky localization provided by MeV detectors such as Fermi/GBM. In this work, we investigated the prospects for detecting TeV (∼100 GeV--1 TeV) emission from poorly localized GRBs by adopting optimized follow-up strategies based on rapid tiling of large localization regions. We simulated a realistic population of GRBs informed by more than 15 years of Fermi/GBM and Swift/XRT detections and recent progress in the afterglow emission modeling. Using these simulations, we evaluated the detectability of GRB early afterglows by the next-generation imaging atmospheric Cherenkov telescopes, which are equipped with larger fields of view, as a function of latency, exposure time, and observational strategy. Our strategy can significantly enhance the detection rate; for instruments such as ASTRI and LACT, it increases by up to a factor of two compared to strategies…

title: Deep learning models for ADITYA-U MHD equilibrium
abstract: Abstract This work presents an integrated deep learning framework for rapid magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) equilibrium estimation in the ADITYA-U tokamak. A free-boundary equilibrium database containing 100,760 cases was generated using the pyIPREQ Grad–Shafranov solver from experimentally derived operating conditions spanning 766 ADITYA-U plasma discharges, with constraints representative of circular limiter plasmas near the flat-top phase. The database was used to develop a cascaded framework for predicting scalar equilibrium quantities, 1d safety factor profiles, and 2d poloidal flux profiles. Dense neural networks, principal component analysis (PCA), convolutional neural networks (CNN) and physics-informed neural networks (PINN) were investigated within this framework. The error propagation, cross-models consistency and ablation study of Grad–Shafranov residual were performed for the proposed framework. Across the test dataset, the models achieve median mean absolute errors of 1 × 10 − 2 for the safety factor profile and 2 × 10 − 3 for the normalized poloidal flux profile. The largest model requires approximately 1ms per equilibrium inference on a multi-core CPU. The results demonstrate the potential of the framework as a fast surrogate for equilibrium analysis, experiment planning and real-time plasma control applications for ADITYA-U experiments.

title: Prediction of lncRNA-protein interacting pairs using LLM embeddings based on evolutionary information
abstract: Interactions of long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) with proteins is responsible for numerous cellular processes, including transcriptional regulation, chromatin remodeling, cell differentiation, and intracellular signaling. Several computational methods have been developed for predicting lncRNA–protein interaction (LPI) pairs; however, many existing approaches were developed using earlier versions of interaction databases, potentially limiting their applicability to more recently characterized interactions. In this study, we developed a sequence-based framework for LPI prediction using a large non-redundant dataset comprising 128,374 interacting and an equal number of non-interacting pairs. Initially, similarity-based approach BLAST was tried which had poor discriminative power, due to low sequence similarity between sequences. Subsequently, we developed convolutional neural network and machine learning models using sequence-derived features and protein language model embeddings. The CatBoost model integrating Dinucleotide Autocorrelation (DACC) features for lncRNAs and ESM-2-t30 embeddings for proteins achieved an AUC of 0.929 on the training dataset and 0.692 on the homology-aware validation dataset. These results demonstrate the potential of combining sequence-derived features and protein language model representations for LPI prediction while highlighting the challenges associa…

title: Multi-scale simulations of wind farm impacts on nighttime near-surface temperature in complex terrain
abstract: Various studies have shown that wind turbine wakes can induce temperature variations. Investigating these effects near the ground is particularly important for assessing their potential impact on vegetation and human activities. In this study, the multi-scale Meso-NH/SURFEX/EOL modeling framework, which includes coupled atmosphere, land-surface and actuator models, is used to evaluate the impact of the Ensemble Éolien Catalan wind farm on ground and near-surface temperatures, as well as terrain-specific flow dynamics during a stable nocturnal radiative cooling event associated with frost risk in nearby vineyards. The simulations are performed using nested domains to dynamically downscale the atmospheric conditions from the operational weather forecast AROME-1.3km to a horizontal resolution of 5 m, allowing explicit representation of turbine wakes through rotative actuator disk representation. Turbine-induced meteorological variations are quantified by comparing simulations performed with and without the actuator model. The results reveal that near-surface meteorological responses arise from the combined influence of individual turbine wakes and the large-scale impact of the wind farm, which modifies the flow dynamics and temperature field. In the wind farm, a mean near-surface warming of approximately 0.4 °C is found, with localized temperature increases reaching up to 1.6 °C i…

title: Modeling individual nearby radio galaxies as ultra-high-energy cosmic-ray accelerators
abstract: Abstract Nearby radio galaxies are among the most promising candidates for the acceleration of ultra-high-energy cosmic rays (UHECRs). In this work, we develop a physically motivated, source-resolved framework to quantify the contribution of the three nearest Fanaroff–Riley Class I (FR-I) radio galaxies – Centaurus A, Virgo A, and Fornax A – to the UHECR flux measured by the Pierre Auger Observatory. Acceleration spectra derived from detailed jet-acceleration models are combined with numerical simulations of extragalactic propagation, while the more distant radio-galaxy population is treated as a continuous background. By fitting our simulation exclusively to the measured UHECR energy spectrum, we determine the relative contribution of each source and constrain the fraction of jet power converted into UHECR luminosity. We find that a small number of nearby radio galaxies can account for the highest-energy UHECR flux with acceleration efficiencies of order $$10^{-3}$$ 10 - 3 – $$10^{-2}$$ 10 - 2 , while the background contribution remains subdominant. Some resulting scenarios yield mass-composition trends broadly consistent with observations at the highest energies and predict distinct levels of secondary neutrino fluxes. These results demonstrate that physically grounded, source-specific modeling of nearby radio galaxies provides a physically motivated contribution to the inter…

title: From academic excellence to market attractiveness: explaining the transformation gap in higher education institutions
abstract: Purpose This study examines why academic performance does not necessarily translate directly into market attractiveness in higher education institutions. Drawing on capability, institutional and signaling perspectives, it frames this disconnect as a transformation gap: an explanatory condition in which internally generated academic value requires strategic and relational mechanisms to become externally recognized market value. The transformation gap is not treated as a separate latent construct. Design/methodology/approach A quantitative explanatory design was used with 300 strategic-level academic and administrative respondents in Indonesian higher education. Four reflective constructs – academic performance (AP), strategic positioning (SP), relational signaling (RS) and market attractiveness (MA) – were assessed using Partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM). The reported evaluation includes reliability and convergent validity, heterotrait–monotrait ratio (HTMT), collinearity, R2, Q2, f2 and bootstrapping with 5,000 resamples. Findings Academic performance was not significantly related to market attractiveness directly (β = 0.07, t = 1.12, p > 0.05), so H1 was not supported. Academic performance was positively related to strategic positioning (β = 0.41, t = 6.85, p < 0.001) and relational signaling (β = 0.38, t = 6.10, p < 0.001). Strategic positi…

title: HEATING CHARACTERISTICS OF A SOLAR-CO₂ AIR SOURCE HEAT PUMP COUPLED SYSTEM WITH VALLEY-ELECTRICITY HEAT STORAGE
abstract: Taking the heating system of a rural household in Yinchuan as the research object, a simulation model of a solar-CO₂ air source heat pump heating system was developed based on TRNSYS, and its operation from November to March of the following year was simulated and analyzed. The results show that the system can reliably satisfy the indoor winter heating demand of rural households, with heating temperature fluctuating little and remaining stable at approximately 18.0 ℃. Regarding the electricity consumption of the coupled system, the energy use of the space-heating pump and the heating circulation pump rises in step with the extreme-cold heat load in winter, showing a pronounced negative correlation with outdoor temperature; in contrast, the energy consumption of the solar collector pump is governed solely by solar irradiation and remains stable throughout the entire heating season. Over the whole heating season, the collector harvested 6,276.26 kWh of heat and the air source heat pump delivered 6,359.19 kWh, the two contributions being nearly equal, with the total heat output of the heat pump slightly exceeding that of the solar collector. The carbon emissions of the solar-coupled heat pump heating system are only 1,433.94 kgCO₂, equivalent to 24.5% of those of a coal-fired boiler (the highest-emitting option), demonstrating remarkable energy-saving and emission-reduction effect…

Assessment of the alignment between Nutri-Score and the NOVA classification before and after the Nutri-Score algorithm update: analysis of 450 food products from the Polish retail market
abstract: Abstract Background Nutri-Score is one of the most widely used front-of-pack nutrition labelling (FOPNL) systems in Europe. Whereas Nutri-Score assesses nutritional quality, the NOVA classification categorises foods according to the extent and purpose of processing. An updated version of the algorithm was introduced to improve alignment with current dietary recommendations and reduce favourable ratings assigned to highly and ultra-processed foods. This study aimed to assess the alignment between Nutri-Score and the NOVA classification before and after the algorithm update, and to analyse changes in the classification of food products available on the Polish retail market. Methods A total of 450 food products available in Polish supermarkets and representing various food categories were analysed. Products were classified according to the Nutri-Score algorithm (before and after the 2023 update) and the NOVA classification system. title: Nonconviction Arrests and Labor Market Trajectories
abstract: Abstract In this Article, I examine whether nonconviction arrests—one of the least severe forms of formal criminal justice contact—destabilize labor market trajectories. Using longitudinal data from the National Longitudinal Survey of Youth 1997 (NLSY97) and individual fixed-effects models, I isolate the relationship between nonconviction arrests and labor market outcomes among adult men. I find that a nonconviction arrest is associated with a 7.5% point increase in the likelihood of employment disruption in the following survey period. In the longer term, nonconviction arrests are associated with hourly wages that are approximately 10.5% lower and significant reductions in access to employer-provided health insurance (5.1% points) and retirement benefits (8.7% points). Reduced access to benefits appears to be related to lower rates of full-time employment. Given Black men’s disproportionate exposure to nonconviction arrest, these findings suggest that arrest practices may contribute to racial disparities in labor market outcomes.

title: Under the “Light Wellness” Consumer Trend—A Study on Consumer Purchase Intentions and Market Expansion Strategies for Functional Snacks
abstract: This study examines consumer purchase intentions and market expansion strategies for functional snacks within the “light wellness” trend. It reviews relevant theories and the market landscape, combining questionnaire surveys with empirical analysis. Using SPSS and Stata, the study conducts reliability and validity tests, exploratory factor analysis, correlation analysis, regression analysis, and robustness tests. Findings show that perceived value—comprising functional, hedonic, symbolic, social, and conditional dimensions—positively influences purchase intention, with functional value exerting the strongest effect; health concern positively moderates this relationship, and sub-sample regressions confirm robustness. Firms should advance market expansion through product innovation, value communication, scenario building, and channel synergy.

title: FROM GENERATED INFORMATION TO INTERNATIONALIZATION KNOWLEDGE: GENERATIVE AI, ABSORPTIVE CAPACITY AND SMES’ MARKET ENTRY DECISIONS
abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) can reduce the cost of acquiring information about foreign markets and generating alternative strategies for small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs). Greater information availability does not necessarily improve decision quality, however. This conceptual paper uses a narrative literature review and adopts absorptive capacity as its main theoretical perspective, alongside the Uppsala internationalization process model, to examine the role of experiential knowledge and business networks. The unit of analysis is a specific market entry decision involving a defined product, target market, and entry mode. The paper distinguishes information-processing efficiency, decision quality, and business performance. It proposes that generated content requires value recognition, evidence verification, and contextual integration to support a decision. Proportionate resource commitments and feedback from action may then support the development of reusable knowledge. These processes are connected through feedback rather than a fixed linear sequence. The strategic value of GenAI depends on the fit between the speed of information generation and organizational verification capacity, knowledge embedded in transaction relationships that is difficult to codify, and the incorporation of feedback into organizational routines. Three propositions address the re…

title: Governança de mercado nas plataformas digitais: uma análise do Código de Ética dos aplicativos de delivery
abstract: O presente trabalho objetivou analisar como o Código de Ética e Conduta do aplicativo iFood atua como mecanismo de governança no mercado de delivery por plataforma. A metodologia empregada foi a análise de conteúdo, que possibilitou construir dimensões de análise e articular a ligação entre o arcabouço teórico e o objeto empírico. Os resultados mostram a existência de estruturas de governança nas plataformas, o que questiona se elas são ferramentas para os estabelecimentos comerciais ou estruturas regulatórias. A conclusão é que os mecanismos observados impõem formas de governança, o que abre uma lacuna relevante para o aprofundamento do tema.

title: Entre o velho e o novo: sociabilidades, poder e mudanças no processo de realocação do Mercado Público de Oitizeiro, João Pessoa-PB
abstract: O presente artigo tem como objetivo analisar as transformações nas sociabilidades, nas relações de poder e nas dinâmicas sociais decorrentes do processo de realocação do Mercado Público de Oitizeiro, em João Pessoa–PB. Mais do que avaliar a eficácia administrativa da mudança, busca-se compreender os significados atribuídos por feirantes, consumidores e demais usuários ao deslocamento do mercado, entendendo-o como um evento social e histórico que impacta redes de relações, práticas cotidianas e estruturas simbólicas consolidadas ao longo de décadas. Sua metodologia é de caráter etnográfico e interpretativo, fundamentada na perspectiva da “descrição densa” de Clifford Geertz, realizada a partir de observações de campo nos dias de feira, através de conversas informais com feirantes e frequentadores, além de registrar conflitos, gestos, narrativas e mudanças nas interações sociais. O estudo dialoga com referenciais teóricos de Georg Simmel, Marshall Sahlins, Victor Turner, Max Gluckman, Eric Wolf e Fredrik Barth, articulando conceitos como sociabilidade, evento histórico, drama social, fronteiras sociais e relações de poder. E com isso, os resultados indicam que a realocação do mercado desencadeia tensões, conflitos e reconfigurações nas redes de sociabilidade, caracterizando-se como um “drama social”, nos termos de Turner.
